This section of the guidelines lays down these structures, their constitution, and their functions. District Grievance Redressal Committee (DGRC) - will be constituted by the SHA in each district and this is chaired by Head of the District or District Magistrate or District Collector or Deputy Commissioner. The State Grievance Redressal Committee (SGRC) is chaired by CEO of SHA / State Nodal Agency (SNA). The SGRC shall perform all functions related to handling and resolution of all grievances received either directly or escalated through the DGRC. The National Grievance Redressal Committee (NGRC) will be chaired by Deputy CEO of National Health Agency (NHA). The NGRC shall act as the final Appellate Authority at the national level. question: What are the conditions for the Disqualification/Termination of relief under ABVKY?
answer: - During lockout | - Strike resorted to by the employees declared illegal by the competent authority | - Voluntary abandonment of employment/ voluntary retirement/ premature retirement | - Less than two years of contributory service | - On attaining the age of superannuation | - Convicted (i.e. punished for false statement) under the provisions of Section 84 of the ESI Act read with Rule 62 of the ESI (Central) Rule | - On being re-employed elsewhere during the period he/she is in receipt of Relief under ABVKY | - Dismissal/termination under disciplinary action | - On the death of IP

scheme_name: Atal Beemit Vyakti Kalyan Yojana
question: What are the benefits of this scheme?
answer: The scheme provides relief to the extent of 50% of the average per day earnings of employees during their last employment. | The relief amount to be paid up to a maximum of 90 days of unemployment subject to conditions that the employee should have completed two years of Insurable employment and has contributed not less than Seventy-Eight (78) days in each of the three consecutive contribution periods.

scheme_name: Atal Beemit Vyakti Kalyan Yojana
question: What is the minimum employment period required to be eligible for Unemployment Insurance?

scheme_name: Atal Beemit Vyakti Kalyan Yojana
question: How many days of contribution are required in the contribution period preceding unemployment?
answer: The insured person should have contributed for not less than 78 days in the contribution period immediately preceding the unemployment.

scheme_name: Atal Beemit Vyakti Kalyan Yojana
question: Are there any additional contribution requirements in the two years prior to unemployment?
answer: Yes, in addition to the 78 days in the immediate preceding contribution period, the insured person must also have a minimum of 78 days of contribution in one of the remaining three contribution periods within the two years prior to unemployment.

scheme_name: Atal Beemit Vyakti Kalyan Yojana
question: When does an Unemployment Insurance claim become due?

question: Can an individual covered under the ESI scheme be considered unemployed if working for more than one employer?
answer: No, under the ESI scheme, an individual working for multiple employers will be considered unemployed only if they are rendered unemployed with all employers simultaneously.

scheme_name: Atal Beemit Vyakti Kalyan Yojana
question: What happens if an individual covered under the ESI scheme is unemployed with only one of the multiple employers?

scheme_name: Animal Husbandry: Assistance to Small and Marginal Farmers

scheme_name: Animal Husbandry: Assistance to Small and Marginal Farmers

scheme_name: "Advance/High Skill Training in Coir" Component of the "Development of Coir" Scheme

scheme_name: Animal Husbandry
question: What is the purpose of the scheme?
answer: This scheme provides subsidies on the distribution of sheep units, milch animals, and calves, as well as health coverage and artificial insemination for the animals. It is targeted at Adi Dravidar/Tribal communities to improve their livelihood through animal husbandry.

scheme_name: Animal Husbandry

answer: Beneficiaries receive subsidized livestock, including sheep units, milch animals, calves, as well as veterinary services and health cover for the animals.

scheme_name: Animal Husbandry

scheme_name: AYUSH Health and Wellness Centre - Ayushman Bharat Yojana

scheme_name: AYUSH Health and Wellness Centre - Ayushman Bharat Yojana

scheme_name: AYUSH Health and Wellness Centre - Ayushman Bharat Yojana

scheme_name: ASEAN-India Research Training Fellowship
question: What is the “ASEAN-India Research Training Fellowship” scheme?
answer: The scheme is launched as an initiative under the ASEAN-India Science & Technology Development Fund (AISTDF) to support young talented researchers/scientists of ASEAN member countries (namely Brunei Darussalam, Cambodia, Indonesia, Lao PDR, Malaysia, Myanmar, Philippines, Singapore, Thailand, and Vietnam) to carry out research at any of the Indian research/academic Institution.

scheme_name: ASEAN-India Research Training Fellowship
question: What is the objective of scheme?
answer: The AI-RTF scheme is a fellowship scheme with the following objectives: | To promote the mobility of scientists and researchers from the ASEAN-Member Countries to India and provide them the opportunity to work at Indian R&D/ academic institutions to upgrade their research skills and expertise. | To facilitate the exchange of information and contacts between the scientists and researchers of India and ASEAN Countries and create a network for building research collaborations.

scheme_name: ASEAN-India Research Training Fellowship
question: Which is the implementing agency of this scheme?
answer: Federation of Indian Chambers of Commerce & Industry (FICCI), New Delhi

scheme_name: ASEAN-India Research Training Fellowship
question: What are the eligibility criteria for applying/availing the Fellowship?
answer: Applicant must be holding the nationality of any of the ASEAN Member Countries. | Applicant should possess at least a Master's Degree in any Natural Sciences or an equivalent degree in Technology/Engineering/Medicine / allied disciplines. | Applicant should be working/studying and/or affiliated with any national R&D or academic institution in his/her home ASEAN Member Country. | The upper age limit for the applicant is 45 years as of the date of submission of the application.

scheme_name: ASEAN-India Research Training Fellowship
question: Are Indian nationals eligible for the Fellowship?
answer: No, Indian nationals are not eligible for the Fellowship.

scheme_name: ASEAN-India Research Training Fellowship
question: What are the areas covered under this Fellowship?
answer: The fellowship is available in all fields of natural & engineering sciences, including mathematics & statistics, except humanities and behavioral sciences- | Agricultural Sciences | Biological and Medical Sciences | Chemical Sciences & Engineering | Computer Science & Engineering | Physical Sciences and Mathematics | Ocean, Earth & Atmospheric Sciences | Engineering Sciences | Materials, Minerals and Metallurgy | Science Policy/IPR Management/Technology Transfer & Commercialization | - Other multi-disciplinary areas of Science, Technology and Innovation in alignment with APASTI

scheme_name: ASEAN-India Research Training Fellowship
question: What is the nature of support for the Fellow?
answer: Full financial assistance will be provided to the selected Fellows which includes the following:- | - Round trip international airfare by lowest economy class and by the shortest route from the international airport in the home country of the applicant to the international airport nearest to the host institution in India; visa fees, overseas medical insurance, etc. | - A consolidated Fellowship amount of Indian Rupees (INR) 60,000/- per month. | - One-time grant of INR 40,000/- as research contingency expenses, airport transfers, domestic travel for attending scientific /events, and field trips within India. | - Institutional overhead charges @ INR 2,500/- per month.

scheme_name: ASEAN-India Research Training Fellowship
question: How many fellowships are awarded per year under the scheme?
answer: Fifty (50) fellowships per year shall be awarded to young scientists and researchers from ASEAN-Member States to get affiliated with Indian academic and R&D institutions.

scheme_name: ASEAN-India Research Training Fellowship
question: What is the duration of fellowship?
answer: The duration of the Fellowship will be for a period of two to six months. No request for extension \ reduction in the duration period shall be entertained after the award of the fellowship.

scheme_name: ASEAN-India Research Training Fellowship
question: How to apply for the fellowship?
answer: The applications are to be submitted only ONLINE at (https://aistic.gov.in/ASEAN/aistdfFellowship). The hard copies of the application are not required. The applications submitted through any other form or channel shall not be considered.

scheme_name: AICTE-INAE Travel Grant Scheme For Engineering Students From AICTE Approved Engineering College/Institution

answer: The scheme is implemented by the Uttarakhand State Council for Science and Technology (UCOST) through the Regional Science Center, Dehradun, in collaboration with Intel.

scheme_name: AICTE - Scheme For Promoting Interests, Creativity And Ethics Among Students
question: Q.1 What Is AICTE Expecting From The Institution?
answer: A. AICTE expects institutions to fund its other clubs in a similar fashion and intensify their activities. Vibrant clubs will attract the attention of other institutions and inspire the latter to emulate. Thus there will be an intensification of club activities across the country.

scheme_name: AICTE - Scheme For Promoting Interests, Creativity And Ethics Among Students
question: Q.2 What Are The Strong Points Which Enhance The Possibility Of Support From AICTE?
answer: A. Past achievements of the club, its interface with industry/professional body, achievements of the Faculty Coordinator, and Credentials of the institute.

scheme_name: AICTE - Scheme For Promoting Interests, Creativity And Ethics Among Students
question: Q.3 Are Student Chapters/Societies Also Eligible To Apply?
answer: A. Yes.

scheme_name: AICTE - Scheme For Promoting Interests, Creativity And Ethics Among Students
question: Q.4 How Many Proposals Can Be Submitted By The Institute?
answer: A. Institute can seek support for one club only, for which it must be willing to support financially also.

scheme_name: AICTE - Scheme For Promoting Interests, Creativity And Ethics Among Students
question: Q.5 Will My Institute Be Eligible To Apply Again If The Project Is Granted Once?
answer: A. No. Institute will be eligible to receive the grant under the SPICES scheme only once. AICTE expects the institute to support other clubs in a similar fashion.

scheme_name: AICTE - Scheme For Promoting Interests, Creativity And Ethics Among Students
question: Q.6 Can Non-Technical/ Non-Engineering Clubs Apply Under This Scheme?
answer: A. Yes, the club from any discipline/ theme/ stream in an AICTE-approved institution can be proposed under this Scheme, provided it fulfills other eligibility conditions.

scheme_name: AICTE - Scheme For Promoting Interests, Creativity And Ethics Among Students
question: Q.7 What Is The Total Duration To Complete The SPICES Project?
answer: A. It's a one-year project which starts from the date of the Offer Letter/Sanction Letter.

scheme_name: AICTE - Scheme For Promoting Interests, Creativity And Ethics Among Students
question: Q.8 When Does The One-Year Project Duration Start?
answer: A. For the 2020-2021 batch, the date of receipt of funds is reckoned as the date of start of the project which must be intimated to AICTE. However, for those sanctioned in 2021- 2022, the date of the Offer Letter is the date of the start of the project.

scheme_name: AICTE - Scheme For Promoting Interests, Creativity And Ethics Among Students
question: Q.9 If Both Coordinator & Co-Coordinator Are Transferred/ Changed, Then How To Update The Details Of Another Coordinator?
answer: A. The institute must appoint another faculty as a coordinator whose qualifications and experience must be matching with the previous one and take approval from AICTE. One needs to go to "Request for Change of Coordinator/Co-coordinator" on the SPICES Review Portal, attach the requisite documents on the SPICES review portal, duly signed by the Head of Institution, and Coordinator, and submit.

scheme_name: AICTE - Scheme For Promoting Interests, Creativity And Ethics Among Students
question: Q.10 Do We Need To Submit Any Report To AICTE After The Completion Of The Project?
answer: A. Yes, at the end of the project duration, the institute must submit a soft copy and hard copy of the project report and original bills for the closure of the project.

scheme_name: AICTE - Scheme For Promoting Interests, Creativity And Ethics Among Students
question: Q.11 Is There Any Requirement On The Minimum Number Of Activities To Be Conducted Under This Scheme? Can We Conduct One Single Event/Activity?
answer: A. Club must conduct as many activities as possible, spread throughout the year. Club members may be encouraged to raise funds from other sponsors.

scheme_name: AICTE - Scheme For Promoting Interests, Creativity And Ethics Among Students
question: Q.12 Can We Conduct The Event/Activities In The Club Online Mode Or Hybrid Mode?
answer: A. AICTE recommends club activities to be held offline to enhance student interaction between peers and experts invited.

scheme_name: AICTE - Scheme For Promoting Interests, Creativity And Ethics Among Students
question: Q.13 Can We Collaborate With Other Councils/Clubs In Our College To Conduct An Activity?
answer: A. We encourage collaborative activities with not just clubs in your institutions but also with those focussed in your area, in nearby institutions (for example if your club is on Robotics, try collaborating with the Robotics club in a nearby institution). We expect these clubs with whom you shake hands also to reciprocate your gesture. This is equally important. By supporting and focussing on one club under the Scheme, our larger intention is to see other clubs also get energized, that's why your club has been selected to be transformed as a model club. Please document and share the success stories emerging out of such collaborations, with all the beneficiaries under SPICES.

scheme_name: AICTE - Scheme For Promoting Interests, Creativity And Ethics Among Students
question: Q.14 Can We Upload The Details Of The Events/Activity Which Were Conducted Before Receiving The Offer Letter From The Institute?
answer: A. Any activity which was conducted before receiving the Offer Letter will not be acceptable.

scheme_name: AICTE - Scheme For Promoting Interests, Creativity And Ethics Among Students
question: Q.15 Can We Consider Taking Our Students For A One-Day Outdoor Experiential Learning Activity
answer: A. Yes, but the expenditures on account of travel cannot exceed 40%. Additional expenditures, (if any) should be borne by the institute.

scheme_name: AICTE - Scheme For Promoting Interests, Creativity And Ethics Among Students
question: Q.16 We Have Been Sanctioned Project In 2021-2022. When Will The Fund Of Rs. 1 Lakh Will Be Released?
answer: A. Your institute will be reimbursed Rs. 1 lakh once the project is completed, but not before one year. Subject to all other conditions being fulfilled.

scheme_name: AICTE - Scheme For Promoting Interests, Creativity And Ethics Among Students
question: Q.17 What Is The Proportion Of Contribution From The Institute And Support From AICTE Over 100% Of Expenses Incurred On The Student's Club Activities?
answer: A. The total project cost is a minimum of Rs. 2 Lakh with Rs. 1 Lakh from AICTE and the rest coming from the institute (minimum Rs. 1 Lakh). If the expenditure within the project duration is less than Rs. 2 Lakh then a grant from AICTE will be reduced to 50% of actual expenses accrued for the club activities.

scheme_name: AICTE - Scheme For Promoting Interests, Creativity And Ethics Among Students
question: Q.18 Can I Get The Payment In Favor Of The Coordinator’s Account Name?
answer: A. No. The grant can only be released in favor of the Director/ Principal/ Registrar of the institution. Applicant must provide duly-filled mandate form having the seal and signature of the bank authority.

scheme_name: AICTE - Scheme For Promoting Interests, Creativity And Ethics Among Students
question: Q.19 Can The Grant Be Utilized By The Institute On The Expenditures Pertaining To The Faculty Coordinator/ Co-Coordinator Or Any Other Faculty Member?
answer: A. No. The grant can be utilized only for expenditures pertaining to student members of the club.

scheme_name: AICTE - Scheme For Promoting Interests, Creativity And Ethics Among Students
question: Q.20 Can We Buy Hardware/Software From AICTE's Contribution To The Club's Activities
answer: A. No. The funds cannot be used for Hardware/Software. If required, the same must be bought from institute funds.

scheme_name: AICTE - Scheme For Promoting Interests, Creativity And Ethics Among Students
question: Q.21 Can We Allow Registration Fees To Be Collected From Students For The Event(S)/ Activities?
answer: A. It is up to the institute to decide whether to collect the registration fee or not.

scheme_name: AICTE - Scheme For Promoting Interests, Creativity And Ethics Among Students
question: Q.22 Can We Use The Grant For Publishing Books?
answer: A. The grant can be utilized for the publication/printing of promotional material for events/activities organized by the club.

scheme_name: AICTE - Scheme For Promoting Interests, Creativity And Ethics Among Students
question: Q.23 Visiting Industrial/Technical Hubs Can Be Taken As An Event And Submit The Bills For Consideration.
answer: A. No. The industrial/technical hubs visit is part of academic/departmental activities, and the grant cannot be utilized for this purpose.

scheme_name: AICTE - Scheme For Promoting Interests, Creativity And Ethics Among Students
question: Q.24 Are We Allowed To Spend Institute-Committed Funds On Hospitality To Experts, And Participants From Outside Apart From Expenses On Remuneration To Experts, And Prizes To Participants?
answer: A. The funds pooled (AICTE and college) can be used for events and activities organized by the student club to which the project is offered but not for any other club. Not more than 40% of the pooled amount can be used on travel. It can be used to meet the expenses related to experts/ resource persons invited to the events organized by the club.

scheme_name: AICTE - Scheme For Promoting Interests, Creativity And Ethics Among Students
question: Q.25 Our Club Is Selected For The Grant Of Rs. 1 Lakh, And In The Letter, It Is Mentioned That We Can Utilize Its 40% For The Event Registration And Organizing Event, How We Can Utilize 60% Part Of The Grant?
answer: A. Club can utilize 60% amount in event organization expenses viz. publicity, prize money, club merchandise (such as T-Shirts, Cups, etc.)

scheme_name: AICTE - Scheme For Promoting Interests, Creativity And Ethics Among Students
question: Q.26 Can The Institute Use The Fund Amount For Two More Clubs?
answer: A. Funds under the project granted to your institute (contributed by your institute and AICTE) have to be spent on the Club mentioned in the Offer Letter; and NOT on the other clubs. The funded club will serve as a model to other clubs in the institute, the experience gained and good practices of which can be applied to at least two more student clubs that are to be proposed to us.

scheme_name: AICTE - Scheme For Promoting Interests, Creativity And Ethics Among Students
question: Q.27 What Is The Process Of Refunding The Unspent AICTE Grant? (Valid For 2020-2021 Project Batch)
answer: A. Any unspent amount with the institute must be immediately returned through NEFT/ crossed Demand Draft drawn in favor of "Member Secretary, AICTE" payable at New Delhi, within 30 days of approved project completion date.

scheme_name: AICTE - Scheme For Promoting Interests, Creativity And Ethics Among Students
question: Q.28 If We Purchased Some Products Related To The Events Activity Online, Will Online Bills Be Acceptable?
answer: A. Yes, but the product should not be Hardware/Software & bills should bear a GST number.

scheme_name: AICTE - Scheme For Promoting Interests, Creativity And Ethics Among Students
question: Q.29 Is There Any Format Given For Bills Of The Events Conducted, For Uploading On The SPICES Review Portal?
answer: A. No format is prescribed. Institute needs to upload the bills as received.

scheme_name: AICTE - Scheme For Promoting Interests, Creativity And Ethics Among Students
question: Q.30 Is It Mandatory To Submit The GST Bills?
answer: A. Yes, it is mandatory to submit bills with GST numbers.

scheme_name: AICTE - Scheme For Promoting Interests, Creativity And Ethics Among Students
question: Q.31 Can We Promote Activities/Events Being Conducted Under The Club On Social Media?
answer: A. Yes, we recommended promoting activities/events being conducted under the funded club on social media using the #aictespices and #aicte.

scheme_name: AICTE - Scheme For Promoting Interests, Creativity And Ethics Among Students
question: Q.32 Can We Use The AICTE Logo?
answer: A. All publicity materials/ advertisements/ brochures/ invitation cards/ any other collaterals/ event backdrop etc. related to the event(s), must carry the AICTE logo and the name SPICES. scheme_name: AICTE-IDEA (Idea Development, Evaluation & Application) LAB SCHEME
question: What is IDEA Lab scheme?
answer: The purpose of IDEA Lab is to provide all facilities under one roof, for conversion of an idea into a prototype. With these facilities in the campus, more students and faculty will be encouraged to take up creative work and in the process, get training on creative thinking, problem solving, collaboration etc.

scheme_name: AICTE-IDEA (Idea Development, Evaluation & Application) LAB SCHEME
question: For whom the IDEA Lab is meant?
answer: IDEA Lab is meant for students and faculty of the college/ educational campus/University.

scheme_name: AICTE-IDEA (Idea Development, Evaluation & Application) LAB SCHEME
question: Which institutions are eligible for applying for AICTE IDEA Lab?
answer: Institutions (including part of educational campuses or universities) more than 10 years old are eligible for applying and must have at least one course accredited by the NBA.

scheme_name: AICTE-IDEA (Idea Development, Evaluation & Application) LAB SCHEME
question: What type of civil infrastructure is required for an IDEA Lab?
answer: Ideally, a built up area of 5000 sq. ft. is required. But the institution must agree to provide a minimum built-up and furnished space of 2000 sq. ft. for the laboratory and an additional 1000 sq. ft. to facilitate activities under IDEA Lab. The installation of equipment has to be done taking into account all safety and environmental concerns.

scheme_name: AICTE-IDEA (Idea Development, Evaluation & Application) LAB SCHEME
question: What hardware constitutes an IDEA Lab?
answer: In order to support do-it-yourself activities and facilitate translation of ideas into prototypes, each IDEA Lab must be equipped with tools, components and consumables. Equipment and consumables have been identified (in Annexure ) and tools (in Annexure I1) which need to be there for a fully functional IDEA Lab as a complete unit.

scheme_name: AICTE-IDEA (Idea Development, Evaluation & Application) LAB SCHEME
question: Can the institute contribute in raising IDEA Lab through existing equipment?
answer: The institution can shift permanently equipment/ tools they may be having with them to the IDEA Lab. However, they will not be included in the budget but reflected in the inventory.

scheme_name: AICTE-IDEA (Idea Development, Evaluation & Application) LAB SCHEME
question: Can more than one institution join?
answer: The utilization of facilities for the purpose they are given, to the maximum extent, | is of paramount concern for AICTE. Towards this, institutions can come together under a lead institution which is eligible to apply. The Lab has to be in the premises of the lead institution which will be responsible for executing the project and ensuring that participating institutions and industries are not a liability on IDEA Lab/ Institution.

scheme_name: AICTE-IDEA (Idea Development, Evaluation & Application) LAB SCHEME
question: Can the entire non-AICTE funding be from the institution?
answer: Yes, the contribution can be from college but this is an excellent opportunity to reach out to industry inviting them for a national initiative. With gates opened for industry, the revenue generation and hence, prospects for sustenance of Lab enhance significantly. This is besides the live problems/ challenges they can offer to the colleges and technical experts as well.

scheme_name: AICTE-IDEA (Idea Development, Evaluation & Application) LAB SCHEME
question: Who operates and manages IDEA Lab?
answer: The Head of Institute will be the ex-officio Chief Mentor (CM) of the AICTE IDEA Lab, responsible for overall implementation of the project.

scheme_name: AICTE-IDEA (Idea Development, Evaluation & Application) LAB SCHEME
question: How are Student Ambassadors to be selected?
answer: Students from the 3rd/ 4th year of UG or any year of PG course who show keen interest in the activities and regularly participate in them, can be nominated. Institute can frame its own set of rules for this. Upto 3 Ambassadors can be there at a time and should be rotated, maintaining gender equity.

scheme_name: AICTE-IDEA (Idea Development, Evaluation & Application) LAB SCHEME
question: How can other faculty make use of the facilities?
answer: IDEA Labis as much to be used by faculty, as students, including for their research work. They can work on their ideas independently or by involving students. They can create internship projects or practical work which require significant use of IDEA Lab and also facilities in their own departments. Working on interdisciplinary projects involving IDEA Lab would be appreciated.

scheme_name: AICTE-IDEA (Idea Development, Evaluation & Application) LAB SCHEME
question: Can the institution put in place a committee for implementation of the IDEA Lab project?
answer: It's the prerogative of the institution to have one, as an internal mechanism. However, it should in no way become an impediment, at any stage, in the functioning of the Lab.

scheme_name: AICTE-IDEA (Idea Development, Evaluation & Application) LAB SCHEME
question: Can more than one industry join?
answer: As long as interested industries are an asset and not a liability on IDEA Lab/ Institution, they are welcome to contribute and participate. They can be given preference over non-contributing industries, in making use of the facilities of IDEA Lab.

scheme_name: AICTE-IDEA (Idea Development, Evaluation & Application) LAB SCHEME
question: Can we charge the users of IDEA Lab?
answer: Users other than students and faculty can be charged. Revenue generation will be a performance indicator and is strongly encouraged, for sustenance of the Lab. Faculty/ teachers/ staff attending the courses organized by the Lab, which earn a certificate useful for career advancement, can be charged nominally. There can be differential charges for users of facilities and those for a course/ training.

scheme_name: AICTE-IDEA (Idea Development, Evaluation & Application) LAB SCHEME
question: When and how will AICTE release funds?
answer: AICTE will release 80% of sanctioned amount as first instalment only after matching grant is deposited in the exclusive Bank Account of IDEA Lab and proof submitted. The second instalment of 20% will be released based on the (a) performance (b) utilization of AICTE's first instalment (c) deposition of 20% amount from non-AICTE sources and any other funds committed in the sanctioned project, besides other documents stipulated for fund release.

scheme_name: Annapurna Scheme: Seed Exchange Programme

scheme_name: Annapurna Scheme: Seed Exchange Programme
question: If I am a former beneficiary, am I permitted to receive improved seeds again, and if so, are there any restrictions on the crop or variety?

scheme_name: Annapurna Scheme: Seed Exchange Programme
question: Is there a strict maximum limit imposed on the amount of improved seed that can be provided to a single beneficiary farmer, based on land measurement?
answer: Yes, the provision of improved seeds is strictly limited to the requirement necessary for a maximum area of 1 hectare.

scheme_name: Annapurna Scheme: Seed Exchange Programme
question: What is the maximum financial amount or ceiling placed on the subsidy component provided to the selected beneficiaries for the cost of the exchange seed?
answer: The subsidy provided is limited to a maximum amount of ₹1,500/-.

scheme_name: Annapurna Scheme: Seed Exchange Programme
question: What specific quality standard or certification level must the high-yielding variety seed supplied to the eligible farmers generally adhere to?
answer: Certified seed will be provided. If certified seed is scarce, the Director of Agriculture may permit the distribution of true form seed for specific crops.

scheme_name: Annapurna Scheme: Seed Exchange Programme
question: If I offer seed of a crop different from the high-yielding seed I wish to receive, how is the required value of my provided seed calculated?
answer: The seed provided by the farmer must be equivalent to 25% of the actual price of the requested certified seed of the crop they wish to receive.

scheme_name: Annapurna Scheme: Seed Exchange Programme
question: What unique action must a farmer perform concerning their existing harvest or crops in order to successfully receive the improved seeds provided by the program?
answer: Applicants must provide their existing crop or seed to be exchanged for the improved, high-yielding variety seeds offered under the scheme.

scheme_name: Annapurna Scheme: Seed Exchange Programme
question: During the official approval process by the Janpad Panchayat’s Agriculture Standing Committee, how is priority assigned among the selected applicants?
answer: Names that are listed first in the approved primary list of farmers prepared by the Rural Agriculture Extension Officer will be given priority.

scheme_name: Annapurna Scheme: Seed Exchange Programme
question: For how long will the prepared waiting list of farmers, whose names were not prioritized in the final selection, remain valid or active?
answer: The waiting list is considered final and remains valid only until the current crop season concludes.

scheme_name: Annapurna Scheme: Seed Exchange Programme
question: What exact percentage of the actual price of the improved seed being provided in exchange will be covered by the subsidy available under the guidelines?
answer: Applicants are eligible for a 75% subsidy on the actual price of the seed provided in exchange by the distribution organization.

scheme_name: Annapurna Scheme: Seed Exchange Programme
question: When exchanging my existing crop or seed, will the improved seeds I receive in return be provided based on mass or volume equivalence?
answer: The improved seeds of suitable varieties will be provided in a quantity equal to the quantity of the seed provided by the farmer for exchange.

scheme_name: Annapurna Scheme: Seed Exchange Programme
question: Is there a prerequisite concerning my existing financial capacity to purchase high-yielding varieties of foodgrain crops before applying for this benefit?
answer: Yes, the applicant must be a farmer who is currently unable to afford the purchase of improved varieties of high-yielding foodgrain crops.

scheme_name: Annapurna Scheme: Seed Exchange Programme
question: When selecting the type of improved seed to provide, what key characteristic or factor is given the primary consideration by the implementing authorities?
answer: Priority is given to improved varieties of foodgrain crops that are suitable for or prevalent in the specific geographical area of the farmer.

scheme_name: Annapurna Scheme: Seed Exchange Programme
question: How many potential farmers, relative to the actual established district target, does the Rural Agriculture Extension Officer typically select initially?
answer: The Rural Agriculture Extension Officer selects 1.5 times the number of required beneficiaries compared to the established physical target.

scheme_name: Annapurna Scheme: Seed Multiplication Programme
question: How much financial assistance, calculated as a%age of the total seed price, will be granted to the successful participating farmers?
answer: A 75% subsidy is provided on the cost of the Foundation (Aadhaar) or Certified I grade (Pramanit I shreni) seed supplied for participation in the program.

scheme_name: Annapurna Scheme: Seed Multiplication Programme
question: Is it a mandatory requirement for all cultivators participating in this production component to officially register with the quality control institution?
answer: Yes, cultivators are mandatorily required to register with the Seed Certification Agency (Bija Pramanikaran Sanstha).

scheme_name: Annapurna Scheme: Seed Multiplication Programme
question: What is the minimum land area required for a cultivator to dedicate to this particular agricultural activity to qualify for the benefits?
answer: The production activity must be undertaken in a minimum area of $1/2$ acre (0.2 hectare) by the participating cultivator.

scheme_name: Annapurna Scheme: Seed Multiplication Programme
question: Does the land where the production work takes place need to be situated within a certain proximity to designated government facilities?
answer: Yes, the applicant's land must be located within a 10 kilometer perimeter of the selected Government Agricultural Farms (Shaaskiya Krishi Prakshetra).

scheme_name: Annapurna Scheme: Seed Multiplication Programme
question: What is the official deadline for submitting the mandatory application form for quality certification after the sowing of the crops has been completed?
answer: The registration application form must be submitted within 20 days of sowing or before the final date fixed by the government.

scheme_name: Annapurna Scheme: Seed Multiplication Programme
question: If a large number of eligible individuals apply, how is the official priority list for the selection process determined?
answer: The Gramin Krishi Vistar Adhikari (Rural Agricultural Extension Officer) selects 1.5 times the target, and priority is given to the names listed first on the approved list.

scheme_name: Annapurna Scheme: Seed Multiplication Programme
question: Who is responsible for bearing the cost of mandatory fees related to application, inspection, and sample testing required by the certification body?
answer: The payment for registration fees, including the application fee, registration fee, inspection fee, and sample fee, is covered using funds from the scheme budget.

scheme_name: Annapurna Scheme: Seed Multiplication Programme
question: Is there a defined maximum limit on the total land area for which a farmer can receive the subsidized planting material under this program?
answer: Yes, eligibility for the 75% subsidy is restricted to a maximum area of 1 hectare for each participating farmer.

scheme_name: Annapurna Scheme: Seed Multiplication Programme
question: Which specific grades or classifications of high-yielding food grain seeds will be distributed to the selected beneficiaries for multiplication?
answer: Foundation (Aadhaar) or Certified I grade (Pramanit I shreni) seed of high-yielding food grain crops will be made available for production.

scheme_name: Annapurna Scheme: Seed Multiplication Programme
question: What is the obligation regarding the distribution or utilization of the certified quality seed produced under the umbrella of this program?
answer: The produced certified seed must be made available at prescribed rates to other Scheduled Caste and Scheduled Tribe farmers under the scheme in the subsequent year.

scheme_name: Annapurna Scheme: Seed Multiplication Programme
question: How must the remaining 25% of the actual cost of the quality seed, after the subsidy is applied, be settled by the applicant?
answer: The remaining seed cost must be settled by the cultivator either in cash (nagad) or through their own seed, which will be valued at the support price.

scheme_name: Annapurna Scheme: Seed Multiplication Programme
question: Where will the activities necessary for post-harvest preparation, such as grading, stacking, and packing of the raw produce, be performed?
answer: These processes will be conducted at the Government Agricultural Farm or, if facilities are unavailable there, at the processing center of the Seed Corporation or other institutions.

scheme_name: Annapurna Scheme: Seed Multiplication Programme
question: What steps must the farmer take concerning cultivation practices to ensure the purity and quality of the final high-yielding production?
answer: The complete agricultural methodology (Sampuurna Krishi Kaaryamaala) must be adopted for higher production, and undesirable plants (Avaanchhaniy Paudhon) must be removed to maintain seed purity.

scheme_name: Annapurna Scheme: Seed Multiplication Programme
question: Is there any specific legal document or formal understanding that needs to be executed between the farmer and the implementing department?
answer: Yes, an agreement (Anubandh) must be executed between the department and the beneficiary through the Seed Production Committee or Farm Superintendent to ensure production, marketing, and payment are compliant with policy.

scheme_name: Annapurna Scheme: Seed Production Programme
question: Must participants intending to increase agricultural productivity necessarily belong to the specific population groups known as Scheduled Caste or Scheduled Tribe categories?
answer: Yes, participation in the Seed Production Programme is exclusively limited to small and marginal farmers who are confirmed members of the Scheduled Caste or Scheduled Tribe communities.

scheme_name: Annapurna Scheme: Seed Production Programme
question: What specific farming techniques are mandated during the growing season to ensure the produced seeds meet the required purity standards?
answer: Farmers must adopt the complete package of agricultural practices for higher production and mandatorily ensure the removal of undesirable plants to maintain seed purity.

scheme_name: Annapurna Scheme: Seed Production Programme
question: If I receive Foundation or Certified seed through the program, what%age of the actual seed cost must be contributed by the farmer?
answer: The farmer must pay the remaining 25% of the seed cost; the scheme provides a 75% subsidy on the actual cost of the Foundation or Certified seed.

scheme_name: Annapurna Scheme: Seed Production Programme
question: What is the smallest required area of land, measured in either hectares or acres, that a participant must use for the seed production program?
answer: The program must be conducted by the farmer on a minimum area of 1/2 acre (0.2 hectares).

scheme_name: Annapurna Scheme: Seed Production Programme
question: Am I restricted on the maximum amount of land I can use to sow the Foundation or Certified seed that is provided to me by the department?
answer: Yes, the farmer must utilize the seed provided for a maximum area of 1 hectare.

scheme_name: Annapurna Scheme: Seed Production Programme
question: How close must my farming operation be located to a designated Government agricultural farm to qualify for the seed supply program?
answer: The applicant must reside and operate their farm within the 10-kilometer periphery of the selected Government agricultural farms.

scheme_name: Annapurna Scheme: Seed Production Programme
question: If the number of applicants exceeds the available targets, what criteria determine which names receive priority selection?
answer: Preference should be given to the names listed first in the approved list of beneficiaries.

scheme_name: Annapurna Scheme: Seed Production Programme
question: What quality level of seeds, such as Foundation or Certified Grade, will be made available to farmers participating in the production activity?
answer: Farmers will be provided with Foundation or Certified Grade I seeds of improved, high-yielding food grain varieties.

scheme_name: Annapurna Scheme: Seed Production Programme
question: Do the requirements state that I must hold a particular size of land holding, such as being classified as a small or marginal farmer, to qualify?
answer: Yes, the applicant must meet the criteria of being identified as a small farmer or a marginal farmer.

scheme_name: Annapurna Scheme: Seed Production Programme
question: Is there a maximum limit set on the agricultural land area for which an applicant can receive subsidized seed under this production initiative?
answer: The eligibility for the grant is limited up to a maximum area of 1 hectare.

scheme_name: Annapurna Scheme: Seed Production Programme
question: Must an interested applicant explicitly declare their intention or willingness to participate in the entire Seed Production Programme process?
answer: Yes, the applicant must be willing and interested in participating in the Seed Production Programme.

scheme_name: Annapurna Scheme: Seed Production Programme

scheme_name: Annapurna Scheme: Seed Production Programme

answer: It is mandatory for the farmers to register with the Seed Certification Agency, and this application must be submitted within 20 days of sowing or before the government-fixed final date.

scheme_name: Annapurna Scheme: Seed Production Programme
question: If I am required to cover the remaining 25% of the improved seed cost, how can I make this required contribution?
answer: The remaining amount can be paid in cash or by providing your own seed, the price of which will be valued based on the support price.

scheme_name: Academic Scholarship Scheme (Labor Welfare Board Madhya Pradesh)

scheme_name: Academic Scholarship Scheme (Labor Welfare Board Madhya Pradesh)

scheme_name: Academic Scholarship Scheme (Labor Welfare Board Madhya Pradesh)

scheme_name: Academic Scholarship Scheme (Labor Welfare Board Madhya Pradesh)
question: Will I continue receiving the scholarship if I fail a class?

scheme_name: Ashram Schools (Scheduled Tribes)

scheme_name: Ashram Schools (Scheduled Tribes)

scheme_name: Ashram Schools (Scheduled Tribes)

scheme_name: Ashram Schools (Scheduled Tribes)

scheme_name: Ashram Schools (Scheduled Tribes)

scheme_name: Ashram Schools (Scheduled Tribes)

scheme_name: Antya Sanskar Sahay Yojana
question: Is there a specific timeframe within which the applicant must apply for the scheme after the occurrence of death?
answer: Yes, in cases where the applicant seeks assistance based on their relationship with a deceased Scheduled Tribe individual, the application must be made within 12 months from the time of the individual's death.

scheme_name: Antya Sanskar Sahay Yojana
question: How does the scheme ensure that the applicants meet the eligibility criteria?
answer: The scheme requires essential documents such as a Caste Certificate issued by the Competent Authority, Death Certificate of the deceased, Income Certificate issued by the Competent Authority, Ration Card, Election Card, and Aadhar Card. These documents collectively serve as evidence to verify the eligibility of the applicant and the deceased.

scheme_name: Antya Sanskar Sahay Yojana
question: What is the maximum financial assistance offered under this scheme?
answer: The scheme provides financial assistance of up to [?] 20,000 or the actual cost, whichever is less, to cover the expenses associated with the funeral and religious ceremonies of Scheduled Tribe families.

scheme_name: Antya Sanskar Sahay Yojana
question: Could you provide insights into the special case scenario mentioned in the scheme?
answer: Certainly. In cases where the applicant is not from a Scheduled Tribe family but the deceased individual is, the applicant can still claim assistance under the scheme. However, to be eligible, the applicant must establish a direct relationship with the deceased person. This claim should be made within 12 months from the occurrence of the death within the kin's family.

scheme_name: Antya Sanskar Sahay Yojana
question: Who is eligible to apply for the benefits of the "Antya Sanskar Sahay Yojana"?
answer: The scheme is open to Scheduled Tribe families. The eligibility criteria specify that either the deceased individual or the applicant seeking assistance must belong to a Scheduled Tribe family. Additionally, the family's annual income should not exceed [?] 3,00,000.

scheme_name: Antya Sanskar Sahay Yojana
question: What is the primary objective of the "Antya Sanskar Sahay Yojana" launched by the Department of Tribal Welfare in Goa?
answer: The main objective of the "Antya Sanskar Sahay Yojana" is to provide financial support to Scheduled Tribe families in covering the expenses associated with the funeral and religious ceremonies of deceased family members.

scheme_name: Antya Sanskar Sahay Yojana
question: How does the scheme address cases where the applicant seeking assistance is not from a Scheduled Tribe family, but the deceased person is?
answer: In such scenarios, the applicant can still apply for assistance, provided they establish a direct relationship with the deceased. This ensures that eligible individuals, even if not from a Scheduled Tribe background, can access the benefits if they can prove their relationship with the deceased.

scheme_name: Antya Sanskar Sahay Yojana
question: What are the documents required to prove the annual income eligibility criterion?
answer: To establish that the annual family income does not exceed [?] 3,00,000, applicants need to submit an Income Certificate issued by the Competent Authority. This certificate verifies their income status and ensures compliance with the scheme's income threshold.

scheme_name: Antya Sanskar Sahay Yojana
question: How does the scheme determine the actual cost of funeral and religious ceremonies?
answer: The scheme allows financial assistance of up to [?] 20,000 or the actual cost, whichever is less. The "Vouchers Receipts" document is significant here, as it serves as a record of expenses incurred during the ceremonies, enabling accurate calculation of assistance based on actual costs.

scheme_name: Antya Sanskar Sahay Yojana
question: Can you provide insights into the "Sanctioning Authority" and the decision-making process within the scheme?
answer: The Director of Tribal Welfare scrutinizes the applications in the prescribed manner. Approved applications are then sanctioned by the Directorate of Tribal Welfare, and the sanctioned benefits are electronically transferred to the bank accounts of the beneficiaries. Any difficulties in implementation are resolved by a state-level committee, ensuring transparency and fair decision-making.

scheme_name: Antya Sanskar Sahay Yojana
question: Can you explain the significance of the "Mandate Form" among the required documents?
answer: The "Mandate Form" is essential as it provides the necessary authorization for the financial assistance to be transferred to the beneficiary's bank account. This ensures a seamless and secure transfer process, allowing beneficiaries to receive the sanctioned amount promptly.

scheme_name: Atal Shresth Shahar Yojna
question: What is the 'Atal Shresth Shahar Yojna (ASSY)'?
answer: The Atal Shresth Shahar Yojna is a scheme initiated by the State Government to recognize and reward the top-performing Urban Local Bodies (ULBs) in the state based on various performance indicators.

scheme_name: Atal Shresth Shahar Yojna
question: Who is eligible to participate in ASSY?
answer: The scheme is applicable to all Urban Local Bodies (ULBs) in the state, and it is mandatory for all ULBs to participate. There is no bar on any ULB, even if it has won the ASSY prize in previous years.

scheme_name: Atal Shresth Shahar Yojna
question: What are the indicators for assessment under ASSY?
answer: The top-performing ULBs will be assessed based on indicators such as Swachh Survekshan, public service delivery, increase in ULB income, fund utilization, public infrastructure, and audit paras settlement and audited accounts.

scheme_name: Atal Shresth Shahar Yojna
question: How are ULBs ranked in the scheme?
answer: ULBs will be ranked based on the scores obtained in Swachh Survekshan of the preceding year and the scores obtained in the other five State Parameters.

scheme_name: Atal Shresth Shahar Yojna
question: How is the prize money distributed among the winners?
answer: The top-performing Municipal Corporation, Municipal Council, and Nagar Panchayat will be awarded cash prizes, with the first, second, and third prizes having specified amounts. In case of a tie, the prize money will be distributed equally among the tied ULBs.

scheme_name: Atal Shresth Shahar Yojna
question: Can ULBs use the award money for any purpose?
answer: The award money is provided as an un-tied grant and should not form part of the income of the ULBs. It cannot be spent on salaries/wages of ULB employees. However, ULBs may formulate a scheme to reward their employees for outstanding contributions within certain limits.

scheme_name: Atal Shresth Shahar Yojna
question: What is the timeline for the ASSY competition?
answer: ULBs need to submit their claims by September 30th each year. The screening process occurs by October 20th, followed by field assessment/verification by a Third Party Agency (TPA) by November 20th. Prize distribution takes place on December 25th.

scheme_name: Atal Shresth Shahar Yojna
question: How is the final decision on the winners made?
answer: The field assessment/verification is conducted by a Third Party Agency (TPA), and based on their report, the Director of Urban Development recommends the names of the winning ULBs to the State Level Apex Committee for final approval. The Apex Committee's decision is final.

scheme_name: Atal Shresth Shahar Yojna
question: Is there any provision for rectification of mistakes in the claims?
answer: ULBs will be given additional time to rectify any clerical mistakes. The Department may provide this additional time after the field verification stage.

scheme_name: Award Of Scholarships To Young Artists In Different Cultural Fields

scheme_name: Award Of Scholarships To Young Artists In Different Cultural Fields

scheme_name: Award Of Scholarships To Young Artists In Different Cultural Fields

scheme_name: Award Of Scholarships To Young Artists In Different Cultural Fields

scheme_name: Ayurswasthya Yojana: AYUSH and Public Health
question: What is the "AYUSH and Public Health" component under "Ayurswasthya Yojana"?
answer: The "AYUSH and Public Health" component is a Central Sector Grant-in-Aid initiative that supports AYUSH-based interventions to improve community health outcomes.

scheme_name: Ayurswasthya Yojana: AYUSH and Public Health
question: What is the main objective of this component?
answer: The main objective of this component is to demonstrate the effectiveness of AYUSH interventions in public health and integrate them into national health programmes.

scheme_name: Ayurswasthya Yojana: AYUSH and Public Health
question: Who can apply for funding under this component?
answer: Eligible applicants include State Directorates of Health or AYUSH, Government institutions, universities, research councils, and non-profit organizations with relevant experience.

scheme_name: Ayurswasthya Yojana: AYUSH and Public Health
question: What is the minimum experience required for non-profit organizations?
answer: A non-profit organization should have at least 5 years of experience in public health or AYUSH-related activities to be eligible.

scheme_name: Ayurswasthya Yojana: AYUSH and Public Health
question: What types of health issues can be covered under this component?
answer: Projects can cover communicable diseases, non-communicable diseases, maternal and child health, geriatric care, mental health, disaster management, and other public health concerns.

scheme_name: Ayurswasthya Yojana: AYUSH and Public Health
question: What is the minimum population coverage requirement?
answer: The proposal should generally cover at least one block and benefit a minimum of 1,000 persons, unless relaxed by the competent authority in special areas.

scheme_name: Ayurswasthya Yojana: AYUSH and Public Health
question: What is the maximum financial assistance provided under this component?
answer: The scheme provides financial assistance up to ₹1,50,00,000/- for a project duration of up to 3 years.

scheme_name: Ayurswasthya Yojana: AYUSH and Public Health
question: How is the grant amount released to the selected organization?
answer: The grant amount is released in three installments of 40%, 40%, and 20%, subject to submission of required reports and utilization certificates.

scheme_name: Ayurswasthya Yojana: AYUSH and Public Health
question: What conditions must be met for release of subsequent installments?
answer: Subsequent installments are released after at least 75% utilization of the previous installment and submission of Utilization Certificates and progress reports.

scheme_name: Ayurswasthya Yojana: AYUSH and Public Health
question: Can an organization receive funding if it has received similar funding earlier?
answer: The organization should not have received funding for the same purpose from another Central Government Ministry in the last 5 years.

scheme_name: Ayurswasthya Yojana: AYUSH and Public Health
question: Are collaborations with other organizations allowed?
answer: Collaboration with national and international organizations is encouraged to strengthen project implementation and outcomes.

scheme_name: Ayurswasthya Yojana: AYUSH and Public Health
question: What are the responsibilities of the selected implementing organization?
answer: The implementing organization must execute the project as approved, maintain records, submit reports, and ensure proper utilization of funds.

scheme_name: Ayurswasthya Yojana: AYUSH and Public Health
question: What happens if the funds are misused or conditions are violated?
answer: In case of misuse or deviation from scheme conditions, the Ministry can recover the grant amount with 12% interest and take appropriate legal action.

scheme_name: Ayurswasthya Yojana: AYUSH for Sports Medicine
question: What is the "AYUSH for Sports Medicine" component under the "Ayurswasthya Yojana"?
answer: The AYUSH for Sports Medicine component is a scheme initiative that supports AYUSH-based interventions for prevention, treatment, and rehabilitation of sports-related injuries and for promoting fitness among sports persons.

scheme_name: Ayurswasthya Yojana: AYUSH for Sports Medicine
question: What are the main objectives of the "AYUSH for Sports Medicine" component?
answer: The objectives of this component are to promote AYUSH interventions for health and fitness of sports persons and to support AYUSH therapeutic interventions for treatment and rehabilitation of sports-related injuries.

scheme_name: Ayurswasthya Yojana: AYUSH for Sports Medicine
question: Who can apply for funding under this component?
answer: AYUSH teaching institutions and AYUSH hospitals with collaboration with recognized national or international sports bodies are eligible to apply for the scheme.

scheme_name: Ayurswasthya Yojana: AYUSH for Sports Medicine
question: What type of collaborations are required for eligibility?
answer: The applicant institution must have collaboration with recognized sports bodies such as Sports Authority of India, All India Football Federation, Indian Olympic Association, BCCI, ICC, or other recognized national or international sports organizations.

scheme_name: Ayurswasthya Yojana: AYUSH for Sports Medicine
question: What is the minimum beneficiary coverage under one project?
answer: Each approved project should benefit a minimum of 200 sports persons.

scheme_name: Ayurswasthya Yojana: AYUSH for Sports Medicine
question: What is the maximum financial assistance provided under this component?
answer: The scheme provides financial assistance up to ₹1.00 crore for one project with a duration of up to 18 months.

scheme_name: Ayurswasthya Yojana: AYUSH for Sports Medicine
question: How is the grant amount released to the implementing institution?
answer: The grant amount is released in two installments of 60% and 40% of the total sanctioned amount.

scheme_name: Ayurswasthya Yojana: AYUSH for Sports Medicine
question: What are the conditions for release of the second installment?
answer: The second installment is released after at least 75% utilization of the first installment and submission and acceptance of the Utilization Certificate.

scheme_name: Ayurswasthya Yojana: AYUSH for Sports Medicine
question: What types of interventions can be supported under this component?
answer: The component supports AYUSH interventions for sports injury treatment, rehabilitation, fitness promotion, and preventive health measures for sports persons.

scheme_name: Ayurswasthya Yojana: AYUSH for Sports Medicine
question: Is the "Fit India" Movement linked to this component?
answer: This component aligns with the "Fit India" Movement and supports national efforts to promote physical activity, sports, and healthy lifestyles through AYUSH interventions.

scheme_name: Ayurswasthya Yojana: Up-gradation of Facilities to Centre of Excellence (CoE)
question: - What is the objective of the "Centre of Excellence (CoE)" component?

scheme_name: Ayurswasthya Yojana: Up-gradation of Facilities to Centre of Excellence (CoE)

scheme_name: Ayurswasthya Yojana: Up-gradation of Facilities to Centre of Excellence (CoE)

scheme_name: Assam Tea Plantations Provident Fund Scheme

scheme_name: Assam Tea Plantations Provident Fund Scheme

scheme_name: Assam Tea Plantations Provident Fund Scheme

scheme_name: Assam Tea Plantations Provident Fund Scheme

scheme_name: Assam Tea Plantations Provident Fund Scheme

scheme_name: Assam Tea Plantations Provident Fund Scheme

scheme_name: Assistance Towards Sugarcane Supplied By The Sugarcane Growers

scheme_name: Assistance Towards Sugarcane Supplied By The Sugarcane Growers

scheme_name: Agnipath Yojana

scheme_name: Biotechnology Ignition Grant Scheme
question: What is BIG scheme and its salient features?
answer: Biotechnology Ignition Grant (BIG) Scheme is grant-in-aid funding to support individuals and startups in the field of Biotechnology. The BIG scheme invests in ideas that have clear potential to translate into commercial products/technologies. The scheme provides funding, mentorship, access to incubation, and other support for ideation to proof of concept. Funding will be in the form of Grant-in-Aid up to [?]50 Lakhs. So, if you have an idea, a strong rationale supporting it, addressing an unmet need, you can apply for BIG funding to progress from ideation to Proof-of-concept.

scheme_name: Biotechnology Ignition Grant Scheme
question: What are the Biotechnology areas supported under BIG?
answer: Healthcare, Life sciences including Drugs, Biologics, Delivery systems, Medical Devices, Diagnostics, Biomaterials, others; Industrial Biotechnology including enzymes, biofertilizers, bioprocesses, waste treatment, others; Agriculture and allied areas such as Nutrition, Fisheries, Poultry, Sericulture, Animal Husbandry, Aquaponics, others; Waste to value; Sanitation; Biofuels, Clean Energy; Bioservices and Bioanalytics including Big Data, Artificial intelligence, Machine Learning, Internet of Things, Automation integrated in Biotech applications

scheme_name: Biotechnology Ignition Grant Scheme
question: What all is supported under the upto ₹ 50 Lakhs grant?
answer: The BIG award provides funding support for buying equipment, reagents, and components, hiring skilled manpower for team building, travel, incubation charges, rentals, engaging services, etc. in the 18 months period of the BIG grant. During the BIG tenure, BIRAC extends several networking opportunities to connect with experts, mentors, industry, investors, peer-to-peer learning, specialized training & workshops, and exposure to various platforms on a merit basis. These opportunities are made available through BIRAC's ecosystem-supporting partners including BIG partners, BioNEST clusters, and a huge network of extended partners.

scheme_name: Biotechnology Ignition Grant Scheme
question: Who all can apply?
answer: Individual Entrepreneur, a registered Startup including LLP.

scheme_name: Biotechnology Ignition Grant Scheme
question: I am a person of Indian origin but hold a foreign passport can I apply?
answer: No, only Indians with Indian passports are eligible to apply for this scheme. OCIs are not eligible to apply.

scheme_name: Biotechnology Ignition Grant Scheme
question: Can I apply as an undergraduate student?
answer: No, the Project leader must have completed basic graduation at the time of application submission.

scheme_name: Biotechnology Ignition Grant Scheme
question: Can I apply as a faculty/scientist/research scholar/PG student?
answer: Yes, if you are pursuing translational research leading to the formation of a startup. As a procedural requirement, you are required to obtain a No Objection Certificate (NOC) from your institute/employer. Faculty members who are not willing to create a Startup within the BIG term of 18 months are encouraged to apply under other schemes of BIRAC for Faculty.

scheme_name: Biotechnology Ignition Grant Scheme
question: I am employed with a company; can I apply for this scheme?
answer: Yes, you can apply as an individual but need to provide an undertaking that you will terminate your association with the current employer and take up the project full time, if selected. | Or, your application should be submitted under the Company/LLP category with the employer company being the applicant company.

scheme_name: Biotechnology Ignition Grant Scheme
question: What age of startup is considered as eligible age to apply?
answer: The date of incorporation of the Company/LLP should not be earlier than 5 years from the date of BIG Call launch.

scheme_name: Biotechnology Ignition Grant Scheme
question: Does Project Leader have to be a shareholder in the Company/LLP?
answer: Yes, the Project Leader must be a shareholder in the applicant company .

scheme_name: Biotechnology Ignition Grant Scheme
question: What minimum percentage of shares does a PI must own to be eligible for the BIG?
answer: There is no such criterion of minimum percentage.

scheme_name: Biotechnology Ignition Grant Scheme
question: Can proprietorship firm apply for BIG scheme?
answer: No, the legal entity should be a company registered under the Companies Act.

scheme_name: Biotechnology Ignition Grant Scheme
question: Can Institute apply for BIG scheme?
answer: No, Institutes/Universities are not eligible to apply for this scheme. Students may be eligible to apply.

scheme_name: Biotechnology Ignition Grant Scheme
question: Our firm is registered under Society’s act, are we eligible to apply for BIG scheme?
answer: No, the legal entity should be a company registered under the Companies Act.

scheme_name: Biotechnology Ignition Grant Scheme
question: Is DSIR recognition needed to apply for this scheme?
answer: No, DSIR certification is not needed to apply for this scheme.

scheme_name: Biotechnology Ignition Grant Scheme
question: Where to apply?
answer: Only online applications are accepted. To apply under BIG Scheme, applicant needs to register on BIRAC website "https://www.birac.nic.in/desc_new.php?id=327"under 'New User' and submit the application.

scheme_name: Biotechnology Ignition Grant Scheme

answer: Please use a different user name and e-mail id for submitting BIG proposal.

scheme_name: Biotechnology Ignition Grant Scheme
question: What are the evaluation criteria for selection of BIG Grantees?
answer: The indicative criteria for evaluation of an application include Unmet need, Value proposition/differentiation, Technical viability, Team strength. Proposed product/ technology must have Commercialization Potential.

scheme_name: Biotechnology Ignition Grant Scheme
question: What is the process of selection?
answer: It is 4 tier selection process. All eligible applications go through following steps: | a. Preliminary Selection Committee (PSC) screens the proposals for scheme fit, adequacy of details, and plagiarism | b. The PSC-recommended proposals are then reviewed Online by subject experts | c. The recommended applicants are then called for F2F presentations before the Technical Evaluation Panel (TEP). The proposal will be scored on a scale of 100. | d. Expert Selection Committee (ESC) will decide the final cutoff of marks and recommend the proposals for BIG funding.

scheme_name: Biotechnology Ignition Grant Scheme
question: When can I get to know the final decision made by ESC?
answer: It typically takes 4 months for the final announcement of BIG results from closing of the call. You will be updated at each stage by BIG Partners about your application status.

scheme_name: Biotechnology Ignition Grant Scheme

answer: The project must complete within 18 months

scheme_name: Biotechnology Ignition Grant Scheme
question: Where to obtain Letter of Intent?
answer: Write to the incubator where you intend to incubate.

scheme_name: Biotechnology Ignition Grant Scheme
question: What is an Incubator and BIG Partner and their relationship?
answer: Incubator is a center that has the required lab infrastructure, required network to support your proposed BIG work. Certain BioNEST incubators have been officially recognized as BIRAC's BIG Partners. These incubators are mandated to implent the BIG Scheme (Facilitate and mentor the aspirant applicants and BIG grantees). BIG Partners are responsible for initial screening of the proposal, technical due diligence, financial due diligence, project monitoring, fund disbursement, arranging for workshops etc.

scheme_name: Biotechnology Ignition Grant Scheme
question: Can my institute be my Incubator?
answer: The Incubators should have a legal status i.e. should be either a registered society or a | registered trust or a registered company.

scheme_name: Biotechnology Ignition Grant Scheme
question: Can my BIG Partner be my incubator?
answer: Yes, but it is NOT mandatory. You may choose to incubate at the incubator of your choice. This may include BIG partner or any other incubator offering facilities and services required for the execution of your project. | a) BIRAC supported BioNEST Bio Incubators list can be viewed here:

scheme_name: Biotechnology Ignition Grant Scheme
question: In case of Individual applicants, who will receive the funds?
answer: The applicant will receive the fund in a separate dedicated, auditable no-lien account. The fund disbursement is linked with milestones through BIRAC's BIG Partners.

scheme_name: Biotechnology Ignition Grant Scheme
question: Do I have to pay royalty?

question: What Is Biju Swasthya Kalyan Yojana?
answer: "Every life is precious..." has always been the guiding principle of the Hon'ble Chief Minister Naveen Patnaik. The vision of the Hon'ble Chief Minister has been to provide assurance of quality health care to all the citizens of the State, especially the vulnerable sections. With this objective, Biju Swasthya Kalyan Yojana has been launched as a pathbreaking program to provide universal health coverage, with special emphasis on the health protection of economically vulnerable families. To achieve its objectives, the BSKY has two components: | A. State Government will bear the full cost of all health services delivered to all patients | (irrespective of income, status, or residence) in all State Government health care facilities starting from Sub center level to District Head Quarter and Government Medical College Hospital and Blood Bank level. | B. State Government will bear the cost of healthcare provided in impaneled private hospitals for over 9,65,00,000 economically vulnerable families in the State, amounting to Annual Health coverage of [?] 5,00,000 per family and an additional [?] 5,00,000 for the women members of the family after exhaustion of the initial limit.

All families are eligible for healthcare services at Government Healthcare Institutions to District Head Quarter Hospitals and Government Medical College Hospitals and the Blood Bank level, for which the state Govt will bear the total cost. | B. For additional healthcare facilities beyond the District Headquarters hospital level, through annual health coverage of [?] 5,00,000 per annum per family and an additional Rs. 5lakh for the women members of the family after exhausting of initial limit, all BSKY Smart Card holders and NFSA/ SFSA card holders are eligible to avail of the special health coverage, for which State Government will bear the cost.

scheme_name: Biju Swasthya Kalyan Yojana

answer: A. All health services charges are borne by the State Government, including those for drugs, diagnostics, dialysis, Cancer chemotherapy, OT, I.C.U, in-patient admission blood bank services, etc., in all government health institutions up to Government Medical College Hospital level, for all persons. | B. Families having BSKY Smart Health Card can avail of cashless treatment at any impaneled private hospital under BSKY within or outside the State. Cardholder families can help with facilities such as registration, consultation, medical tests, pathologies, treatment, IPD, and follow-up consultation under BSKY at any impaneled private hospital. State Government will bear the cost up to the annual coverage amount.

BSKY Smart Card holders can avail treatment at any impaneled private hospitals within or outside of the State for which the State Government will bear the cost up to the annual coverage amount.

scheme_name: Balram Talab Yojana
question: What is the maximum financial assistance available for constructing a pond on agricultural land under this government initiative for water conservation?
answer: The maximum subsidy provided is ₹1,00,000/- for Scheduled Caste or Scheduled Tribe farmers, representing 75% of construction costs, while general category and small-marginal farmers receive up to ₹80,000/-.

scheme_name: Balram Talab Yojana
question: If I belong to the Scheduled Caste category and want to build a rainwater harvesting structure, what%age of the total construction cost will the state government bear?
answer: Farmers from Scheduled Caste or Scheduled Tribe categories receive 75% of the construction cost as subsidy, with a maximum limit of ₹1,00,000/-, for building rainwater conservation structures.

scheme_name: Balram Talab Yojana
question: Is it mandatory for farmers to have any specific irrigation equipment already installed on their farmland before they can apply for assistance?
answer: Yes, only those farmers who have installed drip or sprinkler irrigation sets in financial year 2017-18 or thereafter, and these systems are currently operational, are eligible for subsidized pond construction approval.

scheme_name: Balram Talab Yojana
question: Can a farmer who has previously received benefits under this water conservation program apply again for constructing another pond on different agricultural land?
answer: No, the benefit of this scheme is provided to each farmer only once, meaning a farmer cannot apply multiple times even if they own different parcels of agricultural land.

scheme_name: Balram Talab Yojana
question: What is the minimum requirement regarding land ownership for farmers interested in participating in this rainwater harvesting scheme?
answer: Farmers must construct the pond on their own agricultural land as subsidy will not be provided for pond construction on leased or rented land, making land ownership a mandatory requirement.

scheme_name: Balram Talab Yojana
question: How much time does it typically take for the subsidy amount to be transferred to the beneficiary's bank account after the pond construction is completed?
answer: The subsidy is provided within 30 days based on the evaluation and assessment conducted by the Soil Conservation Staff after completion of the construction work.

scheme_name: Balram Talab Yojana
question: Are farmers from all social and economic categories eligible to participate in this agricultural water management program being implemented statewide?
answer: Yes, all categories of farmers including general category, small and marginal farmers, and Scheduled Caste or Scheduled Tribe farmers are eligible to avail benefits under this scheme.

scheme_name: Balram Talab Yojana
question: What happens if a farmer who has received subsidy does not install the mandatory safety signboard at the pond location as required?
answer: In the absence of a mandatory safety board at the pond site, if any drowning or accident occurs, the farmer will be solely and completely responsible for all consequences.

scheme_name: Balram Talab Yojana
question: Is there any difference in the subsidy%age provided to small and marginal category farmers compared to general category farmers under this initiative?
answer: Yes, small and marginal farmers receive 50% of construction costs or maximum ₹80,000/-, which is higher than the 40% or maximum ₹80,000/- provided to general category farmers.

scheme_name: Bhavantar Bharpai Yojana
question: What is the Bhavantar Bharpayee Yojana (BBY)?
answer: BBY is a unique scheme by the Haryana Government to compensate horticulture producers when they receive lower prices for their produce in the market. It aims to reduce the risk of price volatility and encourage crop diversification among farmers.

scheme_name: Bhavantar Bharpai Yojana
question: Which crops are covered under the scheme?
answer: The scheme covers 21 crops: Okra (Bhindi), Chili, Bottle Gourd (Lauki), Bitter Gourd (Karela), Cabbage (Patta Gobhi), Radish (Mooli), Tomato, Onion, Potato, Cauliflower (Phool Gobhi), Carrot (Gajar), Pea (Matar), Capsicum (Shimla Mirch), Brinjal (Baingan), Turmeric (Haldi), Garlic (Lahsun), Mango (Aam), Kinnow, Guava (Amrud), Litchi, and Ber.

scheme_name: Bhavantar Bharpai Yojana
question: What is the primary objective of the scheme?
answer: The main objectives are to mitigate the risk of low prices during the sale of vegetables and fruits by providing compensation up to a protected price and to encourage farmers to diversify their crops.

scheme_name: Bhavantar Bharpai Yojana
question: Who is eligible to benefit from the scheme?
answer: Landowners, lessees, or tenant farmers cultivating the specified crops are eligible to benefit from the scheme.

scheme_name: Bhavantar Bharpai Yojana
question: Is registration mandatory to avail benefits under the scheme?
answer: Yes, farmers must register on the "Meri Fasal, Mera Byora" portal during the sowing period to avail benefits under the scheme.

scheme_name: Bhavantar Bharpai Yojana
question: Where can farmers register for the scheme?
answer: Registration facilities are available at Saral Kendras, e-Disha Kendras, Marketing Board offices, Horticulture Department offices, Agriculture Department offices, and internet kiosks.

scheme_name: Bhavantar Bharpai Yojana
question: Who verifies the registered crop area?
answer: The Horticulture Department verifies the crop area registered by the farmers.

scheme_name: Bhavantar Bharpai Yojana
question: Is there any fee for registration under the BBY?
answer: No, the registration for the scheme is free of cost.

scheme_name: Bhavantar Bharpai Yojana
question: When is the registration period open for the BBY?
answer: Registration is open only during the specified period, which is announced by the authorities. Farmers should register within this timeframe to be eligible for benefits.

scheme_name: Bhavantar Bharpai Yojana
question: Is it mandatory to sell produce through 'J-Forms' to avail benefits?
answer: Yes, to avail benefits under the scheme, it is mandatory to sell the produce through 'J-Forms'.

scheme_name: Bhavantar Bharpai Yojana
question: Where can farmers upload their sales details under the scheme?
answer: After selling their produce using 'J-Forms', farmers can upload their sales details on the BBY e-portal (www.bby.hortharyana.gov.in). Facilities for this are available at the respective Market Committee offices.

scheme_name: Bhavantar Bharpai Yojana
question: How is the compensation calculated under the scheme?
answer: If the wholesale price of the produce during the sale period is less than the protected price, the government compensates the difference to the registered farmers. The compensation is based on the quantity sold through 'J-Forms' and the per-acre production determined as per the scheme's guidelines.

scheme_name: Bhavantar Bharpai Yojana
question: How is the average daily wholesale price determined?
answer: The average daily wholesale price is determined based on the daily prices from designated mandis by the Mandi Board, following the scheme's standards and guidelines.

scheme_name: Bhavantar Bharpai Yojana
question: How is the compensation amount disbursed to farmers?
answer: The compensation amount is directly credited to the farmer's Aadhaar-linked bank account.
