scheme_name: Bima Yojana - Direct Benefit to Artisan
question: What is the Bima Yojana - Direct Benefit to Artisan (BYDBTA)?
answer: The BYDBTA is a social welfare scheme launched by the Ministry of Textiles on 15th August 2022, aimed at providing monthly financial support up to ₹8,000 to senior and award-winning artisans in the handicraft sector.

scheme_name: Bima Yojana - Direct Benefit to Artisan
question: Who is eligible for the BYDBTA scheme?
answer: To be eligible, the applicant must: | - Be a master craftsperson aged 60 years or above- Have received Shilp Guru, National Award, Merit Certificate, or similar national-level recognitions- Have an annual income not exceeding ₹1,00,000- Not be receiving similar financial aid from other government schemes  |  Note: Age relaxation is available for artisans with disabilities.

scheme_name: Bima Yojana - Direct Benefit to Artisan
question: What is the maximum benefit provided under the scheme?
answer: The maximum financial assistance is ₹8,000 per month, which may be given as: | - A monthly allowance- A lump sum grant, or- Both, but not exceeding the monthly cap of ₹8,000.

scheme_name: Bima Yojana - Direct Benefit to Artisan
question: Is this scheme applicable to all artisans?
answer: No, only senior and award-winning artisans who meet the eligibility criteria are covered under this scheme.

scheme_name: Bima Yojana - Direct Benefit to Artisan
question: How can one apply for the BYDBTA scheme?
answer: The application process is offline: | - Fill the prescribed application form | - Submit it at the nearest Handicrafts Service Centre (HSC) along with required documents

scheme_name: Bima Yojana - Direct Benefit to Artisan
question: What documents are required to apply for this scheme?
answer: Applicants must provide: | - Aadhaar Card | - Artisan ID Proof issued by DC (Handicrafts)- Birth Certificate (for age verification)- Bank Account Details (for benefit transfer)- Passport-sized Photograph- Annual income certificate and affidavit signed by a 1st Class Magistrate

scheme_name: Bima Yojana - Direct Benefit to Artisan
question: Can artisans receiving MUDRA loans apply for this scheme?
answer: Yes, provided they are not receiving similar financial assistance from other government sources. The artisan must be registered with the Office of Development Commissioner (Handicrafts).

scheme_name: Bima Yojana - Direct Benefit to Artisan
question: Who implements the BYDBTA scheme?
answer: The scheme is implemented by the Office of the Development Commissioner (Handicrafts) under the Ministry of Textiles, Government of India.

scheme_name: Bima Yojana - Direct Benefit to Artisan

answer: Yes, financial assistance is transferred directly to the artisan’s bank account linked with their Aadhaar.

scheme_name: Bima Yojana - Direct Benefit to Artisan
question: Do artisans need to renew their application every year?
answer: Yes, beneficiaries must submit a fresh income certificate and affidavit every year, duly countersigned by a 1st Class Magistrate, to continue receiving the benefit.

scheme_name: Biotechnology Young Entrepreneur Award
question: What is the “Biotechnology Young Entrepreneur (BYE) Award” programme?
answer: The "Biotechnology Young Entrepreneur (BYE) Award" programme is aimed to raise awareness of commercialization of bioscience ideas among post graduate students in Biotechnology and to encourage them to develop biotechnology entrepreneurship. This is an annual competition organized along with a workshop. The participants will then develop a Business Plan which will be judged by a panel of experts.

scheme_name: Biotechnology Young Entrepreneur Award
question: Which is the implementing agency of this programme?
answer: Kerala Biotechnology Commission (KBC) under the Kerala State Council for Science, Technology and Environment (KSCSTE)

scheme_name: Biotechnology Young Entrepreneur Award
question: Who is eligible to get the benefits under the programme?
answer: The students who are pursuing post-graduate programmes (including integrated PG degree programmes), doctoral degree, B.E. or B.Tech. in Biotechnology or in the area of life sciences related to biotechnology (bioinformatics/Molecular biology/microbiology/biochemistry/Genetics and/or related subjects) from universities/Institutes in the State of Kerala are eligible to apply.

scheme_name: Biotechnology Young Entrepreneur Award
question: What is the prize money given to the winning team?
answer: The winning teams will be given cash awards by Kerala Biotechnology Commission. The first prize will be [?]1,00,000/-, 2nd prize will be [?]50,000/- and third prize will be [?]25,000/-.

scheme_name: Biotechnology Young Entrepreneur Award
question: What should be the aim of the proposal?
answer: The proposals should aim at possible commercialisation of a product / patent.

scheme_name: Biotechnology Young Entrepreneur Award
question: In which areas of biotechnology proposal can be submitted?
answer: The Proposals need to be submitted in the core areas of biotechnology which include: Agriculture, Aquaculture, Bio-energy, Biologicals and Applications, Bioprocess Engineering, Biosensors, Drug discovery & Development, Environment, Food, Medical Diagnostics/Devices, Nanobiology/Nanobiotechnology, Nutraceuticals, Vaccines and other related areas. The proposals could be either for a product, service or an application.

scheme_name: Biotechnology Young Entrepreneur Award
question: How many students should there be in a team?
answer: The applicants should form a team of five students. At least three members in the team of five should be with Life Science background and other members can be from disciplines other than life sciences/Biotechnology.

scheme_name: Biotechnology Young Entrepreneur Award
question: Can an individual team member only be from the same Institute/University?

scheme_name: Biotechnology Young Entrepreneur Award

scheme_name: Biotechnology Young Entrepreneur Award

scheme_name: Banglar Yuba Sathi

scheme_name: Cash Award (A.B.O.C.W.W.B)

scheme_name: Cultural Function And Production Grant Scheme

scheme_name: Craft & Gear (Unit: Boats of Appropriate Sizes Including Nets, Fish & Ice Holding Boxes, Etc.)

scheme_name: Craft & Gear (Unit: Boats of Appropriate Sizes Including Nets, Fish & Ice Holding Boxes, Etc.)

scheme_name: Craft & Gear (Unit: Boats of Appropriate Sizes Including Nets, Fish & Ice Holding Boxes, Etc.)

scheme_name: Comprehensive Handicrafts Cluster Development Programme
question: What is the Comprehensive Handicrafts Cluster Development Programme (CHCDP)?
answer: The CHCDP is a scheme by the Ministry of Textiles designed to develop handicrafts clusters with world-class infrastructure, aiming to enhance production, export, skill training, and business competitiveness for artisans and SMEs.

scheme_name: Comprehensive Handicrafts Cluster Development Programme
question: What is the main objective of CHCDP?
answer: The objective is to assist artisans and entrepreneurs in: | - Setting up modern, well-equipped units | - Accessing cutting-edge technology | - Receiving training and HR development | - Getting market linkages and support for production diversification

scheme_name: Comprehensive Handicrafts Cluster Development Programme
question: Who can apply under this scheme?
answer: Only a Special Purpose Vehicle (SPV) can apply. The SPV must be a legal entity (preferably a company) comprising stakeholders like: | - Leading manufacturers | - Suppliers | - Buyers | - Artisan federations or Self-Help Groups (SHGs)

scheme_name: Comprehensive Handicrafts Cluster Development Programme
question: How is the SPV selected?
answer: Generally, the SPV is selected through an open competitive bidding process. However, due to the unorganized nature of the handicrafts sector, the Project Approval and Monitoring Committee (PAMC) or the Government may select SPVs directly in special cases.

scheme_name: Comprehensive Handicrafts Cluster Development Programme
question: What are the key interventions or benefits offered under the CHCDP?
answer: The scheme supports: | Baseline survey & activity mapping | Skill training & capacity building | Improved toolkits | Marketing events, seminars, and design workshops | Establishment of Common Facility Centres, Raw Material Banks, Emporiums, and Design & Resource Centres

scheme_name: Comprehensive Handicrafts Cluster Development Programme
question: Is this scheme for individual artisans?
answer: No, this is a cluster-level infrastructure development scheme. However, individual artisans benefit indirectly through enhanced production facilities, skill training, market access, and better working environments.

scheme_name: Comprehensive Handicrafts Cluster Development Programme
question: What infrastructure will be created under this scheme?
answer: The scheme will help develop: | - Trade Common Production Centres | - Design & Resource Centres | - Facilitation Centres | - Emporiums and Common Facility Centres (CFCs) for artisans’ use

scheme_name: Comprehensive Handicrafts Cluster Development Programme
question: What documents are required to apply for CHCDP?
answer: The Executing Agency (EA) must submit: | - Detailed Project Report (DPR) | - Nature of SPV | - Sale/Lease Deed of land/building in the name of SPV- Non-agricultural land certificate | - Approved layout plan

scheme_name: Comprehensive Handicrafts Cluster Development Programme
question: What is the application process for the scheme?
answer: The process is offline. The Executing Agency (EA) must submit the application and necessary documents at the concerned Regional Office of the Textile Commissioner.

scheme_name: Comprehensive Handicrafts Cluster Development Programme
question: Who implements the CHCDP scheme?
answer: The scheme is implemented through a Special Purpose Vehicle (SPV) selected by the Project Approval and Monitoring Committee (PAMC) under the Office of the Development Commissioner (Handicrafts), Ministry of Textiles.

answer: You must submit your application within 1 year of the date of commencement of operation to be eligible for the claim.

scheme_name: Capital Investment Subsidy for Creation of Infrastructure
question: Are there any mandatory employment requirements regarding local residents that I must satisfy to be eligible for the capital subsidy?
answer: Yes, to be eligible for the capital subsidy, it is mandatory to provide employment to 70% of the total staff to residents of Madhya Pradesh.

scheme_name: Capital Investment Subsidy for Creation of Infrastructure
question: Once I have received the subsidy, is there a mandatory minimum period during which I must keep my tourism unit operational?
answer: You are required to run the unit for at least 3 years from the date of availing the subsidy and must submit a self-declaration regarding continuous operation annually.

scheme_name: Capital Investment Subsidy for Creation of Infrastructure
question: What are the financial consequences if I am unable to sustain the operation of my unit and have to close it within three years?
answer: If the unit closes within 1, 2, or 3 years of receiving the subsidy, you must refund 80%, 60%, or 50% of the subsidy amount, respectively.

scheme_name: Commemoration of Jubilees/Birth Anniversaries of Tiatr Artistes of Yesteryears
question: How far in advance should I submit my application if I want to organize a memorial programme for a departed cultural figure?
answer: Your complete application must reach the office of the Tiatr Academy of Goa at least 30 days before your proposed programme date. Applications are processed on a "First come First Serve" basis, subject to fund availability.

scheme_name: Commemoration of Jubilees/Birth Anniversaries of Tiatr Artistes of Yesteryears
question: What documentation about my programme content and performers do I need to provide when applying for this cultural commemoration scheme?
answer: You must submit a detailed proposal that includes the complete typed script, all lyrics to be presented during the programme, and the names of all artistes who will be performing. This comprehensive documentation is required at the application stage.

scheme_name: Commemoration of Jubilees/Birth Anniversaries of Tiatr Artistes of Yesteryears
question: Are there any restrictions on what I can say or present during the commemorative programme about government policies or religious matters?
answer: Yes, you must ensure no adverse remarks are made in written or verbal form against any Government, Individual, or Institution, and avoid anything against caste, creed, or religion that may hurt religious sentiments. Content must remain respectful and non-controversial throughout.

scheme_name: Commemoration of Jubilees/Birth Anniversaries of Tiatr Artistes of Yesteryears
question: What is the minimum duration requirement for cultural programmes organized under this commemorative scheme?
answer: The programme duration must be at least 2 hours. This minimum time requirement ensures adequate coverage of the artiste's history and provides sufficient cultural content to honor their legacy properly.

scheme_name: Commemoration of Jubilees/Birth Anniversaries of Tiatr Artistes of Yesteryears
question: How many performance venues and shows am I allowed to organize if my application gets approved for this memorial scheme?
answer: You can organize a maximum of 4 shows at 4 different locations, including 3 shows in cities like Panaji, Margao, Curchorem, or Vasco, and 1 show compulsorily in the deceased artiste's area of residence. Additionally, 2 more village shows may be granted subject to fund availability.

scheme_name: Commemoration of Jubilees/Birth Anniversaries of Tiatr Artistes of Yesteryears
question: What specific information about the honored artiste must be included as part of every commemorative programme under this scheme?
answer: The programme must compulsorily include narration of the complete history and life story of the late artiste to whom the programme is dedicated. This biographical content is essential for educating the audience about their contributions.

scheme_name: Commemoration of Jubilees/Birth Anniversaries of Tiatr Artistes of Yesteryears
question: Do I need to invite specific people to attend the commemorative function, and are there any mandatory guests required?
answer: Family members of the deceased artiste must be compulsorily invited to the function. Additionally, the President or Vice President of the Tiatr Academy of Goa will serve as either the Chief Guest or Guest of Honour at your event.

scheme_name: Commemoration of Jubilees/Birth Anniversaries of Tiatr Artistes of Yesteryears
question: What acknowledgment requirements must I follow in all promotional materials and advertisements for my commemorative cultural programme?
answer: All advertisements, whether oral, print, electronic media, or banners, must include the phrase "This programme is held in collaboration with Tiatr Academy of Goa." This acknowledgment is mandatory across all promotional activities and materials.

scheme_name: Commemoration of Jubilees/Birth Anniversaries of Tiatr Artistes of Yesteryears
question: What banner and logo display requirements do I need to follow during Tiatr performances versus Musical Shows?
answer: For Tiatr performances, you must display the Tiatr Academy of Goa's banner on the front side wing of the stage and return it afterward. For Musical Shows, display a minimum 6ft x 10ft banner carrying the Tiatr Academy logo as backdrop.

scheme_name: Commemoration of Jubilees/Birth Anniversaries of Tiatr Artistes of Yesteryears
question: What financial documentation and receipts do I need to submit after completing my commemorative programme to receive reimbursement?
answer: You must submit a statement of expenditure with all original bills enclosed. If any bill exceeds ₹5,000/-, you need a stamped receipt. This financial documentation is required for benefit disbursement and audit purposes.

scheme_name: Commemoration of Jubilees/Birth Anniversaries of Tiatr Artistes of Yesteryears
question: What photographic evidence and records do I need to provide to the Academy after completing my commemorative cultural programme?
answer: You must send 5 copies of photographs from the function to the Tiatr Academy of Goa for their records. Two of these photographs must specifically show the Tiatr Academy banner prominently displayed during the performance.

answer: Jan Aadhaar is "one number, one card, one identity" scheme, Its main objective is to prepare a. database of demographic and socio-economic information of the resident families of the state and through the Jan Aadhaar card, the identity of the family and its members.

scheme_name: Appointment of Contract Sports Coaches
question: Who can apply under this scheme?
answer: Eligible state-level players and qualified sports coaches can apply for contractual appointment.

scheme_name: Appointment of Contract Sports Coaches
question: Is it mandatory for the coach to be a permanent resident of Uttarakhand?
answer: No, it is not mandatory for a contract trainer to be a domicile or permanent resident of Uttarakhand.

scheme_name: Appointment of Contract Sports Coaches
question: What qualifications are required to become a contract sports coach?
answer: Applicants should have the required educational and sports-related qualifications, as prescribed in the notification issued each year.

scheme_name: Appointment of Contract Sports Coaches
question: How are applications for training camps submitted?

scheme_name: Appointment of Contract Sports Coaches
question: How often are the training camps organized?

scheme_name: Appointment of Contract Sports Coaches
question: How long do the training camps run each year?
answer: The camps run for a maximum period of 11 months, from 15th April to 15th March.

scheme_name: Appointment of Contract Sports Coaches
question: How are coaches appointed?
answer: Coaches are appointed on a contract basis, based on applications received and requirements at the district level.

scheme_name: Appointment of Contract Sports Coaches
question: When is the notification for the scheme issued?
answer: The notification is usually issued in the month of March through daily newspapers.

scheme_name: Appointment of Contract Sports Coaches
question: What types of sports are covered under these training camps?
answer: Various sports recognized by the Department of Sports are included, depending on district-level requirements.

scheme_name: Compensation for Loss of Life and Property Caused by Wild Animals in and around Forest Areas: Assistance for Loss of Cattle Due to Wild Animal Attacks
question: Who is eligible to apply for the scheme?
answer: Any permanent resident of Uttarakhand whose domestic animal or cattle has been killed by wild animals in forest areas or surrounding regions is eligible.

scheme_name: Compensation for Loss of Life and Property Caused by Wild Animals in and around Forest Areas: Assistance for Loss of Cattle Due to Wild Animal Attacks
question: Which animals are covered under this scheme?
answer: Compensation is applicable for losses caused by tiger, leopard, snow leopard, all species of bear, hyena, wild boar, crocodile/gharial, and snake.

scheme_name: Compensation for Loss of Life and Property Caused by Wild Animals in and around Forest Areas: Assistance for Loss of Cattle Due to Wild Animal Attacks
question: What is the minimum and maximum compensation amount per animal?
answer: - Maximum: ₹40,000/- per animal | - Minimum: ₹3,000/- per animal

scheme_name: Compensation for Loss of Life and Property Caused by Wild Animals in and around Forest Areas: Assistance for Loss of Cattle Due to Wild Animal Attacks
question: How can I report an incident of wild animal attack?
answer: Incidents can be reported through the toll-free number 1800-890-9715, issued by the Forest Department.

scheme_name: Compensation for Loss of Life and Property Caused by Wild Animals in and around Forest Areas: Assistance for Loss of Cattle Due to Wild Animal Attacks
question: Who verifies the killing of the animal?
answer: Verification is done by the village head or a currently serving public representative and the forest guard of the concerned area.

scheme_name: Compensation for Loss of Life and Property Caused by Wild Animals in and around Forest Areas: Assistance for Loss of Cattle Due to Wild Animal Attacks
question: What is the procedure for claiming compensation?
answer: - The owner must submit a written report to the range office within two days of the incident. | - Verification is conducted by local authorities and forest staff. | - 20% of the payable amount is released in advance, and the remaining is paid after the final investigation report.

scheme_name: Compensation for Loss of Life and Property Caused by Wild Animals in and around Forest Areas: Assistance for Loss of Cattle Due to Wild Animal Attacks
question: Who approves and disburses the ex-gratia amount?
answer: The Divisional Forest Officer/Deputy Director approves and disburses the final ex-gratia payment based on the final investigation report of the Assistant Conservator of Forests/Wildlife Warden.

scheme_name: Compensation for Loss of Life and Property Caused by Wild Animals in and around Forest Areas: Assistance for Damage to Houses Due to Wild Elephant Attacks
question: Who is eligible to apply?
answer: Any resident of Uttarakhand whose house or structure has been damaged by wild elephants is eligible to apply.

scheme_name: Compensation for Loss of Life and Property Caused by Wild Animals in and around Forest Areas: Assistance for Damage to Houses Due to Wild Elephant Attacks
question: What types of houses are covered?
answer: The scheme covers kutcha houses, boundary walls, huts, and pucca houses damaged by wild elephants.

scheme_name: Compensation for Loss of Life and Property Caused by Wild Animals in and around Forest Areas: Assistance for Damage to Houses Due to Wild Elephant Attacks
question: What is the compensation range under the scheme?
answer: Compensation ranges from a minimum of ₹900 to a maximum of ₹95,000, depending on the extent and type of damage.

scheme_name: Compensation for Loss of Life and Property Caused by Wild Animals in and around Forest Areas: Assistance for Damage to Houses Due to Wild Elephant Attacks
question: How should the damage be reported?
answer: The incident must be reported in writing to the concerned Range Office within two days of the damage.

scheme_name: Compensation for Loss of Life and Property Caused by Wild Animals in and around Forest Areas: Assistance for Damage to Houses Due to Wild Elephant Attacks
question: Who verifies the reported damage?
answer: The Forest Inspector or Deputy Forest Range Officer immediately confirms the incident, and the damage is jointly assessed by the Naib Tehsildar and Range Officer of the concerned area.

scheme_name: Compensation for Loss of Life and Property Caused by Wild Animals in and around Forest Areas: Assistance for Damage to Houses Due to Wild Elephant Attacks
question: Who approves the compensation?
answer: The Divisional Forest Officer/Deputy Director receives the final report and has full authority to approve and disburse the ex-gratia compensation.

scheme_name: Compensation for Loss of Life and Property Caused by Wild Animals in and around Forest Areas: Assistance for Damage to Houses Due to Wild Elephant Attacks
question: What is the timeline for the final investigation report?
answer: The Assistant Conservator of Forests/Wildlife Warden must submit the final investigation report to the Divisional Forest Officer/Deputy Director within one month of the incident.

scheme_name: Compensation for Loss of Life and Property Caused by Wild Animals in and around Forest Areas: Assistance for Crop Losses Due to Wild Animal Attacks
question: Who can apply for compensation under this scheme?
answer: Any farmer who is a resident of Uttarakhand and owns or cultivates land affected by wild animal attacks can apply.

scheme_name: Compensation for Loss of Life and Property Caused by Wild Animals in and around Forest Areas: Assistance for Crop Losses Due to Wild Animal Attacks
question: Which animals are covered under this scheme?
answer: Compensation is provided for damage caused by wild elephants, wild boars, nilgai (blue bulls), peacocks, sambar, chital, barking deer, monkeys, and kakar.

scheme_name: Compensation for Loss of Life and Property Caused by Wild Animals in and around Forest Areas: Assistance for Crop Losses Due to Wild Animal Attacks
question: What is the range of compensation provided?
answer: The compensation ranges from a minimum of ₹8,000/- per acre to a maximum of ₹25,000/- per acre, depending on the extent of crop damage.

scheme_name: Compensation for Loss of Life and Property Caused by Wild Animals in and around Forest Areas: Assistance for Crop Losses Due to Wild Animal Attacks
question: How should a farmer report crop damage?
answer: The damage must be reported in writing to the local forest officer within two days of the incident.

scheme_name: Compensation for Loss of Life and Property Caused by Wild Animals in and around Forest Areas: Assistance for Crop Losses Due to Wild Animal Attacks
question: Who assesses the crop damage?
answer: The Tehsildar/Patwari and the local forest officer of the area jointly verify and assess the damage.

scheme_name: Compensation for Loss of Life and Property Caused by Wild Animals in and around Forest Areas: Assistance for Crop Losses Due to Wild Animal Attacks
question: Who prepares the investigation report?
answer: The investigation report is prepared by the local forest officer and made available to the Assistant Conservator of Forests/Wildlife Warden through the Range Officer.

scheme_name: Compensation for Loss of Life and Property Caused by Wild Animals in and around Forest Areas: Assistance for Crop Losses Due to Wild Animal Attacks
question: Who approves the compensation amount?
answer: The Divisional Forest Officer/Deputy Director receives the final investigation report and has full authority to approve and disburse the ex-gratia compensation.

scheme_name: Car Loan Scheme
question: How do I create an account and begin the registration process on the application portal?
answer: To create your account, visit the PIPDIC website at https://pipdic.in/, click "Login", and then select the "New customer" link. Enter a unique username, your email address, a secure password, and the Captcha code, then click "Register" to complete the registration process.

scheme_name: Car Loan Scheme
question: What is the purpose of the One-Time Password verification during the login process?
answer: The OTP is a security measure sent to your registered email address to verify your identity and ensure that only authorized users can access your account. You must enter this OTP and click "Login" to proceed to your customer dashboard.

scheme_name: Car Loan Scheme
question: What information am I required to provide when updating my profile after successful login?
answer: Upon logging in, you must access the "Edit Profile" option in the top right corner of your dashboard and complete all required profile details as requested by the system. These details are necessary for the loan application processing and verification purposes.

scheme_name: Car Loan Scheme
question: What documents and information should I prepare before starting my loan application?
answer: Before beginning your loan application, gather all Know Your Customer (KYC) documents and supporting documents as specified in the application checklist. Additionally, prepare detailed biodata information for the Promoter, Partner, or Director, as you will need to upload these documents during the application process.

scheme_name: Car Loan Scheme
question: Where can I access the loan application form once I have completed my profile setup?
answer: After completing your profile update, navigate to the "Applications" tab on your customer dashboard to access the loan application form section.

scheme_name: Car Loan Scheme
question: What is included in the checklist that appears before I can proceed with the loan application?
answer: The pop-up checklist displays the General Terms and Conditions, interest rate structure, investigation fees, and collateral security norms applicable to your loan. You must carefully review this information and confirm that you have gathered all necessary documents before proceeding.

scheme_name: Car Loan Scheme
question: What declaration must I read and agree to before submitting my loan application?
answer: You must read the comprehensive declaration within the application form, which covers confirmation of true and accurate information provided, absence of unauthorized borrowing arrangements, and consent to verification and investigation by PIPDIC officials.

scheme_name: Car Loan Scheme
question: How many steps does the loan application form typically contain, and what should I do if I need to pause my application?
answer: The loan application is structured as a multi-step form across several stages. While the document does not specify a save-and-resume feature, you should complete all mandatory fields across each required step before proceeding to the next stage.

scheme_name: Car Loan Scheme
question: What is the process for uploading Know Your Customer and supporting documents after submitting my application details?
answer: After completing the main application form submission, the system will redirect you to enter your Promoter, Partner, or Director biodata information in a multi-step process. For each required document field, click the "Choose File" button, select the appropriate file from your computer in the format specified by the portal, and upload it to the system.

scheme_name: Car Loan Scheme
question: What are the applicable application fees for different loan amounts under this scheme?
answer: For loan amounts up to ₹25,00,000/-, the application fee is ₹100/-. For loan amounts exceeding ₹25,00,000/-, the application fee is ₹200/-.

scheme_name: Car Loan Scheme
question: How do I make the payment for my application fee, and what happens after successful payment?
answer: Once your application and biodata submission is complete, proceed to pay the applicable application fee. If you select online payment, the system will automatically redirect you to a payment summary page where you can verify your details and complete the payment transaction.

scheme_name: Car Loan Scheme
question: What should I do with the payment receipt I receive after paying my application fee?
answer: Upon successful payment, a receipt for your application fee is generated automatically. You can print this receipt or save it to your computer as a PDF for future reference and record-keeping purposes.

scheme_name: Car Loan Scheme
question: How can I track the status of my submitted loan application after submission?
answer: You can monitor your application status by clicking the "View My Application" link on your customer dashboard and selecting your relevant loan application from the drop-down menu. Your application will initially display a status such as "UNDER REVIEW" as it progresses through processing.

scheme_name: Car Loan Scheme
question: What contact information and support channels are available if I need assistance or wish to file a grievance regarding my application?
answer: You can contact the Managing Director at the Pondicherry Industrial Promotion Development and Investment Corporation Limited office located at No.60, Romain Rolland Street, Puducherry 605001. The office phone number is 0413-2334361, and you can email your queries to info@pipdic.com. The General Manager (Administration) is also available via mobile contact at 9894653835. You can also submit a grievance form at https://pipdic.in/grievance_form.

scheme_name: Composite Loan Scheme
question: What are the eligibility criteria for Persons with Disabilities applying under the scheme?
answer: Applicants must have a disability of at least 40%, be Delhi residents, and have an annual family income below [?]1,20,000/-.

scheme_name: Composite Loan Scheme
question: Is there a residency requirement for applicants under the scheme?
answer: Yes, applicants must be residents of Delhi to be eligible for the scheme.

scheme_name: Composite Loan Scheme
question: What is the age range required for applicants to qualify for the scheme?
answer: Applicants must be between 18 and 50 years old to be eligible for the scheme.

scheme_name: Composite Loan Scheme
question: What is the maximum annual family income allowed for applicants under the scheme?
answer: The annual family income of the applicant must not exceed [?]1,20,000/- from all sources.

scheme_name: Composite Loan Scheme
question: What type of activities must applicants be willing to pursue to qualify for the scheme?
answer: Applicants must be willing to pursue income-generating activities listed in the scheme guidelines.

scheme_name: Composite Loan Scheme
question: Is there a requirement for applicants to have a workplace for their proposed activity?
answer: Yes, applicants must have a proper workplace, either owned or rented, to start their proposed activity.

scheme_name: Composite Loan Scheme
question: Can applicants who have defaulted on other schemes apply for this scheme?
answer: No, applicants must not have been declared defaulters under any schemes implemented by DSFDC.

scheme_name: Composite Loan Scheme
question: What is the maximum loan amount available for applicants from the Scheduled Caste category?
answer: Applicants from the Scheduled Caste category can avail of a need-based loan of up to [?]3,00,000/-.

scheme_name: Composite Loan Scheme
question: What is the maximum loan amount for applicants from OBC, Minority, and PwD categories?
answer: Applicants from OBC, Minority, and PwD categories can avail of a need-based loan of up to [?]1,00,000/-.

scheme_name: Composite Loan Scheme
question: What documents are accepted as proof of age for applicants?
answer: Accepted documents include a birth certificate, school leaving certificate, or an affidavit as proof of age.

scheme_name: Composite Loan Scheme
question: What additional document is needed if the workplace is owned by a relative?
answer: Applicants must provide an affidavit of a No Objection Certificate if the workplace is owned by a relative.

scheme_name: Composite Loan Scheme
question: Are guarantors required for loans above ₹2,00,000/-?
answer: Yes, for loans above [?]2,00,000/-, applicants must provide five blank post-dated cheques from a guarantor.

scheme_name: Credit Linked Subsidy Scheme for Middle Income Group
question: What is Affordable Housing through Credit Linked Subsidy Scheme for MIG?
answer: Under Credit Linked Subsidy Scheme, beneficiaries of Middle-Income Group (MIG) can seek housing loans from Banks, Housing Finance Companies and other such institutions for acquisition/ construction of house (including re-purchase). The credit linked subsidy will be available only for loan amounts upto Rs. 9 lakhs for MIG-I and Rs 12 lakhs for MIG-II and such loans would be eligible for an interest subsidy at the rate of 4 % and 3% respectively for a tenure of 20 years or during tenure of loan whichever is lower. The Net Present Value (NPV) of the interest subsidy will be calculated at a discount rate of 9%. Any additional loan amount beyond the limit will be at non-subsidized rate. However, the carpet area of the house should be strictly restricted within the permissible carpet area of 160 sq m and 200 sq m for MIG-I and MIG-II categories respectively.

scheme_name: Credit Linked Subsidy Scheme for Middle Income Group
question: What are the income norms for various categories?
answer: MIG I households with an annual income more than Rs.6 lakh and up to Rs.12 lakh. | MIG II households with an annual income more than Rs. 12 lakh and up to Rs. 18 lakh.

scheme_name: Credit Linked Subsidy Scheme for Middle Income Group
question: When was the PMAY scheme launched by the Government for MIG?
answer: CLSS under vertical of Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana -Urban for Middle Income Groups was launched by the Government of India with the effect from January 1, 2017.

scheme_name: Credit Linked Subsidy Scheme for Middle Income Group
question: What is the process of crediting the interest subsidy?
answer: The subsidy is released by the CNAs based on the disbursements made by PLIs to the beneficiaries. Subsidy, disbursed by the CNA to the PLI, is credited by the PLI to the borrower's home loan account upfront by deducting it from the principal loan amount. As a result, the borrower will pay EMI on the remainder of the principal loan amount.

scheme_name: Credit Linked Subsidy Scheme for Middle Income Group
question: What is the role of States/ UTs/ ULBs for Affordable Housing through Credit Linked Subsidy scheme?
answer: Role of States/UTs/ULBs under this vertical would be as under: | States/UTs/ULBs/PLIs shall ensure link beneficiary identification through Aadhaar for de-duplication. State Level Nodal Agency (SLNA) identified by State/UT for implementing the PMAY(U) will facilitate the identified eligible beneficiaries in getting approvals and documents, etc. to avail of Credit Linked Subsidy Scheme.

scheme_name: Credit Linked Subsidy Scheme for Middle Income Group
question: Who are the Central Nodal Agencies (CNAs) and what is their role in disbursal of subsidy under CLSS to PLIs?
answer: As of now, HUDCO, NHB and SBI have been identified as CNAs to channelize the credit linked subsidy to the PLIs and monitor the progress of CLSS. Ministry may notify other Institutions as CNA in future.

scheme_name: Credit Linked Subsidy Scheme for Middle Income Group
question: Which are the PLIs through whom this interest subsidy is released or credited?
answer: Primary Lending Institutions such as Scheduled Commercial Banks (SCB), Housing Finance Companies (HFCs), Regional Rural Banks (RRBs), State Cooperative Banks, Urban Cooperative Banks (Scheduled as well as Non-scheduled), Small Finance Banks (as approved by the Reserve Bank of India) and Non-Banking Financial Company-Micro Finance Institutions (NBFC-MFIs) (as registered with Reserve Bank of India) which have signed MoUs with any one of the CNAs.

scheme_name: Credit Linked Subsidy Scheme for Middle Income Group
question: Whether PLIs have to sign MoUs with CNAs for claiming subsidies?
answer: Yes, PLIs can register with any CAN after signing MoU as provided in Annexure-I in the PMAY (U) guidelines.

scheme_name: Credit Linked Subsidy Scheme for Middle Income Group
question: How subsidy is disbursed to the CNAs?
answer: An advance subsidy is released to each CNA at the start of the scheme. Subsequent amount of credit linked subsidy will be released to the CNAs after 70% utilization of earlier amounts based on claims raised by CNAs.

scheme_name: Credit Linked Subsidy Scheme for Middle Income Group
question: Is there any preferential treatment for beneficiaries proposed for Affordable Housing through Credit Linked Subsidy Scheme?
answer: Yes, Preference under the CLSS will be given to Manual Scavengers, Women (with overriding preference to widows), persons belonging to Scheduled Castes/ Scheduled Tribes/ Other Backward Classes, Minorities, Persons with disabilities and Transgenders subject to beneficiaries being from EWS / LIG, MIG -I & II segments as applicable.

scheme_name: Credit Linked Subsidy Scheme for Middle Income Group
question: What happens when the subsidy has already been disbursed, but due to certain reasons, the construction of the house is stalled?
answer: In cases where the construction of house is not completed within 36 months from the date of release of the first disbursement, subsidy is to be recovered by the PLI and refunded to the CNA who had released the subsidy.

scheme_name: Credit Linked Subsidy Scheme for Middle Income Group
question: Since the subsidy is released to the PLI post claim, does it mean that PLI has to charge the EMI on the entire loan amount and after the CLSS claim amount is released, adjust the same to the loan and thereafter calculate the revised EMI payable by the beneficiary?
answer: Yes

scheme_name: Credit Linked Subsidy Scheme for Middle Income Group
question: Is there any limit or upper cap on the value (Cost) of the property for which home loan can be availed?
answer: No.

scheme_name: Credit Linked Subsidy Scheme for Middle Income Group
question: Where can we get list of approved Towns where the scheme is operational?
answer: The list of Statutory Towns along with any other towns notified subsequently is provided through CNAs and may be accessed on the website of the CNAs and PMAY(U).

scheme_name: Credit Linked Subsidy Scheme for Middle Income Group
question: The disbursal of subsidy amount is in maximum of 4 instalments whereas a builder could demand construction linked instalments in more than this number. How to deal with such cases?
answer: In such cases, the number of disbursal instalments can be decided based on the discussions between CNAs and PLIs for availing the benefit under the CLSS, provided all other requirements of the scheme are complied with.

scheme_name: Credit Linked Subsidy Scheme for Middle Income Group
question: Whether MoHUA is contemplating to share the burden, where a loan becomes NPA and the PLI concerned is unable to recover the entire outstanding amount from the beneficiaries?
answer: It is the responsibility of the PLIs to carry out due diligence of the borrower as per their due diligence norms and as such recovery of NPAs, if any, is their responsibility. However, where the construction of the unit is stalled due to any reason, the subsidy released by MoHUA is to be recovered along with loan recovery by the PLI.

scheme_name: Credit Linked Subsidy Scheme for Middle Income Group
question: Is there any State Government sponsorship or approval required for availing benefits under this scheme for Private Developers?
answer: No

scheme_name: Credit Linked Subsidy Scheme for Middle Income Group
question: Is resale from (builder/seller) allowed under CLSS?
answer: Resale cases would be allowed but it is incumbent upon banks to adopt their due diligence and banking mechanism processes to curtail speculative cases in this scenario.

scheme_name: Credit Linked Subsidy Scheme for Middle Income Group
question: Can NRIs be considered under this scheme?
answer: NRIs can be considered provided they are eligible under the Scheme Guidelines and are also in compliance with other GoI/RBI rules, if any, applicable to NRIs.

scheme_name: Credit Linked Subsidy Scheme for Middle Income Group
question: Whether PLIs can fix the repayment tenure of more than 20 years to benefit eligible loanees under the scheme?
answer: The interest subsidy will be for tenure of 20 years or during the tenure of the loan whichever is lower. PLIs can fix the repayment tenure of more than 20 years, but the interest subsidy will be calculated for tenure upto 20 years.

scheme_name: Credit Linked Subsidy Scheme for Middle Income Group
question: What is the maximum tenure on which the credit linked subsidy is applicable?
answer: The credit linked subsidy is available for a maximum tenure of 20 years or the actual tenure of loan, whichever is less.

scheme_name: Credit Linked Subsidy Scheme for Middle Income Group
question: Is there any loan amount limit for CLSS availing benefit under?
answer: No, there is no loan amount limit for loan accounts which are booked under CLSS. However, subsidy will be restricted to the loan amount of 9 Lakh and Rs.12 Lakh for MIG-I & MIG-II respectively.

scheme_name: Credit Linked Subsidy Scheme for Middle Income Group
question: Are there any additional eligibility norms apart from income, first pucca house and carpet area norms?
answer: The property on which the subsidy is to be availed has to have | Basic amenities such as water, sanitation, sewerage, roads, electricity etc. | Property must be located at Statutory Towns as per Census 2011 and towns notified subsequently, including Notified Planning/ Development Areas.

scheme_name: Credit Linked Subsidy Scheme for Middle Income Group

scheme_name: Chief Minister’s Shasakt Kisan Yojana

scheme_name: Chief Minister Arogya Arunachal Yojana

question: Who are Eligible under CMHIS (GEN) Category:

scheme_name: Chief Minister’s Health Insurance Scheme - Nagaland
question: Who are Eligible under CMHIS (EP) Category:
answer: CMHIS (EP) category includes State government employees who are eligible for monthly Medical Allowance (MA) and or reimbursement of medical expenses under Medical Re-imbursement scheme viz (1). Regular employees, (2). Pensioners, (3). Serving Legislators/ Ex- Legislators, (4). Employees of State Public Sector Undertakings, Corporations and Autonomous Bodies, (5). Workcharge employees (on Scale Pay), and their dependent family members.

scheme_name: Chief Minister’s Health Insurance Scheme - Nagaland

AB PM-JAY Beneficiaries including Building and other Construction Workers will not be covered under CMHIS (GEN) category. | b. scheme_name: Chief Ministers House Rent

scheme_name: Chief Ministers House Rent

scheme_name: Chief Minister Help Scheme

scheme_name: Chief Minister Help Scheme

scheme_name: Chief Minister Help Scheme

scheme_name: Support for Marginalized Individuals for Livelihood and Enterprise (SMILE): Composite Medical Health for Transgender Persons

scheme_name: Support for Marginalized Individuals for Livelihood and Enterprise (SMILE): Composite Medical Health for Transgender Persons

scheme_name: Support for Marginalized Individuals for Livelihood and Enterprise (SMILE): Composite Medical Health for Transgender Persons

scheme_name: Support for Marginalized Individuals for Livelihood and Enterprise (SMILE): Composite Medical Health for Transgender Persons
question: What is the total maximum financial coverage value provided annually to each eligible beneficiary under this specific health care offering?

scheme_name: Support for Marginalized Individuals for Livelihood and Enterprise (SMILE): Composite Medical Health for Transgender Persons

scheme_name: Support for Marginalized Individuals for Livelihood and Enterprise (SMILE): Composite Medical Health for Transgender Persons

scheme_name: Support for Marginalized Individuals for Livelihood and Enterprise (SMILE): Composite Medical Health for Transgender Persons

scheme_name: Support for Marginalized Individuals for Livelihood and Enterprise (SMILE): Composite Medical Health for Transgender Persons

scheme_name: Support for Marginalized Individuals for Livelihood and Enterprise (SMILE): Composite Medical Health for Transgender Persons

scheme_name: Support for Marginalized Individuals for Livelihood and Enterprise (SMILE): Composite Medical Health for Transgender Persons

scheme_name: Support for Marginalized Individuals for Livelihood and Enterprise (SMILE): Composite Medical Health for Transgender Persons

scheme_name: Mukhyamantri Hunar Yojana

scheme_name: CM's Jibon Anuprerana Scheme

scheme_name: CM's Jibon Anuprerana Scheme

scheme_name: CM's Jibon Anuprerana Scheme
question: Am I eligible for this scheme if I am currently employed while pursuing my PhD?

scheme_name: CM's Jibon Anuprerana Scheme

scheme_name: CM's Jibon Anuprerana Scheme

scheme_name: CM's Jibon Anuprerana Scheme

scheme_name: CM's Jibon Anuprerana Scheme

scheme_name: CM's Jibon Anuprerana Scheme

answer: The main objective is to provide accommodation and food facilities to tourists while creating employment opportunities for rural residents within their own homes.

scheme_name: Atithi Uttarakhand Home-Stay Registration
question: Who is eligible to register under this scheme?
answer: Any house owner in Uttarakhand who is willing to offer residential rooms to tourists and resides in the same house with their family is eligible.

scheme_name: Atithi Uttarakhand Home-Stay Registration
question: How many rooms can be registered for home stay purposes?
answer: A minimum of one and a maximum of six rooms can be registered.

scheme_name: Atithi Uttarakhand Home-Stay Registration
question: Is it mandatory for the homeowner to live in the same house?
answer: Yes, the home stay must be part of a residential unit where the owner and their family live.

scheme_name: Atithi Uttarakhand Home-Stay Registration
question: What are the basic requirements for the accommodation?
answer: The accommodation must be clean, well-maintained, equipped with fire safety tools, structurally sound, and must have a toilet.

scheme_name: Atithi Uttarakhand Home-Stay Registration
question: How can one apply for home stay registration?
answer: Applications must be submitted online at https://homestay.uttarakhandtourism.gov.in/.

scheme_name: Atithi Uttarakhand Home-Stay Registration
question: What is the registration fee?
answer: The registration fee is ₹500/-, payable via NEFT, online, or offline.

scheme_name: Atithi Uttarakhand Home-Stay Registration
question: Who conducts the inspection after submission?
answer: Departmental officers of the Tourism Department conduct an on-site inspection.

scheme_name: Atithi Uttarakhand Home-Stay Registration
question: When is the registration number issued?
answer: The registration number is issued after verification and successful inspection by officials.

scheme_name: Development of Manures & Fertilizers: Assistance for Construction/Installation of Vermi-Compost Units

scheme_name: Development of Manures & Fertilizers: Assistance for Construction/Installation of Vermi-Compost Units
question: How will the approved financial subsidy be transferred to my account after the sanction has been granted by the competent authority?

scheme_name: Development of Manures & Fertilizers: Assistance for Construction/Installation of Vermi-Compost Units
question: Are there any circumstances under which the government can provide exceptions or modifications to the standard eligibility conditions specified in the scheme?

scheme_name: Development of Manures & Fertilizers: Assistance for Construction/Installation of Vermi-Compost Units

scheme_name: Development of Manures & Fertilizers: Assistance for Construction/Installation of Vermi-Compost Units

scheme_name: Development of Manures & Fertilizers: Assistance for Construction/Installation of Vermi-Compost Units

scheme_name: Uttarakhand Startup Policy-2023

answer: A startup is an entity registered as a Private Limited Company, LLP, or Registered Partnership Firm that meets the criteria of innovation, scalability, employment or wealth generation potential, and complies with turnover and age limits specified in the policy.

scheme_name: Uttarakhand Startup Policy-2023
question: What is the maximum age of a startup to be eligible under this policy?
answer: The startup should not be more than ten years old from the date of incorporation.

scheme_name: Uttarakhand Startup Policy-2023
question: What is the turnover limit for startups under this policy?

scheme_name: Uttarakhand Startup Policy-2023

scheme_name: Uttarakhand Startup Policy-2023

scheme_name: Uttarakhand Startup Policy-2023

scheme_name: Uttarakhand Startup Policy-2023

scheme_name: Uttarakhand Startup Policy-2023
question: Is there any provision for a venture fund?

scheme_name: Uttarakhand Startup Policy-2023
question: Can startups registered outside Uttarakhand apply?

scheme_name: Uttarakhand Startup Policy-2023
question: How can startups apply for benefits under the policy?
answer: Applications must be submitted online through the portal https://startuputtarakhand.uk.gov.in/.

scheme_name: Spice Area Expansion

scheme_name: Spice Area Expansion

scheme_name: Spice Area Expansion

scheme_name: Spice Area Expansion

scheme_name: Spice Area Expansion

scheme_name: Spice Area Expansion

scheme_name: Cost of Spectacle for the Construction Workers

scheme_name: Cost of Spectacle for the Construction Workers

scheme_name: Cost of Spectacle for the Construction Workers

scheme_name: Cost of Spectacle for the Construction Workers

scheme_name: Cost of Spectacle for the Construction Workers

scheme_name: Cost of Spectacle for the Construction Workers

scheme_name: Cost of Spectacle for the Construction Workers

scheme_name: Certification Program for Goan IT Professionals

scheme_name: Certification Program for Goan IT Professionals

scheme_name: Certification Program for Goan IT Professionals

scheme_name: Certification Program for Goan IT Professionals

scheme_name: Coconut Palm Insurance Scheme
question: What is the 'Coconut Palm Insurance Scheme (CPIS)'?
answer: The Coconut Palm Insurance Scheme is a program initiated by the Coconut Development Board, Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare, Government of India. It aims to provide insurance coverage to coconut palms against natural calamities, climatic risks, pests, diseases, and other perils.

scheme_name: Coconut Palm Insurance Scheme
question: What are the objectives of this scheme?
answer: Assist coconut growers in insuring coconut palms, against natural and other perils. | Provide timely relief to farmers, who suffer income loss due to sudden death of palms. | - Minimize risk and encourage replanting and rejuvenation to make coconut farming remunerative.

scheme_name: Coconut Palm Insurance Scheme
question: Who is eligible for coverage under CPIS?
answer: All healthy nut-bearing coconut palms in the age group of 4 to 60 years, whether grown as mono or intercropped, on bunds farms or homestead, and of all varieties including Tall, Dwarf, and Hybrids are eligible for coverage. Unhealthy and senile palms will be excluded.

scheme_name: Coconut Palm Insurance Scheme
question: How is the age range determined for coverage?
answer: For Dwarf and Hybrid varieties, coverage begins from the 4th year of planting, while Tall variety coconut palms are eligible for coverage from the 7th year onwards, up to the age of 60 years.

scheme_name: Coconut Palm Insurance Scheme
question: Which areas and states are covered under the scheme?
answer: This insurance scheme will be implemented in the selected districts of all the States/UTs, growing coconut palms. | All bearing and healthy palms will be insured, in a contiguous area, by farmer/grower and every effort will be made by CDB, to get all bearing and healthy palms insured, in cluster villages of district(s).

scheme_name: Coconut Palm Insurance Scheme
question: How is this scheme implemented?
answer: The scheme is implemented through the Agriculture Insurance Company and collaborating State Governments in all coconut-growing states. Every effort is made by the Coconut Development Board to encourage farmers in cluster villages to insure all bearing and healthy palms in their respective districts.

scheme_name: Coconut Palm Insurance Scheme
question: How is the premium for CPIS determined?
answer: The premium for CPIS is subsidized to make it accessible for farmers. The Coconut Development Board (CDB) contributes 50%, the State Government covers 25%, and the remaining 25% is the responsibility of the farmer or grower. In certain cases, if the State government does not agree to bear its share, the farmer may need to pay 50%.

scheme_name: Coconut Palm Insurance Scheme
question: Is there any premium subsidy provided to farmers?
answer: Yes, there is a premium subsidy. The CDB and participating State Governments provide a subsidy amounting to 75% of the premium. The subsidy is released to the Insurance Company in advance based on estimates and is replenished/adjusted on a quarter/yearly basis.

scheme_name: Coconut Palm Insurance Scheme
question: Is there a waiting period for coverage under CPIS?
answer: Yes, there is a waiting period of 30 days from the inception of insurance during which loss or death of palms is not payable. However, this condition is not applicable for renewals without a time gap.

scheme_name: Coconut Palm Insurance Scheme
question: What happens if a farmer wishes to retain an unproductive palm without felling it?
answer: If a farmer/grower chooses to retain an unproductive palm without felling it, a salvage value of 50% of the sum insured will be deducted from the claim. Loss of the palm must be established through evidence of the occurrence of the insured peril.

scheme_name: Coconut Palm Insurance Scheme
question: Who is eligible to enroll in the Scheme?
answer: Individual farmers or growers offering a minimum of 5 healthy nut-bearing palms falling within the specified age group are eligible for insurance. For Dwarf and Hybrid varieties, the age group is 4-60 years, and for Tall varieties, it is 7-60 years.

scheme_name: Coconut Palm Insurance Scheme
question: Is the insurance based on individual palms or the entire plantation area?
answer: The insurance under CPIS is for individual palms and is not area-based. Each eligible palm must be individually insured.

scheme_name: Coconut Palm Insurance Scheme
question: Can a farmer opt for partial insurance of their coconut plantation?
answer: No, partial insurance of the plantation is not allowed under the CPIS. The entire contiguous area or plot with a minimum of 5 healthy nut-bearing palms must be covered under the scheme.

scheme_name: Coconut Palm Insurance Scheme
question: How is the age group determined for insurance coverage?
answer: The insured farmer or grower can self-declare the age group of the palms in the insurance proposal. However, the Insurance Company has the authority to verify the age of the insured palms at any time before the policy expires or a claim is paid. The insurance becomes void in case of a wrong declaration of age or any material fact by the insured regarding the insurance.

scheme_name: Coconut Palm Insurance Scheme
question: How can a farmer/grower apply under the scheme?
answer: Farmers/growers desiring insurance may directly contact representatives/authorized agents of Insurance Company or may contact nearest office of Agriculture/Horticulture Department. Premium will be paid by farmer/grower, net off premium subsidy, through cash, cheque/bank draft, drawn in favour of Insurance Company.
