answer: Students may be enrolled in class 10 or 11 if they have shown excellent performance in previous examinations and missed entry at class 9 level for any reason.

scheme_name: Centrally Sponsored Scheme of Upgradation of Merit of Scheduled Caste Students
question: How many years of continuous coaching support can a student expect to receive through this educational enhancement initiative?
answer: Students receive four years of continuous coaching support from class 9 to class 12, ensuring sufficient time for addressing educational deficiencies and competitive exam preparation.

scheme_name: Centrally Sponsored Scheme of Upgradation of Merit of Scheduled Caste Students
question: What specific subjects and areas are covered under the remedial coaching component of this merit upgradation program?
answer: Remedial coaching focuses on removing educational deficiencies in linguistic skills, Science and Mathematics, while also promoting proper study habits among Scheduled Caste students.

scheme_name: Centrally Sponsored Scheme of Upgradation of Merit of Scheduled Caste Students
question: Are there any special provisions or preferences given to girl students during the selection process for this coaching scheme?
answer: Awards are allocated in a 50:50 ratio between boys and girls, with unutilized awards by girls being transferable to boys and vice-versa to ensure optimal utilization.

scheme_name: Centrally Sponsored Scheme of Upgradation of Merit of Scheduled Caste Students
question: What percentage of seats are reserved for students with disabilities in this educational support program for merit enhancement?
answer: The target is to include at least 3% representation for disabled Scheduled Caste students wherever possible, ensuring inclusive participation in the coaching program.

scheme_name: Centrally Sponsored Scheme of Upgradation of Merit of Scheduled Caste Students
question: Which districts are prioritized for implementing this merit upgradation scheme for Scheduled Caste students seeking educational advancement?
answer: Priority is given to 2-3 districts with highest Scheduled Caste population that are identified as Educationally Backward Districts, particularly those with lower literacy rates.

scheme_name: Centrally Sponsored Scheme of Upgradation of Merit of Scheduled Caste Students
question: How is the scholarship amount disbursed to beneficiaries under this centrally sponsored educational coaching scheme?
answer: Scholarship amounts are disbursed through Direct Benefit Transfer system using Unique Identification Authority of India enabled bank accounts to ensure timely and correct payment to beneficiaries.

scheme_name: Centrally Sponsored Scheme of Upgradation of Merit of Scheduled Caste Students
question: What type of special coaching is provided to prepare students for competitive examinations in professional courses like Engineering and Medical?
answer: Special coaching is organized specifically for competencies required by professional institutions, conducted on Sundays, holidays, and during summer/winter vacations with expert-designed syllabi.

scheme_name: Centrally Sponsored Scheme of Upgradation of Merit of Scheduled Caste Students
question: Can students avail both remedial coaching and special coaching simultaneously under this educational merit enhancement program?
answer: There is no bar for any student to avail coaching for both purposes, allowing students to benefit from both remedial and special coaching simultaneously.

scheme_name: Centrally Sponsored Scheme of Upgradation of Merit of Scheduled Caste Students
question: What are the boarding and lodging arrangements provided to students enrolled in residential schools under this coaching scheme?
answer: Residential school students receive boarding and lodging charges of ₹900/- per month for 10 months totaling ₹9,000/- annually as part of their package grant.

scheme_name: Centrally Sponsored Scheme of Upgradation of Merit of Scheduled Caste Students
question: How many fresh students are covered annually under this centrally sponsored merit upgradation scheme for Scheduled Caste learners?
answer: A maximum of 2,050 fresh students are covered annually under the scheme, with implementation across 19 States and Union Territories.

scheme_name: Centrally Sponsored Scheme of Upgradation of Merit of Scheduled Caste Students
question: What provisions exist for students who need escort assistance due to severe physical disabilities in this educational support program?
answer: Severely handicapped day scholar students with lower extremity disability are eligible for escort allowance of ₹100/- per month to facilitate their participation in the coaching program.

scheme_name: Cancer Suraksha Scheme
question: What is the “Cancer Suraksha Scheme”?
answer: The Government of Kerala launched the "Cancer Suraksha Scheme" on 1st November 2008 for children below the age of 18 who suffer from cancer and belong to such families which are too poor to afford treatment

scheme_name: Cancer Suraksha Scheme
question: What is the objective of the scheme?
answer: Those patients found eligible would be registered under the scheme and a Patient Card would be issued. Registered patients would be provided treatment free of cost at the designated hospitals. On further verification, if it is found that any registered patient is ineligible for assistance, the assistance would be stopped forthwith.

scheme_name: Cancer Suraksha Scheme
question: Who is eligible to get the benefits under the scheme?
answer: Cancer patients up to the age of 18 years in the Below Poverty Line (BPL) groups are eligible to be included in this scheme.

scheme_name: Cancer Suraksha Scheme
question: Is this scheme only for Cancer patients?
answer: Yes, this scheme is only for Cancer patients.

scheme_name: Cancer Suraksha Scheme
question: Is this scheme only for the applicant belonging to Below Poverty Line (BPL) category?
answer: Yes, the applicants should belong to Below Poverty Line (BPL) category.

scheme_name: Cancer Suraksha Scheme
question: Is this scheme only for a resident of Kerala?
answer: Yes, the applicant should be a resident of Kerala State and the scheme is applicable only to patients from Kerala.

scheme_name: Cancer Suraksha Scheme
question: What is the age limit to apply under the scheme?
answer: The age limit of the applicant has to be 18 years or below.

scheme_name: Cancer Suraksha Scheme
question: Is a patient receiving free treatment in a government hospital eligible to apply under the scheme?
answer: No, the patient already receiving free treatment in government hospitals is not eligible.

scheme_name: Cancer Suraksha Scheme
question: Does the patient who has medical insurance eligible to apply under the scheme?
answer: No, those patients who avail of the pay ward facility and are eligible for medical reimbursement from other sources or have medical insurance are not eligible for this scheme.

scheme_name: Cancer Suraksha Scheme
question: What is the benefit of the scheme?
answer: Under this scheme, children under 18 years would be given free treatment for cancer through designated Government hospitals in the state.

scheme_name: Cancer Suraksha Scheme
question: Can the hospital incur additional expenditure?
answer: Yes, the hospital can incur additional expenditure, based on the report of the committee comprising the Oncologist/treating doctor, the Head of the Radiology Department, and the Superintendent, subject to ratification by the Mission.

scheme_name: Cancer Suraksha Scheme
question: How can an applicant avail of the benefits of the scheme?
answer: To avail of the benefits of the scheme, the applicant may contact the Scheme counselor who is appointed at selected hospitals/covered hospitals under this scheme or the concerned District Social Justice Officer.

scheme_name: Centrally Sponsored Scheme for Implementation of the Protection of Civil Rights Act, 1955 and the Scheduled Castes and the Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989
question: What is the funding pattern for states and union territories under this scheme?
answer: Special Courts are designated District Session Courts specified by State Governments with Chief Justice concurrence for speedy trial, with all participating states having designated such courts for handling cases under the Prevention of Atrocities Act.

scheme_name: Centrally Sponsored Scheme for Implementation of the Protection of Civil Rights Act, 1955 and the Scheduled Castes and the Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989
question: Can individuals from Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes communities who face discrimination or violence approach this program for support and rehabilitation?
answer: Yes, members of Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes who are victims of atrocities as defined under the respective Acts can receive relief and rehabilitation support through this centrally sponsored program.

scheme_name: Centrally Sponsored Scheme for Implementation of the Protection of Civil Rights Act, 1955 and the Scheduled Castes and the Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989
question: How many exclusive courts have been established across different states specifically for handling cases under the Prevention of Atrocities legislation?
answer: A total of 192 Exclusive Special Courts have been set up by thirteen States to ensure speedy trial of cases, with states like Madhya Pradesh having 43 courts, Uttar Pradesh having 40 courts, and Gujarat having 26 courts.

scheme_name: Centrally Sponsored Scheme for Implementation of the Protection of Civil Rights Act, 1955 and the Scheduled Castes and the Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989
question: What constitutional provision forms the basis for implementing these protective measures against untouchability and caste-based discrimination?
answer: Article 17 of the Constitution of India has abolished 'untouchability' and forbidden its practice in any form, which forms the constitutional basis for these protective Acts and their implementation.

scheme_name: Centrally Sponsored Scheme for Implementation of the Protection of Civil Rights Act, 1955 and the Scheduled Castes and the Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989
question: Are there any financial incentives available for couples who choose to marry across different caste boundaries, particularly involving scheduled communities?
answer: Yes, incentive amounts are provided for inter-caste marriages where one partner belongs to Scheduled Castes or Scheduled Tribes, with amounts ranging from ₹10,000 to ₹5,00,000 depending on the respective state government policies.

scheme_name: Centrally Sponsored Scheme for Implementation of the Protection of Civil Rights Act, 1955 and the Scheduled Castes and the Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989
question: Which government departments or agencies are responsible for the actual implementation of this centrally sponsored program at the ground level?
answer: The concerned State Governments and Union Territory Administrations are responsible for implementation, with applications processed through the Social Welfare Department of respective State Government or Union Territory.

scheme_name: Centrally Sponsored Scheme for Implementation of the Protection of Civil Rights Act, 1955 and the Scheduled Castes and the Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989
question: What types of institutional support mechanisms are strengthened through this central assistance program for protecting vulnerable communities?
answer: The program strengthens Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes Protection Cells, Special Police Stations, exclusive Special Courts, and implements awareness generation programs for comprehensive community protection.

scheme_name: Centrally Sponsored Scheme for Implementation of the Protection of Civil Rights Act, 1955 and the Scheduled Castes and the Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989
question: When did the merger of similar schemes take effect, requiring new applicants to apply through this centrally sponsored program instead?
answer: The merger took effect from 1st April 2023, after which all Inter Caste Marriage and Atrocity cases must apply through the procedures of Social Welfare Department of respective State Government or Union Territory.

scheme_name: Centrally Sponsored Scheme for Implementation of the Protection of Civil Rights Act, 1955 and the Scheduled Castes and the Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989
question: How is the monitoring and evaluation of this scheme's implementation carried out by the central government authorities?
answer: Monitoring is done through detailed performance formats for ascertaining physical and financial performance, officer visits to States and Union Territories, and discussions during conferences of Ministers and Secretaries of Social Welfare Departments.

scheme_name: Centrally Sponsored Scheme for Implementation of the Protection of Civil Rights Act, 1955 and the Scheduled Castes and the Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989
question: Which parliamentary Acts provide the legal framework and authority for implementing these protective and supportive measures for scheduled communities?
answer: The Protection of Civil Rights Act, 1955 and the Scheduled Castes and the Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989 provide the legal framework for implementation of protective measures.

scheme_name: Centrally Sponsored Scheme for Implementation of the Protection of Civil Rights Act, 1955 and the Scheduled Castes and the Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989
question: What role do Special Courts play in ensuring justice delivery under this program, and how are they established across different judicial districts?
answer: Special Courts are designated District Session Courts specified by State Governments with Chief Justice concurrence for speedy trial, with all participating states having designated such courts for handling cases under the Prevention of Atrocities Act.

scheme_name: Centrally Sponsored Scheme of Post-Matric Scholarship for OBC Students for studying in India
question: How does the scholarship program define the duration of awards, and how does this duration policy impact the recipients' education?
answer: The scholarship is awarded from the stage at which it is given until the completion of the course. This policy provides consistent support throughout the recipient's academic journey, encouraging them to pursue their education with dedication.

scheme_name: Centrally Sponsored Scheme of Post-Matric Scholarship for OBC Students for studying in India
question: What is the rationale behind transitioning to Smart Cards for the disbursal of scholarship amounts, and how does this benefit both the authorities and beneficiaries?
answer: The move to Smart Cards is aimed at ensuring efficient and secure disbursal of scholarship amounts. It reduces administrative complexities and ensures timely payments to beneficiaries while also offering them a more convenient and secure mode of receiving funds.

scheme_name: Centrally Sponsored Scheme of Post-Matric Scholarship for OBC Students for studying in India
question: Could you elaborate on the significance of providing financial support for thesis typing/printing charges to research scholars, and how this support aids in their academic pursuits?
answer: The provision for thesis typing/printing charges assists research scholars in the final stages of their academic journey. It helps cover essential expenses related to the preparation of their research work, ensuring a smooth and successful completion.

scheme_name: Centrally Sponsored Scheme of Post-Matric Scholarship for OBC Students for studying in India
question: The scholarship document mentions specific provisions regarding income calculation. Could you clarify how income is assessed when a student has one or both parents alive, and what happens if both parents have passed away?
answer: When either of the parents (or the husband in the case of married unemployed girl students) is alive, only their income should be considered, excluding the income of other family members, even if they are earning. However, when both parents (or the husband in the case of married but unemployed girl students) have passed away, the income of the guardian who is supporting the student in their studies should be considered. In cases where a student's parent's income is affected due to the death of one earning parent and falls within the income ceiling prescribed under the scheme, they become eligible for the scholarship, provided they meet other eligibility conditions. This applies from the month in which the parent's death occurred.

scheme_name: Centrally Sponsored Scheme of Post-Matric Scholarship for OBC Students for studying in India
question: Could you provide examples of situations where an applicant would be ineligible based on these exclusions?
answer: Certainly. Applicants would be ineligible if they are studying in the same stage of education in a different subject after passing one stage of education. Additionally, they would be ineligible if they have completed their educational career in one professional line, such as pursuing LLB after B.T/B. Ed. Furthermore, if they are studying in XI class of the Higher Secondary School courses or the XII class of the Multipurpose High School, they are ineligible, unless their tenth class examination is treated as equivalent to Matriculation, and they join other courses.

scheme_name: Centrally Sponsored Scheme of Post-Matric Scholarship for OBC Students for studying in India
question: I'd like to know more about the eligibility criteria for beneficiaries receiving coaching. What are the conditions that disqualify them from receiving a stipend?
answer: Scholarship holders receiving coaching with financial assistance from the Central Government or State Government are not eligible for a stipend under the coaching schemes for the duration of the coaching program.

scheme_name: Centrally Sponsored Scheme of Post-Matric Scholarship for OBC Students for studying in India
question: I'm considering pursuing correspondence courses. How does the scholarship apply to students studying through correspondence courses, and what expenses are covered?
answer: If you're pursuing studies through correspondence courses, you are eligible for reimbursement of non-refundable fees and an annual allowance of Rs. 900 for essential and prescribed books, as applicable.

scheme_name: Centrally Sponsored Scheme of Post-Matric Scholarship for OBC Students for studying in India
question: I noticed that students can accept free lodging, grants, or ad-hoc financial assistance from other sources in addition to the scholarship. Could you clarify the specific conditions for accepting these additional forms of support?
answer: Students are allowed to accept free lodging or a grant, along with ad-hoc monetary assistance from the State Government or any other source, for the purchase of books, equipment, or meeting board and lodging expenses, in addition to the scholarship amount paid under the Scheme. There are no restrictions on accepting these forms of support in conjunction with the scholarship.

scheme_name: Centrally Sponsored Scheme of Post-Matric Scholarship for OBC Students for studying in India
question: Can scholarship recipients hold other scholarships or stipends concurrently, and if not, how do they choose between them?
answer: Scholarship recipients cannot hold multiple scholarships or stipends simultaneously under this scheme. If they are awarded more than one scholarship or stipend, they must select the one that is more beneficial to them. The process for making this selection involves informing the awarding authority through the Head of the Institution. Once a scholarship is accepted, no further scholarships can be received.

scheme_name: Centrally Sponsored Scheme of Post-Matric Scholarship for OBC Students for studying in India
question: I'm curious about the eligibility for post-graduate courses in medicine. Could you elaborate on the condition related to practicing during the course?
answer: Eligibility for pursuing post-graduate courses in medicine under this scholarship is contingent on the student not being allowed to practice during the period of their course. This condition is essential for determining their eligibility.

scheme_name: Centrally Sponsored Scheme of Post-Matric Scholarship for OBC Students for studying in India
question: Can you explain the income criteria for unemployed applicants, specifically regarding their parents or guardians' income?
answer: Unemployed applicants are eligible if their parents or guardians' income from all sources does not exceed Rs. 1.50 lakh per annum. This income threshold is vital in determining their eligibility for the scholarship.

scheme_name: Centrally Sponsored Scheme of Post-Matric Scholarship for OBC Students for studying in India
question: I'd like to understand the financial aspects of eligibility. How is the income of employed applicants and their parents or guardians assessed?
answer: Employed applicants and their eligibility are linked to income. They can be eligible if the combined income of both the applicant and their parents or guardians does not exceed Rs. 1.50 lakh per annum. This income assessment is a crucial factor in determining eligibility.

scheme_name: Centrally Sponsored Scheme of Post-Matric Scholarship for OBC Students for studying in India
question: I'm curious about the study tour charges. What are the conditions under which study tour charges are paid, and what is the maximum amount allowed?
answer: Study tour charges are paid to scholars studying professional and technical courses when the head of the institution certifies that the study tour is essential for the scholar to complete their course of study. The maximum amount allowed for study tour charges is up to Rs. 900 per annum, limited to the actual expenditure incurred by the student on transportation and related expenses during the study tour.

scheme_name: Centrally Sponsored Scheme of Post-Matric Scholarship for OBC Students for studying in India
question: The document mentions that certain fees are covered by the scholarship. Can you provide examples of the types of fees that are considered and those that are excluded?
answer: The scholarship covers fees such as enrolment/registration, tuition, games, union, library, magazine, medical examination, and other fees that are compulsory for the scholar to pay to the institution or University/Board. However, fees that are refundable, such as caution money and security deposit, are excluded.

scheme_name: Centrally Sponsored Scheme of Pre-matric Scholarship to Other Backward Classes (OBC) for Studies in India
question: What is the main objective of the Pre-Matric Scholarship for OBCs?
answer: The primary objective of the scheme is to address the low literacy levels, particularly among backward classes, by providing education and economic support to children belonging to OBCs.

scheme_name: Centrally Sponsored Scheme of Pre-matric Scholarship to Other Backward Classes (OBC) for Studies in India
question: How is the income of the parents or guardians calculated for scholarship eligibility?
answer: He income of either of the parents (or husband in the case of a married unemployed girl student) is considered, and no other family members' income is taken into account unless both parents (or husband) have passed away.

scheme_name: Centrally Sponsored Scheme of Pre-matric Scholarship to Other Backward Classes (OBC) for Studies in India
question: What happens if a student's parent's income is affected due to the death of one earning parent?
answer: In such cases, if a student's family income falls within the income ceiling, the student becomes eligible for the scholarship from the month in which the unfortunate death occurred.

scheme_name: Centrally Sponsored Scheme of Pre-matric Scholarship to Other Backward Classes (OBC) for Studies in India
question: Are there any exemptions for specific sources of income in the calculation of scholarship eligibility?
answer: House Rent Allowance received by parents is exempted from income calculations for scholarship eligibility if permitted for Income-Tax purposes.

scheme_name: Centrally Sponsored Scheme of Pre-matric Scholarship to Other Backward Classes (OBC) for Studies in India
question: How often is the income certificate required for scholarship eligibility?
answer: An income certificate is required only once, at the time of admission to courses that last for more than one year.

scheme_name: Centrally Sponsored Scheme of Pre-matric Scholarship to Other Backward Classes (OBC) for Studies in India
question: At which academic levels are the scholarships available, and for how long?
answer: Scholarships are available for students enrolled in pre-matric classes, specifically from class I to class X. The scholarship covers a duration of 10 months in an academic year.

scheme_name: Centrally Sponsored Scheme of Pre-matric Scholarship to Other Backward Classes (OBC) for Studies in India
question: In which institutions is the scholarship tenable?
answer: The scholarship is tenable only in institutions and pre-matriculation courses recognized by the respective State Governments and Union Territory Administrations.

scheme_name: Centrally Sponsored Scheme of Pre-matric Scholarship to Other Backward Classes (OBC) for Studies in India
question: Can scholarship recipients avail benefits from other pre-matric scholarship schemes?
answer: No, scholarship recipients under this scheme are not allowed to avail benefits under any other pre-matric scholarship scheme.

scheme_name: Centrally Sponsored Scheme of Pre-matric Scholarship to Other Backward Classes (OBC) for Studies in India
question: What is the reserved quota for students with disabilities under this scheme?
answer: At least 5% of the beneficiaries should be students with disabilities.

scheme_name: Centrally Sponsored Scheme of Pre-matric Scholarship to Other Backward Classes (OBC) for Studies in India
question: Is Aadhar seeding of bank accounts necessary for beneficiaries?
answer: Yes, to avoid duplication, bank accounts of the target beneficiaries should be Aadhar seeded.

scheme_name: Centrally Sponsored Scheme of Pre-matric Scholarship to Other Backward Classes (OBC) for Studies in India
question: What percentage of the scholarship beneficiaries are reserved for girl students?
answer: 30% of the beneficiaries are reserved for girl students.

scheme_name: Centrally Sponsored Scheme of Pre-matric Scholarship to Other Backward Classes (OBC) for Studies in India
question: How is the scholarship renewed for the next academic year?
answer: The scholarship may be renewed for the next academic year by the concerned State Government or Union Territory Administration, unless the competent school authority recommends discontinuation.

scheme_name: Centrally Sponsored Scheme of Pre-matric Scholarship to Other Backward Classes (OBC) for Studies in India
question: Is the Pre-Matric Scholarship Scheme a 'funds-limited' scheme?
answer: Yes, the scheme is 'funds-limited,' and the budget allocated is apportioned to States on a pro-rata basis.

scheme_name: Centrally Sponsored Scheme of Pre-matric Scholarship to Other Backward Classes (OBC) for Studies in India
question: What is the role of States/UTs in managing the financial aspects of the scheme?
answer: States/UTs are expected to incur expenditure under the scheme to at least the sum total of "Central Assistance or NA and matching State share" and should limit the number of scholarships accordingly.

scheme_name: COP-37 (General Area) 50% Capital Subsidy Scheme for Project of Taluka & District Co-op. Purchase Sale Union
question: What is the main objective of the "COP-37 (General Area) 50% Capital Subsidy Scheme for Project of Taluka & District Co-op. Purchase Sale Union"?
answer: The main objective of the "COP-37 (General Area) 50% Capital Subsidy Scheme for Project of Taluka & District Co-op. Purchase Sale Union" is to financially strengthen Taluka and District-level cooperative purchase and sale unions by offering capital subsidies to develop infrastructure and services that support agricultural procurement, processing, storage, and marketing, thereby enabling better quality services and financial benefits for farmers.

scheme_name: COP-37 (General Area) 50% Capital Subsidy Scheme for Project of Taluka & District Co-op. Purchase Sale Union
question: Who is eligible to apply for assistance under the "COP-37 (General Area) 50% Capital Subsidy Scheme"?
answer: Taluka and District Co-operative Purchase and Sale Unions located within the state of Gujarat that possess ownership of the land intended for project development are eligible to apply for financial assistance under the Scheme.

scheme_name: COP-37 (General Area) 50% Capital Subsidy Scheme for Project of Taluka & District Co-op. Purchase Sale Union
question: What percentage of the project cost is covered under the subsidy?
answer: Under the scheme, 50% of the total cost of an eligible project is covered as capital subsidy, subject to a maximum limit of ₹20,00,000.

scheme_name: COP-37 (General Area) 50% Capital Subsidy Scheme for Project of Taluka & District Co-op. Purchase Sale Union
question: Is there a cap on the maximum financial assistance that can be availed under the scheme?
answer: Yes, the maximum financial assistance that can be availed under the "COP-37 (General Area) 50% Capital Subsidy Scheme for Project of Taluka & District Co-op. Purchase Sale Union" is ₹20,00,000 per project, even if the total project cost exceeds this amount.

scheme_name: COP-37 (General Area) 50% Capital Subsidy Scheme for Project of Taluka & District Co-op. Purchase Sale Union
question: What kinds of projects qualify for financial assistance under this scheme?
answer: Projects related to agricultural procurement, processing, grading, cleaning, washing, shorting, packaging, branding, storage godowns, and marketing infrastructure are considered eligible for financial assistance.

scheme_name: COP-37 (General Area) 50% Capital Subsidy Scheme for Project of Taluka & District Co-op. Purchase Sale Union
question: Is the subsidy provided in one lump sum or in phases?
answer: The financial assistance is not disbursed in a single lump sum but is released in phases based on the completion of work and verification by the concerned authorities.

scheme_name: COP-37 (General Area) 50% Capital Subsidy Scheme for Project of Taluka & District Co-op. Purchase Sale Union
question: Which authority is responsible for implementing and monitoring this scheme?
answer: The scheme is implemented and monitored by the Registrar of Co-operative Societies, Gujarat State, Gandhinagar, in coordination with the Deputy Directors and District Registrars of Co-operative Societies of the respective districts.

scheme_name: COP-37 (General Area) 50% Capital Subsidy Scheme for Project of Taluka & District Co-op. Purchase Sale Union
question: Is land ownership a mandatory condition for eligibility under the scheme?
answer: Yes, it is mandatory for the applicant cooperative union to own the land on which the project is proposed in order to be eligible for financial assistance.

scheme_name: COP-37 (General Area) 50% Capital Subsidy Scheme for Project of Taluka & District Co-op. Purchase Sale Union
question: How can an eligible cooperative union apply under the scheme?
answer: The eligible union must prepare a detailed project proposal and submit it through the District Registrar and Deputy Director of Co-operative Societies to the Registrar of Co-operative Societies, who forwards the proposal to the Department of Agriculture, Farmers Welfare and Co-operation for final approval.

scheme_name: COP-37 (General Area) 50% Capital Subsidy Scheme for Project of Taluka & District Co-op. Purchase Sale Union
question: Where can applicants get more information or assistance related to the scheme?
answer: Applicants can contact their respective District Registrar Co-operative Societies or approach the Registrar of Co-operative Societies, Gujarat State, Gandhinagar, for more information, guidance, and clarification regarding the application process and documentation.

scheme_name: Central Sector Scheme for Rehabilitation of Bonded Labourer
question: How frequently can a State/UT Government conduct surveys of bonded laborers, and what is the financial assistance available for this purpose?
answer: A State/UT Government can conduct surveys once every three years per sensitive district, with financial assistance of Rs. 4.50 lakh per district.

scheme_name: Central Sector Scheme for Rehabilitation of Bonded Labourer
question: How are funds released for the scheme, and what are the modalities for fund transfer?
answer: Funds are released by the Ministry of Labour and Employment directly to the State/UT Government, which then transfers the funds to the concerned District Magistrate/Collector for the purpose of the Bonded Labourer Rehabilitation Scheme.

scheme_name: Central Sector Scheme for Rehabilitation of Bonded Labourer
question: How do District Magistrates/Administrations submit proposals for financial demands to the Central Government?
answer: District Magistrates/Administrations send proposals to the concerned State Ministry/Department responsible for the Bonded Labour Rehabilitation Scheme, which, in turn, scrutinizes and submits the proposal to the Central Government.

scheme_name: Central Sector Scheme for Rehabilitation of Bonded Labourer
question: What is the financial assistance available for evaluatory studies, and how does it work?
answer: States can conduct up to five evaluatory studies per year for eradicating bonded labor, with financial assistance of Rs. 1.5 lakh for each study. The Central Government provides 50% of the required amount in advance.

scheme_name: Central Sector Scheme for Rehabilitation of Bonded Labourer
question: How is awareness generated for the eradication of bonded labor, and what financial assistance is available for this purpose?
answer: States can conduct awareness generation programs, and financial assistance for this purpose is reimbursed on a case-to-case basis, subject to a maximum limit of Rs. Ten lakh per State/UT per annum.

scheme_name: Central Sector Scheme for Rehabilitation of Bonded Labourer
question: Can you explain the process of conducting a survey of bonded laborers and the financial assistance provided for it?
answer: States may conduct a survey of bonded laborers once every three years per sensitive district, with a financial assistance of Rs. 4.50 lakh per district. This amount can be used to finance the efforts of NGOs in identifying bonded laborers.

scheme_name: Central Sector Scheme for Rehabilitation of Bonded Labourer
question: How does the scheme ensure that the benefits provided are in addition to any other cash or non-cash benefits that a beneficiary might be entitled to from other schemes or laws?
answer: The scheme explicitly states that the benefits it offers are supplementary to any other benefits that a beneficiary may be entitled to under other existing schemes or laws.

scheme_name: Central Sector Scheme for Rehabilitation of Bonded Labourer
question: What role does the scheme play in employable skill development for adult bonded laborers?
answer: Employable skill development training is a compulsory element of rehabilitation for adult bonded laborers who do not fall into special beneficiary categories.

scheme_name: Central Sector Scheme for Rehabilitation of Bonded Labourer
question: Could you clarify the components of assistance for female freed bonded laborers?
answer: The State Government provides financial assistance for marriage and other capacity-building measures for female freed bonded laborers.

scheme_name: Central Sector Scheme for Rehabilitation of Bonded Labourer
question: How does the scheme address the capacity building of child bonded laborers?
answer: The District Administration, in a convergence approach, ensures proper education, psycho-social counseling, short stay homes for education up to class 12th, and skill development as part of the rehabilitation package for child bonded laborers.

scheme_name: Central Sector Scheme for Rehabilitation of Bonded Labourer
question: What is the maximum amount of immediate financial assistance that can be provided to a rescued person from the District Bonded Labour Rehabilitation Fund?
answer: The District Administration can provide immediate financial assistance up to Rs. 30,000, with the possibility of higher amounts if justified, subject to the maximum entitlement under the scheme.

scheme_name: Central Sector Scheme for Rehabilitation of Bonded Labourer
question: What measures are taken for the immediate care and protection of rescued persons during the summary trial?
answer: The scheme allows for immediate assistance, including lodging, medical aid, legal support, and victim/witness protection, provided under other laws or schemes, regardless of the entitlements prescribed under this scheme.

scheme_name: Central Sector Scheme for Rehabilitation of Bonded Labourer
question: How does the scheme address situations where individuals are not in a condition of bondage but still require socio-economic assistance?
answer: When individuals are not in a condition of bondage but require socio-economic assistance, the District Magistrate may provide state assistance under other relevant schemes administered by them.

scheme_name: Central Sector Scheme for Rehabilitation of Bonded Labourer
question: Could you elaborate on the circumstances under which the rehabilitation assistance is set at Rs. Three lakhs?
answer: In cases involving extreme deprivation or marginalization, such as trans-genders, women or children rescued from sexual exploitation, the rehabilitation assistance is set at Rs. Three lakhs, with a significant portion placed in an annuity scheme.

scheme_name: Pradhan Mantri Uchchatar Shiksha Protsahan (PM-USP) Central Sector Scheme of Scholarship for College and University students
question: What is the methodology adopted for generating merit list for selecting the beneficiaries under the scheme?
answer: From the eligible applicants, merit list is drawn based on gender (50 boys: 50 girls), stream (3-Science: 1-Commerce: 3-Humanities), Category (SC-15 %, ST-7.5 % and OBC-27 %), and 5 % horizontal reservation is provided for students with Benchmark Disabilities (Disability of 40% or more) from the allocated slots of respective State Education Boards. In case of shortfall in the number of applications, the scholarship slots shall be interoperable among categories (Gen, OBC, SC & ST), gender (Female, Male) and State Quota to maximize use of slots for fresh scholarships with effect from academic year 2022-23, subject to the condition that guidelines of Ministry of Finance and NITI Aayog regarding SC/ST fund allocation of the schemes are adhered to.

scheme_name: Pradhan Mantri Uchchatar Shiksha Protsahan (PM-USP) Central Sector Scheme of Scholarship for College and University students
question: What is the rate of scholarship under the scheme?
answer: The rate of scholarship is Rs. 12,000/- per annum at Graduation level for first three years of College and University courses and Rs. 20,000/- per annum at Post-Graduation level. Students pursuing technical courses are paid Rs. 20,000/- per annum in the 4th and 5th year. Students pursing B.Tech/ BE would get scholarship for 4 years only i.e Rs. 12000 per annum for first three years and Rs. 20,000 per annum in the 4th year.

scheme_name: Pradhan Mantri Uchchatar Shiksha Protsahan (PM-USP) Central Sector Scheme of Scholarship for College and University students
question: What is the duration of scholarships and criteria for renewal under the scheme?
answer: A student will be eligible for the scholarship for a total duration not exceeding 5 years. A scholarship under the scheme is renewable on year-to-year basis up to Post Graduate level (except for the students pursuing technical courses leading to degree at graduation level). Student must secure at least 50% marks and maintain adequate attendance of at least 75%.

scheme_name: Pradhan Mantri Uchchatar Shiksha Protsahan (PM-USP) Central Sector Scheme of Scholarship for College and University students
question: What is the methodology for disbursement of scholarship under the scheme?
answer: Scholarship is disbursed through Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT) mode i.e. directly into the bank accounts of the beneficiary. The scholarship amount will be disbursed in the Aadhaar Seeded Bank Account. To have seamless disbursal of scholarships, students are required to seed the Aadhaar with the bank account as mentioned in the application form. The student can track his/her payment status from the template “Know Your Payment” in the Public Financial Management System (PFMS) portal and can also check status on NSP with their login credentials. If the PFMS status is shown as “Success”, then the student is required to check the status of the bank account which was seeded with Aadhaar at the time of transaction.
