question: Can A Person Who Is Domiciled In Madhya Pradesh Also Apply To This Scheme?
answer: No, this scheme is open to applicants who are domiciled in the state of Jharkhand.

scheme_name: Chikitsa Sahayata Yojana
question: Is It Mandatory For The Applicant To Be A Registered Construction Worker (Nirman Shramik) In Order To Be Eligible To Apply?
answer: Yes, in order to be eligible to apply, the applicant should be a Registered Construction Worker (Nirman Shramik).

scheme_name: Chikitsa Sahayata Yojana
question: Where Can I Find The Link To The User Manual Of The Application Process?
answer: The User Manual of the Application Process can be found at this link - https://shramadhan.jharkhand.gov.in/ftp/WebAdmin/documents/BOC_SCHEME_BENEFIT_APPLICANT_SIDE.pdf

scheme_name: Chikitsa Sahayata Yojana
question: What Is The Full Form Of JBOCWWB?
answer: Jharkhand Building and Other Construction Worker Welfare Board (JBOCWW Board).

scheme_name: Chikitsa Sahayata Yojana
question: What Shall Be The Rate Of Payment Of Wages?
answer: Payment of minimum wages at the prescribed rate for unskilled category workers.

scheme_name: Chikitsa Sahayata Yojana
question: For How Many Days Will The Payment Be Paid?
answer: Payment is equivalent to a maximum of 40 working days.

scheme_name: Children's Tiatr Competition
question: What is the maximum age limit for child performers who want to participate in this theatrical competition?
answer: All child performers must be aged up to 16 years on the date fixed for submission of application.

scheme_name: Children's Tiatr Competition
question: How much refundable security deposit do we need to submit along with our application for participation?
answer: You must submit a refundable security deposit of ₹3,000/- in the form of cash or a Demand Draft in favour of Member Secretary, Tiatr Academy of Goa payable at Panaji.

scheme_name: Children's Tiatr Competition
question: What specific format requirements must our theatrical production follow to be considered for this competition?
answer: Your Tiatr must have 6 to 7 acts (podd'dde) with at least 4 cantos, comedy linked to the story, and at least 8 Kantaram including specified interactive components.

scheme_name: Children's Tiatr Competition
question: Can we stage our script at other venues before participating in this competition organized by the Academy?
answer: Not more than 2 shows of the given script must have been performed prior to the performance at the competition.

scheme_name: Children's Tiatr Competition
question: What type of themes are acceptable for our theatrical production in this children-focused competition?
answer: Themes of Tiatr should be compulsorily based on the lives of children only, and scripts having no relevance to children's lives will not be considered.

scheme_name: Children's Tiatr Competition
question: How many Educational Institutions, Sports and Cultural Associations, or Individual Producers can participate in this annual competition?
answer: 15 Educational Institutions, Sports and Cultural Associations, or Individual Producers will be given an opportunity to participate in the production and staging.

scheme_name: Children's Tiatr Competition
question: What happens if we withdraw from the competition after the schedule has been finalized by the organizing authority?
answer: If any applicant withdraws after the schedule is drawn by Tiatr Academy of Goa, their full security deposit will stand forfeited.

scheme_name: Children's Tiatr Competition
question: What is the minimum and maximum duration requirement for our theatrical performance including the interval period?
answer: The duration should not be less than one hour and a half and not more than two hours and a half, including an interval of minimum 10 minutes and maximum 15 minutes.

scheme_name: Children's Tiatr Competition
question: When do we need to submit the final typed copy of our script and songs before the competition begins?
answer: The final typed copy of the script and songs (kantaram) must be submitted during office hours 3 days before the date of commencement of the competition.

scheme_name: Children's Tiatr Competition
question: What documents do we need to provide to prove the age of all our child performers for eligibility verification?
answer: You must submit self-attested copies of Birth or Baptism Certificates, or a certificate by the Headmaster or Headmistress of a recognized school certifying the birth date.

scheme_name: Children's Tiatr Competition
question: How will the selection process work if more than the allowed number of applications are received for participation?
answer: If more than 15 applications are received, a meeting will be called and the selection of remaining 12 troupes will be done by lots.

scheme_name: Children's Tiatr Competition
question: What specific interactive musical components must be included in our theatrical production according to the competition guidelines?
answer: Your production must include at least 8 Kantaram with 1 duet (Interactive), 1 Duo (Interactive), 1 Trio (Interactive), 1 Quartet or Quintet (Interactive), 1 Choral Song and Solos.

scheme_name: Children's Tiatr Competition
question: Are there any restrictions on the content we can include in our scripts, lyrics, or performances during the competition?
answer: There should not be any adverse remarks against any Governments, Individuals, Institutions or anything against caste, creed and religion that may hurt anyone's sentiments.

scheme_name: Children's Tiatr Competition
question: Can our technical crew members and musicians work with multiple participating groups in the same competition?
answer: Artistes including technicians and backstage artistes can participate only under one troupe, but musicians can take part in more than one troupe.

scheme_name: Consortia & Tender Marketing Scheme
question: What is Consortia & Tender Marketing Scheme?
answer: Micro & Small Enterprise in their Individual Capacity faces problems to procure and execute large order, which inhibit and restrict their growth. NSIC accordingly, adopts Consortia approach and forms consortia of units manufacturing the same products, thereby easing out marketing problems of MSEs.

scheme_name: Consortia & Tender Marketing Scheme
question: What is the minimum size of a consortia?
answer: Minimum two number of MSEs.

scheme_name: Consortia & Tender Marketing Scheme
question: Whether pre-inspection of the unit is mandatory?
answer: Yes, to physically verify the MSEs who wants to supply their goods/services are in production and have the infrastructure to execute the tender in which they want to supply their goods/services.

scheme_name: Consortia & Tender Marketing Scheme
question: Whether commitment of the consortia leader with NSIC will be binding on the consortium members?
answer: Yes, Consortium leader so elected would be empowered to interact with NSIC office for participation in tenders and related matters.

scheme_name: Consortia & Tender Marketing Scheme
question: Whether Security Deposit is exempted under Public Procurement Policy?
answer: After issuing of Public Procurement Order 2012 for MSEs, the Security Deposit has been abolished.

scheme_name: Consortia & Tender Marketing Scheme
question: What is the provision if Security Deposit/Performance Bank Guarantee, deposited by NSIC?
answer: The participating MSEs will provide either Back-to-Back Bank Guarantee or deposit 100% value of Security Deposit for the period of which Bank Guarantee given by NSIC to the Buying Department.

scheme_name: Consortia & Tender Marketing Scheme
question: Whether all the consortia members shall be jointly and severally responsible for penalty / damage or only defaulted unit?
answer: Yes.

scheme_name: Consortia & Tender Marketing Scheme
question: How much %age of the Monetary Limit under SPRS will be fixed for limit under Consortia & Tender Marketing Scheme?
answer: 300% of the monetary limit fixed for the unit under the Single Point Registration Scheme. While participating in a tender as consortia, the overall limit to be fixed for units operating as a consortium, the limits fixed in respect of individual units, shall be clubbed.

scheme_name: Consortia & Tender Marketing Scheme
question: What is the validity period of monetary limit fixed under Consortia & Tender Marketing Scheme?
answer: The limit fixed shall remain valid for a year and is subject to review/ renewal annually.

scheme_name: Consortia & Tender Marketing Scheme
question: Who will bear the charges while participating in the tender under Consortia & Tender Marketing?
answer: All the charges for Bank Guarantee, Security Deposit, Performance Bank Guarantee etc. will be borne by the unit.

scheme_name: Consortia & Tender Marketing Scheme
question: Whether NSIC finance under Consortia & Tender Marketing?
answer: Yes. MSEs willing to avail financial assistance for the supplies against each tender made by them can apply under the Bill Discounting Scheme of the Corporation.

scheme_name: Consortia & Tender Marketing Scheme
question: What is the minimum percentage for overall procurement of Central Govt. Department/PSUs from MSEs?
answer: Every Central Ministries / Departments / PSUs shall set an annual goal of minimum 20% of the total annual purchases of the products or services produced or rendered by MSEs.

scheme_name: Consortia & Tender Marketing Scheme
question: How much percentage is earmarked for MSEs owned by SC/ST under Public Procurement Policy?
answer: Out of annual requirement of 20% procurement from MSEs, 4% is earmarked for units owned by Scheduled Castes / Scheduled Tribes.

scheme_name: Consortia & Tender Marketing Scheme
question: Whether Public Procurement Policy allow purchases through NSIC under consortia?
answer: Yes. As per Public Procurement Order 2012 for MSEs which is mandatory from 2015, annual goal of procurement also includes consortia of MSEs formed by NSIC.

scheme_name: Consortia & Tender Marketing Scheme
question: How many item are reserved for under Public Procurement Policy?
answer: 358 items.

scheme_name: Consortia & Tender Marketing Scheme
question: Whether medium enterprises are eligible to avail the benefits under Public Procurement Policy?
answer: No.

scheme_name: Consortia & Tender Marketing Scheme
question: What is the price preference (price band) available to MSEs under Public Procurement Policy?
answer: In tender participation, MSEs quoting price within the price band of L1+15 percent shall also be allowed to supply a portion up to 20% of requirement by bringing down their price to L1 price where L1 is non MSEs.

scheme_name: Consortia & Tender Marketing Scheme
question: What action can be taken by NSIC in case of default?
answer: The enlistment certificate under the Tender Marketing Scheme can be revoked in case the unit failed to supply/comply order including specification, size, quantity, quality and/or wrong delivery, non delivery, short-delivery, delayed delivery, defective delivery etc. of goods/services.

scheme_name: Craftsman Training Scheme - Maharashtra
question: Who is eligible for this stipend?
answer: All trainees belonging to various categories such as SC, ST, OBC, and economically weaker sections with a family income of up to [?]8,00,000/- per annum are eligible.

scheme_name: Craftsman Training Scheme - Maharashtra
question: What is the minimum attendance required to receive the stipend?
answer: A minimum of 80% attendance is required for each three-month period.

scheme_name: Craftsman Training Scheme - Maharashtra
question: Is this benefit available to all trainees in ITIs?
answer: Yes, the benefit is available to all eligible trainees under the Craftsman Training Scheme at Government ITIs.

scheme_name: Craftsman Training Scheme - Maharashtra
question: Can this stipend be availed by more than two children from the same family?
answer: No, the benefit is limited to two children per family.

scheme_name: Craftsman Training Scheme - Maharashtra
question: How can a trainee apply for the stipend?
answer: Trainees can apply through the MahaDBT portal by registering, filling out the application form, and submitting the required documents.

scheme_name: Craftsman Training Scheme - Maharashtra
question: What is the process for the disbursement of the stipend?
answer: The stipend will be disbursed quarterly into the trainee's Aadhaar-linked bank account after verification.

scheme_name: Craftsman Training Scheme - Maharashtra
question: What happens if a trainee does not maintain the required attendance?
answer: Trainees who do not maintain the required attendance or are disqualified for other reasons will not receive the stipend for that period.

scheme_name: Craftsman Training Scheme - Maharashtra
question: How will trainees know if their stipend has been approved?
answer: Trainees will receive a notification on the MahaDBT portal regarding the approval and disbursal status of their stipend.

scheme_name: Craftsman Training Scheme - Maharashtra
question: What is the deadline to apply for the stipend each academic year?
answer: The deadline will be announced by the Directorate of Vocational Education and Training. Trainees should regularly check the MahaDBT portal for updates.

scheme_name: Craftsman Training Scheme - Maharashtra
question: Can trainees from private ITIs apply for this stipend?
answer: No, the stipend is only for trainees enrolled in Government ITIs under the Artisan Training Scheme.

scheme_name: Craftsman Training Scheme - Maharashtra
question: Will the stipend amount be revised in the future?
answer: The stipend amount may be revised based on government decisions and policy changes.

scheme_name: Craftsmen Training Scheme
question: What are the minimum educational qualifications I need to have completed before I can apply for training in different trades?
answer: You must have completed minimum educational qualifications as prescribed for specific trades, which typically range from 8th standard to 12th standard depending on the particular trade you wish to pursue.

scheme_name: Craftsmen Training Scheme
question: Do I need to demonstrate any special abilities or skills for certain trades before I can get admitted to the training program?
answer: Yes, you must demonstrate basic aptitude for your chosen trade, and certain trades have specific requirements such as color vision testing for electrical trades.

scheme_name: Craftsmen Training Scheme
question: What happens if I miss too many training sessions during my vocational training period and my attendance falls below the required threshold?
answer: You need to maintain minimum 80% attendance throughout your training to be eligible to appear in the Final Trade Test, so poor attendance will disqualify you from certification.

scheme_name: Craftsmen Training Scheme
question: How long will I need to dedicate to complete the entire vocational training program from start to finish?
answer: Training duration varies from 6 months to 2 years depending on the specific trade you choose to pursue.

scheme_name: Craftsmen Training Scheme
question: What language proficiency do I need to have to successfully participate in the training program and understand the course materials?
answer: You must be able to read and write in either the local language, Hindi, or English to effectively participate in the training program.

scheme_name: Craftsmen Training Scheme
question: Are there any physical health conditions or disabilities that would prevent me from being accepted into the training program?
answer: You must be physically and medically fit to undergo the specific trade training and must not have any physical disabilities that would prevent you from performing the trade activities.

scheme_name: Craftsmen Training Scheme
question: What is the age range within which I must fall to be eligible for admission to the vocational training program?
answer: You must meet the age requirements specified for different trades, which generally fall between 14 to 40 years of age.

scheme_name: Craftsmen Training Scheme
question: What kind of certificate will I receive after successfully completing my vocational training and passing all required examinations?
answer: You will receive a National Council for Vocational Training certificate upon successful completion, which is recognized across India for employment purposes.

scheme_name: Craftsmen Training Scheme
question: Do I need to be an Indian citizen to apply for this vocational training program, or can foreign nationals also participate?
answer: You must be an Indian citizen to be eligible for this training program and must provide valid proof of residence.

scheme_name: Craftsmen Training Scheme
question: What type of medical documentation do I need to submit to prove that I am fit for the physical demands of my chosen trade?
answer: You must submit a Medical Fitness Certificate issued by a Registered Medical Practitioner to demonstrate your fitness for the specific trade training.

scheme_name: Craftsmen Training Scheme
question: How can I obtain the official application form and where should I go to start the application process for the training program?
answer: You must visit the Industrial Training Institute where you wish to train and obtain the prescribed application form from there.

scheme_name: Craftsmen Training Scheme
question: What types of identity and educational documents do I need to gather and submit along with my completed application form?
answer: You need to submit educational certificates, age proof certificate, Aadhaar card copy, passport size photographs, and if applicable, caste certificate and income certificate for fee concessions.

scheme_name: Craftsmen Training Scheme
question: When do the application deadlines typically occur throughout the year and how much advance notice is usually given to prospective applicants?
answer: Application deadlines vary by institute and are typically announced before each academic session, usually during April-May for August session and October-November for February session.

scheme_name: Craftsmen Training Scheme
question: What should I do immediately after submitting my application to ensure I have proper proof of my application submission?
answer: You must request a receipt or acknowledgement from the concerned authority containing essential details such as date, time of submission, and unique identification number if applicable.

scheme_name: Computer Training Scheme
question: What is Computer Training Scheme ?
answer: The scheme is being operated with the objective to provide better chances of employment to the youth by enhancing their skills.

scheme_name: Computer Training Scheme
question: Who are the beneficiaries ?
answer: All Unemployed youth who full fill the eligibility criteria.

scheme_name: Computer Training Scheme
question: What is the education qualification criteria ?
answer: Youth who passed the Intermediate examination (10+2).

scheme_name: Computer Training Scheme
question: What Is The annual income eligibility Criteria ?
answer: The annual income of parents/guardians should be up to Rs. 1,00,000/- or less.

scheme_name: Computer Training Scheme
question: What is the application process ?
answer: - Youth have to visit official web portal. | - Complete the registration process. | - Full fill the application form. | - Submit.

scheme_name: Computer Training Scheme
question: What benefits are provided under this scheme ?
answer: Computer training program.

scheme_name: Computer Training Scheme
question: How many training program are offered ?
answer: Two training programs are offered. | - For 'O' computer training. | - For 'CCC' computer training.

scheme_name: Computer Training Scheme
question: Do the trainee need to pay fee to the institute ?
answer: Students need not pay any fee to the institute on account of registration and training. The examination fee for any examination conducted by the NIELIT (National Institute of Electronics and Information Technology), will have to pay by the trainee to 'NIELIT' in online mode.

scheme_name: Computer Training Scheme
question: How much attendance is Compulsory during training ?
answer: 75% biometric attendance of trainees will be compulsory during the training session.

scheme_name: Computer Training Scheme
question: May trainee get the scheme benefits again ?
answer: No, only at once.

scheme_name: Computer Training Scheme for Visually Impaired Persons
question: Who is eligible for the scheme?
answer: Individuals who are residents of Madhya Pradesh with 40% or more visual impairment, belong to BPL households, and have passed Class 8 with at least 50% marks.

scheme_name: Computer Training Scheme for Visually Impaired Persons
question: How many times can a person receive training under this scheme?
answer: Only once. The scheme provides a one-time benefit.

scheme_name: Computer Training Scheme for Visually Impaired Persons
question: What is the duration of the training program?
answer: The training lasts two months.

scheme_name: Computer Training Scheme for Visually Impaired Persons
question: Is a laptop provided to trainees?
answer: Yes, a laptop is provided after successful completion of training.

scheme_name: Computer Training Scheme for Visually Impaired Persons
question: Where is the training conducted?
answer: Training is conducted in seven divisions: Bhopal, Indore, Jabalpur, Gwalior, Sagar, Rewa, and Ujjain.

scheme_name: Computer Training Scheme for Visually Impaired Persons
question: Is there any monetary assistance given directly to the beneficiary?
answer: No, all benefits are provided in kind.

scheme_name: Computer Training Scheme for Visually Impaired Persons
question: What software will be used during training?
answer: NBTR screen-reading software will be used to assist visually impaired trainees.

scheme_name: Computer Training Scheme for Visually Impaired Persons
question: Is internet connectivity available during training?
answer: Yes, 4G internet connectivity is provided at each center.

scheme_name: Computer Training Scheme for Visually Impaired Persons
question: What documents are needed to apply?
answer: Applicants must submit the Class 8th Marksheet, Disability Certificate (40% or more visual impairment issued by Medical Board), Domicile Certificate, Proof of Residential Address (Electricity Bill, Ration Card, Voter ID, etc.), Below Poverty Line (BPL) Certificate, Aadhaar Card, Samagra ID, etc.

scheme_name: Computer Training Scheme for Visually Impaired Persons
question: Can an applicant from another state apply?
answer: No, only permanent residents of Madhya Pradesh are eligible.

scheme_name: Coir Udyami Yojana
question: Is there any age limit to apply under Coir Udyami Yojana?
answer: The applicant must be at least 18 years of age to be eligible for the scheme.

scheme_name: Coir Udyami Yojana
question: Who monitors the implementation of the scheme?
answer: The Coir Board, its regional offices, and the concerned bank jointly monitor implementation and verify the physical setup of units.

scheme_name: Coir Udyami Yojana
question: What are the financial benefits under this scheme?
answer: - Beneficiary contribution: 5% of the project cost- Bank credit: 55%- Subsidy: 40% (on project cost excluding working capital)- Working capital: Not eligible for subsidy and must not exceed 25% of the project cost.

scheme_name: Coir Udyami Yojana
question: What is the role of the Regional Level Selection Committee?
answer: The committee evaluates applications and recommends eligible cases to banks for further processing.

scheme_name: Coir Udyami Yojana
question: What documents are required for applying?
answer: Documents include a project report, ID proof, title deed, machinery invoice, DIC certificate, and others as listed in the guidelines.

scheme_name: Coir Udyami Yojana
question: Can I apply if I already received a subsidy from another government scheme?
answer: No, beneficiaries who have availed similar subsidies under any Central or State Government schemes are not eligible.

scheme_name: Coir Udyami Yojana
question: Can I sell or transfer the unit or machinery after receiving the subsidy?
answer: No, machinery and assets created under the scheme cannot be sold or transferred without permission from the Coir Board.

scheme_name: Coir Udyami Yojana
question: Are there any preferences for SC/ST or North East Region applicants?
answer: Yes, the scheme encourages participation from SC/ST candidates and those from the North Eastern Region.

scheme_name: Coir Udyami Yojana
question: What are Mode of Disbursement ?
answer: - The bank releases the term loan after receiving the Margin Money (subsidy) from the Coir Board. | - Subsidy kept as Term Deposit Receipt (TDR) for 2 years. | - After 2 years, the subsidy is credited to the beneficiary’s loan account.

scheme_name: Coir Udyami Yojana
question: Is the subsidy given before or after setting up the unit?
answer: The subsidy is released after loan disbursement and is held as a Term Deposit Receipt for 2 years.

scheme_name: Central Vigilance Commission (CVC) Internship Scheme
question: What Is The Central Vigilance Commission (CVC) Internship Scheme?
answer: The CVC Internship Scheme is an initiative by the Central Vigilance Commission to engage Indian nationals who are graduates or postgraduate students in reputed universities/institutions, both in India and abroad, as interns. It aims to provide them with exposure to the Commission's functioning and contribute to its policy formulation.

scheme_name: Central Vigilance Commission (CVC) Internship Scheme
question: Who Is Eligible To Apply For The CVC Internship Scheme?
answer: Indian nationals who are graduates (awaiting final year results)/postgraduate or research students enrolled in reputed universities/institutions, preferably studying Law, IT, MBA, Social Sciences, and associated subjects, are eligible to apply.

scheme_name: Central Vigilance Commission (CVC) Internship Scheme
question: What Is The Duration Of The Internship?
answer: The internship period is a minimum of one month, which can be extended up to two months.

scheme_name: Central Vigilance Commission (CVC) Internship Scheme
question: Are Interns Required To Maintain Confidentiality During The Internship?
answer: Yes, interns are required to furnish a Declaration of Secrecy prior to the commencement of the internship, indicating their commitment to maintaining confidentiality.

scheme_name: Central Vigilance Commission (CVC) Internship Scheme
question: How Many Interns Are Permitted To Work In The Commission?
answer: A minimum of three interns are allowed to work in the Commission, and they will receive a token remuneration between May and August 2019.

scheme_name: Central Vigilance Commission (CVC) Internship Scheme
question: Will Interns Receive Any Remuneration?
answer: Interns may receive a stipend of [?]10,000 per month to meet their conveyance and daily needs. However, it's important to note that the internship does not guarantee future employment.

scheme_name: Central Vigilance Commission (CVC) Internship Scheme
question: What Support Will Be Provided To The Interns?
answer: The Commission will provide interns with working space, internet facility, and other necessary amenities as determined by the Branch heads. However, interns need to arrange their own transport and accommodation at their own expense.

scheme_name: Central Vigilance Commission (CVC) Internship Scheme
question: Will Interns Receive A Certificate Upon Completion Of The Internship?
answer: Yes, interns who satisfactorily complete the internship and submit their end-of-assignment report will receive a certificate from the Commission. The report will be evaluated by the Branch Officer to whom the intern is attached.

scheme_name: Central Vigilance Commission (CVC) Internship Scheme
question: Can International Students Apply For The CVC Internship Scheme?
answer: Yes, both Indian and international students enrolled in reputed universities/institutions are eligible to apply for the internship.

scheme_name: Central Vigilance Commission (CVC) Internship Scheme
question: How Should Applicants Submit Their Applications?
answer: Interested candidates can submit their applications in the provided Performa either by post or by hand to Sh. Nitin Kumar, Director, CVC, Room No. 406 Satarkta Bhawan, GPO Complex, Block A, INA, New Delhi - 110023. Alternatively, they can email their applications to nitin.72@gov.in.

scheme_name: Central Vigilance Commission (CVC) Internship Scheme
question: How Are Candidates Selected For The Internship?
answer: The Screening Committee will assess candidates based on their marks and the Statement of Purpose (SOP) submitted as part of the application. The selection committee's decision will be final and binding.

scheme_name: Central Vigilance Commission (CVC) Internship Scheme
question: What Documents Are Required To Apply For The Internship?
answer: Applicants need to submit a Letter of NOC (No Objection Certificate) from their present institution indicating their student status and a Statement of Purpose (SOP) not exceeding 200 words.

scheme_name: Central Vigilance Commission (CVC) Internship Scheme
question: What Are The Requirements At The End Of The Internship?
answer: Interns are required to submit an end-of-assignment report and make a presentation on the assigned subject. They will also provide feedback on their experience to the Secretary of the CVC.

scheme_name: Central Vigilance Commission (CVC) Internship Scheme
question: Can Interns Apply For The Scheme During Their Final Year Of Graduation?
answer: Yes, graduates awaiting final year results can apply for the CVC Internship Scheme.

scheme_name: Central Vigilance Commission (CVC) Internship Scheme
question: Are There Any Specific Fields Of Study Preferred For The Internship?
answer: Preference is given to students studying Law, IT, MBA, Social Sciences, and associated subjects, although applicants from other fields may also be considered.

scheme_name: Central Vigilance Commission (CVC) Internship Scheme
question: Is The Internship Considered A Job Opportunity?
answer: No, the internship is neither a job nor a promise for a job in the future. It is a learning opportunity and a chance to contribute to the Commission's work.

scheme_name: Central Vigilance Commission (CVC) Internship Scheme
question: How Will Grievances Be Addressed During The Internship?
answer: The guidelines do not specify a separate grievance redressal process. However, interns can approach the designated authorities within the Commission for any grievances or concerns.

scheme_name: Central Vigilance Commission (CVC) Internship Scheme
question: Can Interns From Different Countries Participate In The CVC Internship Scheme?
answer: Yes, the internship scheme is open to Indian nationals as well as international students enrolled in reputed universities/institutions.

scheme_name: 6 Varsh Se Adhik Aayu Ke Bahuviklang Aur Mansik Roop Se Aviksit Nisaktjan Ke Liye Sahayata Anudan Yojana
question: What is Chhe Varsh Se Adhik Aayu Ke Bahuviklang Aur Mansik Roop Se Aviksit Nisaktjan Ke Liye Sahayata Anudan Yojana?
answer: The objective of the scheme is M.P. To provide assistance to multiple handicapped and mentally underdeveloped persons above the age of six years who are unable to earn a living. At present there is no such provision; their parents and family members have to face a lot of difficulty in taking care of such disabled people.

scheme_name: 6 Varsh Se Adhik Aayu Ke Bahuviklang Aur Mansik Roop Se Aviksit Nisaktjan Ke Liye Sahayata Anudan Yojana
question: What are the benifit of this scheme?
answer: The government gives 600/- per month to handicapped and mentally underdeveloped persons.

scheme_name: 6 Varsh Se Adhik Aayu Ke Bahuviklang Aur Mansik Roop Se Aviksit Nisaktjan Ke Liye Sahayata Anudan Yojana
question: Is this Scheme for all indian citizen?
answer: No, only for the natives of Madhya Pradesh.

scheme_name: 6 Varsh Se Adhik Aayu Ke Bahuviklang Aur Mansik Roop Se Aviksit Nisaktjan Ke Liye Sahayata Anudan Yojana
question: Is there any percent of disability?
answer: Yes, there are 40 percent or more disability.

scheme_name: 6 Varsh Se Adhik Aayu Ke Bahuviklang Aur Mansik Roop Se Aviksit Nisaktjan Ke Liye Sahayata Anudan Yojana
question: Is there are any age criteria?
answer: Yes, the applicant should be more than 6 years old.

scheme_name: 6 Varsh Se Adhik Aayu Ke Bahuviklang Aur Mansik Roop Se Aviksit Nisaktjan Ke Liye Sahayata Anudan Yojana
question: What are the document are required ?
answer: - Age certificate 2. Native resident certificate of Madhya Pradesh. 3. Certificate regarding one's disability as per the Persons with Disabilities (Equal Opportunities, Protection of Rights and Full Participation) Act 1995, in which it is mandatory to describe the disabled person as having multiple disabilities/mentally underdevelopment.

scheme_name: 6 Varsh Se Adhik Aayu Ke Bahuviklang Aur Mansik Roop Se Aviksit Nisaktjan Ke Liye Sahayata Anudan Yojana
question: Can i apply online?
answer: Yes, you can visit this website https://socialsecurity.mp.gov.in/# and follow the steps given in the scheme.

scheme_name: 6 Varsh Se Adhik Aayu Ke Bahuviklang Aur Mansik Roop Se Aviksit Nisaktjan Ke Liye Sahayata Anudan Yojana
question: Can i apply offline ?
answer: Yes, the designated officer, Gram Panchayat, or Public Service Center. and follow the step given in the scheme.

scheme_name: 6 Varsh Se Adhik Aayu Ke Bahuviklang Aur Mansik Roop Se Aviksit Nisaktjan Ke Liye Sahayata Anudan Yojana
question: Is There Any Application Fee For The Scheme?
answer: No, is there no application fee for the scheme.

scheme_name: 6 Varsh Se Adhik Aayu Ke Bahuviklang Aur Mansik Roop Se Aviksit Nisaktjan Ke Liye Sahayata Anudan Yojana
question: Is there any beneficiary category?
answer: Yes, there are General, Other Backward Caste, Scheduled Caste, Scheduled Tribe beneficiary categories.

scheme_name: Coir Vikas Yojana- Coir Industry Technology Upgradation Scheme
question: What is CITUS Scheme?
answer: The scheme "Coir Industry Technology Upgradation Scheme (CITUS)" is a component of the "Coir Vikas Yojana". The scheme was launched by the Ministry of Micro, Small & Medium Enterprises, Government of India for providing modern infrastructure facilities to the production units resulting in improvement of productivity and quality.

scheme_name: Coir Vikas Yojana- Coir Industry Technology Upgradation Scheme
question: What is the objective of this scheme?
answer: The objectives of this component are: | To provide modern infrastructure facilities to the production units resulting in improvement of productivity and quality. | To support the establishment of new 'State-of-the-Art' Coir Processing Units. To spread the industry to potential areas. | To promote enhanced utilization of available raw materials. | To create more employment opportunities, especially for women in rural areas. To attract new generation entrepreneurs to the industry. | To modernize the existing coir units. | To promote the development and installation of information technology including Enterprise Resource Planning (ERP). | To support the production of high-value customer-oriented products. To make the Coir Industry integrated and competitive with modern technologies. | To facilitate the adoption of eco-friendly production techniques. | To achieve the target of a pollution-free coir industry with technological advancements.

scheme_name: Coir Vikas Yojana- Coir Industry Technology Upgradation Scheme
question: Which is the implementing agency of this scheme?
answer: Coir Board, Kochi

scheme_name: Coir Vikas Yojana- Coir Industry Technology Upgradation Scheme
question: Who are eligible for the assistance under the scheme CITUS?
answer: Assistance will be available to entrepreneurs in the categories of individuals/partnership firms, SHGs, Associations, enterprises from small scale / medium / co-operative/ private sector / public sector, interested for production of value added coir /coir blended items, where coir is the dominant fiber by setting up new coir unit or upgrading the existing unit.

scheme_name: Coir Vikas Yojana- Coir Industry Technology Upgradation Scheme
question: Is it necessary for Coir Unit to register with the Coir Board?
answer: Yes, all coir production/processing units registered with the Coir Board under Coir Industry (Registration) Rules, 2008, and having Udyog Aadhaar are eligible to apply for financial assistance for modernization under this scheme.

scheme_name: Coir Vikas Yojana- Coir Industry Technology Upgradation Scheme
question: What is the nature of assistance which is provided under scheme?
answer: The financial assistance shall be 25% of the cost of admissible items of Plant and Machinery procured by the Coir units. The upper ceiling of the financial assistance will be [?]2.50 crore per coir unit/project.

scheme_name: Coir Vikas Yojana- Coir Industry Technology Upgradation Scheme
question: What is the purpose of providing financial assistance?
answer: All eligible Coir units under the component will be entitled to get financial assistance for the procurement of eligible Plants and Machinery for modernization, upgradation, and/or establishing a new unit on making an application in the prescribed format for the purpose.

scheme_name: Coir Vikas Yojana- Coir Industry Technology Upgradation Scheme
question: How the financial assistance will be paid under the scheme?
answer: The financial assistance will be payable only in Indian Rupees in India through Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT) mode and Public Finance Management System (PFMS) as reimbursement of the amount invested.

scheme_name: Coir Vikas Yojana- Coir Industry Technology Upgradation Scheme
question: Which types of entrepreneurs are not eligible for assistance?
answer: The financial assistance under this component will be available to entrepreneurs who have not availed of any Central Government subsidy under PMEGP, CUY, DPI, TUF, etc. for the same purpose.

scheme_name: Coir Vikas Yojana- Coir Industry Technology Upgradation Scheme
question: How to apply for the scheme?
answer: Submit a Detailed project report (DPR) in the prescribed format to the nearest ROs/SROs of the Board through online.

scheme_name: Coir Vikas Yojana- Export Market Promotion Scheme
question: What is “Export Market Promotion Scheme”?
answer: Coir Board is implementing the Central Sector Scheme "Export Market Promotion Scheme" with a view to improving the export performance of the Indian Coir Sector through various export market promotion activities such as sponsoring delegations, participation in seminars and conferences, organizing participation in international fairs, undertaking generic publicity abroad, extending financial assistance to Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises and Exporters, presenting Coir Industry Awards on an annual basis to recognize the outstanding performance in the areas of export, domestic trade, R&D, functioning of units & societies etc.

scheme_name: Coir Vikas Yojana- Export Market Promotion Scheme
question: Which is the implementing agency of this scheme?
answer: Coir Board, Ministry of Micro, Small & Medium Enterprises, Government of India

scheme_name: Coir Vikas Yojana- Export Market Promotion Scheme
question: Who are eligible for the assistance under the scheme?
answer: Manufacturers, Entrepreneurs, and Exporters of Coir are eligible to apply under the scheme.

scheme_name: Coir Vikas Yojana- Export Market Promotion Scheme
question: Is it necessary for MSME Unit to register with the Coir Board?
answer: Yes, Exporters and micro, small & medium enterprises of coir and coir products should be registered with the Coir Board, and would be eligible for assistance under the scheme, provided they have not availed the facility from any other source for the same purpose.

scheme_name: Coir Vikas Yojana- Export Market Promotion Scheme
question: What is the nature of assistance which is provided under scheme?
answer: Delegation, Consultancy & Information Sourcing, Participation in International seminars and conferences and organizing capacity-building programmes in export-related areas, Participation in international fairs/product promotion programmes, catalogue shows and organizing exclusive international fairs and buyer-seller meets for coir, Publicity abroad, External Market Development Assistance & Coir Industry Awards.

scheme_name: Coir Vikas Yojana- Export Market Promotion Scheme
question: What is the amount of space rent which is paid to the applicant unit?
answer: 100% of the space rent subject to a maximum of [?]1.00 lakh or actual rent paid in the case of foreign countries, whichever is lower per exporter/enterprise.

scheme_name: Coir Vikas Yojana- Export Market Promotion Scheme
question: What is the amount of airfare which is paid to the applicant unit?
answer: 100% of the economy class airfare subject to a maximum of [?]1.50 lakh/ and [?]1 Lakh in India or actual fare paid, whichever is lower to one representative of the exporter.

scheme_name: Coir Vikas Yojana- Export Market Promotion Scheme
question: What is the amount of Freight charges which is paid to the applicant unit?
answer: Freight charges- Actual subject to a maximum of [?]25,000/- in foreign countries and [?]20,000/- in India- per exporter/enterprise.

scheme_name: Coir Vikas Yojana- Export Market Promotion Scheme
question: Which types of entrepreneurs are not eligible for assistance?
answer: The Enterprise/exporter charged/debarred/ prosecuted/ blacklisted under the Foreign Trade Policy of the Government of India or by the Coir Board will not be eligible to apply under the scheme.

scheme_name: Coir Vikas Yojana- Export Market Promotion Scheme
question: How to apply for the scheme?
answer: The applicant may fill up the Online Application through the Board online. https://www.coirservices.gov.in/Forgetpassword.aspx

scheme_name: Coir Vikas Yojana-Skill Upgradation and Mahila Coir Yojana
question: What is the “Skill Upgradation and Mahila Coir Yojana”?
answer: Under the scheme the Board is conducting various programmes like Entrepreneurship Development Programme, Awareness Programme, Workshop, Seminar, Exposure Tour, etc. for attracting more entrepreneurs to start coir processing units. In order to create skilled manpower required for the coir industry, the Board is implementing various training programmes such as training on manufacturing of value added coir products, spinning, weaving and other product diversification process. All these training programmes are also available for women under the Mahila Coir Yojana.

scheme_name: Coir Vikas Yojana-Skill Upgradation and Mahila Coir Yojana
question: What is the objective of this scheme?
answer: The objective of the scheme is to train personnel, transfer of technology, self-employment to rural woman artisans, inculcating quality consciousness and Skill-Upgradation of Coir workers.

scheme_name: Coir Vikas Yojana-Skill Upgradation and Mahila Coir Yojana
question: Which is the implementing agency of this scheme?
answer: Regional/ Sub-regional offices/ training centres of the Board, Coir Board, Kochi

scheme_name: Coir Vikas Yojana-Skill Upgradation and Mahila Coir Yojana
question: Which types of organizations are eligible to apply under the scheme?
answer: Self Help Groups (SHGs), NGOs registered in the Darpan Portal of NITI Ayog, and Government Organizations can apply through the Regional /Sub Regional Office of the Board for organizing training programs at the field level.

scheme_name: Coir Vikas Yojana-Skill Upgradation and Mahila Coir Yojana
question: What type of facilities should organizations have before applying under the scheme?
answer: The Self-help Groups (SHGs), NGOs, and Government Organizations should have adequate infrastructural facilities such as work sheds, power connections, equipment, and raw materials.

scheme_name: Coir Vikas Yojana-Skill Upgradation and Mahila Coir Yojana
question: What is the nature of assistance which is provided under scheme?
answer: Coir workers/entrepreneurs will get an awareness of modern technologies developed by the Coir Board. The training programme will help the trainees/ artisans to upgrade their skills in producing coir yarn and other diversified coir products. Management skills can also be acquired by attending EDP programmes to the entrepreneurs to run the Coir units more effectively and efficiently.

scheme_name: Coir Vikas Yojana-Skill Upgradation and Mahila Coir Yojana
question: What is the amount stipend which is given to the trainee under the scheme?
answer: The candidates undergoing these skill development training programmes are given a monthly stipend amounting to [?]3000/- per month and in the case of training programmes of less than one-month duration, the stipend will be disbursed on a pro-rata basis.

scheme_name: Coir Vikas Yojana-Skill Upgradation and Mahila Coir Yojana
question: What is the amount honorarium given to the trainer under the scheme?
answer: The honorarium for the trainer will be limited to [?]15,000/- per month.

scheme_name: Coir Vikas Yojana-Skill Upgradation and Mahila Coir Yojana
question: How much is the amount of financial assistance given to the training sponsoring agency?
answer: An amount of [?]400/- per head per month will be provided as financial assistance to the training sponsoring agency to meet the operational cost of the training for raw material, power charges, other incidentals etc. on submission of a self-certification of Expenditure from the Sponsoring Agency which will be verified and passed by the Regional/Sub Regional Officer for effecting the payment.

scheme_name: Coir Vikas Yojana-Skill Upgradation and Mahila Coir Yojana
question: What is the amount of financial assistance obtained under the PMEGP scheme for procurement of machines/equipment?
answer: The financial assistance for procurement of machines/equipment may be obtained under the PMEGP scheme for setting up new coir units for which the maximum project cost is up to [?]25 lakhs.

scheme_name: Coir Vikas Yojana-Skill Upgradation and Mahila Coir Yojana
question: How to apply for the scheme?
answer: Self Help Groups (SHGs), NGOs registered in the Darpan portal of NITI Aayog, and Government Organizations can apply through the Regional /Sub Regional Office of the Board for organizing training programs at the field level.

scheme_name: Chai Vikas Yojana
question: What is the objective of “Chai Vikas Yojana"?
answer: The objective of "Chai Vikas Yojana" is to promote tea cultivation and enhance productivity in the selected districts of Bihar.

scheme_name: Chai Vikas Yojana
question: Which districts are covered under the scheme?
answer: The scheme covers the districts of Kishanganj, Araria, Supaul, Purnia, and Katihar.

scheme_name: Chai Vikas Yojana
question: Who is eligible to apply for “Chai Vikas Yojana”?
answer: Farmers with a minimum land area of 2 acres, cultivating tea in the specified districts and meeting the minimum landholding requirements are eligible to apply for the scheme.

scheme_name: Chai Vikas Yojana
question: How is the planting material subsidy provided under the scheme?
answer: The planting material subsidy is provided in two installments: 75% of the cost is paid in the first year, and 25% is paid in the second year if 90% of the plants from the previous year's plantation survive.

scheme_name: Chai Vikas Yojana
question: What are the minimum landholding requirements for availing subsidies?
answer: The minimum landholding requirements vary depending on the equipment: | A minimum of 2 acres is required for pruning machines, mechanical harvesters, and plucking shears. | A minimum of 10 acres is required for leaf carriage vehicles. | A minimum of 5 acres is required for leaf collection sheds.

scheme_name: Chai Vikas Yojana
question: What is the maximum subsidy available for a pruning machine?
answer: Farmers are eligible for a subsidy of 50% of the actual cost or [?]60,000/-, whichever is less, for purchasing a pruning machine.

scheme_name: Chai Vikas Yojana
question: Are beneficiaries of new area expansion eligible for mechanized organ subsidies?
answer: Beneficiaries of new area expansion under "Chai Vikas Yojana" are not eligible for mechanized organ subsidies.

scheme_name: Chai Vikas Yojana
question: What is the survival rate condition for receiving the second installment of the planting material subsidy?
answer: To receive the second installment of the planting material subsidy, at least 90% of the plants from the previous year must survive.

scheme_name: Chai Vikas Yojana
question: How many plucking shears can a farmer receive subsidies for?
answer: A farmer can receive subsidies for a maximum of 20 plucking shears under the scheme.

scheme_name: Chai Vikas Yojana
question: What is the maximum subsidy available for a mechanical harvester?
answer: The maximum subsidy available for a mechanical harvester is 50% of the actual cost or [?]50,000, whichever is less.

scheme_name: Chai Vikas Yojana
question: Does the scheme provide subsidies for managing existing tea plantations?
answer: Yes, the scheme provides subsidies for various horticultural machines to manage existing tea plantations.

scheme_name: Chai Vikas Yojana
question: What is the maximum subsidy provided for leaf carriage vehicles?
answer: Farmers cultivating tea on a minimum of 10 acres can receive a subsidy of 50% of the cost or [?]7,50,000, whichever is less, for leaf carriage vehicles.

scheme_name: Chai Vikas Yojana
question: What is the benefit provided for leaf collection sheds under the scheme?
answer: The scheme provides a subsidy of 50% of the actual cost or [?]37,500, whichever is less, for constructing leaf collection sheds for farmers cultivating tea on at least 5 acres.

scheme_name: Chai Vikas Yojana
question: What specific benefits does the scheme offer to small-scale tea farmers?
answer: Small-scale tea farmers cultivating a minimum of 2 acres are eligible for subsidies on affordable equipment like plucking shears, pruning machines, and mechanical harvesters.

scheme_name: PMMSY: Cycle with Ice Boxes-Haryana
question: What is the main objective of this scheme?
answer: The scheme aims to provide central assistance for Cycle with Ice Box costs for the initial crop only in the purchase of newly purchased Cycle with Ice Box.

scheme_name: PMMSY: Cycle with Ice Boxes-Haryana
question: Who are the intended beneficiaries of this scheme?
answer: Beneficiaries involved in fisheries activities are the intended recipients.

scheme_name: PMMSY: Cycle with Ice Boxes-Haryana
question: What is the financial assistance provided under this scheme?
answer: The project cost is ₹0.10 lakh per unit.

scheme_name: PMMSY: Cycle with Ice Boxes-Haryana
question: What percentage of subsidy can a General Category beneficiary expect?
answer: General Category beneficiaries are eligible for a subsidy limited to 40% of the project cost.

scheme_name: PMMSY: Cycle with Ice Boxes-Haryana
question: What percentage of subsidy is available for SC/Women beneficiaries?
answer: SC/Women beneficiaries are eligible for a subsidy limited to 60% of the project cost.

scheme_name: PMMSY: Cycle with Ice Boxes-Haryana
question: Will the central assistance cover the cost of multiple crops?
answer: No, central assistance for Cycle with Ice Box costs is provided for the initial crop only.

scheme_name: PMMSY: Cycle with Ice Boxes-Haryana
question: What documents are required to apply for this scheme?
answer: Required documents include an Agreement deed between vendor and Fisheries Department, Date of Birth Certificate, Voting Card/Birth Certificate/Aadhar Card/Matriculation Certificate, Caste Certificate, Training Certificate, Bills/Receipts/Vouchers, Photographs of beneficiary with Cycle with Ice-Box, Detail of Bank Account and Pan Card, and Detailed Project Report (DPR)/Self Contained Proposal (SCP) as per PMMSY guidelines.

scheme_name: PMMSY: Cycle with Ice Boxes-Haryana
question: Is a training certificate necessary for the application?
answer: Yes, a Training Certificate of Vendor/beneficiary is required.

scheme_name: PMMSY: Cycle with Ice Boxes-Haryana
question: Do I need to submit photographs with the application?
answer: Yes, photographs of the beneficiary with the Cycle with Ice-Box are required.

scheme_name: PMMSY: Cycle with Ice Boxes-Haryana
question: What financial details are required in the application?
answer: Details of your Bank Account and PAN Card are required

scheme_name: PMMSY: Cycle with Ice Boxes-Haryana
question: Is there a specific report or proposal required for the application?
answer: Yes, the beneficiary will submit a Detailed Project Report (DPR)/Self-Contained Proposal (SCP) as per PMMSY guidelines.

scheme_name: PMMSY: Cycle with Ice Boxes-Haryana
question: What specific condition must be maintained for the fish transport facilities?
answer: Beneficiaries should ensure that fish transport facilities are maintained in operational condition.

scheme_name: PMMSY: Cycle with Ice Boxes-Haryana
question: Does the scheme cover procurement, operation, maintenance, and management costs for the fish transport facilities?
answer: No, the Government of India and the Government of Haryana are not responsible for losses incurred on these aspects.

scheme_name: Construction Workers Night Shelter Scheme (MPBOCWWB)
question: Who is eligible for the night shelter under this scheme?
answer: Construction workers and their family members holding valid identity cards.

scheme_name: Construction Workers Night Shelter Scheme (MPBOCWWB)
question: Where will the night shelters be built?
answer: Night shelters will be built in urban bodies and large Gram Panchayats where construction workers temporarily stay for work.

scheme_name: Construction Workers Night Shelter Scheme (MPBOCWWB)
question: How is the site for night shelters selected?
answer: A district-level committee, including various local officials, selects the site and determines the shelter's capacity.

scheme_name: Construction Workers Night Shelter Scheme (MPBOCWWB)
question: What costs are covered by the scheme for the night shelter?
answer: Costs for building construction, decoration, furniture, bedding, lockers, and other essentials.

scheme_name: Construction Workers Night Shelter Scheme (MPBOCWWB)
question: How is the funding for night shelters provided?
answer: The Board provides the amount in two installments as a non-recurring expenditure grant, based on the recommendations of the committee.

scheme_name: Construction Workers Night Shelter Scheme (MPBOCWWB)
question: What is the funding limit for major cities?
answer: [?]25 lakh for four metro cities: Bhopal, Gwalior, Indore, and Jabalpur.

scheme_name: Construction Workers Night Shelter Scheme (MPBOCWWB)
question: What is the funding limit for other Municipal Corporations?
answer: [?]2 million for other Municipal Corporations.

scheme_name: Construction Workers Night Shelter Scheme (MPBOCWWB)
question: What is the funding limit for Municipalities?
answer: [?]1.5 million for Municipalities.

scheme_name: Construction Workers Night Shelter Scheme (MPBOCWWB)
question: How much funding is provided for Nagar Panchayats?
answer: [?]10 lakh for Nagar Panchayats.

scheme_name: Construction Workers Night Shelter Scheme (MPBOCWWB)
question: What is the funding limit for Gram Panchayats?
answer: [?]10 lakh for Gram Panchayats, with conditions based on population and construction activity.

scheme_name: Construction of Water Storage Tanks for Drip Irrigation
question: What is the objective of the "Construction of Water Storage Tanks for Drip Irrigation" scheme?
answer: The scheme aims to provide financial assistance to farmers for constructing water storage tanks to support efficient drip irrigation practices.

scheme_name: Construction of Water Storage Tanks for Drip Irrigation
question: Who is eligible to apply for the scheme?
answer: Any farmer residing in Gujarat who intends to install a cemented water tank for drip irrigation can apply for the scheme.

scheme_name: Construction of Water Storage Tanks for Drip Irrigation
question: What is the subsidy amount offered to general category farmers?
answer: General category farmers are eligible to receive 50% of the tank’s construction cost, up to a maximum of ₹50,000/-.

scheme_name: Construction of Water Storage Tanks for Drip Irrigation
question: What financial assistance is provided to Scheduled Caste and Scheduled Tribe farmers?
answer: Scheduled Caste and Scheduled Tribe farmers can receive 75% of the cost, limited to a maximum of ₹75,000/-.

scheme_name: Construction of Water Storage Tanks for Drip Irrigation
question: Is there a minimum size requirement for the water tank?
answer: Yes, the tank must have a minimum storage capacity of 25.50 cubic meters to be eligible for assistance.

scheme_name: Construction of Water Storage Tanks for Drip Irrigation
question: What type of tank is permitted under this scheme?
answer: Only cemented water storage tanks are allowed under this scheme.

scheme_name: Construction of Water Storage Tanks for Drip Irrigation
question: Is the installation of a drip irrigation set mandatory?
answer: Yes, installation of a drip irrigation set is compulsory as part of the scheme requirements.

scheme_name: Construction of Water Storage Tanks for Drip Irrigation
question: Can a farmer apply for the scheme more than once?
answer: No, the benefit under this scheme can be availed only once per account on the i-Khedut portal.

scheme_name: Construction of Water Storage Tanks for Drip Irrigation
question: Where can a farmer submit an application for the scheme?
answer: Applicants can apply on the iKhedut portal to avail the benefits of the scheme.

scheme_name: Construction of Water Storage Tanks for Drip Irrigation
question: Is it necessary to submit a cost estimation certificate for the tank?
answer: Yes, applicants must submit a certified cost estimate from a Government Valuer, Taluka Surveyor, or MNREGA Surveyor.

scheme_name: Construction of Water Storage Tanks for Drip Irrigation
question: Is there any income limit for eligibility under this scheme?
answer: No, there is no income limit for individual or family income under this scheme.

scheme_name: Construction of Water Storage Tanks for Drip Irrigation
question: What documents are required to apply for this scheme?
answer: Applicants need to submit their Aadhaar card, 7/12 land record, caste certificate (if applicable), bank passbook or cancelled cheque, and tank cost certificate.

scheme_name: Construction of Water Storage Tanks for Drip Irrigation
question: Who should the applicant contact for help or more information about the scheme?
answer: The applicant should contact the nearest agriculture office or visit the iKhedut portal for more information.

scheme_name: Co-Working Space/ Incubators/ Accelerators Subsidy Scheme
question: What are the maximum reimbursement periods for startups at co-working spaces, incubators, and accelerators under the "Co-Working Space/ Incubators/ Accelerators Subsidy Scheme" in Goa?
answer: Start-ups can avail benefits for a maximum of two years at co-working spaces, one year at incubators, and three months at accelerators.

scheme_name: Co-Working Space/ Incubators/ Accelerators Subsidy Scheme
question: How is the reimbursement calculated for seats at co-working spaces, and what is the maximum benefit per seat?
answer: Start-ups are reimbursed 50% of the seat cost, with a maximum benefit of [?]3000 per seat, and can claim this for a maximum of 8 seats.

scheme_name: Co-Working Space/ Incubators/ Accelerators Subsidy Scheme
question: Can a startup claim reimbursement for seats on any plan offered by co-working spaces, incubators, or accelerators listed by the Startup Promotion Cell (SPC)?
answer: Yes, reimbursement can be claimed on any plan offered by the listed co-working spaces, incubators, or accelerators.

scheme_name: Co-Working Space/ Incubators/ Accelerators Subsidy Scheme
question: What is the total number of subsidized seats available each year for co-working spaces, incubators, and accelerators under this scheme?
answer: The scheme subsidizes 100 seats in co-working, 50 seats each in incubators and accelerators annually.

scheme_name: Co-Working Space/ Incubators/ Accelerators Subsidy Scheme
question: Under what circumstances might the SPC reimburse up to 100% of the amount paid by deserving startups?
answer: Deserving startups, as per SPC guidelines, may receive up to 100% reimbursement based on internal evaluation.

scheme_name: Co-Working Space/ Incubators/ Accelerators Subsidy Scheme
question: What is the eligibility criterion for startups to participate in this scheme?
answer: Start-ups certified by the Start-up Promotion Cell (SPC) are eligible, and they must pay digitally to the listed co-working spaces/ incubators/ accelerators.

scheme_name: Co-Working Space/ Incubators/ Accelerators Subsidy Scheme
question: What documents are required for the application process, apart from the original bill?
answer: Start-ups need to submit the form and documents as mentioned in Annexure-1 along with the original bill.

scheme_name: Co-Working Space/ Incubators/ Accelerators Subsidy Scheme
question: Can startups apply offline for the "Co-Working Space/ Incubators/ Accelerators Subsidy Scheme"?

scheme_name: Co-Working Space/ Incubators/ Accelerators Subsidy Scheme
question: What is the timeline for startups to apply for the scheme within the financial year?
answer: Startups can apply at any time during the financial year but must do so within 6 months of incurring the relevant expenditure.

scheme_name: Co-Working Space/ Incubators/ Accelerators Subsidy Scheme
question: How long does the SPC take to evaluate and notify the approval or rejection of applications?
answer: The SPC evaluates and notifies approval or rejection within 45 days from the receipt of the application.

scheme_name: Co-Working Space/ Incubators/ Accelerators Subsidy Scheme
question: What is the objective of the Goa Start-up Policy 2017?

scheme_name: Children With Special Needs Under Goa Sarva Shiksha Abhivan
question: What is the objective of the CWSN scheme?
answer: The scheme aims to cater to the special educational needs of children with disabilities, ensuring they receive comprehensive support for their education and overall development.

scheme_name: Children With Special Needs Under Goa Sarva Shiksha Abhivan
question: Who is eligible to apply for the CWSN scheme?
answer: Parents/guardians of children with disabilities, heads of schools where CWSN are enrolled, and other stakeholders directly involved in their care and education can apply.

scheme_name: Children With Special Needs Under Goa Sarva Shiksha Abhivan
question: What types of disabilities are covered under the scheme?
answer: The scheme covers various disabilities including intellectual disabilities, physical disabilities, and others as specified in the eligibility criteria.

scheme_name: Children With Special Needs Under Goa Sarva Shiksha Abhivan
question: What types of assistance are provided under the scheme?
answer: The scheme provides cash grants for activities related to CWSN such as medical assessments, resource rooms, home-based education, training of educators, and provision of assistive aids.

scheme_name: Children With Special Needs Under Goa Sarva Shiksha Abhivan
question: How can I apply for the CWSN scheme?
answer: Applicants need to submit a plain application detailing the specific individual needs of the child with disabilities along with any available medical certificates.

scheme_name: Children With Special Needs Under Goa Sarva Shiksha Abhivan
question: What documents are required to apply for the scheme?
answer: Applicants typically need to submit a detailed application, medical certificates (if available), and other supporting documents as specified by the scheme guidelines.

scheme_name: Children With Special Needs Under Goa Sarva Shiksha Abhivan
question: Who oversees the implementation and monitoring of the CWSN scheme?
answer: The implementation and monitoring of the scheme are overseen by relevant educational authorities or government bodies responsible for special education and disability support.

scheme_name: Deendayal Antyodaya Yojana - National Rural Livelihoods Mission
question: What Is NRLM - Aajeevika ?
answer: National Rural Livelihoods Mission (NRLM) - Aajeevika was launched by the Ministry of Rural Development (MoRD), Government of India in June 2011 as a restructured version of Swarna Jayanti Gram Swarozgar Yojna (SGSY). NRLM has the mandate of reaching out to 100 million rural poor in 6 lakh villages across the country. | The poor have innate capabilities to overcome poverty. NRLM strives towards unleashing this entrepreneurial capability by creating appropriate platforms for the poor through a dedicated and sensitive support structures.

scheme_name: Deendayal Antyodaya Yojana - National Rural Livelihoods Mission
question: How Is It Different From Swarna Jyanti Swarozgar Yojana (SGSY)?
answer: NRLM has adopted 'demand driven' strategy, in place of SGSY's 'allocation based' strategy. This implies that under NRLM, states have greater autonomy to plan for implementing the programme. NRLM encourages states to prepare State Perspective for Implementation Plans (SPIP) for seven years and Annual Action Plans (AAPs). The allocation for the state is released against the approved AAP. | NRLM has adopted a Participatory Identification of Poor (PIP) instead of the BPL to identify its beneficiaries.

scheme_name: Deendayal Antyodaya Yojana - National Rural Livelihoods Mission
question: What Are The Key Features Of NRLM?
answer: NRLM rests on three major pillars - universal social mobilization, financial inclusion and livelihoods enhancement. It works towards bringing at least one member (preferably a woman) from all poor families into the SHG network. The SHGs and their federations offer their members services such as savings, credit and livelihoods support. As the Institutions of the Poor (IoP) mature, they are facilitated to take up livelihoods/income-generating activities.

scheme_name: Deendayal Antyodaya Yojana - National Rural Livelihoods Mission
question: How Is NRLM Being Implemented?
answer: NRLM has put in place a dedicated, sensitive support structure to facilitate the creation and functioning of IoP. The SRLMs are given the responsibility of implementing the programme in the states based on their States Perspective Implementation Plans (SPIPs) and Annual Action Plans (AAPs). District Mission Management Units (DMMU) and Block Mission Management Units (BMMU) are established to implement the programme. | At the national level, the National Rural Livelihoods Promotion Society (NRLPS) has been set up to serve as the technical support agency to NRLM. NRLPS supports the SRLMs in strategizing, planning and implementing NRLM.

scheme_name: Deendayal Antyodaya Yojana - National Rural Livelihoods Mission
question: Who Are Eligible For Benefits Under NRLM?
answer: The NRLM Target Households (NTH) are identified through the Participatory Identification of Poor (PIP) instead of the BPL. The PIP is a community-driven process where the CBOs themselves dentify the poor in the village using participatory tools. The list of poor identified by the CBO is vetted by the Gram Sabha.

scheme_name: Deendayal Antyodaya Yojana - National Rural Livelihoods Mission
question: What Are Institutions Of The Poor (IOPs)?
answer: SHGs, their federations at the village, cluster levels and beyond, and other collectives of the poor constitute Institutions of Poor (IoP). | SHGs are affinity-based homogenous groups of 10-20 members (usually women). They follow five cardinal principles or Panchsutra (regular meetings, regular savings, internal lending, regular repayment and bookkeeping). The SHGs are federated at the village (Village Organisation), sub-block and higher levels. They are supported to become self-sufficient and community-managed institutions over time. | Institutions of the poor such as SHGs and their village level and higher level federations are necessary to provide space, voice and resources for the poor, and for reducing their dependence on external agencies. They empower them. They also act as instruments of knowledge and technology dissemination, and hubs of production, collectivization and commerce. NRLM, therefore, would focus on setting up these institutions at various levels. | In case of special SHGs i.e. groups in remote tribal areas and in difficult areas, groups with vulnerable persons like disabled persons, the group may be as small as 5 members. Only for groups to be formed with Persons with disabilities, and other special categories like elders, transgender, NRLM will have both men and women in the SHGs.

scheme_name: Deendayal Antyodaya Yojana - National Rural Livelihoods Mission
question: What Are The Functions Of The Group?
answer: SHGs are affinity-based savings and credit groups to begin with. They offer solidarity. They provide microfinance services - savings, credit, bank linkages, insurance, remittances, equity etc. They also offer collectivization and group activities. The SHGs offer social security and social action in various fronts including health, nutrition, food, gender, convergence etc., directly or through their federations.

scheme_name: Deendayal Antyodaya Yojana - National Rural Livelihoods Mission
question: What Is The Role Of The Bookkeeper?
answer: The bookkeeper of the SHG is a literate member of the group or any literate person known to the group members. The bookkeeper is selected by the SHG members and is trained in SHG bookkeeping. A SHG has 4-7 books - member passbook, minutes book, attendance and savings book, cash book, loan ledger, activity/enterprise book(s) etc.

scheme_name: Deendayal Antyodaya Yojana - National Rural Livelihoods Mission
question: What is the role of the SHG leader?
answer: The SHG leaders motivate the SHG to follow the Panchasutra. They serve as the link between the SHG and other institutions such as banks.

scheme_name: Deendayal Antyodaya Yojana - National Rural Livelihoods Mission
question: Is NRLM Only For Women?
answer: NRLM's priority is to reach out to the poorest, most vulnerable and marginalized. It begins with targeting women and they are considered as representatives of their households. In case of extremely vulnerable persons like Persons with Disabilities (PwDs), elders etc., NRLM mobilizes both men and women. Further, other interventions of NRLM like Rural Self Employment Training Institutes (RSETIs), Aajeevika Skills would reach out to poor in general.

scheme_name: Deendayal Antyodaya Yojana - National Rural Livelihoods Mission
question: Will Aajeevika Strengthen All Existing SHGs And Federations Of The Poor?
answer: There are existing institutions of the poor women formed by Government efforts and efforts of NGOs. NRLM would strengthen all existing institutions of the poor in a partnership mode. NRLM strives to build on what exists on ground in terms of SHGs of poor and their federations. After assessing the existing mobilization, NRLM mobilizes the remaining poor in a saturation basis. The new and existing institutions would be strengthened to become selfsustaining accountable and transparent institutions serving the needs of their members. All NRLM compliant institutions would be eligible institutions would receive funds like revolving fund, community investment fund and interest subvention.

scheme_name: Deendayal Antyodaya Yojana - National Rural Livelihoods Mission
question: How Many Blocks Is NRLM Being Implemented In?
answer: NRLM is presently working in 1009 blocks in an 'intensive' mode. Of these, 50 blocks are being developed as resource blocks to create local human and social capital (IoPs, internal Community Resource Persons (CRPs) etc.) that would support in implementing NRLM in other blocks. The implementation in resource blocks is supported by National Resource Organisations (NROs) such as SERP (AP), Jeevika (Bihar), Kudumbashree (Kerala) etc. In about 50 blocks, NRLM is partnering with existing Federations and NGOs to saturate the block. In the remaining intensive blocks, the NRLM is fielding its field implementation teams. | NRLM's presence in the remaining blocks in the country, referred as non-intensive blocks, is limited to the extent of supporting the existing mobilization, strengthening the existing institutions, providing revolving fund and bank linkages, and taking up other activities in a limited way.

scheme_name: Deendayal Antyodaya Yojana - National Rural Livelihoods Mission
question: How Are Partners Taken Aboard In NRLM?
answer: NRLM works with a variety of organizations for various purposes. It has identified the SRLMs of certain states (AP, Kerala and Bihar) and NROs for implementation support. It has identified National Support Organisations (NSOs) such as PRADAN to provide thematic support. NRLM has also forged partnerships with Capacity Building Agencies (CBAs) and Academic and Management Institutes to meet its capacity building and technical assistance needs. It has also entered into partnerships with CBOs and NGOs to implement the programme in certain blocks of the country. The NRLPS identifies and empanels these organizations while the SRLMs take their services directly. SRLMs also identify and partner with various partner organizations on their own.

scheme_name: Deendayal Antyodaya Yojana - National Rural Livelihoods Mission
question: How Are The SHGs Supported Under NRLM?
answer: Support to the SHGs of poor is in terms of knowledge, skills, funds, bank linkages and interest subvention. NRLM ensures that the poor are provided with the requisite knowledge and skills to the members, the leaders and the bookkeepers of the SHGs for: managing their institutions, enhancing their credit absorption capacity and credit worthiness, linking up with markets, managing their existing livelihoods, etc. | A multi-pronged approach is envisaged for continuous capacity building of the targeted families, SHGs, their federations, government functionaries, bankers, NGOs and other key stakeholders.

scheme_name: Deendayal Antyodaya Yojana - National Rural Livelihoods Mission
question: What Other Measures Has NRLM Taken Towards Financial Inclusion?
answer: NRLM facilitates the SHGs to open and operate bank accounts and bank linkages. It also facilitates access to insurance to members. It is encouraging individual members too to open bank accounts.

scheme_name: Deendayal Antyodaya Yojana - National Rural Livelihoods Mission
question: What Is A Micro Plan Of An SHG?
answer: Micro planning is a process where members are encouraged to recognize, understand and evaluate their resources; analyze challenges they face; identify needs and make future plans to overcome vulnerabilities by making optimum utilization of resources and fostering convergences. The SHGs receive their CIF only on developing their micro plans or microcredit plans.

scheme_name: Deendayal Antyodaya Yojana - National Rural Livelihoods Mission
question: What Is Aajeevika Skills Development Programme (ASDP)?
answer: ASDP, Aajeevika Skills, gives young people from poor communities an opportunity to upgrade their skills and enter the skilled work force in growing sectors of the economy. Skill Training and Placement projects are run in partnership with public, private, non-government and/or community organizations.

scheme_name: Deendayal Antyodaya Yojana - National Rural Livelihoods Mission
question: Who Will Be Eligible To Be Selected For Skills And Placement Under ASDP?
answer: Trainees between the age of 18-35 yrs and who belong to a rural poor household [that has been identified as being poor following the participatory identification of the poor (PIP) process undertaken as part of Aaajevika are eligible under ASDP. Till such time PIP is completed, BPL status or vetting by Gram Panchayat saying the candidate is from poor background, would suffice for being eligible for this selection under Skills and Placement under ASDP.

scheme_name: Deendayal Antyodaya Yojana - National Rural Livelihoods Mission
question: What Are PIAs?
answer: PIAs (Project Implementing Agencies) are for profit or not-for-profit registered entities identified by ASDP for skilling and placing the identified youth in various sectors as per their interest.

scheme_name: Deendayal Antyodaya Yojana - National Rural Livelihoods Mission
question: What Kind Of Training And Support Is Available Under The Aajeevika Skills?
answer: Youth identified under the programme get skilled in wide range of trades, including IT and soft skills. After training and placement, support is provided in terms of finding accommodation, opening a bank account when placed outside the home district and counseling at workplace.

scheme_name: Deendayal Antyodaya Yojana - National Rural Livelihoods Mission
question: Is There Any Self-Employment Generation Component In Aajeevika?
answer: Aajeevika is encouraging public sector banks to set up Rural Self Employment Training Institutes (RSETIs) in all districts of the country on line lines of Rural Development Self-Employment Institute (RUDSETI) model for promoting self-employment. National Academy of RUDSETIs is supporting RSETIs in this effort. RSETIs provide self-employment training and link the candidates with bank loans for taking up self-employment. NRLM provides the costs of the training to RSETIs.

scheme_name: Deendayal Antyodaya Yojana - National Rural Livelihoods Mission
question: How Does NRLM Support Farm-Based Livelihoods?
answer: Mahila Kisan Sashaktikaran Pariyojana (MKSP), launched in 2010-11, is a special programme for livelihood enhancement under NRLM. It is a concerted effort to recognize the role of women in agriculture and an investment is being made to enhance their capacities and increase their income. The MKSP has two streams - Agriculture (and Livestock) and NTFP (Non-timber Forest Produce).

The fellowship amount is determined by the committee after reviewing the submitted research project.

scheme_name: D. D. Kosambi Research Fellowship Scheme

However, if the research work is undertaken on a full-time basis, the fellowship amount can be up to Rs. 30,000 per month, with the research period determined by the selection committee. The amount is assessed based on the recommendation of the selection committee after the submission of the research project.

scheme_name: D. D. Kosambi Research Fellowship Scheme

question: How can craftspersons benefit financially under this scheme?
