scheme_name: "Design Development Training For Master Crafts Persons" Component of the "Development of Handicrafts" Scheme
question: What does the scheme offer to the Training Unit/Institution in terms of financial support?
answer: The Training Unit/Institution receives payment for the course fee as prescribed.

scheme_name: "Design Development Training For Master Crafts Persons" Component of the "Development of Handicrafts" Scheme
question: How is the period of training determined for craftspersons?
answer: The period of training is determined as prescribed by the Training Unit/Institution.

scheme_name: "Design Development Training For Master Crafts Persons" Component of the "Development of Handicrafts" Scheme
question: What is the significance of the scheme in the context of modern art and craft techniques?
answer: The scheme aims to have a significant impact on the development of modern art and techniques in crafts, possibly introducing new crafts from other regions.

scheme_name: "Design Development Training For Master Crafts Persons" Component of the "Development of Handicrafts" Scheme
question: How does the scheme contribute to the marketability of traditional crafts?
answer: By enhancing craftspersons' skills, the scheme makes traditional crafts more appealing to customers, thereby increasing marketability.

scheme_name: "Design Development Training For Master Crafts Persons" Component of the "Development of Handicrafts" Scheme
question: Where can applicants find the necessary application forms for this scheme?
answer: Application forms can be downloaded from the official website at https://dic.py.gov.in/application-forms-download-area.

scheme_name: "Design Development Training For Master Crafts Persons" Component of the "Development of Handicrafts" Scheme
question: What financial support does the scheme provide for craftspersons' accommodation?

scheme_name: "Design Development Training For Master Crafts Persons" Component of the "Development of Handicrafts" Scheme
question: What is the role of the Department of Industries and Commerce, Union Territory of Puducherry, in the scheme?
answer: The department oversees the permanent registration of the unit and ensures the implementation of the training for craftspersons.

scheme_name: "Design Development Training For Master Crafts Persons" Component of the "Development of Handicrafts" Scheme
question: Where can individuals raise grievances related to the scheme?
answer: Grievances can be addressed through the Grievance Redressal Mechanism at https://industry.py.gov.in/grievance-redressal-mechanism.

scheme_name: "Design Development Training For Master Crafts Persons" Component of the "Development of Handicrafts" Scheme
question: What kind of crafts does the scheme focus on for design development training?

scheme_name: "Design Development Training For Master Crafts Persons" Component of the "Development of Handicrafts" Scheme
question: How is the course fee for the training determined?

scheme_name: Deen Dayal Upadhyaya Bunkar Yojana
question: Can men apply for the Deen Dayal Upadhyaya Bunkar Yojana?
answer: No, the scheme is exclusively for women weavers.

scheme_name: Deen Dayal Upadhyaya Bunkar Yojana
question: Are companies and partnership firms eligible for the scheme?
answer: No, the scheme is applicable only to individual women weavers or groups of women weavers.

scheme_name: Deen Dayal Upadhyaya Bunkar Yojana
question: What is the maximum loan amount eligible for the interest subvention?
answer: The interest subvention is applicable for working capital loans up to Rs. 2.00 lakh, irrespective of the loan amount extended by the bank.

scheme_name: Deen Dayal Upadhyaya Bunkar Yojana
question: Can I apply if I don't own a working loom?
answer: Ownership or possession of a working loom(s) is a requirement for eligibility under the scheme.

scheme_name: Deen Dayal Upadhyaya Bunkar Yojana
question: Is there any age limit to apply for the scheme?
answer: The scheme does not specify any age restrictions for applicants.

scheme_name: Deen Dayal Upadhyaya Bunkar Yojana
question: How long does it take for the loan amount to be disbursed?
answer: The loan amount will be disbursed after the completion of the application process and approval by the bank. The time may vary depending on the bank's procedures.

scheme_name: Deen Dayal Upadhyaya Bunkar Yojana
question: Is collateral required to avail the benefits of the scheme?
answer: No, the scheme does not require collateral for short-term credit, cash credit limit, working capital limit, weavers' credit card, or Swarojgar credit card up to Rs. 2.00 lakh.

scheme_name: Deen Dayal Upadhyaya Bunkar Yojana
question: Are loans availed from cooperative banks eligible for the interest subvention?
answer: No, loans from cooperative banks are not eligible for the interest subvention. Only loans from commercial banks and regional rural banks are eligible.

scheme_name: Deen Dayal Upadhyaya Grah Aawas (Home-Stay) Vikas Yojana
question: Who is eligible to apply for this scheme?
answer: Permanent/original residents of Uttarakhand who own a building in non-municipal areas and reside there with their family are eligible to apply.

scheme_name: Deen Dayal Upadhyaya Grah Aawas (Home-Stay) Vikas Yojana
question: Can applicants construct new homestays or renovate existing ones?
answer: Yes, the scheme provides funds/subsidy for both construction of new homestays and upgradation, extension, renovation, or improvement of existing buildings, including toilet construction.

scheme_name: Deen Dayal Upadhyaya Grah Aawas (Home-Stay) Vikas Yojana
question: What is the minimum and maximum number of guest rooms allowed?
answer: Applicants can construct a minimum of one and a maximum of six guest rooms.

scheme_name: Deen Dayal Upadhyaya Grah Aawas (Home-Stay) Vikas Yojana
question: Is there a preference for a particular building style?
answer: Preference is given to buildings constructed or developed in traditional hill-style architecture.

scheme_name: Deen Dayal Upadhyaya Grah Aawas (Home-Stay) Vikas Yojana
question: Is the applicant required to contribute any amount?
answer: Yes, the beneficiary must contribute 12.5% of the project cost at the time of taking the loan.

scheme_name: Deen Dayal Upadhyaya Grah Aawas (Home-Stay) Vikas Yojana
question: Where can applicants submit their application?
answer: Applications must be submitted online at https://msy.uk.gov.in/frontend/web/index.php

scheme_name: Deen Dayal Upadhyaya Grah Aawas (Home-Stay) Vikas Yojana
question: What is the process after submitting the online application?
answer: The application is forwarded to the District Tourism Development Officer (DTDO). A committee chaired by the District Magistrate schedules an interview for the applicant to review the proposal.

scheme_name: Deen Dayal Upadhyaya Grah Aawas (Home-Stay) Vikas Yojana
question: How is the loan processed?
answer: Once the committee approves the proposal, it is sent online to the bank chosen by the applicant. The bank then initiates the loan approval process and disburses the amount if approved.

scheme_name: Deen Dayal Upadhyay Grameen Kaushalya Yojana
question: What sectors does the DDU-GKY program offer skill training in?
answer: The program provides skill training in diverse sectors such as agriculture, construction, retail, and hospitality.

scheme_name: Deen Dayal Upadhyay Grameen Kaushalya Yojana
question: Explain the 3-tier implementation model of DDU-GKY.
answer: The model includes the DDU-GKY National Unit for policy-making, State Skill Missions for co-funding, and Project Implementing Agencies (PIAs) for on-ground implementation.

scheme_name: Deen Dayal Upadhyay Grameen Kaushalya Yojana
question: What support does DDU-GKY offer during the job search process?
answer: The program assists beneficiaries with resume writing, interview preparation, and connects them with potential employers.

scheme_name: Deen Dayal Upadhyay Grameen Kaushalya Yojana
question: What is the upper age limit for women candidates under DDU-GKY?
answer: Women candidates, along with other specific groups, have an upper age limit of 45 years.

scheme_name: Deen Dayal Upadhyay Grameen Kaushalya Yojana
question: How are poor youth identified for DDU-GKY?
answer: The Participatory Identification of Poor (PIP) process is used, considering factors like MGNREGA work, RSBY card, Antyodaya Anna Yojana, SHG membership, and auto inclusion parameters.

scheme_name: Deen Dayal Upadhyay Grameen Kaushalya Yojana
question: Explain the reservation criteria for SCs and STs at the national level.
answer: 50% of funds are earmarked for SCs and STs, with the proportion determined by the Ministry of Rural Development.

scheme_name: Deen Dayal Upadhyay Grameen Kaushalya Yojana
question: What is the minimum reservation for persons with disabilities in DDU-GKY?
answer: States are mandated to ensure that at least 3% of beneficiaries are persons with disabilities.

scheme_name: Deen Dayal Upadhyay Grameen Kaushalya Yojana
question: How does DDU-GKY incentivize Project Implementing Agencies for higher placements?
answer: The program provides incentives to PIAs for placing beneficiaries in higher-paying jobs, encouraging alignment with their skills and experience.

scheme_name: Deen Dayal Upadhyay Grameen Kaushalya Yojana
question: What is the role of State Skill Missions in DDU-GKY implementation?
answer: State Skill Missions, part of State Rural Livelihood Missions, provide co-funding and implementation support in the state for DDU-GKY.

scheme_name: Deen Dayal Upadhyay Grameen Kaushalya Yojana
question: Explain the career progression support provided by DDU-GKY.
answer: The program offers training, mentorship, and access to networking opportunities to help beneficiaries advance in their careers.

scheme_name: Deen Dayal Upadhyay Grameen Kaushalya Yojana
question: What is the purpose of the Participatory Identification of Poor (PIP) process?
answer: PIP is crucial for identifying poor youth and is an integral part of the NRLM strategy until they are identified through existing BPL lists.

scheme_name: Deen Dayal Upadhyay Grameen Kaushalya Yojana
question: What is the significance of the 15-day work criterion for MGNREGA households?
answer: Youth from MGNREGA households with at least 15 days of work in the previous financial year are considered eligible for DDU-GKY.

scheme_name: Deen Dayal Upadhyay Grameen Kaushalya Yojana
question: Explain the earmarking of funds for minority groups in DDU-GKY.
answer: 15% of funds are set aside for beneficiaries from minority groups to ensure inclusivity and diversity in the program.

scheme_name: Deen Dayal Upadhyay Grameen Kaushalya Yojana
question: How can DDU-GKY beneficiaries access post-placement support?
answer: The program provides post-placement support through mentorship, counseling, and access to resources to help beneficiaries adjust to their new jobs.

scheme_name: Deen Dayal Upadhyay Grameen Kaushalya Yojana
question: Can targets for SC and ST beneficiaries be interchanged?
answer: Yes, targets from SC and ST can be interchanged if no eligible beneficiaries are available, certified by the District Rural Development Agency (DRDA).

scheme_name: Deen Dayal Upadhyay Kaushal Kendra (DDUKK)- Mega Skill Centre
question: What is Deen Dayal Upadhyay Kaushal Kendra?
answer: A scheme to provide skill training with on-job training under a PPP model.

scheme_name: Deen Dayal Upadhyay Kaushal Kendra (DDUKK)- Mega Skill Centre
question: Who can apply for the training?
answer: Unemployed youth aged 18-35 years, meeting the educational and residency criteria.

scheme_name: Deen Dayal Upadhyay Kaushal Kendra (DDUKK)- Mega Skill Centre
question: What sectors are covered under this scheme?
answer: Over 20 sectors, including IT/ITES, Healthcare, Automotive, Agriculture, and Tourism.

scheme_name: Deen Dayal Upadhyay Kaushal Kendra (DDUKK)- Mega Skill Centre
question: Is the training residential?
answer: Yes, all training is fully residential.

scheme_name: Deen Dayal Upadhyay Kaushal Kendra (DDUKK)- Mega Skill Centre
question: What is the duration of the training?
answer: Minimum 576 hours, with 160 hours for IT and soft skills.

scheme_name: Deen Dayal Upadhyay Kaushal Kendra (DDUKK)- Mega Skill Centre
question: How many candidates will be trained annually?
answer: The target is 60,000 candidates per year.

scheme_name: Deen Dayal Upadhyay Kaushal Kendra (DDUKK)- Mega Skill Centre
question: What is the infrastructure requirement for the training centers?
answer: A minimum of 25,000 sq. ft. area for training and hostels.

scheme_name: Deen Dayal Upadhyay Kaushal Kendra (DDUKK)- Mega Skill Centre
question: Are there any fees for the training?
answer: No, the training is free for eligible candidates.

scheme_name: Deen Dayal Upadhyay Kaushal Kendra (DDUKK)- Mega Skill Centre
question: What is On Job Training (OJT)?
answer: Practical, hands-on training in real industry environments to prepare candidates for jobs.

scheme_name: Deen Dayal Upadhyay Kaushal Kendra (DDUKK)- Mega Skill Centre
question: How can I apply for the scheme?
answer: Apply online through JSDMS or at designated centers or online.

scheme_name: Deen Dayal Upadhyaya Sahkarita Kisan Kalyan Yojana
question: Who is eligible to apply under this scheme?
answer: General, small, and marginal farmers, farmers living below the poverty line (BPL), their family members, and self-help groups (SHGs) are eligible, provided they are members of a cooperative society or hold a savings account in the District Cooperative Bank.

scheme_name: Deen Dayal Upadhyaya Sahkarita Kisan Kalyan Yojana
question: What is the loan amount available under the scheme?
answer: - Up to ₹1.00 lakh for agricultural activities. | - Up to ₹3.00 lakh for non-agricultural activities (e.g., animal husbandry, poultry, fisheries, horticulture, etc.). | - Up to ₹5.00 lakh for self-help groups (SHGs).

scheme_name: Deen Dayal Upadhyaya Sahkarita Kisan Kalyan Yojana
question: What activities are covered under non-agricultural work?
answer: Non-agricultural activities include animal husbandry, dairy, poultry, fisheries, cultivation of herbs, aromatic plants, spices, mushrooms, floriculture, horticulture, organic farming, agricultural processing, mechanization, poly-house farming, and off-season vegetable production.

scheme_name: Deen Dayal Upadhyaya Sahkarita Kisan Kalyan Yojana
question: What is the definition of a small and marginal farmer under the scheme?
answer: - Small Farmer: Owns up to 5 acres of unirrigated land or up to 2.5 acres of irrigated land. | - Marginal Farmer: Owns up to 2.5 acres of unirrigated land or up to 1.25 acres of irrigated land.

scheme_name: Deen Dayal Upadhyaya Sahkarita Kisan Kalyan Yojana
question: Can more than one member of a family apply for the loan?
answer: No. Only one member per family is eligible to avail of the benefits under this scheme.

scheme_name: Deen Dayal Upadhyaya Sahkarita Kisan Kalyan Yojana
question: Are there any income limits prescribed under the scheme?
answer: No. Currently, there is no income limit prescribed for farmers to avail of the scheme’s benefits.

scheme_name: Deen Dayal Upadhyaya Sahkarita Kisan Kalyan Yojana
question: Are defaulters of cooperative societies eligible for this loan?
answer: No. Defaulters of any cooperative institution are not eligible for benefits under this scheme.

scheme_name: Deen Dayal Upadhyaya Sahkarita Kisan Kalyan Yojana
question: Who is responsible for selecting the beneficiaries?
answer: A Block-Level Committee reviews all applications and selects eligible beneficiaries. The committee then approves and forwards the cases for loan disbursement under the scheme.

scheme_name: Deen Dayal Upadhyaya Swawlamban Yojana
question: What is the genesis of DDUSY?
answer: The Government of Arunachal Pradesh launched this startup loan scheme to provide financial assistance via subsidies on loans. It was announced in the State Budget in March 2017 to promote entrepreneurship among unemployed youth through formal banking channels, utilizing the network of scheduled commercial banks across the State.

scheme_name: Deen Dayal Upadhyaya Swawlamban Yojana
question: What is the objective of the scheme?
answer: The scheme encourages unemployed youth to access low-cost capital for entrepreneurial ventures. It offers 40% front-ended subsidy on project costs from ₹10 L to ₹50 L. Women entrepreneurs get an additional 5% annual interest subsidy, provided the loan doesn’t become a Non-Performing Entity (NPE). Sectors supported include: | - Food processing (agriculture/allied) | - Eco-tourism (homestays, tour operations) | - Traditional textile weaving | - Small manufacturing/bamboo processing/service/diagnostic units | - Other innovative business ideas

scheme_name: Deen Dayal Upadhyaya Swawlamban Yojana
question: Who is eligible?
answer: Unemployed APST (Arunachal Pradesh Scheduled Tribes) entrepreneurs planning to set up new business enterprises are eligible for loans and subsidies.

scheme_name: Deen Dayal Upadhyaya Swawlamban Yojana
question: Which institution provides loans?
answer: Any branch of a Scheduled Commercial Bank in Arunachal Pradesh can provide the loan. The loan typically covers 30–50% of project cost (excluding land and building). Entrepreneurs must contribute 10–30% as their own margin; preference is given to higher contributions.

scheme_name: Deen Dayal Upadhyaya Swawlamban Yojana
question: What is the interest rate?
answer: Rates vary by bank. For State Bank of India (SBI), it’s approximately 3.25–3.50% above EBLR (about 7.55% currently).

scheme_name: Deen Dayal Upadhyaya Swawlamban Yojana
question: What government support is available?
answer: Government support includes a 40% front-ended capital investment subsidy under DDUSY. Women entrepreneurs also receive a 5% interest subvention annually, contingent on the account not turning NPE.

scheme_name: Deen Dayal Upadhyaya Swawlamban Yojana
question: What is front-ended capital subsidy?
answer: This means the subsidy amount is credited upfront to the loan account soon after loan sanction, helping early-stage cashflow.

scheme_name: Deen Dayal Upadhyaya Swawlamban Yojana
question: What is the 5% interest subvention for women beneficiaries?
answer: If the bank charges 12% interest, a woman entrepreneur would effectively pay 7% after the 5% subvention, in addition to the capital subsidy.

scheme_name: Deen Dayal Upadhyaya Swawlamban Yojana
question: What is margin money/own contribution?
answer: Applicants must contribute 10–30% of total project cost as their margin. Preference is given to those who contribute more.

scheme_name: Deen Dayal Upadhyaya Swawlamban Yojana
question: How to apply?
answer: Applicants must apply via the DDUSY online web portal and prepare a Concept Note/Detailed Project Report (DPR) for the enterprise they wish to establish, then submit it through the portal or the Deputy Commissioner’s Office.

scheme_name: Deen Dayal Upadhyaya Swawlamban Yojana
question: How are applications processed?
answer: - Scrutiny by District Planning Officer (DPO); CIBIL check by District Lead Bank Manager. | - District Level Screening Committee (DLSC) meeting chaired by the Deputy Commissioner. | - Eligible applicants present before DLSC; suitable projects are field-verified. | - DLSC recommends projects to banks; banks evaluate and sanction viable loans.

scheme_name: Deen Dayal Upadhyaya Swawlamban Yojana
question: What other schemes exist for projects up to ₹10 L?
answer: Banks can sanction loans below ₹10 L under the Mudra Scheme; visit www.mudra.org.in for details.

scheme_name: Deen Dayal Upadhyaya Swawlamban Yojana
question: What security is required?
answer: Loans are covered under CGTMSE (Credit Guarantee Fund Trust for Micro and Small Enterprises), so collateral is not insisted upon. If the borrower doesn’t want to bear the guarantee fee, collateral per bank norms is needed.

scheme_name: Deen Dayal Upadhyaya Swawlamban Yojana
question: What is the repayment tenure?
answer: Repayment depends on the activity and useful life of assets, not exceeding 7 years, including a moratorium of up to 6 months. Annual reviews are done.

scheme_name: Deen Dayal Upadhyaya Swawlamban Yojana
question: How to get handholding support?
answer: The Arunachal Pradesh Innovation and Investment Park (APIIP) in Itanagar provides resources and expertise for startups and new ventures under DDUSY.

scheme_name: Deen Dayal Upadhyaya Swawlamban Yojana
question: Is plantation activity eligible?
answer: No. Only value-addition activities under agri-horti and allied sectors are eligible.

scheme_name: Deen Dayal Upadhyaya Swawlamban Yojana
question: How will banks claim the subsidy?
answer: Banks scrutinise and sanction loans per their norms, then submit subsidy claims to the Planning & Investment Division with relevant loan details.

scheme_name: Deen Dayal Upadhyaya Swawlamban Yojana
question: Will government agencies prepare DPRs?
answer: Applicants must prepare their own DPRs, but they can seek assistance from APIIP or district officials if needed.

scheme_name: Destitute/Deserted Wives Pension Scheme
question: Do I need to visit the government office to apply for the scheme?
answer: No, you can apply online through the nearest Common Service Center (CSC).

scheme_name: Destitute/Deserted Wives Pension Scheme
question: What is the amount of the monthly pension?
answer: The monthly pension under this scheme is [?]1,000.

scheme_name: Destitute/Deserted Wives Pension Scheme
question: Do I get the free saree and rice every month?
answer: No, the sarees are distributed during Pongal and Deepavali festivals, and the free rice is provided through Anganwadi centers, with varying quantities based on participation in the nutritious meal program.

scheme_name: Destitute/Deserted Wives Pension Scheme
question: I am 28 years old and destitute. Am I eligible for the scheme?
answer: No, the minimum age requirement is 30 years old.

scheme_name: Destitute/Deserted Wives Pension Scheme
question: My husband left me 5 years ago, but I have savings of ₹1.5 lakh. Can I still apply?
answer: The maximum limit for fixed assets is [?]1 lakh. Your savings exceed the limit, so you might not be eligible.

scheme_name: Destitute/Deserted Wives Pension Scheme
question: Can I track the status of my application?
answer: You can inquire about the application status by visiting the CSC where you submitted it or contacting the Social Welfare and Women Empowerment Department.

scheme_name: Destitute/Deserted Wives Pension Scheme
question: Can you clarify the criteria for receiving free rice at Anganwadi Centres?
answer: Beneficiaries who take nutritious meals at Anganwadi Centres are entitled to receive 2kg of free rice per month. However, those not availing nutritious meals receive 4kg of free rice every month.

scheme_name: Destitute/Deserted Wives Pension Scheme
question: Is there any age restriction for applicants to the 'Destitute/Deserted Wives Pension Scheme'?
answer: Yes, applicants must be 30 years old or above to qualify for the scheme.

scheme_name: Destitute/Deserted Wives Pension Scheme
question: What is the significance of the abandonment certificate in the list of required documents?
answer: The abandonment certificate is a crucial document that certifies the applicant's status of being legally divorced or deserted for a minimum of 5 years, meeting one of the eligibility criteria for the scheme.

scheme_name: Destitute/Deserted Wives Pension Scheme
question: How often is the pension disbursed to the beneficiaries?
answer: Beneficiaries receive the pension amount of [?]1,000 per month.

scheme_name: Destitute/Deserted Wives Pension Scheme
question: Are there any specific guidelines regarding the fixed assets of the applicant?
answer: Yes, to be eligible, the applicant's fixed assets should not exceed [?]1,00,000.

scheme_name: Ex-Gratia Grant for Clothes, Utensils, and Household Items to Disaster-Affected Families
question: Who is eligible to receive assistance under this scheme?
answer: Families whose houses have been washed away, completely or substantially damaged, or affected by waterlogging for more than two days due to a natural disaster are eligible.

scheme_name: Ex-Gratia Grant for Clothes, Utensils, and Household Items to Disaster-Affected Families
question: How much financial assistance is provided under this scheme?
answer: An ex-gratia grant of ₹2,500 per family is provided for damage to clothes and an additional ₹2,500 per family is provided for damage to utensils or household items.

scheme_name: Ex-Gratia Grant for Clothes, Utensils, and Household Items to Disaster-Affected Families
question: How are the relief funds distributed to the beneficiaries?
answer: After approval from the District Magistrate, the relief funds are disbursed to beneficiaries at the Tehsil level.

scheme_name: Ex-Gratia Grant for Clothes, Utensils, and Household Items to Disaster-Affected Families
question: Is this financial assistance given per person or per family?
answer: The assistance is provided per family.

scheme_name: Ex-Gratia Grant for Clothes, Utensils, and Household Items to Disaster-Affected Families
question: Who verifies the damage caused by the disaster?
answer: The Patwari of the concerned area verifies the damage and records it in the P-20 form.

scheme_name: Ex-Gratia Grant for Clothes, Utensils, and Household Items to Disaster-Affected Families
question: Who gives the final approval for providing financial assistance?
answer: The District Magistrate gives the final approval for the disbursement of relief funds.

scheme_name: Disha - Early Intervention and School Readiness Scheme
question: What is Disha-Early Intervention and School Readiness Scheme?
answer: This scheme aims at setting up Disha Centres for early intervention for Person with Disability (PwD) in 0-10 years of age covered under the National Trust Act, through therapies, trainings and providing support to family members.

scheme_name: Disha - Early Intervention and School Readiness Scheme
question: Which department has launched this scheme?
answer: Disha-Early Intervention and School Readiness Scheme was launched by the Department of Empowerment of Persons with Disabilities.

scheme_name: Disha - Early Intervention and School Readiness Scheme
question: What are the main benefits of this scheme?
answer: Disha Centre/Registered Organization(RO) should provide facilities to the PwD like day care,staffing, infrastructure,assessment and evaluation etc.

scheme_name: Disha - Early Intervention and School Readiness Scheme
question: What are the main benefits of this scheme?
answer: Disha Centre/Registered Organization(RO) should provide facilities to the PwD like day care,staffing, infrastructure,assessment and evaluation etc.

scheme_name: Disha - Early Intervention and School Readiness Scheme
question: From where the PwD can get the facilities?
answer: PwD can avail the benefits from Disha Centre or Registered Organisation.

scheme_name: Disha - Early Intervention and School Readiness Scheme
question: What is the main purpose of the scheme?
answer: This is an early intervention and school readiness scheme for the children.

scheme_name: Disha - Early Intervention and School Readiness Scheme
question: Does the facilities will be only applicable to the children?
answer: No, this scheme aims at providing training (specifically school readiness) and counselling to both children and parent.

scheme_name: Disha - Early Intervention and School Readiness Scheme
question: Who will be covered under this scheme?
answer: Person with Disability (PwD) in 0-10 years of age will be covered under this scheme.

scheme_name: Disha - Early Intervention and School Readiness Scheme
question: What is the enrolment process of the of PwD at the Disha Centre?
answer: Parent/legal guardian of the PwD have to come together at the Disha Centre.Then the centre will conduct a PwD Assessment Test with the help of a Therapist or Counsellor.

scheme_name: Disha - Early Intervention and School Readiness Scheme
question: What are the documents required for the enrolment?
answer: - Enrolment form. | - Birth Certificate or Date of Birth proof of the PwD. | - Disability Certificate. | - BPL certificate or Income certificate of Parent or Guardian issued by competent authority as authorized by the concerned State/ Union Territory (for LIG or BPL family). | - ID proof of parent or guardian. | 6.Residence (Local) proof (Mandatory in case of LIG parent or guardian or for parents of PwD availing transport facility.

scheme_name: Dairy Equipment Scheme
question: Can a farmer who owns dairy animals but does not live in Goa apply for the subsidy benefit under this scheme?
answer: Only farmers who are bona fide residents of Goa for at least the last 5 years are eligible to apply for the subsidy.

scheme_name: Dairy Equipment Scheme
question: If a farmer has a cattle shed and milch animals outside Goa, can the application still be considered?
answer: The applicant must own a cattle shed with milch animals located within the State of Goa to qualify for assistance.

scheme_name: Dairy Equipment Scheme
question: Is a person eligible if they have already received a subsidy for the same equipment under another Government programme?
answer: Applicants who have claimed subsidies for similar equipment under any other scheme are not eligible for this scheme.

scheme_name: Dairy Equipment Scheme
question: Can the subsidy be availed for second-hand, refurbished or used dairy equipment?
answer: The subsidy is strictly available only for the purchase of new dairy equipment and implements.

scheme_name: Dairy Equipment Scheme
question: Is there a specific limit on how much subsidy can be availed under this scheme?
answer: Yes. The subsidy is provided at 75% of the permissible equipment cost, limited to ₹2,00,000/- per beneficiary.

scheme_name: Dairy Equipment Scheme
question: Are there any conditions regarding the dealers from whom the equipment must be purchased?
answer: Equipment must be purchased from authorised dealers registered with the Directorate of Animal Husbandry and Veterinary Services, Government of Goa.

scheme_name: Dairy Equipment Scheme
question: Can a farmer purchase the equipment first and then apply for the subsidy?
answer: No. Prior approval from the Directorate must be obtained before purchasing the equipment to be eligible for the subsidy.

scheme_name: Domestic Funding Of Foreign Training
question: What is the DFFT Scheme?
answer: The Domestic Funding of Foreign Training (DFFT) Scheme is a scheme introduced by the Government of India in 2001 with the objective to upgrade the knowledge & skills of Government officers as well as provide exposure to international best practices by deputing them to different long/short-term training programmes.

scheme_name: Domestic Funding Of Foreign Training
question: Who is eligible for training under the DFFT scheme?
answer: The officers belonging to IAS, CSS, and SCS are eligible to undergo foreign training under the | Scheme. Officers of the other two All India Services, viz., IPS and IFoS, and those of other organized Group `A' Central Civil Services are eligible under the Scheme only when they are holding posts on deputation under the Central Staffing Scheme.

scheme_name: Domestic Funding Of Foreign Training
question: Where can I find the Circular giving the terms and conditions along with the eligibility criteria for applying under the Scheme?
answer: The circular is issued every year and hosted on the website of this Ministry (www.persmin.nic.in)

scheme_name: Domestic Funding Of Foreign Training
question: How and when can I apply under the Scheme?
answer: The circular for training programmes to be conducted in a financial year (April to March) is | generally issued in the month of October of the preceding year, e.g., for training programmes to be offered in FY 2011-12, the circular was issued in October 2010. The circular also contains an | application form for filling up by interested officers.

scheme_name: Domestic Funding Of Foreign Training
question: Is there a common Circular for the Long term as well as the Short term Programmes?
answer: Yes

scheme_name: Domestic Funding Of Foreign Training
question: Which are the areas for Long term and short term programmes sponsored under the DFFT Scheme?
answer: The long-term programmes are mainly in the fields of public policy, public management, | public administration, etc. while the themes for the short-term programmes are leadership, | executive development, fiscal decentralization, tax analysis & revenue forecasting, project | management, corruption & anti-corruption, health sector reforms, public administration, public | finance management, infrastructure, and PPP, training of trainers, and advance competencies for | trainers, environmental policy issues, etc. The specific programmes both Long Term and short term | are included in the Circular issued each year.

scheme_name: Domestic Funding Of Foreign Training
question: How are the selections made?
answer: It is mandatory to apply `online' for the training programmes under the DFFT scheme. A software-based eligibility list is generated, followed by a merit list. Based on the date available through these lists, a duly constituted Committee recommends officers for long-term and short-term training programmes taking into account the relevance and suitability factors and takes approval of the competent authority.

scheme_name: Domestic Funding Of Foreign Training
question: Who bears the cost of the programme and what are the entitlements for living/daily allowances and accommodation allowance?
answer: The entire cost of the participation of officers in training programmes under the DFFT scheme is | met by the Training Division, except for certain pre-departure expenses. A detailed circular dated 19th January 2011 indicating various entitlements is available on the Ministry's website (www.persmin.nic.in).

scheme_name: Domestic Funding Of Foreign Training
question: Is the air travel also arranged by the DOPT? If so,how do we get the air tickets ?
answer: Yes, the travel in the entitled class (on an excursion fare basis) is arranged through Air India by | the DOPT. For this purpose, vouchers are issued to the Air India office at Safdarjung Airport. The | name and contact details of the concerned officers in Air India are intimated to the nominated | officers who then get in touch with them and reserve tickets to their respective destinations.

scheme_name: Domestic Funding Of Foreign Training
question: Does nomination by DoPT guarantee admission to the programmes?
answer: Not necessarily. The concerned institutes also have their own selection procedures which may sometimes reject the nominations made by DOPT.

scheme_name: Domestic Funding Of Foreign Training
question: When I can apply for the support under the Partial Funding Scheme?
answer: The applications can be made throughout the year but only after securing admission to the | chosen programme/ University. However, the period from April to June is ideal as most of the | programmes commence in August/September.

scheme_name: Domestic Funding Of Foreign Training
question: If I fulfil all the eligibility criteria as per the Circular can I be sure to get the Partial Funding support from the DoPT?
answer: DOPT administers the partial funding scheme. However, the Central Establishment Board is | the final authority in the matter which may lay down its own criteria such as public interest, budget, etc. while deciding the cases of partial funding.

scheme_name: Production Linked Incentive Scheme (PLI) For Promoting Telecom & Networking Products Manufacturing In India
question: Can An Existing PLI Beneficiary Company, Claim Additional Incentives Of 1% Over And Above The Applicable Rates Of Incentive For Products Qualified Under Design Led Manufacturing, As Defined At Clause 2.8A And Under Normal Rates Applicable For PLI Scheme, For The Products Not Complying With Design-Led Manufacturing Criteria?
answer: The amendments are applicable for both, the existing PLI beneficiaries and new companies applying under the 2nd window of applications. These companies can claim additional incentives of 1% over and above the applicable rates of incentive for products qualified under Design-led Manufacturing, as defined in Clause 2.8A and under normal rates applicable for PLI Scheme, for the products not complying with Design-led Manufacturing criteria. | In respect of the existing PLI beneficiary, they have to give a declaration for specific products that satisfy the Design-led criteria, during the current application window. Based on their eligibility, these specific products will be listed under Design-led manufacturing and will be treated accordingly for the period of this scheme. | However, in the case of existing companies, the total year-wise incentive payable shall be limited to the year-wise incentive amount already approved for the company.

scheme_name: Production Linked Incentive Scheme (PLI) For Promoting Telecom & Networking Products Manufacturing In India
question: If A New Applicant Manufactures A Mix Of Products I.E. Some Products Complying With The Criteria Defined Under Clause 2.8A And Some Non-Complying Products, Then How Will It Be Selected During The New Application Process?
answer: New Applicant companies who apply for a mix of products & declare that only some of them would comply with Design-led manufacturing criteria; shall be treated as non-compliant Design-led manufacturers. | Their applications will be considered as per Clause 2.3 of the amendment dated 20th June 2022. However, these companies will get priority over companies in whose case all the products are non-compliant with the Design-led manufacturing criteria. | Further, such companies have to demonstrate their capabilities to comply with Design-led Manufacturing Criteria at the time of scrutiny of application.

scheme_name: Production Linked Incentive Scheme (PLI) For Promoting Telecom & Networking Products Manufacturing In India
question: If An Applicant Company At The Time Of Application Submits That All Its Products Comply With The Design-Led Criteria (As Defined In Clause 2.8A), But At A Later Stage Some Of The Products Are Found Non-Compliant, Then How The Incentives Will Be Decided?
answer: Applicant companies who now apply for all products complying with Design-led criteria should give a certificate declaring that all the products manufactured by them under this Scheme satisfy the Design-led Manufacturing criteria as defined in Clause 2.8A, to be given priority over manufacturers not compliant with Design-led criteria at the time of ranking for selection under the Scheme. | Further, such companies have to demonstrate their capabilities to comply with Design-led Manufacturing Criteria at the time of scrutiny of the application. | If any product fails to satisfy some of the Design-led Manufacturing criteria at a later stage, then they will be eligible for incentives at normal rates as applicable to the PLI Scheme for those particular products.

scheme_name: Production Linked Incentive Scheme (PLI) For Promoting Telecom & Networking Products Manufacturing In India
question: Can An Existing PLI Beneficiary Company Apply For Revision Of Committed Investment / Net Incremental Sales Forecast In The Existing Approval Under The Scheme?
answer: The existing PLI beneficiary company which intends to revise the committed investment / net incremental sales forecast has the option to apply as a fresh Applicant. On selection, the company has to exit from the existing approval and forego their investment made during Financial Year 2021-22.

scheme_name: Production Linked Incentive Scheme (PLI) For Promoting Telecom & Networking Products Manufacturing In India
question: Can An Existing PLI Beneficiary Company Claim Incentive For FY2021-22 With The Achieved Investment / Net Sales Figures And Also Apply For New Application Under Design-Led PLI For The Remaining 4 Years With A Higher Committed Investment / Net Incremental Sales Forecast?
answer: The existing company can claim the incentive for FY2021-22 with the achieved investment / net sales figures under normal rates of PLI Scheme and higher rates for products for the rest of the 4 years only complying with Design-led Manufacturing criteria but within the year-wise incentive amount approved for the company subject to submission of declaration for products which satisfy the Design-led criteria during the current application window. | However, if these companies want to revise the committed investments/net sales; they have to apply as a fresh company and on selection have to forego investment as per the amended Guidelines. The existing company cannot revise committed investment / net incremental sales forecast without participation and selection under the window provided now.

scheme_name: Production Linked Incentive Scheme (PLI) For Promoting Telecom & Networking Products Manufacturing In India
question: Can An Existing PLI Beneficiary Company Choose 5 Consecutive Years Of Incentives At The End Of The Scheme Tenure?
answer: The choice of 5 consecutive years of incentives has to be made in the current application window i.e. open till 25.08.2022.

scheme_name: Production Linked Incentive Scheme (PLI) For Promoting Telecom & Networking Products Manufacturing In India
question: What Is Production Linked Incentive (PLI) Scheme For Telecom And Networking Products Manufacturing In India?
answer: The Production Linked Incentive (PLI) Scheme would promote Telecom and Networking Products manufacturing in India and accordingly, a financial incentive is proposed to boost domestic manufacturing and attract investments in the target segments of telecom and networking products in order to encourage "Make in India". The Scheme is also expected to boost export of telecom and networking products "Made in India".

scheme_name: Production Linked Incentive Scheme (PLI) For Promoting Telecom & Networking Products Manufacturing In India
question: What Is The Scheme Outlay And Tenure?
answer: The Scheme will be implemented within the overall financial limits of Rs 12,195 Crores only (Rupees Twelve Thousand One Hundred and Ninety-Five Crore only) over a period of 5 years. The scheme is effective from 1st April, 2022. The investment will be permitted to be made in made in India from 01.04.2022 onwards and up to Financial Year (FY) 2025-2026 only, subject to qualifying incremental annual thresholds. The support under the Scheme shall be provided for a period of five (5) years, i.e. from FY 2022-23 to FY 2026-27.

scheme_name: Production Linked Incentive Scheme (PLI) For Promoting Telecom & Networking Products Manufacturing In India
question: Who Are The Eligible Applicants To Apply Under The PLI Scheme For Telecom And Networking Products Manufacturing In India?
answer: Applicant for the purpose of the Scheme is a company registered in India under the Companies Act 2013, proposing to manufacture goods covered under Scheme Target Segments as defined hereinafter, and making an application seeking approval under the Scheme. | The Applicant can set up new or use existing manufacturing facility(ies) to manufacture goods covered under the Scheme Target Segments. The aforesaid manufacturing can be carried out at one or more locations in India, which will however be prior intimated to Department of Telecommunications (DoT). The Applicants who are declared as Non-Performing Asset (NPA) as per RBI guidelines or wilful defaulter or reported as fraud by any bank, financial institution or non-banking financial company etc. would be considered as ineligible. Further, there should not be any insolvency proceedings admitted against the Applicant in the National Company Law Tribunal (NCLT), etc.

scheme_name: Production Linked Incentive Scheme (PLI) For Promoting Telecom & Networking Products Manufacturing In India
question: What Are The Different Categories Of Applicants Who Can Apply Under The PLI Scheme For Telecom And Networking Products?
answer: Application can be made under following two categories: | a)MSME: Companies registered as Micro, Small & Medium Enterprises (MSME) with the Ministry of MSME, Government of India. | b) Non MSMEs: Companies which do not fall under the MSME category will be classified as Non MSMEs. The Non MSMEs category shall be further sub-divided in two categories: | i. Domestic Company: As per the FDI Policy 2020, a company is considered as 'Owned' by resident Indian citizens if more than 50% of the capital in it is beneficially owned by resident Indian citizens and / or Indian companies, which are ultimately "owned" and "controlled" by resident Indian citizens. Such a company will be defined as "Domestic Company" for the purpose of these guidelines. | ii. Global Company: Global Company means a company which does not qualify as Domestic Company as defined above and is having business in one or more than one country either by itself or including its Group Companies (Refer FAQ No.8).

scheme_name: Production Linked Incentive Scheme (PLI) For Promoting Telecom & Networking Products Manufacturing In India
question: What Will Be The Eligibility Criteria For The Applicants Under The PLI Scheme For Telecom And Networking Products Manufacturing In India?
answer: Applicants have to satisfy the following criteria to be eligible under the PLI Scheme for Telecom and Networking Products manufacturing in India: | a) Minimum Global Revenue defined as per the Scheme Guidelines for Global, Domestic and MSME Companies. | b) Eligibility will be subject to achievement of a minimum threshold of cumulative incremental investment over a period of four years and incremental sales of manufactured goods (covered under Scheme Target Segments) net of taxes (as distinct from traded goods) over the Base Year (FY2019-2020). The cumulative investment can be made at one go, subject to annual cumulative threshold as prescribed for four years being met. An applicant is expected to meet all the minimum threshold conditions to be eligible for disbursement of incentive. The Company/entity may invest in single or multiple eligible products to meet minimum incremental investment and sales threshold. | c) There will be a minimum investment threshold of [?] 10 Crores for MSME an [?] 100 Crores for others. Land and building cost will not be counted as investment. | Total number of beneficiaries will be limited owing to the fixed ceiling of the budgetary outlay.

scheme_name: Production Linked Incentive Scheme (PLI) For Promoting Telecom & Networking Products Manufacturing In India
question: What Is The Eligibility Qualification Criteria For Global Revenue As Per The PLI Scheme For Telecom And Networking Products?
answer: The following will be the eligibility qualification criteria for Global Revenue as per the PLI Scheme for Telecom and Networking Products: | a) MSMEs: Global Revenue should be more than Rs. 10 Crore in the base year (2019-20). | b) Domestic Companies: Global Revenue should be more than Rs.250 Crore in the base year. | c) Global Companies: Global Revenue should be more than Rs. 10,000 Crore in the base year. | In case of Group companies of Applicant, whose revenues for the Base year have not been consolidated in INR, the revenue in the respective currency shall be converted to INR at an average of currency exchange rates as on April 01, 2019 and March 31, 2020.

scheme_name: Production Linked Incentive Scheme (PLI) For Promoting Telecom & Networking Products Manufacturing In India
question: Whether Global Revenue Includes Taxes?
answer: Yes, the global revenue is Consolidated Gross Revenue.

scheme_name: Production Linked Incentive Scheme (PLI) For Promoting Telecom & Networking Products Manufacturing In India
question: Whether Global Revenue Includes Revenue From Contract Manufacturing?
answer: Yes, the Global revenue includes all the revenues in the electronics, IT/ITES including software, telecom and networking segments.

scheme_name: Production Linked Incentive Scheme (PLI) For Promoting Telecom & Networking Products Manufacturing In India
question: What Is Group Company With Reference To The Global Revenue As Defined In The PLI Scheme For Telecom And Networking Products?
answer: As per the Scheme Guidelines, Group Company means two or more enterprises which, directly or indirectly, are in a position to: | a) Exercise twenty-six percent or more of voting rights in other enterprise; or | b) Appoint more than fifty percent of members of board of directors in the other enterprise.

scheme_name: Production Linked Incentive Scheme (PLI) For Promoting Telecom & Networking Products Manufacturing In India
question: My Group Company Is Located In A Country Where The FY Starts In Jan 2021. How To Provide You The Gross Revenue?
answer: In case any group company of the applicant is located in a country where FY doesn't match with FY as in India, they would provide revenues of the company for the period of the base year, instead of their FY.

scheme_name: Production Linked Incentive Scheme (PLI) For Promoting Telecom & Networking Products Manufacturing In India
question: How To Convert The Global Revenue In Any Foreign Currency To INR While Applying?
answer: In case of Group companies of Applicant, whose revenues for the Base year have not been consolidated in INR, the revenue in the respective currency shall be converted to INR at an average of currency exchange rates as on April 01, 2019 and March 31, 2020.

scheme_name: Production Linked Incentive Scheme (PLI) For Promoting Telecom & Networking Products Manufacturing In India
question: What Are The Scheme Target Segments?
answer: The Scheme Target Segments consists of Specified Telecom and Networking Products which will be allowed to be manufactured under this PLI Scheme. The list of products have been classified as mentioned below: | a) Core Transmission Equipment. | b) 4G/5G, Next Generation Radio Access Network and Wireless Equipment. | c) Access & Customer Premises Equipment (CPE), Internet of Things (IoT) Access Devices and Other Wireless Equipment. | d) Enterprise equipment: Switches, Routers. | New Product have been added vide DoT Office Memorandum dated 20-06-2022. For complete list of the Specified Telecom & Networking Products please visit our website.

scheme_name: Production Linked Incentive Scheme (PLI) For Promoting Telecom & Networking Products Manufacturing In India
question: Whether Companies Would Need To Predict All Products Which It Will Manufacture In Future And Take Approval In The Application, Or The Products Can Be Added At A Later Stage. For E.G. If A Company Files Application With 5 Categories Of Products. However, In Future It Manufactures 7 Products. Whether All The Products Need To Be Added In The Application At This Stage Itself.
answer: Yes, the claim can only be filed for the products covered under the approval letter issued to the Applicant company. New product cannot be added at a later stage.

scheme_name: Production Linked Incentive Scheme (PLI) For Promoting Telecom & Networking Products Manufacturing In India
question: What Will Be The Baseline For Investment & Net Sales Of Goods Manufactured In India?
answer: Baseline for investment in the Scheme will be as on 31/03/2022. Base Year for Net Sales of Goods Manufactured in India (covered under the Scheme Target Segment) will be from 01.04.2019 to 31.03.2020

scheme_name: Production Linked Incentive Scheme (PLI) For Promoting Telecom & Networking Products Manufacturing In India
question: What Are The Eligible Categories Of Investment As Per The PLI Scheme For Telecom And Networking Products?
answer: Investment under the PLI Scheme for Telecom and Networking Products can be made in the Scheme Target Segments, capitalized in the books of accounts of the Applicants under the following categories: | a) Plant, Machinery, Equipment and Associated Utilities. | b) Research and Development. | c) Transfer of Technology (ToT) Agreements.

scheme_name: Production Linked Incentive Scheme (PLI) For Promoting Telecom & Networking Products Manufacturing In India
question: Will There Be Any Upper Limit On The Eligible Categories Of Investment As Per The PLI Scheme For Telecom And Networking Products?
answer: As per the amendments to the Scheme Guidelines dated 20-06-2022, the limits on the eligible investment made in Research & Development and the Transfer of Technology Agreements have been removed.

scheme_name: Production Linked Incentive Scheme (PLI) For Promoting Telecom & Networking Products Manufacturing In India
question: Are Taxes And Duties Included In The Expenditure That Is Considered Towards Investment In The Scheme?
answer: All non-creditable taxes and duties would be included towards the expenditure incurred on eligible category of investment as per the PLI Scheme for Telecom and Networking Products.

scheme_name: Production Linked Incentive Scheme (PLI) For Promoting Telecom & Networking Products Manufacturing In India
question: Will The Expenditure Incurred On Land And Building Be Considered Under Eligible Category Of Investment As Per The PLI Scheme For Telecom And Networking Products?
answer: The expenditure incurred on land and building (including factory building / construction) required for the project / unit is not covered under the Scheme and, therefore, will not be considered for determining eligibility under the Scheme. However, expenditure incurred on civil works associated with installation and erection of plant, machinery, equipment, and associated utilities shall be eligible.

scheme_name: Production Linked Incentive Scheme (PLI) For Promoting Telecom & Networking Products Manufacturing In India
question: In Case There Is Any Plant, Machinery Or Equipment Which Is Common For Target Product And Other Product, The Cost Of Such Equipment Will Be Regarded As Eligible Investment.
answer: Yes. The usage of such machinery for manufacturing of other products also is not prohibited. However, the Applicant must submit a declaration about usage of machinery for each year during the period that such Applicant is claiming incentive under the Scheme.

scheme_name: Production Linked Incentive Scheme (PLI) For Promoting Telecom & Networking Products Manufacturing In India
question: Base Line Turnover Is Required To Be Provided For Each Product. Whether Incremental Turnover Will Be Considered Product Wise Or For Company As Whole. For Example, If A Company Is Manufacturing 5 Products At Present And In Future It Manufactures Only 3 Whether Base Line For Only Such 3 Products Will Be Considered To Calculate Incremental Turnover Or All 5 Products.
answer: As per clause 9.1 of the Scheme Guidelines, the baseline will be considered for all the products covered in the Scheme Target Segments (as per Annexure 1 of the scheme guidelines) net of taxes. | For Example, if in the base year, the company is manufacturing 5 products under the Scheme Target Segment, the baseline will be considered for all 5 products for calculating incremental turnover, irrespective of whether the company produces only 3 of those 5 products in the claim year.

scheme_name: Production Linked Incentive Scheme (PLI) For Promoting Telecom & Networking Products Manufacturing In India
question: If Company Adds Any Additional Product Which It Is Not Manufacturing Currently And Baseline For Such Product Is Zero. Whether All Turnover Pertaining To Said Product Will Be Considered As Incremental.
answer: Yes, all turnover pertaining to the additional product will be considered for calculation of net incremental sales, provided the product is covered under the Scheme Target Segment and mentioned in the approval letter issued to the Applicant company by the PMA (as per clause 10.6.3)

scheme_name: Production Linked Incentive Scheme (PLI) For Promoting Telecom & Networking Products Manufacturing In India
question: Can A Company Claim Incentive For The Products Under Scheme Target Segment Manufactured At Location Other Than Those Mentioned In Application Form?
answer: The manufacturing can be carried out at one or more locations in India, which is however to be prior intimated to DoT i.e. before commencement of manufacturing activity at the new location.

scheme_name: Production Linked Incentive Scheme (PLI) For Promoting Telecom & Networking Products Manufacturing In India
question: If A Company Is MSME During The Time Of Application. However, During The Duration Of The Scheme, The Company Moves Out Of MSME Category, Can It Still Claim Incentives Under MSME Segment.
answer: Yes, as per clause 3.8, the status of Applicants as MSMEs or Non-MSMEs will be determined at the time of selection only and it will remain so during the entire duration of the Scheme.

scheme_name: Electronics Component Manufacturing Scheme

scheme_name: Electronics Component Manufacturing Scheme

scheme_name: Electronics Component Manufacturing Scheme

scheme_name: Electronics Component Manufacturing Scheme

scheme_name: Electronics Component Manufacturing Scheme

scheme_name: Electronics Component Manufacturing Scheme

scheme_name: Electronics Component Manufacturing Scheme

scheme_name: Electronics Component Manufacturing Scheme

scheme_name: Electronics Component Manufacturing Scheme

scheme_name: Electronics Component Manufacturing Scheme

scheme_name: Establishment of 1 to 20 Milch Animal Farm

scheme_name: Establishment of 1 to 20 Milch Animal Farm

question: What does EPCG stand for and what is the benefit of an EPCG authorisation?
answer: EPCG stands for Export Promotion Capital Goods. The objective of this scheme is to facilitate the import of capital goods to produce quality goods and services to enhance India’s export competitiveness. EPCG scheme allows import of capital goods for pre-production, production, and post-production at zero customs duty.

scheme_name: Export Promotion Capital Goods Scheme
question: Who can benefit from the EPCG Scheme?
answer: Manufacturer exporters with or without supporting manufacturer(s), merchant exporters tied to supporting manufacturer(s) and service provider(s), and service providers. Refer to FTP and HBP for the latest details.

scheme_name: Export Promotion Capital Goods Scheme
question: If my IEC is in DEL/cancelled/suspended, am I eligible to apply for the EPCG authorisation?

scheme_name: Export Promotion Capital Goods Scheme
question: How is my export obligation period divided into blocks?
answer: Your export obligation period is defined for six years from the date of issuance of the authorisation. These six years are divided into two blocks, namely, the first block and the second block. The first block period is for the first four years from the date of issuance of the authorisation. Whereas, the following two years are known to be the second block period of your authorisation.

scheme_name: Export Promotion Capital Goods Scheme
question: Is there a time period for amendment of an issued authorisation?
answer: An authorisation may only be allowed for amendment until its import validity period. No authorisations shall be permitted for amendment post the validity period of the authorisation.

scheme_name: Export Promotion Capital Goods Scheme
question: What is the significance of initial and revised value of my authorisation validity dates?
answer: The initial and the revised values of the authorisation validity dates show the import and export validity dates as per the issued authorisations and amended validity dates (if any). If no extensions have been granted against the selected authorisation, the initial and the revised values shall be the same.

scheme_name: Export Promotion Capital Goods Scheme
question: What is the application fee for amendment?
answer: One per thousand for differential duty saved amount to be enhanced in addition to a flat fee of INR 200/- for amendment to the issued authorisation. No additional fee is required if the maximum prescribed fee has been paid initially.

scheme_name: Export Promotion Capital Goods Scheme

answer: You can only decrease the quantities of imported items if the bill of entries of these items already exists in the Shipping Bill Repository, i.e., post importing the item, you shall not be allowed to decrease the quantity of the item.

answer: Yes, those Goan employees paid a gross salary of less than ₹8,000/- per month are eligible for counting towards the percentage of Goan manpower, but they are excluded from the actual subsidy calculation.

scheme_name: Employment Subsidy Scheme, 2017
question: Is there a specific deadline by which my company must initiate the application process if we wish to avail of benefits that extend beyond the scheme's formal validity date?
answer: Yes, to be eligible for benefit disbursement beyond the scheme's validity (September 30, 2022), the applicant must submit an application for at least one claim to the Directorate of Industries, Trade and Commerce during the scheme’s validity period.

scheme_name: Employment Subsidy Scheme, 2017
question: How is an employee defined as a "Goan" for the strict purpose of calculating the percentage of local manpower required for eligibility?
answer: A "Goan" is defined as a person born in Goa, or a person having a ten years Residence Certificate issued by the Mamlatdar, or a person possessing other suitable documentation proving residence in Goa issued prior to ten years, such as a Driving license, Ration card, Election Photo Identity Card (EPIC), or Passport.

scheme_name: Employment Subsidy Scheme, 2017
question: Is there any maximum age limit specified for Goan employees whose salaries are included when determining the amount of the employment subsidy?
answer: Yes, for Goan employees to be considered eligible for inclusion in the subsidy calculation, they must be up to sixty years of age.

scheme_name: Employment Subsidy Scheme, 2017
question: If my company claims financial support for employment benefits under this program, am I barred from claiming assistance for similar expenses elsewhere?
answer: Yes, this scheme specifically states that it shall not be applicable to cases where a similar benefit has already been claimed under any other scheme or program operated by the Government of Goa.

scheme_name: Employment Subsidy Scheme, 2017
question: Are projects specifically related to tourism also allowed to apply, and if so, what special criteria must these projects meet?
answer: Yes, projects categorized as Hinterland Eco tourism in lesser developed talukas are eligible, provided they are registered with or recognized by the Department of Tourism, Goa-Investment Promotion Board, Town & Country Planning, Planning and Development Authority, or Eco Sensitive Zone Authority.

scheme_name: Employment Subsidy Scheme, 2017
question: Will an enterprise be eligible for this employment subsidy if they are currently receiving or have previously received incentives from the Department of Information Technology?
answer: No, enterprises that are currently taking or have previously taken any benefit under any policy offered by the Department of Information Technology, Government of Goa, shall not be eligible.

scheme_name: Employment Subsidy Scheme, 2017
question: For the purpose of meeting the required 60% Goan employment threshold, how must the employees be maintained on the enterprise’s records?
answer: The employees counted for the percentage calculation must be employed on the enterprise’s payroll continuously throughout the duration of the claim year to be considered for both the benefit calculation and the percentage requirement.

scheme_name: Employment Subsidy Scheme, 2017
question: What is the minimum percentage of local manpower that must be engaged by the enterprise to qualify for receiving benefits under this program?
answer: Enterprises must engage a minimum of 60% of Goan manpower on regular employment to be eligible for benefits under this scheme.

scheme_name: Employment Subsidy Scheme, 2017
question: Should I include family members or individuals related to me when calculating the total number of eligible employees for this employment program?
answer: No, relations defined under section 56 of the Income Tax Act, 1961, cannot be counted as employees for the purpose of calculating eligibility or subsidy under this scheme.

scheme_name: Entrepreneur Support Scheme
question: What is the aim of the scheme?
answer: The scheme aims to provide financial assistance to Micro, Small, and Medium Enterprises engaged in manufacturing activities in the State, proportional to the capital investment made.

scheme_name: Entrepreneur Support Scheme
question: What is the objective of the scheme?
answer: The objective of the scheme is to provide extensive support to micro, small and medium enterprises and give one-time support to entrepreneurs, with due regard to special categories by optimal utilization of funds and giving more flexibility of operation while implementing the Scheme.

scheme_name: Entrepreneur Support Scheme

scheme_name: Entrepreneur Support Scheme

scheme_name: Entrepreneur Support Scheme

answer: A person who has filed Entrepreneur Memorandum as per MSMED Act 2006 before the Industries Department and has taken effective steps to set up an industrial unit. (For the purpose of this scheme "effective steps" means purchase of land, apply for bank loan, placing orders for purchase of machinery or other demonstrable event in the life cycle of an industry.

scheme_name: Entrepreneur Support Scheme
question: What does 'Enterprise' mean?
answer: An industrial unit falling under Micro, Small or Medium category in the MSMED Act 2006.

scheme_name: Entrepreneur Support Scheme
question: What does “Women enterprise” mean?
answer: An enterprise in which at least 50% of the promoters are women.

scheme_name: Entrepreneur Support Scheme
question: What does “Young entrepreneur” mean?

At the time of filing application for assistance under Entrepreneur Support Scheme, the entrepreneur (s) should have attained 18 years of age as on the 1st April of the concerned financial year and should not have attained 46 years of age as on the 1st April of the concerned financial year.

scheme_name: Entrepreneur Support Scheme
question: What does “Scheduled Caste and Scheduled Tribe entrepreneur” mean?

In case of more than one promoter, then to be eligible for assistance under this Scheme, at least 50 % of the promoters shall be SC/ST.

scheme_name: Entrepreneur Support Scheme
question: What does “Negative List” mean?

scheme_name: Entrepreneur Support Scheme
question: What does “Pucca’ building” mean?

scheme_name: Entrepreneur Support Scheme
question: What does “Semi-pucca’ building” mean?

scheme_name: Entrepreneur Support Scheme
question: What does “New Technology” mean?

scheme_name: Entrepreneur Support Scheme

The recommending authority shall accept applications, receive due application fees, process the applications, place them before the sanctioning authority and disburse the assistance.

scheme_name: Entrepreneur Support Scheme
question: What does “Sanctioning authority” mean?

scheme_name: Entrepreneur Support Scheme

scheme_name: Entrepreneur Support Scheme

scheme_name: Entrepreneur Support Scheme

scheme_name: Entrepreneur Support Scheme

scheme_name: National Livestock Mission: Establishment of State Semen Bank

scheme_name: National Livestock Mission: Establishment of State Semen Bank

scheme_name: National Livestock Mission: Establishment of State Semen Bank

scheme_name: National Livestock Mission: Establishment of State Semen Bank

scheme_name: National Livestock Mission: Establishment of State Semen Bank

scheme_name: Foster Care Scheme (Vatsalaya)
question: How Are The Records Of Each Foster Care Case Maintained?
answer: The Child Care Coordinator maintains individual case files for each foster care case, which include school progress reports, medical investigations, and evaluation reports of the placement.

scheme_name: Foster Care Scheme (Vatsalaya)
question: How Can A Biological Family Or Legal Guardian Receive Financial Help For The Care Of Their Child After Restoration?
answer: If the biological family or legal guardian requires financial assistance for the care of their child after restoration, they may be referred for assistance under the Sponsorship Scheme.

scheme_name: Foster Care Scheme (Vatsalaya)
question: What Is The Process For Restoring A Child In Foster Care To Their Biological Parent Or Legal Guardian?
answer: Before restoring a child in foster care to their biological family, the Child Care Coordinator conducts a social inquiry to assess the family's suitability as a "fit person." The report is then presented to the Child Welfare Committee, which declares the family "fit" for restoration.

scheme_name: Foster Care Scheme (Vatsalaya)
question: What Kind Of Support Services Are Available To Foster Families When Necessary?
answer: The State provides supplementary services, including material and financial assistance for transport and medical expenses, as well as referrals to other community services like family counseling, child guidance clinics, community centers, and rehabilitation centers when necessary.

scheme_name: Foster Care Scheme (Vatsalaya)
question: How Is The Child's Health And Progress Monitored While In Foster Care?
answer: The foster parent(s) are responsible for conducting an annual medical check-up of the child. Additionally, the Child Care Coordinator prepares an annual progress report that includes the child's school progress reports, medical investigations, and evaluation reports of the placement.

scheme_name: Foster Care Scheme (Vatsalaya)
question: What Kind Of Programs Are Organized For The Foster Parents And Children Placed In Foster Care?
answer: Periodic programs are conducted by the Child Care Coordinator, focusing on enhancing parenting skills and providing awareness on health, immunization, and nutrition. Interactive sessions for foster parents and children are also organized.

scheme_name: Foster Care Scheme (Vatsalaya)
question: How Is The Placement Of A Child In Foster Care Regularly Assessed?
answer: The Child Care Coordinator conducts periodic assessments of the foster care placement and presents the reports for evaluation to the Child Welfare Committee. During the first year, assessment visits are conducted every three months, and later, they are carried out bi-annually.

scheme_name: Foster Care Scheme (Vatsalaya)
question: What Kind Of Assistance Do The Child Welfare Committee And The Child Care Coordinators Receive During Their Work?
answer: The Child Welfare Committee and the two Child Care Coordinators are assisted by a team of professionals, including a Social Worker, Child Psychologist, Legal Expert, and Doctor, drawn from an empanelled list of experts maintained by the Child Welfare Committee.

scheme_name: Foster Care Scheme (Vatsalaya)
question: How Are Foster Families Prepared For Their Role Before The Placement?
answer: Prior to the placement, the foster family receives orientation and periodic training from the Child Care Coordinator and the Department of Women and Child Development. These sessions aim to educate the foster parents about the needs and behavior of children and their roles and responsibilities.

scheme_name: Foster Care Scheme (Vatsalaya)
question: What Important Information Should Foster Care Applicants Be Aware Of Regarding Their Role And Responsibilities?
answer: Foster care applicants need to be informed about their role in executing rehabilitation plans, periodic assessment visits by the Child Care Coordinator or designated Case Worker, the duration of the placement, and the conditions that may lead to termination of the placement.

scheme_name: Foster Care Scheme (Vatsalaya)
question: After The Meeting, What Are The Next Steps For The Prospective Foster Parent(S)?
answer: The prospective foster parent(s) are given the opportunity to express their opinion on the placement within a week. They are also permitted to visit the child at least twice a week to facilitate bonding.

scheme_name: Foster Care Scheme (Vatsalaya)
question: What Is A Child Study Report, And Who Prepares It?
answer: The Child Care Coordinator prepares a Child Study Report within 15 days, providing details about the child who may be placed in foster care.

scheme_name: Foster Care Scheme (Vatsalaya)
question: What Happens After The Child Care Coordinator Completes The Assessment Of The Prospective Foster Parents?
answer: The assessment report is presented to the Child Welfare Committee within 15 days for discussion and approval. If needed, the Child Care Coordinator may seek assistance from NGOs during this process.

scheme_name: Foster Care Scheme (Vatsalaya)
question: How Are Prospective Foster Parents Assessed, And Who Is Responsible For Conducting This Assessment?
answer: The prospective foster parents undergo an assessment conducted by the Child Care Coordinator. The assessment includes home visits, meetings with family members, and collateral contacts, such as anganwadi workers, school personnel, and hospital staff. The assessment focuses on evaluating the potential, motivation, and capacities of the prospective foster parents.

scheme_name: Foster Care Scheme (Vatsalaya)
question: What Are The Initial Steps Taken When A Family Applies For Foster Care Under The Scheme?
answer: Upon receiving applications for foster care, the Child Welfare Committee holds an initial meeting with the foster care applicants to conduct preliminary inquiries and inform them about the scheme.

scheme_name: Foster Care Scheme (Vatsalaya)
question: What Happens When A Child In Need Of Foster Care Has Potential Foster Parents Related To Them, And Why Is It Necessary?
answer: In cases where the child's potential foster parents are related to them (e.g., foster parents could be relatives or family friends), the Child Welfare Committee may allow the child to reside with the family during the inquiry and assessment process to maintain the child's normal routine.

question: What is APEDA ?
answer: The Agricultural and Processed Food Products Export Development Authority (APEDA) was | established by the Government of India under the Agricultural and Processed Food Products Export Development Authority Act, 1985. The primary objective of APEDA is to undertake the development and promotion of the export of the following products. | i. Fruits, vegetables and their products, | ii. Meat and meat products, | iii. Poultry and poultry products, | iv. Dairy products, | v. Confectionary, biscuits, and bakery products, | vi. Honey, jaggery and sugar products, | vii. Cocoa and its products, chocolates of all kinds, | viii. Alcoholic and non-alcoholic beverages, | ix. Cereals and Cereal products, | x. Groundnuts, peanuts and walnuts, | xi. Pickles, chutneys and papads, | xii. Guar Gum | xiii. Floriculture and floriculture products, | xiv. Herbal and medicinal plants. | xv. Cashew kernels, cashew nut shell liquid, cardanol | The following specific objectives have been laid down in Section 10(2) of the APEDA Act: | i. The development of industries relating to the Scheduled products for export by way of providing financial assistance or otherwise for undertaking surveys and feasibility studies, | participation in the equity capital through joint ventures and other reliefs and subsidy | schemes; | ii. the registration of persons as exporters of the Scheduled products on payment of such fees as may be prescribed; | iii. The fixing of standards and specifications for the Scheduled products for the purposes of | export; | iv. the carrying out of inspection of meat and meat products in any slaughterhouse, processing, | plant, storage premises, conveyances, or other places where such products are kept or handled for the purpose of ensuring the quality of such products; | v. the improving of packaging of the Scheduled products; | vi. the improving of the marketing of the Scheduled products outside India; | vii. the promotion of export-oriented production and development of the Scheduled products; | viii. the collection of statistics from the owners of factories or establishments engaged in the | production, processing, packaging, marketing, or export of the Scheduled products or from | such other persons as may be prescribed on any matter relating to the Scheduled products; | and the publication of the statistics so collected, or of any portions thereof or extracts there | from; | ix. the training in various aspects of the industries connected with the Scheduled products; | x. such other matters as may be prescribed. | In addition to the above, APEDA has also been entrusted with the task of registration and protection of Intellectual Property rights in respect of 'Special Products' in India or Outside India. At present, the only 'Special Product', as listed in the Second Schedule to the APEDA Act, is Basmati Rice. After protracted efforts, APEDA was able to obtain GI registration for Basmati Rice in February 2016. APEDA is also the Secretariat for the National Programme for Organic Production, specifying the accreditation and certification programs for organic production. The organic certification programme covers all agricultural commodities including non-APEDA scheduled products. More than 10 lakh farmers are registered under the programme and the certification is a mandatory requirement for organic products exports. | For more information please visit: https://apeda.gov.in/apedawebsite/
