scheme_name: Modernisation And Removal Of Obsolescence
question: What Are The Names Of The Three Variants Of This Scheme?
answer: This scheme has three variants - | (i) MODROB- Aspiring Institutes | (ii) MODROB- Polytechnic | (iii) MODROB- Regular

scheme_name: Modernisation And Removal Of Obsolescence
question: For What Purposes Can The Funds Be Utilized?
answer: The funds under this Scheme could ideally be used to create technical infrastructure for a revised curriculum. for up-gradation of equipment in existing laboratories, enhancement of performance of existing equipment, or replacement of depreciated equipment with modern equipment.

scheme_name: Modernisation And Removal Of Obsolescence
question: What Will Be The Duration Of The Project?
answer: The duration of the project will be two years from the date of receipt of funds in the institute's account.

scheme_name: Modernisation And Removal Of Obsolescence
question: What Is The Limit Of Funding From AICTE?
answer: Funding for the sanctioned project will not exceed [?] 20,00,000 (covering recurring and non-recurring expenditures) per the proposal.

scheme_name: Modernisation And Removal Of Obsolescence
question: Will The Funds Be Disbursed In Installments Or As A Lump Sum?
answer: Disbursement of the Funds: | 80% of the sanctioned amount as advance to the institutions will be disbursed followed by 20% as reimbursement on submission of the Utilization Certificate and other supporting documents as specified in the terms and conditions of MODROB.

scheme_name: Modernisation And Removal Of Obsolescence
question: What Is The Eligibility Criteria For "MODROBS - Aspiring Institutions"?
answer: MODROBS - Aspiring Institutions | a) AICTE-approved technical institutions / University Departments with at least 10 years of existence (at least 5 years if the institute is located in a rural area). | b) The Institute shall have more than 50% admission for the past 3 years. | c) The Institute had not been sanctioned any MODROB Project earlier. | d) Maximum 3 proposals per institute per year (Not more than one proposal is accepted from the same department)

scheme_name: Modernisation And Removal Of Obsolescence
question: What Is The Eligibility Criteria For "MODROBS - Regular"?
answer: A) AICTE-approved technical institutions / University Departments with at least 10 years of existence (at least 5 years if the institute is located in a rural area) having live NBA accreditation | b) The Institute shall have more than 60% admission for the past 3 years. | c) The department applying should not have received the MODROB project in the last two years i.e. the department who have received a grant in the last two years are not eligible. | d) Maximum 3 proposals per institute per year (Including sanctioned earlier but not completed) would be considered. | e) Preference will be given to the institution having the involvement of industry in the modernization of the laboratory.

scheme_name: Modernisation And Removal Of Obsolescence
question: What Is The Eligibility Criteria For "MODROBS - Polytechnic"?
answer: MODROBS - Polytechnic | a) The Polytechnic Institute is approved by AICTE with at least 10 years of existence (at least 5 years if the institute is located in a rural area) | b) The Institute shall have more than 60 % admission for the past 3 years | c) Maximum 3 proposals per institute per year (Not more than one proposal is accepted from the same department)

scheme_name: Modernisation And Removal Of Obsolescence
question: We Are A Private University? Are We Eligible To Apply For This Scheme?
answer: AICTE-approved Technical Institutions (including Polytechnics) / University Departments can only apply for this Scheme. If, however, the private university is approved by AICTE, then you are eligible to apply.

scheme_name: Modernisation And Removal Of Obsolescence
question: The Project Duration Is 2 Years From The Date Of Receipt Of Funds In The Institute’s Account. Suppose, Due To Unforeseen Circumstances The Project Is Unable To Complete. Can I Get Extension From AICTE To Complete The Project?
answer: A.2 Yes. But, the institute must seek approval from AICTE at least two months before completion of the project duration and it may be extended upto a year/six months at a time. If you do not complete within this period, the sanctioned amount alongwith interest earned on it should be refunded to AICTE. It may be noted that delay beyond approved duration will affect consideration of proposals submitted in future.

scheme_name: Maintenance Of Pregnant Desi/Indigenous Cow/Buffalo Ration Scheme For BPL Families Belonging To Scheduled Caste (SC) Category

answer: The objective of this scheme is to (1) Increase milk production thereby providing more economic gains to the farmers. (4) Ensure the birth of healthy calves free of diseases and malnutrition so that they grow to become higher-producing animals (5) Motivate the farmers to rear such animals.

scheme_name: Maintenance Of Pregnant Desi/Indigenous Cow/Buffalo Ration Scheme For BPL Families Belonging To Scheduled Caste (SC) Category

scheme_name: Maintenance Of Pregnant Desi/Indigenous Cow/Buffalo Ration Scheme For BPL Families Belonging To Scheduled Caste (SC) Category

scheme_name: Meghalaya Piggery Development Scheme

scheme_name: The Mizoram Provisional Employees Savings Scheme

scheme_name: Meghalaya Poultry Farming Scheme

scheme_name: Madhya Pradesh Fasal Vividhikaran (Crop Diversification) Encouragement Scheme

scheme_name: Madhya Pradesh Fasal Vividhikaran (Crop Diversification) Encouragement Scheme

scheme_name: Madhya Pradesh Fasal Vividhikaran (Crop Diversification) Encouragement Scheme

scheme_name: Madhya Pradesh Fasal Vividhikaran (Crop Diversification) Encouragement Scheme

scheme_name: Madhya Pradesh Fasal Vividhikaran (Crop Diversification) Encouragement Scheme

scheme_name: Madhya Pradesh Fasal Vividhikaran (Crop Diversification) Encouragement Scheme
question: What is the crucial documentation that must be compulsorily submitted along with the initial application when applying to the Director, Farmer Welfare and Agriculture Development Department?
answer: The applicant Company, Firm, or Institution must prepare and present the Detailed Project Report (DPR) along with the application. This report is essential for project screening and final approval.

scheme_name: Madhya Pradesh Fasal Vividhikaran (Crop Diversification) Encouragement Scheme

scheme_name: Madhya Pradesh Fasal Vividhikaran (Crop Diversification) Encouragement Scheme

scheme_name: Madhya Pradesh Fasal Vividhikaran (Crop Diversification) Encouragement Scheme

scheme_name: Madhya Pradesh Fasal Vividhikaran (Crop Diversification) Encouragement Scheme

scheme_name: Madhya Pradesh Fasal Vividhikaran (Crop Diversification) Encouragement Scheme

scheme_name: Madhya Pradesh Janani Suraksha Yojana

scheme_name: Madhya Pradesh Janani Suraksha Yojana

scheme_name: National Post Doctoral Fellowship
question: Who can apply for NPDF? What are the eligibility criteria for availing the post-doctoral fellowship?
answer: The applicant should hold Ph.D. degree in Science or Engineering or M.D or M.S degree in any area of medicine. Those who have submitted their PhD/M. D/M. S thesis and are awaiting award of the degree are also eligible to apply. Applicants should have an outstanding track record as evident from the quality of the research outputs and publications. The selection will be based on the recommendations of an Expert Committee.

scheme_name: National Post Doctoral Fellowship
question: What is the age limit for availing NPDF?
answer: The upper age limit for the fellowship is 35 years at the time of the submission of application. Age relaxation of 5 (five) years will be given to candidates belonging to SC/ST/OBC/Physically Challenged & Women candidates.

scheme_name: National Post Doctoral Fellowship
question: What is the amount of fellowship?Is my fellowship taxable? Is the fellowship tenable outside India?
answer: The Fellowship amount for NPDF is [?]55,000/- per month. For those who have submitted their Ph.D. degree, [?]35,000/- per month will be offered till they are awarded the eligible degree. The fellowship is taxable under the Income Tax rules of India. The fellowship is tenable only in India and can be implemented in any of the recognized academic institutions, national laboratories and other recognized R&D institutions. The host institution should provide necessary administrative and infrastructural support.

scheme_name: National Post Doctoral Fellowship
question: What is the tenure of the NPDF? Can it be extended?
answer: The fellowship is purely a temporary assignment, and is tenable initially for a period of 2 years. In exceptional cases, depending on the progress of research, the fellowship can be extended for one more year. There is no provision to extend the tenure beyond three years in any case.

scheme_name: National Post Doctoral Fellowship
question: What is the upper age limit up to which the J C Bose fellowship can be availed?Can I avail the NPDF from the same institution from where I have obtained the Ph. D. degree? Can I avail other fellowship grants?
answer: The fellowship is generally not availed at the same institution where one has obtained or worked for the PhD/M.S./M.D degree. Also, the fellowship cannot be availed with the doctoral thesis supervisor or co-supervisor as a mentor. The fellows are not eligible to receive fellowship/salary from any other Government or Non-Governmental source during the tenure of the SERB National Post-Doctoral Fellowship.

scheme_name: National Post Doctoral Fellowship
question: What is the nature of support in NPDF scheme?
answer: National Post-Doctoral Fellow will be entitled to receive grants under the following budget heads. | The fellows will be entitled to receive the grants given below: | Fellowship | ([?]55,000/- per month (consolidated)) | ([?]35,000/ p.m. for candidates who have submitted the thesis but the degree has not yet been awarded) | Research Grant ([?]2,00,000/- per annum) | Overheads ([?]1,00,000/- per annum)

scheme_name: National Post Doctoral Fellowship
question: When should I apply for NPDF? Can I apply for the National Post-Doctoral Fellowship (N- PDF) projects throughout the year?
answer: The applicant must first identify the host institution and a suitable Mentor in the host institution under which the proposed research objectives will be pursued. The call for applications for SERB- NPDF will be notified through the website www.serbonline.in and www.serb.gov.in Usually one month window will be provided to submit the application along with other documents. All applications should be submitted through the SERB online portal www.serbonline.in.

scheme_name: National Post Doctoral Fellowship
question: Who is eligible to be a Mentor? Can my Ph.D. supervisor or co-supervisor act as a mentor?
answer: The Mentor should hold a regular academic or research position in the host institution. The fellowship cannot be availed with the doctoral thesis supervisor or co-supervisor as a mentor.

scheme_name: National Post Doctoral Fellowship
question: How should I apply for NPDF? What documents should I submit?
answer: All applications should be submitted through the SERB online portal www.serbonline.in. Usually, a month window is provided to submit the application along with other documents. The following documents are mandatory. | Research proposal (see www.serbonline.in for the correct format). | Proof of Date of Birth (Class X certificate or Date of Birth Certificate). | Proof of Caste (only for cases seeking age relaxation). | Proof of Ph.D. Degree or proof of Ph.D. thesis submission certificate. | Endorsement Certificate signed by Mentor and Head of the Host Institution (format can be downloaded from www.serbonline.in). | Undertaking Certificate by the applicant (see online portal for its format). | Reprints of your two best publications. | CV of the Mentor (see online portal for its format). | The applicants are advised to follow detailed instructions provided in the SERB online portal www.serbonline.in.

scheme_name: National Post Doctoral Fellowship
question: When will I be informed of my selection?
answer: The selection process on an average takes at least two months from the last date of submission of the applications. All selected candidates shall receive an Email notification through the SERB online portal, who are then required to download the offer letter.

scheme_name: National Post Doctoral Fellowship
question: Is there any break up available for the NPDF research grant?
answer: Flexibility is provided to the Fellow and the Mentor for utilising the Research Grant as per the needs of the research work. Generally, the Research grant can be used for purchasing minor equipment, consumables and contingencies. The grant can also be utilised for travel in India to attend workshops/conferences and other research-related activities. In this regard, the host institution's norms shall apply for TA/DA.

scheme_name: National Post Doctoral Fellowship
question: Can I recruit a manpower under this scheme?
answer: There is no provision for providing manpower under this scheme. The Fellow is expected to undertake research himself/herself during the entire duration of the fellowship.

scheme_name: National Post Doctoral Fellowship
question: I have received my fellowship for the first year. What documents should I send to receive my scholarship for the second year?
answer: The Fellows should upload annual Progress Report and financial statements at the end of each financial year. The release of the next instalment of the grant will be considered only after submission of (a) Proper Utilization Certificate and Statement of Expenditure, financial year wise and (b) Annual Progress Report through the SERB online portal.

scheme_name: National Post Doctoral Fellowship
question: I intend to change my Mentor/Host Institution? What procedure should I follow?
answer: Change of Mentor/Host Institution is generally discouraged and can be allowed only in exceptional cases. Change of Host Institution shall be undertaken only after obtaining due approval from SERB. The new host institute in any case should not be the institution from which the applicant has worked for his Ph.D. or obtained his Ph.D. degree. The transfer of the fellowship along with balance grant and the assets to the new institute is allowed, provided the administrative authority of both institutes agree in writing. NOC from the previous host institute and Endorsement Form from the new host Institute &new Mentor must be sent to SERB through the online portal.

scheme_name: National Post Doctoral Fellowship
question: I wish to resign as NPDF? What documents must I send to SERB?
answer: If the one wishes to terminate the fellowship and leave the institute, he/she shall inform the SERB through the host institution immediately. The implementing institute should not incur any expenditure from the date of termination of the project or the date of resignation of fellow.

scheme_name: National Post Doctoral Fellowship
question: What are the rules for availing leave?
answer: The NPDF is entitled to leave as per the norms of the host institution. Participation in scientific workshops held in India or abroad will be treated as on duty. Maternity leave, as per the Govt. of India instructions issued from time to time, would be available to female candidates in all categories.

scheme_name: National Post Doctoral Fellowship
question: Is SERB terminate NPDF fellowship?
answer: SERB reserves the right to terminate the Fellowship at any stage if it is convinced that appropriate progress is not being made or the grant has not been utilized properly.

scheme_name: National Post Doctoral Fellowship
question: Can I be away from the implementing Institute when I am working as National Post-Doctoral Fellow?
answer: The fellows must seek the consent of SERB if he/she intends to be away from the implementing institute (except for field work related to the project) continuously for a period more than eight weeks.

scheme_name: National Post Doctoral Fellowship
question: What should be done for the unspent grant under National Post-Doctoral Fellowship (N- PDF) after the completion of the tenure of the fellowship?
answer: The following documents should be sent to the SERB after the duration of the Fellowship is completed: | Final Consolidated Statement of Expenditure (in duplicate), giving expenditure financial year wise (FY) from date of start till date of completion. | Utilization Certificates (FY wise) for all FYs (in duplicate) matching with Statement of Expenditure figures in that FY. | Project Completion Report (PCR) with list of publications, and patents filed. | DD/ cheque for the unspent grant, drawn in favor of 'Fund for Science & Engineering Research' | Mentor and PDF candidate are responsible for the timely submission of progress report, utilization certificate, project closure report (PCR), refund of unspent balance amount etc. at the end or early closure of the project.

scheme_name: National Agriculture Insurance Scheme
question: What is the National Agriculture Insurance Scheme (NAIS)?
answer: The National Agriculture Insurance Scheme (NAIS) is a government initiative aimed at providing financial protection to farmers against crop losses due to natural calamities, pests, and diseases. It offers coverage for food crops, oilseeds, and select horticultural crops.

scheme_name: National Agriculture Insurance Scheme
question: Who is eligible to apply for NAIS?
answer: All farmers growing insurable crops and availing Seasonal Agricultural Operations (SAO) loans from Banks / PACS are compulsorily covered under the | Scheme by the Banks/ PACS, whereas the non-borrowing farmers growing insurable crops can also avail the benefit of the Scheme by submitting prescribed proposal forms at the nearest Banks/ PACS.

scheme_name: National Agriculture Insurance Scheme
question: How can famar apply for the NAIS?
answer: Loanee Farmers: The application is processed through the bank or financial institution from where the loan is availed. The premium is deducted directly from the loan amount. | Non-Loanee Farmers: They need to approach the nearest bank or insurance office, fill out the application form, submit required documents, and pay the premium.

scheme_name: National Agriculture Insurance Scheme
question: What is the premium amount for the scheme?
answer: Food Crops (Kharif): 3.5% of the sum insured. | Food Crops (Rabi): 1.5% of the sum insured. | Commercial and Horticultural Crops: Premium is based on actuarial rates.

scheme_name: National Agriculture Insurance Scheme
question: Are there any subsidies on the premium?
answer: Yes, the government provides premium subsidies, particularly for small and marginal farmers, to make the scheme affordable. The premium subsidy is shared between the central and state governments.

scheme_name: National Agriculture Insurance Scheme
question: What documents are required to apply for NAIS?
answer: Aadhaar card or another government-issued identity proof. | Proof of land records (ownership or tenancy). | Crop sowing certificate (if applicable). | Bank account details for claim settlement.

scheme_name: National Agriculture Insurance Scheme
question: How are claims processed under NAIS?
answer: Farmers must inform the local authorities or insurer about crop loss within 48 hours. | A joint assessment of the loss is carried out by insurance representatives and local officials. | After verification, the claims are settled and directly transferred to the farmer's bank account.

scheme_name: National Agriculture Insurance Scheme
question: Can non-loanee farmers apply for NAIS?
answer: Yes, non-loanee farmers can voluntarily apply for NAIS by visiting an authorized bank branch or insurance office. They need to submit necessary documents and pay the premium.

scheme_name: National Agriculture Insurance Scheme
question: How many states are participating in the scheme?
answer: At present this scheme is being implemented in 23 States and UTs (except Punjab, Manipur, Nagaland, Mizoram and Arunachal Pradesh among the States | and Chandigarh, Daman & Diu, Delhi, Dadra & Nagar Haveli and Lakshadweep among the UTs).

answer: Crop loans disbursed/withdrawn through KCCs are also eligible for coverage as per the terms and conditions applicable to the regular crop loans.

scheme_name: National Action for Mechanised Sanitation Ecosystem (NAMASTE) - "Emergency Response Sanitation Unit (ERSU) Formation and Functionalisation"
question: What is the primary purpose of establishing Emergency Response Sanitation Units across urban areas in India?
answer: Emergency Response Sanitation Units are established to systemize human entry into sewer and septic tanks through the organization of a professional, well-trained, motivated and appropriately equipped establishment for mechanized cleaning operations.

scheme_name: National Action for Mechanised Sanitation Ecosystem (NAMASTE) - "Emergency Response Sanitation Unit (ERSU) Formation and Functionalisation"
question: Which authority is responsible for overseeing the Emergency Response Sanitation Units in each district?
answer: The District Magistrate in every district can be designated as the Responsible Sanitation Authority with clearly defined roles and responsibilities through statute to oversee sanitation response operations.

scheme_name: National Action for Mechanised Sanitation Ecosystem (NAMASTE) - "Emergency Response Sanitation Unit (ERSU) Formation and Functionalisation"
question: Where will the Emergency Response Sanitation Units be physically located within the district structure?
answer: A well-equipped Sanitation Response Unit shall be set up in the headquarters of the Urban Local Body of the district, with a mandate to serve the entire district covering both rural and urban areas.

scheme_name: National Action for Mechanised Sanitation Ecosystem (NAMASTE) - "Emergency Response Sanitation Unit (ERSU) Formation and Functionalisation"
question: What is the geographical coverage area that each Emergency Response Sanitation Unit is expected to serve?
answer: Each Emergency Response Sanitation Unit established in the largest Urban Local Body of each district shall service emergency cleaning operations in both urban areas and the peripheral rural jurisdiction of that district.

scheme_name: National Action for Mechanised Sanitation Ecosystem (NAMASTE) - "Emergency Response Sanitation Unit (ERSU) Formation and Functionalisation"
question: How many Emergency Response Sanitation Units are anticipated to be established nationwide under this initiative?
answer: Approximately 1000 Sanitation Response Units are likely to be set up across the country for emergency cleaning of sewers and septic tanks.

scheme_name: National Action for Mechanised Sanitation Ecosystem (NAMASTE) - "Emergency Response Sanitation Unit (ERSU) Formation and Functionalisation"
question: What is the preferred helpline number that Emergency Response Sanitation Units should operationalize for receiving service requests?
answer: Emergency Response Sanitation Units should operationalize helpline number 14420 to receive service requests from citizens for cleaning of sewer septic tanks and related emergency services.

scheme_name: National Action for Mechanised Sanitation Ecosystem (NAMASTE) - "Emergency Response Sanitation Unit (ERSU) Formation and Functionalisation"
question: Which specific sanitation workers are permitted to undertake manual cleaning operations through Emergency Response Sanitation Units?
answer: Only skilled and certified Sewer and Septic Tank Workers designated as Sewer Entry Professionals will undertake manual cleaning of septic tanks, machine holes, and sewer lines in exceptional cases.

scheme_name: National Action for Mechanised Sanitation Ecosystem (NAMASTE) - "Emergency Response Sanitation Unit (ERSU) Formation and Functionalisation"
question: What safety equipment and devices will Emergency Response Sanitation Units receive for conducting deep cleaning operations?
answer: Emergency Response Sanitation Units will receive safety devices including air compressor for blower, air purified gas mask, breathing apparatus, emergency medical oxygen kit, full body wader suit, safety harness, and other protective equipment.

scheme_name: National Action for Mechanised Sanitation Ecosystem (NAMASTE) - "Emergency Response Sanitation Unit (ERSU) Formation and Functionalisation"
question: What is the maximum financial assistance provided to Emergency Response Sanitation Units for procurement of safety devices?
answer: Safety devices costing up to ₹2,00,000 will be provided to Emergency Response Sanitation Units on reimbursement basis for conducting safe manual cleaning operations in emergency situations.

scheme_name: National Action for Mechanised Sanitation Ecosystem (NAMASTE) - "Emergency Response Sanitation Unit (ERSU) Formation and Functionalisation"
question: Under what conditions will Emergency Response Sanitation Units be eligible to receive safety devices and equipment?
answer: Emergency Response Sanitation Units will receive safety devices after appointment of Responsible Sanitation Authority, establishment of functional helpline number, completion of profiling of Sewer and Septic Tank Workers, and their occupational training.

scheme_name: National Action for Mechanised Sanitation Ecosystem (NAMASTE) - "Emergency Response Sanitation Unit (ERSU) Formation and Functionalisation"
question: Which ministry is responsible for providing specific training to Emergency Response Sanitation Unit staff for emergency cleaning operations?
answer: Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs will provide specific training to Sewer Entry Professionals and Emergency Response Sanitation Unit staff for cleaning sewers and septic tanks in emergency conditions.

scheme_name: National Action for Mechanised Sanitation Ecosystem (NAMASTE) - "Emergency Response Sanitation Unit (ERSU) Formation and Functionalisation"
question: What type of training approach will be adopted for strengthening Emergency Response Sanitation Unit operations?
answer: A competency-based approach for training will be adopted creating an ecosystem for delivering simulation and video-based training, practical assessments and certification matching global standards.

scheme_name: National Action for Mechanised Sanitation Ecosystem (NAMASTE) - "Emergency Response Sanitation Unit (ERSU) Formation and Functionalisation"
question: Which categories of sanitation work are Emergency Response Sanitation Units specifically mandated to handle?
answer: Emergency Response Sanitation Units are mandated to handle emptying of septic tanks, sewerage network maintenance, and mechanized cleaning operations requiring professional intervention.

scheme_name: National Action for Mechanised Sanitation Ecosystem (NAMASTE) - "Emergency Response Sanitation Unit (ERSU) Formation and Functionalisation"
question: How will Emergency Response Sanitation Units coordinate with rural sanitation bodies in their operational area?
answer: Department of Drinking Water and Sanitation shall collaborate with Emergency Response Sanitation Units for sensitization of rural bodies for availing emergency cleaning services in peripheral rural areas.

scheme_name: National Action Plan for Skill Development of Persons with Disabilities
question: O is responsible for developing or customizing job roles for Persons with Disabilities (PwDs) under this scheme, and what types of courses are generally provided?
answer: Sector Skill Councils for PwDs are responsible for job role development, and training is typically offered in NSQF-aligned courses developed by SCPwD and other Sector Skill Councils.

scheme_name: National Action Plan for Skill Development of Persons with Disabilities
question: Can organizations enter into MOUs with specific companies to create special courses, and are assessment and certification based on specific criteria?
answer: Yes, MOUs can lead to customized courses, and assessment and certification are conducted based on National Occupational Standards (NOS).

scheme_name: National Action Plan for Skill Development of Persons with Disabilities
question: What role do Employability Skills (E.S.) courses play in the training, and what are the minimum qualifications and experience required for Trainers?
answer: E.S. courses are mandatory before Domain Skills, and Trainers must meet the qualifications and experience as specified in the Qualification Pack (QP).

scheme_name: National Action Plan for Skill Development of Persons with Disabilities
question: Who conducts the assessment, and what criteria are used, and what is the role of the NDFDC in monitoring training provided by training partners?
answer: Assessment is done by SCPwD or authorized agencies based on QP criteria, and NDFDC monitors training quality.

scheme_name: National Action Plan for Skill Development of Persons with Disabilities
question: Can the Department inspect the premises of Training Partners, and what is the budget allocation for administrative expenses?
answer: Yes, the Department can inspect premises. Administrative expenses utilize 3% of the NAP-SDP budget.

scheme_name: National Action Plan for Skill Development of Persons with Disabilities
question: What are the components covered under administrative expenses, and what norms apply to the funding of this scheme?
answer: Administrative expenses include human resources, publicity, monitoring, software development, and more. The funding norms follow Common Norms for Skill Development Schemes.

scheme_name: National Action Plan for Skill Development of Persons with Disabilities
question: What organizations are responsible for developing the training curriculum, and what are the requirements for linking trainee details?
answer: Sector Skill Councils for PwDs develop the curriculum, and trainee details should be linked with UDID Card numbers or enrollment numbers and disability certificates if UDID cards are unavailable.

scheme_name: National Action Plan for Skill Development of Persons with Disabilities
question: How can organizations prove placements, and when will projects be canceled if they don't commence?
answer: Organizations must submit documents as proof of placements, and projects not commencing within two months from approval will be automatically canceled.

scheme_name: National Centre For Communication Security (NCCS) Internship Scheme
question: What is the full name of NCCS? Which department manages this organization?
answer: The full name of NCCS is "National Centre for Communication Security".

scheme_name: National Centre For Communication Security (NCCS) Internship Scheme
question: What are the areas of activity of NCCS?
answer: NCCS is technical centre of DoT that is vested with the responsibility of developing Security standards/ requirements called Indian | Telecom Security Assurance Requirements (ITSAR) and activities associated with the security testing and certification of Telecom equipment.  |  Framing of ITSAR involves Study of chosen Telecom network element and security testing for sample telecom network elements in areas like Security functional requirements, Software code assurance, Cryptographic related tests by people with specific domain expertise. It also involves certain amount of research work in areas like Hardware level Security, Source Code | analysis (Static and dynamic analysis at HLL, Binary Code Analysis) Crypto algorithm implementation validation and Crypto Module validation, Supply chain vulnerabilities, Run time vulnerabilities in a live network (Advanced Persistent Threats), Back door entry | vulnerabilities, Identification of Intentional/ Hidden Malware in Software/ Firmware of equipment.

scheme_name: National Centre For Communication Security (NCCS) Internship Scheme
question: How many interns are selected for a batch?
answer: The total number of interns engaged shall not exceed 20, at any point in time.

scheme_name: National Centre For Communication Security (NCCS) Internship Scheme
question: What shall be the duration of the internship for the "Category 1" Interns?
answer: For Category 1: The minimum duration of the internship shall be of sixty days.

scheme_name: National Centre For Communication Security (NCCS) Internship Scheme
question: What shall be the duration of the internship for the "Category 2" Interns?
answer: For Category 2: The minimum duration of the internship shall be of six months, extendable up to a maximum of twelve months.

scheme_name: National Centre For Communication Security (NCCS) Internship Scheme
question: Is the duration of the internship extendable?
answer: Yes, extension beyond six months shall be permitted, on the application of an intern duly recommended by the concerned Head of Division and with the approval of the Head of NCCS.

scheme_name: National Centre For Communication Security (NCCS) Internship Scheme
question: Will there be an induction/orientation program for the students selected for the internship?
answer: Yes, an orientation workshop will be held for interns at the beginning of the internship.

scheme_name: National Centre For Communication Security (NCCS) Internship Scheme
question: By whom shall the attendance record of the students be maintained?
answer: The attendance record and the details of work supervision shall be maintained by the Divisions/Units in NCCS.

scheme_name: National Centre For Communication Security (NCCS) Internship Scheme
question: Is the submission of paper a mandatory requirement for the successful completion of the internship?
answer: Yes, the interns will be required to submit a Report/Paper on the work undertaken at the end of the internship to the respective Division. The Report shall be signed by the concerned Officer with whom the intern is attached, as an acceptance of the successful completion of the Internship.

scheme_name: National Centre For Communication Security (NCCS) Internship Scheme
question: How much shall be the token remuneration for ‘Category 1’ Interns?
answer: Interns selected under Category 1 will be paid a token remuneration @ ₹ 7,500/- per month on prorate basis.

scheme_name: National Centre For Communication Security (NCCS) Internship Scheme
question: How much shall be the token remuneration for category 2 interns?
answer: Interns selected under Category 2 will be paid a token remuneration @ ₹ 15,000/- per month on prorate basis.

scheme_name: National Centre For Communication Security (NCCS) Internship Scheme
question: When shall the amount of the token remuneration become payable?
answer: The remuneration shall be paid after the completion of the month subject to satisfactory progress of work duly accepted by the concerned division from the earlier "Professional Services" head of Accounts, which has now been revised to " Salaries" Head of account in view of Operationalization of revised/new object heads under Rule 8 of DFPR,1978.

scheme_name: National Centre For Communication Security (NCCS) Internship Scheme
question: Will any logistics & support be provided by NCCS to the interns?
answer: NCCS shall provide them with working space, workplace Internet facility and other necessities as deemed fit by the concerned Head of Division.

scheme_name: National Centre For Communication Security (NCCS) Internship Scheme
question: Will the laptop/desktop be provided by NCCS?
answer: No, the Interns will be required to have their own laptops.

scheme_name: National Centre For Communication Security (NCCS) Internship Scheme
question: Where can I find the link to the scheme guidelines?
answer: The link to the Scheme Guidelines is: https://nccs.gov.in/public/latest_updates/NCCS%20Internship%20Notification%20-%20Q4%2025%20Signed.pdf

scheme_name: National Centre For Communication Security (NCCS) Internship Scheme
question: Is there any kind of reservation / preference / priority in the selection of the candidates?
answer: Candidates having exposure in the area of intended internship with good academic background and having higher qualifications, based on need shall be given preference.

answer: The full name of NCCS is "National Centre for Communication Security". It is a subordinate office of Department of Telecommunications, Ministry of Communications, Government of India.

scheme_name: National Centre for Communication Security (NCCS) Research Associates Scheme

scheme_name: National Centre for Communication Security (NCCS) Research Associates Scheme

scheme_name: National Centre for Communication Security (NCCS) Research Associates Scheme

scheme_name: National Centre for Communication Security (NCCS) Research Associates Scheme

scheme_name: National Centre for Earth Science Studies Internship Scheme
question: What is the “National Centre for Earth Science Studies Internship” scheme?
answer: The "National Centre for Earth Science Studies Internship" scheme is an initiative by the Earth System Science Organization, Ministry of Earth Sciences, to provide opportunities for school and college students to familiarize themselves with and pursue research in different branches of earth sciences.

scheme_name: National Centre for Earth Science Studies Internship Scheme
question: Who can apply for this internship?
answer: The internship is open to school students as well as college students who are interested in exploring and conducting research in the field of earth sciences.

scheme_name: National Centre for Earth Science Studies Internship Scheme
question: What kind of research opportunities are available under this scheme?
answer: The scheme offers opportunities to work on various branches of earth sciences, including but not limited to geology, oceanography, meteorology, and environmental science. Students can engage in hands-on research projects and gain exposure to advanced scientific methodologies.

scheme_name: National Centre for Earth Science Studies Internship Scheme
question: Is the National Centre for Earth Science Studies (NCESS) recognized for any academic programs?
answer: Yes, NCESS is an R&D institution recognized for doctoral programs in science, environmental, and interdisciplinary topics. It also offers opportunities for Ph.D. registration announced by universities.

scheme_name: National Centre for Earth Science Studies Internship Scheme
question: Are there any programs for scientific exchange at NCESS?
answer: Yes, NCESS hosts eminent scientists for scientific exchange programs, fostering collaboration and knowledge sharing within the scientific community.

scheme_name: National Centre for Earth Science Studies Internship Scheme
question: What opportunities does NCESS offer for students?
answer: NCESS provides various opportunities for school and college students to familiarize themselves with and pursue research in different branches of earth sciences. These include an open day for school students, internship/summer training, and dissertation programs for university students.

scheme_name: National Centre for Earth Science Studies Internship Scheme
question: When is the open day for school students held?
answer: The open day is observed in April every year, coinciding with Earth Day celebrations.

scheme_name: National Centre for Earth Science Studies Internship Scheme
question: What programs are available for university students at NCESS?
answer: NCESS offers Internship/Summer training and Dissertation programs to selected candidates as part of their curriculum. Additionally, research scholars can register for Ph.D. programs under science, environmental, and interdisciplinary topics when announcements are made by the universities.

scheme_name: National Centre for Earth Science Studies Internship Scheme
question: When can students apply for internships/training/dissertation at NCESS?
answer: Applications can be submitted during February and September every year. The online form is active from 01 February to 28 February and from 01 September to 30 September.

scheme_name: National Centre for Earth Science Studies Internship Scheme
question: How should interested candidates apply?
answer: Candidates must apply in the prescribed format available on the NCESS website. Selected candidates need to bring a printout of their application forms, duly signed by the HOD of their respective department with an official seal, at the time of arrival for training.

scheme_name: National Centre for Earth Science Studies Internship Scheme
question: What is the selection process?
answer: Shortlisted candidates, approved by the Director of NCESS, will be announced on the website in the first week of May and the first week of December. The list will also mention the allocated supervisor/group and the title of the internship/training/dissertation.

scheme_name: National Centre for Earth Science Studies Internship Scheme
question: Can candidates choose their supervisors?
answer: No, supervisors and Internship/Training/Dissertation students are not allowed to select each other. A suitable supervisor will be allotted based on the applications and the applicant's research interests.

scheme_name: National Centre for Earth Science Studies Internship Scheme
question: What is the duration of the internship/ training/ dissertation?
answer: Students must undergo at least 8 weeks of training continuously at NCESS.

scheme_name: National Centre for Earth Science Studies Internship Scheme
question: Are field trips allowed during the program?
answer: Only day field trips (no overnight stay) are allowed for visiting students. Prior approval from the Visiting Students Committee and the Director of NCESS is mandatory for any field work.

scheme_name: National Centre for Earth Science Studies Internship Scheme
question: Are students allowed on the NCESS campus during weekends and holidays?
answer: Visiting students are allowed on the NCESS campus on working days only. In exceptional conditions, they may be allowed on weekends and holidays with prior approval from the Supervisor and Group Head.

scheme_name: National Centre for Earth Science Studies Internship Scheme
question: What are the requirements for completing the internship/training/dissertation?
answer: Students must deliver a 15-minute presentation (10-minute presentation + 5-minute discussion) at the end of their training/dissertation period. Post-presentation, students can get their report/dissertation signed by the supervisor and submit it to the visiting students' committee for issuing the certificate. The report/ dissertation must also be submitted to the NCESS library for future reference.

scheme_name: National Centre for Earth Science Studies Internship Scheme
question: Is consent required for publishing work resulting from the project?
answer: Yes, any publication or communication to a journal that results from the project work must have the consent of both the Guide and NCESS.

scheme_name: National Centre for Earth Science Studies Internship Scheme
question: Will accommodation and transport be provided to project students?
answer: No, NCESS does not provide accommodation or transport for project students.

scheme_name: National Centre for Earth Science Studies Internship Scheme
question: Is there a fee for carrying out project works at NCESS?
answer: No, there is no fee for carrying out project works at NCESS.

scheme_name: National Centre for Earth Science Studies Internship Scheme
question: Can NCESS decline or discontinue project requests?
answer: Yes, NCESS reserves the right to not consider any or all requests and to close or discontinue the program without assigning any reasons.

scheme_name: National Centre for Earth Science Studies Internship Scheme
question: Within what time frame the visiting students have to accept the Internship/ Training/ Dissertation offer?
answer: Visiting students need to accept the Internship/Training/Dissertation offer within 7-10 working days from the date of the offer.

scheme_name: National Centre for Earth Science Studies Internship Scheme
question: What happens if a visiting student does not accept the offer within the specified time frame?
answer: If no reply is received within 7-10 working days, the offer will be transferred to other applicants depending on the waiting list.

scheme_name: Nehru Child Literature Prize

answer: The Nehru Children's Literature Prize is an award given to authors of children's literature published in Tamil, aimed at recognizing and encouraging quality writing for children.

scheme_name: Nehru Child Literature Prize
question: Who is eligible to apply for the Nehru Child Literature Prize?
answer: Authors born in Puducherry or who have resided continuously in the Union Territory of Puducherry for at least five years prior to the application date are eligible.

scheme_name: Nehru Child Literature Prize
question: What type of works are eligible for submission?
answer: Eligible works include novels, short stories, poems, plays, travelogues, collections of essays, and other forms of children's literature written in Tamil.

scheme_name: Nehru Child Literature Prize
question: What is the prize for the winning author?
answer: The winning author will receive [?]10,000/- along with a certificate.

scheme_name: Nehru Child Literature Prize

answer: A previous winner is ineligible to apply for the next four years.

scheme_name: Nehru Child Literature Prize

answer: No, translations, abridgements, adaptations, or paraphrases of other texts are not eligible.

scheme_name: Nehru Child Literature Prize
question: What are the requirements for submitting an application?
answer: Applicants must submit a complete application form, a separate form for each publication, five copies of the text, and the author's signature on the application form.

scheme_name: Nehru Child Literature Prize
question: What is the page limit for the submitted children's literature?
answer: The children's literature should not exceed 120 pages.

scheme_name: Nehru Child Literature Prize
question: How are the submitted works evaluated?
answer: A five-member committee of experts appointed by the Government scrutinizes the books and selects the prize winner.

scheme_name: Nehru Child Literature Prize
question: Can multiple authors submit a joint work for the competition?
answer: Yes, joint works can be submitted, and the prize money will be distributed among the authors if they win.

scheme_name: Nehru Child Literature Prize
question: What happens if there are issues with the implementation of the scheme?
answer: The Government's decision regarding any issues with the scheme's implementation is final and binding.

scheme_name: Nehru Child Literature Prize
question: Can the Government change the regulations of the scheme?
answer: Yes, the Government has the full power to amend, alter, or delete any provisions related to the scheme as needed.

scheme_name: Nehru Child Literature Prize
question: When must the submitted texts be published to be eligible?
answer: Texts must be printed and published as first editions by 31st December of the specified year to be eligible.

scheme_name: New Charkha-Loom Scheme

scheme_name: New Charkha-Loom Scheme

scheme_name: New Charkha-Loom Scheme
question: What documents are required to claim the subsidy for an Amber Charkha?
answer: Purchase invoices, Khadi certification, proof of registration, and bank details are needed.

scheme_name: New Charkha-Loom Scheme

answer: The scheme covers both, with separate subsidies (₹8,450/- for Charkhas, ₹19,500/- for looms).

scheme_name: New Charkha-Loom Scheme
question: Where should applicants submit their subsidy application forms?
answer: Forms must be submitted at the nearest Khadi institution or Cottage Industries Office.

scheme_name: New Charkha-Loom Scheme
question: Are non-Khadi weavers eligible for this subsidy?

scheme_name: New Charkha-Loom Scheme

scheme_name: New Charkha-Loom Scheme
question: What proof is required to confirm active Khadi production?
answer: The applicant’s Khadi institution certification serves as proof of active production.

scheme_name: New Charkha-Loom Scheme
question: Can applicants buy equipment from any vendor, or are there approved sellers?
answer: Equipment must be purchased from approved vendors (implied by invoice submission).

scheme_name: New Charkha-Loom Scheme
question: Does the scheme cover repairs or upgrades to existing Charkhas/looms?
answer: No, only new purchases of Amber Charkhas and looms are subsidized.

scheme_name: Natural Calamity Relief to Fishermen of State

scheme_name: Natural Calamity Relief to Fishermen of State

scheme_name: Natural Calamity Relief to Fishermen of State
question: What are the types of fishing nets covered under the scheme, and what is the financial limit for each type?
answer: Gill Nets: [?]50,000, Rampon Nets: [?]1,00,000, Trawl Net: [?]50,000, Purseine Net: [?]5,00,000.

scheme_name: Natural Calamity Relief to Fishermen of State
question: Is there a deadline for submitting applications under this scheme?

scheme_name: Natural Calamity Relief to Fishermen of State
question: What is the mode of application for the scheme, and is there an application fee?

scheme_name: Natural Calamity Relief to Fishermen of State
question: Is financial assistance provided for loss or damage due to accidental fire, and what is the maximum limit?

scheme_name: Natural Calamity Relief to Fishermen of State
question: Are there any restrictions on the type of calamities covered by the scheme?

scheme_name: Natural Calamity Relief to Fishermen of State
question: What actions can disqualify an applicant from receiving financial assistance?

scheme_name: Natural Calamity Relief to Fishermen of State

scheme_name: National Career Service Centers For SC/STs (erstwhile Coaching-cum-Guidance Centre for SC/STs)

scheme_name: National Career Service Centers For SC/STs (erstwhile Coaching-cum-Guidance Centre for SC/STs)

scheme_name: National Career Service Centers For SC/STs (erstwhile Coaching-cum-Guidance Centre for SC/STs)

scheme_name: National Career Service Centers For SC/STs (erstwhile Coaching-cum-Guidance Centre for SC/STs)

scheme_name: National Dhanwantari Ayurveda Award

scheme_name: National Dhanwantari Ayurveda Award
question: Who is eligible for this award?

scheme_name: National Dhanwantari Ayurveda Award
question: What is the minimum age for applicants?
answer: The applicant must be at least 40 years old.

scheme_name: National Dhanwantari Ayurveda Award
question: What qualifications are required?

scheme_name: National Dhanwantari Ayurveda Award
question: Can past awardees apply again?

scheme_name: National Dhanwantari Ayurveda Award
question: How many awards are given annually?

scheme_name: National Dhanwantari Ayurveda Award
question: Who can nominate for the award?

scheme_name: National Dhanwantari Ayurveda Award
question: Is there an online application process?

scheme_name: National Dhanwantari Ayurveda Award
question: What type of contributions are considered?

scheme_name: National Dhanwantari Ayurveda Award

scheme_name: Natural Death Assistance for the Construction Workers
question: Which Department of the NCT of Delhi administers this scheme?
answer: This scheme is administered by the Labour Department, of the National Capital Territory of Delhi.

scheme_name: Natural Death Assistance for the Construction Workers
question: Where can I find the URL of the Delhi Building and Other Construction Workers Welfare Board?
answer: The URL of the Official Website of the Delhi Building and Other Construction Workers Welfare Board is: https://bocw.delhi.gov.in/.

scheme_name: Natural Death Assistance for the Construction Workers
question: What is the URL for the registration of this scheme?
answer: The applicants needs to register through clicking on the "Register" button on DBoCWWB website: https://dbocwwb.delhi.gov.in/cwapp/MyLoginPage?ReturnUrl=%2Fcwapp%2F

scheme_name: Natural Death Assistance for the Construction Workers

scheme_name: Natural Death Assistance for the Construction Workers

scheme_name: Natural Death Assistance for the Construction Workers
question: I am from another state but working as a construction worker in Delhi, can | get registered?

scheme_name: Natural Death Assistance for the Construction Workers
question: Can members in my family also register if they are all registered construction workers?

scheme_name: Natural Death Assistance for the Construction Workers
question: Is there a specific age requirement for construction workers to be eligible for registration?
answer: Yes, construction workers must be at least 18 years old but not more than 65 years old to be eligible for registration under Section 12 of the Main Act.

scheme_name: Natural Death Assistance for the Construction Workers
question: What is the duration of engagement required for construction workers to qualify for registration?
answer: Construction workers must have engaged in building or other construction work for a minimum of 90 days during the preceding 12 months to qualify for registration under Section 12 of the Main Act.

scheme_name: Natural Death Assistance for the Construction Workers
question: What is the Registration/Renewal fee?
answer: Registration : [?] 25/-and Renewal : [?] 20/- and [?] 2/- per month (late fee).

scheme_name: Natural Death Assistance for the Construction Workers

scheme_name: Indira Gandhi National Disabled Pension Scheme (Madhya Pradesh)

scheme_name: Indira Gandhi National Disabled Pension Scheme (Madhya Pradesh)
question: Who is eligible for the scheme?

scheme_name: Indira Gandhi National Disabled Pension Scheme (Madhya Pradesh)
question: How much pension will a beneficiary receive?

scheme_name: Indira Gandhi National Disabled Pension Scheme (Madhya Pradesh)
question: How can I apply for the scheme?
answer: Applicants can submit the completed application form, along with required documents, to the designated officer, Gram Panchayat, or Public Service Center.

scheme_name: Indira Gandhi National Disabled Pension Scheme (Madhya Pradesh)
question: What documents are required for application?
answer: Documents such as proof of identity, disability certificate, and proof of residence are required for the application.

scheme_name: Indira Gandhi National Disabled Pension Scheme (Madhya Pradesh)
question: How will I know if my application is accepted?
answer: After submission, you will receive an acknowledgement receipt from the office, confirming the application is under review.

scheme_name: Indira Gandhi National Disabled Pension Scheme (Madhya Pradesh)
question: What happens after I submit my application?

scheme_name: Indira Gandhi National Disabled Pension Scheme (Madhya Pradesh)
question: What if my application is rejected?
answer: If the documents are found to be incorrect, your application will be rejected, and you will be informed in writing along with the reason for rejection.

scheme_name: Indira Gandhi National Disabled Pension Scheme (Madhya Pradesh)
question: How will the pension be paid?
answer: Once approved, the pension will be directly credited to the beneficiary's bank savings account every month.

scheme_name: Indira Gandhi National Disabled Pension Scheme (Madhya Pradesh)
question: Out of the total amount of the pension, how much is provided by the central government and by the state government?
answer: The pension amount is equally shared between the central and state government, with [?]300 contributed by the central government and [?]300 by the state government.

scheme_name: Nashamukt Gram Panchayat Puraskar Yojana
question: When preparing the application, what specific period of work and accomplishments should the Gram Panchayat document and report to the committee?
answer: The application must be prepared and submitted based on the achievements and work performed and realized during the previous year.

scheme_name: Nashamukt Gram Panchayat Puraskar Yojana
question: What is the overall objective of the scheme in relation to motivating community segments like youth, elderly, and women towards a healthier lifestyle?
answer: The scheme aims to encourage making the state drug-free by awarding one Gram Panchayat where resident youth, elderly, and women are confirmed to be living a drug-free life.

scheme_name: Nashamukt Gram Panchayat Puraskar Yojana
question: What is the financial incentive provided to a Gram Panchayat that is successfully selected for demonstrating excellent work towards de-addiction?
answer: The selected Gram Panchayat receives a cash award of ₹1,00,000/- (Rupees one lakh). This amount is provided per district, per Panchayat.

scheme_name: Nashamukt Gram Panchayat Puraskar Yojana
question: How quickly can the selected Gram Panchayat expect to receive the cash award after the final decision regarding the outstanding performance is announced?
answer: The Collector must provide the cash award to the related Sarpanch (Head of the Gram Panchayat) for the Gram Panchayat within one month of selection for the award.

scheme_name: Nashamukt Gram Panchayat Puraskar Yojana
question: Is it mandatory for the Gram Panchayat to demonstrate that specific legal measures have been enforced regarding the regulation of tobacco products?
answer: Yes, action must have been taken under the Cigarettes and Other Tobacco Products (Prohibition of Advertisement and Regulation of Trade and Commerce, Production, Supply and Distribution) Act 2003.

scheme_name: Nashamukt Gram Panchayat Puraskar Yojana
question: By what specific method or mechanism will the monetary reward be transferred or disbursed to the successful Gram Panchayat once selected?
answer: The award amount will be provided via Cheque or Bank Draft or Real Time Gross Settlement (R.T.G.S.).

scheme_name: Nashamukt Gram Panchayat Puraskar Yojana
question: If a Gram Panchayat comprises multiple villages, must the drug-free status apply uniformly across the entire geographical area?
answer: Yes, the drug-free certification must include all villages that fall under the administrative jurisdiction of the applicant Gram Panchayat.

scheme_name: Nashamukt Gram Panchayat Puraskar Yojana
question: Are there any specific criteria relating to educational institutions operating within the administrative boundaries of the applicant Gram Panchayat?
answer: Students studying in all schools operating within the Panchayat area must be motivated against and resolved not to consume intoxication.

scheme_name: Nashamukt Gram Panchayat Puraskar Yojana
question: How are the expenses incurred by the Sarpanch (Head of the Gram Panchayat) to attend the award ceremony handled?
answer: The Collector will cover the expenses for coming and going travel incurred by the related Sarpanch (Head of the Gram Panchayat) to attend the ceremony at the District Headquarters.

scheme_name: Nashamukt Gram Panchayat Puraskar Yojana
question: Does the application require evidence that habitual addicts within the Panchayat jurisdiction received professional assistance for their addiction issues?
answer: Yes, the Gram Panchayat must confirm that treatment was provided by admitting habitual addicts for medical care in De-addiction cum Rehabilitation Centers.

scheme_name: Nashamukt Gram Panchayat Puraskar Yojana
question: What is the minimum standard required for the population status of the Gram Panchayat regarding de-addiction efforts when submitting an application?
answer: One hundred percent (100%) of the Gram Panchayat’s population must be verified as living a drug-free life, having successfully given up intoxication.

scheme_name: Nashamukt Gram Panchayat Puraskar Yojana
question: To which government authority or administrative body should the relevant Gram Panchayat submit its completed application documents for consideration?
answer: The related Gram Panchayat must present its application to the Collector of the corresponding district.

scheme_name: Nashamukt Gram Panchayat Puraskar Yojana
question: On which significant annual public occasion is the formal Certificate of Appreciation scheduled to be officially presented to the award winner?
answer: The Certificate of Appreciation is scheduled to be presented at a ceremony organized on Republic Day.

scheme_name: Nashamukt Gram Panchayat Puraskar Yojana
question: Apart from the cash reward, what other forms of official recognition or financial assistance are provided to the winning Gram Panchayat?
answer: A Certificate of Appreciation detailing the excellent work is provided, and the Sarpanch (Head of the Gram Panchayat) receives coverage for travel expenses.

scheme_name: National Gopal Ratna Award
question: What is the objective of the National Gopal Ratna Award?
answer: The award aims to motivate farmers to enhance the productivity of indigenous milch breeds scientifically, encourage Artificial Insemination Technicians for 100% AI coverage, and promote competitiveness among dairy cooperatives and milk producer companies.

scheme_name: National Gopal Ratna Award
question: Who can apply for the National Gopal Ratna Award?
answer: Dairy farmers, Dairy Cooperative Societies/Farmer Producer Organisations/Milk Producer Companies, and Artificial Insemination Technicians can apply under their respective categories.

scheme_name: National Gopal Ratna Award
question: Can applicants apply through self-nomination?
answer: Yes, self-nomination is allowed for both individuals (farmers and AI technicians) and organisations (DCS/FPO/MPC).

scheme_name: National Gopal Ratna Award
question: How many awards are given each year?
answer: A total of 12 awards are given annually, with 4 awards in each of the 3 categories.

scheme_name: National Gopal Ratna Award
question: What are the monetary benefits under the scheme?
answer: For Best Dairy Farmer and Best DCS/FPO/MPC categories: | - ₹5,00,000 for 1st rank | - ₹3,00,000 for 2nd rank | - ₹2,00,000 for 3rd rank | - ₹2,00,000 as a special award for NER and Himalayan states

scheme_name: National Gopal Ratna Award
question: Is there any cash prize for Artificial Insemination Technicians?
answer: No, the AIT category receives only a certificate of merit and a memento, with no cash prize.

scheme_name: National Gopal Ratna Award
question: What is the minimum eligibility for dairy organizations?
answer: Organisations must be registered and engaged in dairy activities, collecting at least 100 litres of milk per day with 50 members (Non-NER states) or 20 litres per day with 20 members (NER states).

scheme_name: National Gopal Ratna Award
question: Are Veterinary Doctors eligible for the AIT category?
answer: No, Veterinary Doctors are not eligible for the Artificial Insemination Technician category.

scheme_name: National Gopal Ratna Award
question: How are the awardees selected?
answer: Applications are screened by an agency like QCI, verified through field visits by NDDB or others, and then evaluated by Screening and National Award Committees.

scheme_name: National Gopal Ratna Award
question: When are the awards announced and presented?
answer: The awardees are announced on 25th November, and the awards are presented on 26th November (National Milk Day).

scheme_name: Namami Gange Yojana- Uttarakhand
question: Who is eligible to benefit from this scheme?
answer: Farmers residing in villages located along the banks of the Ganga and its tributaries within Uttarakhand are eligible for assistance under the scheme.

scheme_name: Namami Gange Yojana- Uttarakhand
question: What type of assistance is provided under the scheme?
answer: Assistance is provided to farmers to adopt organic farming practices through the formation of clusters.

scheme_name: Namami Gange Yojana- Uttarakhand
question: How can a farmer apply for the scheme?
answer: Farmers can apply by submitting the prescribed application form available at the Uttarakhand Organic Produce Council office, Kisan Bhawan, Dehradun, Uttarakhand.

scheme_name: Namami Gange Yojana- Uttarakhand
question: Where should the application be submitted?
answer: Applications must be submitted at the office of the Uttarakhand Organic Produce Council, Kisan Bhawan, Dehradun.

scheme_name: Namami Gange Yojana- Uttarakhand
question: What documents are required to apply for the scheme?
answer: Documents are required as per the guidelines of the Uttarakhand Organic Produce Council, which may include identity proof, land ownership documents, etc.

scheme_name: Nandaa Gaura Yojana
question: Who can apply for this scheme?
answer: The applicant must be a permanent resident of Uttarakhand and belong to an eligible family with an income not exceeding ₹6,000/- per month or be a BPL family.

scheme_name: Nandaa Gaura Yojana
question: How much financial assistance is given at the time of birth?
answer: At the time of birth, a girl child born in a hospital/ANM center receives ₹11,000/-.

scheme_name: Nandaa Gaura Yojana
question: How much financial assistance is given after passing Class 12th?
answer: When the girl passes Class 12th, she receives ₹51,000/- as the second installment.

scheme_name: Nandaa Gaura Yojana
question: How many girl children in a family can get the benefit?
answer: The benefit is available for up to two girls per family.

scheme_name: Nandaa Gaura Yojana
question: Is there any time limit to apply for the first installment?
answer: Yes. Applications must be submitted within six months of the girl’s birth.

scheme_name: Nandaa Gaura Yojana
question: When can one apply for the second installment?
answer: Applications for the second installment can be made between July and November of the same year in which the girl passes Class 12th.

scheme_name: Nandaa Gaura Yojana
question: Will the application for the second installment be valid in the next year?
answer: No. If applied in the next year, the application will not be valid.

scheme_name: Nandaa Gaura Yojana
question: Which educational boards are valid for the second installment?
answer: The scheme is valid for girls who have passed Class 12th from the Uttarakhand Board, other State Boards, CBSE, ICSE, or the National Institute of Open Schooling, New Delhi.

scheme_name: Nandaa Gaura Yojana
question: Is it necessary for the girl to be unmarried to get the second installment?
answer: Yes. The girl must be unmarried when applying for the second installment.

scheme_name: Nandaa Gaura Yojana
question: Where can families register for this scheme?
answer: Families must register on the official online portal https://www.nandagaurauk.in

scheme_name: Nandaa Gaura Yojana
question: How is the financial assistance disbursed?
answer: The approved amount is directly transferred to the applicant’s bank account linked with Aadhaar, subject to budget availability.

scheme_name: Nishulk Ganavesh Yojana
question: Who is eligible for the scheme?
answer: All girl students of Classes 1 to 8, all boys belonging to Scheduled Caste (SC) and Scheduled Tribe (ST) categories, and boys from General Category BPL families studying in government and government-aided schools are eligible.

scheme_name: Nishulk Ganavesh Yojana
question: Which classes are covered under the scheme?
answer: The scheme covers students studying in Classes 1 to 8.

scheme_name: Nishulk Ganavesh Yojana
question: How many sets of uniforms are provided under this scheme?
answer: Each eligible student receives two sets of uniforms every year.

scheme_name: Nishulk Ganavesh Yojana
question: Is there any selection process for the scheme?
answer: No, there is no selection process. All eligible students from Classes 1 to 8 receive uniforms or related financial assistance.

scheme_name: Nishulk Ganavesh Yojana
question: Is the scheme applicable only to government schools?
answer: The scheme is applicable to students studying in government and government-aided schools.

scheme_name: Nishulk Ganavesh Yojana
question: Are private school students eligible under this scheme?
answer: No.

scheme_name: National Handicrafts Development Programme: Direct Benefit to Artisans - Supports to Artisans in Indigent Circumstances
question: How is the financial assistance disbursed to selected artisans?
answer: Financial assistance is disbursed through the In-charge in the respective field formation of the Office of the Development Commissioner (Handicrafts) following the finalization of selection by the Core Committee.

scheme_name: National Handicrafts Development Programme: Direct Benefit to Artisans - Supports to Artisans in Indigent Circumstances
question: How are the applications by the artisans processed after submission?
answer: Upon receipt, applications undergo inspections by field officers. Completed applications are processed within 30 days, and a Core Committee finalizes the selection of master craftspersons for financial assistance based on recommendations from the Regional Director.

scheme_name: National Handicrafts Development Programme: Direct Benefit to Artisans - Supports to Artisans in Indigent Circumstances
question: How often do artisans need to submit income certificates and affidavits for seeking financial support?
answer: Master craftspersons are required to submit income certificates and affidavits duly countersigned by a First-Class Magistrate every financial year to continue receiving financial support.

scheme_name: National Handicrafts Development Programme: Direct Benefit to Artisans - Supports to Artisans in Indigent Circumstances
question: What documents are required to be submitted along with the application form?
answer: Applicants need to submit documents such as a photograph, self-attested copy of handicrafts award certificate, income certificate, proof of age, disability certificate (if applicable), and an affidavit in the prescribed format attested by a First-Class Magistrate.

scheme_name: National Handicrafts Development Programme: Direct Benefit to Artisans - Supports to Artisans in Indigent Circumstances
question: How much financial assistance is provided to eligible artisans under this scheme?
answer: Eligible artisans can receive assistance of up to [?]8,000/- per month in the form of a monthly allowance or lump sum grant, facilitated through PFMS/DBT.

scheme_name: National Handicrafts Development Programme: Direct Benefit to Artisans - Supports to Artisans in Indigent Circumstances
question: What is the primary objective of the "Direct Benefit to Artisans - Supports to Artisans in Indigent Circumstances" scheme?
answer: The scheme aims to provide financial assistance to master craftspersons facing indigent circumstances during their old age, thereby supporting their livelihood and welfare.

scheme_name: National Handicrafts Development Programme: Direct Benefit to Artisans - Supports to Artisans in Indigent Circumstances
question: Can artisans receive financial assistance from other sources while availing benefits under this scheme?
answer: No, artisans receiving similar financial assistance from any other source are not eligible to receive benefits under this scheme.

scheme_name: National Handicrafts Development Programme: Direct Benefit to Artisans - Supports to Artisans in Indigent Circumstances
question: Can the financial assistance be revoked if the artisan's income exceeds the specified limit?
answer: Yes, if the artisan's income exceeds [?]1,00,000/- in the preceding financial year, they may no longer be eligible to receive financial assistance under the scheme.

scheme_name: National Handicrafts Development Programme: Direct Benefit to Artisans - Supports to Artisans in Indigent Circumstances
question: Can artisans use the financial assistance for any purpose?
answer: Yes, artisans are free to use the financial assistance for their livelihood and welfare needs as they deem fit.

scheme_name: National Handicrafts Development Programme: Direct Benefit to Artisans - Supports to Artisans in Indigent Circumstances
question: Is there any restriction on the duration for which artisans can receive financial assistance?
answer: As long as the artisan meets the eligibility criteria and submits the required documents annually, they can continue to receive financial assistance.

scheme_name: National Handicrafts Development Programme: Direct Benefit to Artisans - Supports to Artisans in Indigent Circumstances
question: How is the financial assistance disbursed to eligible artisans?
answer: Financial assistance is disbursed through PFMS/DBT in the form of a monthly allowance or lump sum grant, depending on the preference of the artisan.

scheme_name: National Handicrafts Development Programme: Direct Benefit to Artisans - Supports to Artisans in Indigent Circumstances
question: What is the maximum amount of financial assistance provided to eligible artisans?
answer: Eligible artisans can receive financial assistance of up to [?]8,000/- per month in the form of a monthly allowance or lump sum grant.

scheme_name: National Handicrafts Development Programme: Infrastructure And Technology Support: EMPORIA
question: What Is The Full Form Of NHDP?
answer: The Full Form of NHDP is "National Handicrafts Development Programme".

scheme_name: National Handicrafts Development Programme: Infrastructure And Technology Support: EMPORIA
question: What Are The Objectives Of This Scheme?
answer: The basic objective of the component is to provide a marketing platform to the Local Handicrafts Artisans in their respective area through the outlet and emporia.

scheme_name: National Handicrafts Development Programme: Infrastructure And Technology Support: EMPORIA
question: At What Locations Shall The EMPORIA Be Set Up?
answer: These would be set up in commercially viable locations in the implementing agencies' own/rented buildings.

scheme_name: National Handicrafts Development Programme: Infrastructure And Technology Support: EMPORIA
question: For What Purposes Is The Financial Assistance Provided To The Implementing Agencies?
answer: Under this component, assistance would be provided for the setting up of emporia.

scheme_name: National Handicrafts Development Programme: Infrastructure And Technology Support: EMPORIA
question: What Shall Be The Financial Ceiling For Setting Up A New Emporia?
answer: For setting up a New Emporia (Rented/Own building), the Per Unit Cost shall be [?] 60,00,000.

scheme_name: National Handicrafts Development Programme: Infrastructure And Technology Support: EMPORIA
question: What Shall Be The Financial Ceiling For Strengthening / Renovation?

scheme_name: National Handicrafts Development Programme: Infrastructure And Technology Support: EMPORIA
question: What Percentage Of The Admissible Amount Shall Be Borne By The O/O The DC (H)?

scheme_name: National Handicrafts Development Programme: Infrastructure And Technology Support: EMPORIA
question: What Percentage Of The Admissible Amount Shall Be Borne By The Implementing Agency?

scheme_name: National Handicrafts Development Programme: Infrastructure And Technology Support: EMPORIA
question: What Percent Of The Assistance Shall Be Borne By The Office Of The DC (Handicrafts) For The Strengthening / Renovation Of The Existing Emporia?

scheme_name: National Handicrafts Development Programme: Infrastructure And Technology Support: EMPORIA

scheme_name: National Handicrafts Development Programme: Infrastructure And Technology Support: EMPORIA

scheme_name: National Handicrafts Development Programme: Infrastructure And Technology Support: EMPORIA
question: To Whom Shall The Proposal Be Addressed?

scheme_name: National Handicrafts Development Programme: Infrastructure And Technology Support: EMPORIA
question: Are The National Level Apex Societies (Registered Under The Society Act/ Trust Act, Etc.) Also Eligible To Apply?

scheme_name: National Handicrafts Development Programme: Infrastructure And Technology Support: EMPORIA
question: Does This Scheme Accept Online Applications?
