scheme_name: National Handicrafts Development Programme: Infrastructure And Technology Support: URBAN HAAT
question: What Is The Full Form Of NHDP?
answer: The Full Form of NHDP is "National Handicrafts Development Programme".

scheme_name: National Handicrafts Development Programme: Infrastructure And Technology Support: URBAN HAAT
question: What Are The Objectives Of The "Urban Haat" Component Of The Infrastructure & Technology Support Scheme Of NHDP?
answer: The scheme "Infrastructure & Technology Support: URBAN HAAT" is introduced to set up a permanent marketing infrastructure in towns/ metropolitan cities to provide direct marketing facilities to handicrafts artisans/handloom weavers, enabling them to sell their products to a wider target audience.

scheme_name: National Handicrafts Development Programme: Infrastructure And Technology Support: URBAN HAAT
question: What Shall Be The Area Of The Haat?
answer: The haat shall be constructed in an area of not less than 8,000 sq. m. and will have a display gallery, food court, etc.

scheme_name: National Handicrafts Development Programme: Infrastructure And Technology Support: URBAN HAAT
question: Will The Allotment Of The Stalls To The Artisans Be Fixed Or Will It Be On A Rotational Basis?
answer: The stalls are allotted to artisans on a rotational basis for a nominal rent.

scheme_name: National Handicrafts Development Programme: Infrastructure And Technology Support: URBAN HAAT
question: What Is The Full Form Of "SPV"?
answer: The Full Form of "SPV" is "Special Purpose Vehicle".

scheme_name: National Handicrafts Development Programme: Infrastructure And Technology Support: URBAN HAAT
question: What Shall Be The Purpose Of The SPVs?
answer: The implementing agencies will be encouraged to form SPVs with the active participation of the various agencies dealing with the promotion of Tourism, Culture, Food, Processing Industry, etc., involving the tour operators, and hotel operators in addition to those dealing with handloom and handicrafts for broad basing and ensure utilization of facilities for a long duration for management and day-to-day running of the same.

scheme_name: National Handicrafts Development Programme: Infrastructure And Technology Support: URBAN HAAT
question: What Shall Be The Financial Ceiling For The Implementing Agencies?
answer: The financial ceiling for urban haat is [?] 8,00,00,000 for each unit.

scheme_name: National Handicrafts Development Programme: Infrastructure And Technology Support: URBAN HAAT
question: What Percentage Of The Financial Assistance Shall Be Borne By The O/O The DC(HC)?
answer: 40% of the admissible amount shall be borne by the O/o the DC(HC) and DC(HL) each.

scheme_name: National Handicrafts Development Programme: Infrastructure And Technology Support: URBAN HAAT
question: What Percentage Of The Financial Assistance Shall Be Borne By The Implementing Agency?
answer: 20% of the admissible amount will be contributed by the implementing agency.

scheme_name: National Handicrafts Development Programme: Infrastructure And Technology Support: URBAN HAAT
question: In The Case Of Andaman & Nicobar Islands, What Percentage Of The Financial Assistance Shall Be Borne By The O/O The DC(HC)?
answer: In the case of NER, Jammu & Kashmir, Ladakh, and Andaman & Nicobar Islands, Lakshadweep - 45% of the admissible amount will be borne by the O/o the DC (HC) and DC(HL) each. 10% of the admissible amount shall be contributed by the implementing agency.

scheme_name: National Handicrafts Development Programme: Infrastructure And Technology Support: URBAN HAAT
question: What Shall Be The Amount Of The Financial Assistance For Strengthening/Renovation Of Existing Urban Haats?
answer: Assistance will also be given for strengthening/renovation of existing Urban Haats subject to a maximum financial limit of [?] 2,50,00,000 (100% assistance will be borne by the Office of the DC (Handicrafts) & DC (Handlooms).

scheme_name: National Handicrafts Development Programme: Infrastructure And Technology Support: URBAN HAAT
question: What Shall Be The Amount Of The Financial Assistance For "Mini Urban Haats"?
answer: Assistance will also be given for Mini Urban Haats on need-based and feasibility. The financial assistance will be based on the number of stalls, land area & other deliverables in a proportionate manner.

scheme_name: National Handicrafts Development Programme: Infrastructure And Technology Support: URBAN HAAT
question: How Many Stalls Shall Be Erected By The Implementing Agency?
answer: 50-80 Stalls of 10x8 sq. ft. each shall be erected by the Implementing Agency.

scheme_name: National Handicrafts Development Programme: Infrastructure And Technology Support: URBAN HAAT
question: How Many Toilets Shall Be There In The Haat?

scheme_name: National Handicrafts Development Programme: Infrastructure And Technology Support: URBAN HAAT
question: What Additional Facilities Shall Be There In The Haat?

scheme_name: National Handicrafts Development Programme: Infrastructure And Technology Support: URBAN HAAT
question: What Shall Be The Benefits For The Buyers/Tourists?

scheme_name: National Handicrafts Development Programme: Infrastructure And Technology Support: URBAN HAAT
question: Where Can I Find The Link To The Scheme Guidelines?

scheme_name: National Handicrafts Development Programme: Infrastructure And Technology Support: URBAN HAAT
question: Where Can I Find The Link To The Proforma For Proposal?

scheme_name: National Handicrafts Development Programme: Infrastructure And Technology Support: URBAN HAAT
question: To Whom Shall The Proposal Be Addressed?
answer: The proposals in the prescribed proforma along with all the (self-attested) supporting documents in hard copy should be addressed to the concerned Handicraft Service Center (HSC), O/o the DC (HC).

scheme_name: National Handicrafts Development Programme: Research & Development Scheme
question: How Will The Selection Of The Artisans Be Done?
answer: Any artisans having a Pahchan card may participate in the seminar/workshop. Beneficiaries must be selected in a fair & transparent manner, through well-defined objective parameters /criteria, by way of giving equal opportunity to all artisans, under the supervision of the concerned AD(Handicrafts).

scheme_name: National Handicrafts Development Programme: Research & Development Scheme
question: Is There Any Reservation/Preference/Priority In The Selection Of The Artisans?
answer: Yes, preference may be given to the marginalized social groups i.e., SC/ST/Women/Differently enabled persons shall also be incorporated under the schemes irrespective of the crafts they practice to ensure their recognition, equality, and empowerment.

scheme_name: National Handicrafts Development Programme: Research & Development Scheme
question: Where Shall The Details Of The Beneficiaries Be Uploaded?
answer: The details of the beneficiaries shall be uploaded on the portal / MIS of the O/o DC (Handicrafts).

scheme_name: National Handicrafts Development Programme: Research & Development Scheme
question: How Will The Selection Of Project Leader / SRF/ JRF And Resource Persons Be Done?
answer: For conducting Studies/Surveys, eligible candidates will be engaged by the Implementing agency/Institution, upon submission of their detailed profile/resume to the O/o DC (Handicrafts). For seminars/workshops, the Implementing agency/Institution may engage eminent personalities in the respective fields or engage their own faculty/resource persons, with the prior approval of the O/o Development Commissioner (Handicrafts). In either case, the person to be engaged should have adequate proven knowledge in the field of handicrafts and experience in conducting research activities.

scheme_name: National Handicrafts Development Programme: Research & Development Scheme
question: How Will The Inspection And Monitoring Of This Scheme Be Performed?

scheme_name: NPC Students Internship Program
question: Q2. What Services Does NPC Offer To Improve Productivity And Competitiveness?

scheme_name: NPC Students Internship Program
question: Q3. What Is The Code Of Conduct Expected From Interns During Their Internship At NPC?
answer: A3. Interns are expected to demonstrate sincerity, punctuality, courtesy, cooperative attitude, willingness to learn, proper etiquette, and appropriate attire. They must also maintain workplace decorum throughout their internship period.

scheme_name: NPC Students Internship Program
question: Q4. What Are The Responsibilities Of Interns During Their Internship At NPC?
answer: A4. Interns are expected to perform the assigned tasks and duties with due care and diligence as per the instructions provided to them. They must also submit a project/assignment report/paper at the end of their internship to the concerned Head(s) regarding their learning experience.

scheme_name: NPC Students Internship Program
question: Q5. How Does NPC Ensure Confidentiality During The Internship Period?
answer: A5. Interns are required not to disclose any proprietary or confidential information relating to the services, contract, or business operations of NPC or its clients during or after the internship period without seeking prior written consent from NPC.

scheme_name: NPC Students Internship Program
question: Q6. What Happens If An Intern Violates The Non-Disclosure Agreement?

scheme_name: NPC Students Internship Program
question: Q7. Can NPC Terminate An Intern's Engagement Or Program During The Internship?

scheme_name: NPC Students Internship Program

scheme_name: National Pension Scheme For Traders And Self Employed Persons

scheme_name: National Pension Scheme For Traders And Self Employed Persons
question: How much pension would be received through this scheme and at what age?
answer: Under the Scheme, a minimum monthly assured pension of Rs. 3000/- will commence after the beneficiary attains the age of 60 years.

scheme_name: National Pension Scheme For Traders And Self Employed Persons
question: How can I enrol for this scheme?
answer: Under the scheme, the beneficiary may visit the nearest Common Service Centre and get enrolled in the scheme using her/his Aadhar number and savings bank account/Jan-Dhan account number on self-certification basis. Nearest Common Service Centres (CSCs) can be located at locator.csccloud.in/.

scheme_name: National Pension Scheme For Traders And Self Employed Persons
question: Is the Proof of Age/DOB a required document?

scheme_name: National Pension Scheme For Traders And Self Employed Persons
question: What are the exit provisions?
answer: Exit provisions are as under: | in case an eligible beneficiary exits this Scheme within a period of less than ten years from the date of joining the Scheme by him, then his share of contribution only will be returned to him with savings bank rate of interest payable thereon. | if an eligible beneficiary exits after completion of a period of ten years or more from the date of joining the Scheme by him but before his age of sixty years, then his share of contribution only shall be returned to him along with accumulated interest thereon as actually earned by the Pension Fund or the interest at the savings bank interest rate thereon, whichever is higher | if an eligible beneficiary has given regular contributions and died due to any cause, her/his spouse shall be entitled to continue with the Scheme subsequently by payment of regular contribution as applicable or exit by receiving the share of contribution paid by such beneficiary along with accumulated interest, as actually earned thereon by the Pension Fund or at the savings bank interest rate thereon, whichever is higher | in case of exit on account of clauses (i), (ii) and (iii) above, the accumulated share of Government's contribution shall be credited back to the Pension Fund | any other exit provision, including nomination, as may be decided by the Central Government by issuing instructions from time to time. | after death of beneficiary and his or her spouse, the corpus shall be credited back to the fund;

scheme_name: National Pension Scheme For Traders And Self Employed Persons
question: What would be the role of LIC?
answer: The scheme is being implemented through LIC and CSCs. LIC is the pension fund manager and also responsible for pension pay out.

scheme_name: National Pension Scheme For Traders And Self Employed Persons
question: Is auto-debit facility available?
answer: Yes. Monthly subscription shall be automatically debited on a fixed date of every month from her/his linked savings account. Only, first subscription will be paid in cash for which receipt will be provided by concerned CSCs/VLEs.

scheme_name: National Pension Scheme For Traders And Self Employed Persons
question: Is there a fee for enrollment in this scheme?
answer: There is no administrative cost to the beneficiary as it is a Social Security Scheme of the Government of India. The enrollment under the Scheme is free for beneficiaries.

scheme_name: National Pension Scheme For Traders And Self Employed Persons
question: Is there a provision for family pension?
answer: Yes, there is a provision for family pension under the scheme. It is applicable only to the spouse of the beneficiary. If the beneficiary dies, after the pension has commenced, the spouse of the beneficiary shall be entitled to receive 50 % of the pension.

scheme_name: National Pension Scheme For Traders And Self Employed Persons
question: If the payment of the subscription is stopped, can the beneficiary re-join / revive the application again?
answer: If the payment of subscription has been stopped or delayed, the beneficiary can revive the scheme after paying the outstanding subscription with a nominal interest as decided by the Government.

scheme_name: NPS Vatsalya Scheme
question: What is NPS Vatsalya?
answer: NPS Vatsalya is a contributory pension system under the National Pension System (NPS). Its objective is to create a pension society and encourage the empowerment of children by inculcating the habit of saving for retirement from an early age.

scheme_name: NPS Vatsalya Scheme
question: Who can subscribe to NPS Vatsalya?
answer: NPS Vatsalya is open to all citizens of India who are under the age of eighteen years. The account will be opened and operated by the guardian on behalf of the minor.

scheme_name: NPS Vatsalya Scheme
question: What are the benefits of opening a NPS Vatsalya account?
answer: Opening an NPS Vatsalya account provides the child with a head start on saving for retirement and offers valuable financial lessons from an early age. It instils the importance of financial planning and discipline, which can benefit the child throughout their life.

scheme_name: NPS Vatsalya Scheme
question: How is the NPS Vatsalya account operated?
answer: The account is opened by the natural or legal guardian in the name of the minor. | The minor is the sole beneficiary of the account. | A unique Permanent Retirement Account Number (PRAN) is issued in the minor's name. | The account is operated by the guardian for the exclusive benefit of the minor until they reach the age of majority (18 years).

scheme_name: NPS Vatsalya Scheme
question: What is the procedure for opening a NPS Vatsalya account?
answer: The NPS Vatsalya account can be opened through: | Points of Presence (POPs) registered with PFRDA (Major banks, India Post and Pension Funds etc), either online or in physical mode, directly or through Retirement Advisors/Pension Agents. | The online platform (eNPS) of NPS Trust.

scheme_name: NPS Vatsalya Scheme
question: What are the KYC requirements for opening a NPS Vatsalya account?
answer: The KYC norms applicable to the guardian must be in accordance with the standards stipulated by PFRDA. | In the case of a court-appointed legal guardian, a copy of the court order regarding the appointment of the Legal Guardian must be submitted along with the KYC documents.

scheme_name: NPS Vatsalya Scheme
question: What documents of the minor are required for opening a NPS Vatsalya account?
answer: For the minor, proof of date of birth is required. Acceptable documents include: | Birth certificate of the minor School leaving certificate / Matriculations issued by Higher Secondary Board of respective states, ICSE, CBSE, etc. | Passport of the minor | PAN

scheme_name: NPS Vatsalya Scheme
question: Is a bank account required for opening a NPS Vatsalya account?
answer: The bank account details of the minor or a joint account with the minor are not mandatory for opening the account for Indian residents but will be required at the time of partial withdrawal or exit before the age of 18. | For non-residents, details of NRE or NRO account are mandatory.

scheme_name: NPS Vatsalya Scheme
question: What happens when the minor attains the age of 18 years?
answer: The account will continue to be operational and will be seamlessly transitioned into a NPS -Tier 1 Account under the All Citizen Model. | Upon transitioning, the features, benefits, and exit norms of the NPS-Tier I for All Citizen Model will apply. | A fresh KYC of the subscriber must be carried out within three months of reaching majority. | Contributions to the NPS Tier1 Account will be allowed after the submission of fresh KYC.

scheme_name: NPS Vatsalya Scheme
question: Can an NRI or OCI open a NPS Vatsalya account?
answer: The minor must be a citizen of India. | The guardian can be a Non-Resident Indian (NRI) or Overseas Citizen of India (OCI). | A separate form is applicable for guardians who are NRIs or OCIs. | A bank account (NRE or NRO) is mandatory when the guardian is an NRI or OCI.

scheme_name: NPS Vatsalya Scheme
question: Is it required to furnish a nomination while joining the scheme?
answer: No, the guardian becomes the nominee under the scheme.

scheme_name: NPS Vatsalya Scheme
question: How many NPS Vatsalya accounts can I open?
answer: The guardian can open a single account (per child) for the minor.

scheme_name: NPS Vatsalya Scheme
question: Can a guardian who is a NPS subscriber open a NPS Vatsalya account for a minor?
answer: Yes, a guardian who is an NPS subscriber can open an NPS Vatsalya account in the name of the minor.

scheme_name: NPS Vatsalya Scheme
question: What are the minimum and maximum contributions for Accumulation Phase under the NPS Vatsalya account?
answer: The minimum contribution is [?] 1000 per annum, with no upper limit on the maximum contribution. | The initial contribution required for enrollment under the scheme is [?] 1000.

scheme_name: NPS Vatsalya Scheme
question: What are the modes of contribution available for Accumulation Phase under NPS Vatsalya?
answer: A subscriber can contribute through any of the following modes: | Physical mode: By visiting any registered service provider (PoP) and depositing a cheque/cash along with the NPS contribution slip. | Online mode: | o Online facility provided by PoPs. | o eNPS platform of NPS Trust.

scheme_name: NPS Vatsalya Scheme
question: What choices do I need to exercise for Accumulation Phase under NPS Vatsalya?
answer: All choices available under the NPS All Citizen model are also available for NPS Vatsalya, including: | Choice of CRA (Central Recordkeeping Agency): From the registered CRAs with PFRDA. | Choice of Pension Fund (PF): From the registered PFs with PFRDA. | Choice of Allocation of Funds: | o Auto Choice: | Conservative Life Cycle Fund (LC25) | Moderate Life Cycle Fund (LC50) - Default | Aggressive Life Cycle Fund (LC75) | o Active Choice: | Equity (E) - Maximum 75% | Corporate Bonds (C) - Up to 100% | Government Securities (G) - Up to 100% | Alternate Assets (A) - Maximum 5%

scheme_name: NPS Vatsalya Scheme
question: How are the contributions for Accumulation Phase invested in NPS Vatsalya?
answer: The contributions made by the subscriber are invested according to the choices (Pension Fund and Asset allocation) exercised and recorded with CRA, in line with the investment guidelines prescribed by PFRDA for each asset class: | Asset Class E - Equity shares of Top 200 companies under NSE/BSE in terms of market capitalisation. | Asset Class C - Corporate Bonds/Debentures that are listed and rated not below A. | Asset Class G - Government securities and State Development Loans. | Asset Class A - Alternate Assets. For detailed investment guidelines, refer to the Circulars Section of the PFRDA website.

scheme_name: NPS Vatsalya Scheme
question: How do I know about the performance of my NPS investments under Accumulation Phase?
answer: The performance of your NPS investments is available in the Statement of Transactions, which can be accessed online through the subscriber web login or mobile app. Periodic statements are sent by the CRA to the registered email ID of the subscriber, and a physical statement for the financial year is sent to the correspondence address of the subscriber.

scheme_name: NPS Vatsalya Scheme
question: What happens if I don’t make the minimum contribution under Accumulation Phase? Will my account be closed?
answer: If the minimum contribution is not received, the account is categorized as 'frozen' and will be activated upon contributing to the account. The NPS account will be closed only when a subscriber submits a request (physical or online) for exit from NPS to a service provider (PoP).

scheme_name: NPS Vatsalya Scheme
question: How do I access my NPS account under Accumulation Phase?
answer: Subscribers can access their Pension Account through: | Physical mode: By visiting their service provider (PoP). | Online mode: Using the login credentials provided by CRA in the Account Opening Kit.

scheme_name: NPS Vatsalya Scheme
question: Can I partially withdraw money from the NPS Vatsalya account before 18 years?
answer: Partial withdrawals from your NPS Vatsalya account are allowed to address contingency situations. | The reasons/conditions for partial withdrawal include: | o Education of the minor subscriber | o Treatment of specified illnesses of the minor subscriber | o Disability of more than 75% of the minor subscriber | A maximum amount of up to 25% of contributions (excluding returns) can be partially withdrawn. | This facility is available on a declaration basis after a minimum of 3 years from the date of account opening. | The Partial withdrawal can be made a maximum of three times till the subscriber attains 18 years of age.

scheme_name: NPS Vatsalya Scheme
question: What are the exit options under the scheme?
answer: The subscriber can exit on attainment of the age of 18 years. | On such exit, at least eighty percentage of the accumulated corpus available in the account must be utilized for the purchase of an annuity and the remaining balance shall be paid in a lump sum. | In case, the accumulated pension wealth available in the account is equal to or less than two lakh fifty thousand, or the purchase of annuity is not available from empanelled Annuity Service Providers ('ASPs'), the subscriber shall have the option to withdraw the entire accumulated pension wealth.

scheme_name: NPS Vatsalya Scheme
question: What happens in case of death before 18 years?
answer: In the event of the minor subscriber's death, the entire accumulated corpus is to be paid to the guardian. | If the guardian registered under the account dies during the account's subsistence, another guardian must be registered on behalf of the minor subscriber by submitting the KYC documents as specified by the PFRDA from time to time. | In case of the death of both parents, the legally appointed guardian can continue the account with or without making contributions to the account, and upon attainment of 18 years of age, the subscriber can exit from the scheme.

scheme_name: NSAP - Indira Gandhi National Old Age Pension Scheme
question: What Does NSAP Stand For And When Was It Launched?
answer: NSAP stands for National Social Assistance Programme. NSAP was launched on 15th August 1995.

scheme_name: NSAP - Indira Gandhi National Old Age Pension Scheme
question: What Is The Objective Of NSAP?
answer: In providing social assistance benefits to poor households in the case of old age, death of the breadwinner, and maternity, the NSAP aims at ensuring minimum national standards, in addition to the benefits that the States are currently providing or might provide in future. It also aims at ensuring that social protection to the beneficiaries everywhere in the country is uniformly available without interruption.

scheme_name: NSAP - Indira Gandhi National Old Age Pension Scheme
question: What Are The Components Of NSAP?
answer: The NSAP at its inception in 1995 had three components namely (1) National Old Age Pension Scheme (NOAPS, (2) National Family Benefit Scheme (NFBS), and (3) National Maternity Benefit Scheme (NMBS). The National Maternity Benefit Scheme (NMBS) was subsequently transferred on 1st April, 2001 from the Ministry of Rural development to the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare. | On 1st April 2000 a new Scheme known as Annapurna Scheme was launched. This scheme aimed at providing food security to meet the requirement of those senior citizens who, though eligible, have remained uncovered under the NOAPS. | In February 2009, two new Schemes known as Indira Gandhi National Widow Pension Scheme (IGNWPS) and Indira Gandhi National Disability Pension Scheme (IGNDPS) were introduced. | Presently NSAP comprises of five schemes, namely - (1) Indira Gandhi National Old Age Pension Scheme (IGNOAPS), (2) Indira Gandhi National Widow Pension Scheme (IGNWPS), (3) Indira Gandhi National Disability Pension Scheme (IGNDPS), (4) National Family Benefit Scheme NFBS) and (5) Annapurna.

scheme_name: NSAP - Indira Gandhi National Old Age Pension Scheme
question: Who Implements NSAP?
answer: The NSAP is implemented in the States/UTs in accordance with the general conditions applicable to all components of the NSAP as well as specific conditions applicable to each component. The NSAP Schemes are mainly implemented by the Social Welfare Departments in the States. But NSAP is implemented by Rural Development Department in the States of Andhra Pradesh, Assam, Goa, Meghalaya and West Bengal; by the Department of Women & Child Development in Orissa and Puducherry; by the Revenue Department in Karnataka and Tamil Nadu and by the Department of Labour Employment & Training in Jharkhand. The NSAP extends to both the rural as well as urban areas

scheme_name: NSAP - Indira Gandhi National Old Age Pension Scheme
question: What Is The Basic Eligibility Criterion Under NSAP?
answer: For getting benefits under NSAP the applicant must belong to a Below Poverty Line (BPL) family according to the criteria prescribed by the Govt. of India.

scheme_name: NSAP - Indira Gandhi National Old Age Pension Scheme

answer: Under NOAPS, old age pensions were granted to a person who is 65 years old or higher and who is destitute in the sense of having little or no means of regular income. Pension under IGNOAPS is now granted to a person who is 60 years or above and belongs to a household below the poverty line instead of only to destitute.

scheme_name: National Science Chair- Scientific Excellence
question: How/When can the individual start his NSC Award?
answer: A letter is sent by the SERB to the nominee as well as to the host Institute informing the award of NSC. After receiving the same the nominee has to join the chair within six months of the date of offer letter and to send his / her Acceptance Letter to the Host Institute, indicating the tentative Date / Month when the nominee wants to start the award. Then the Institute will forward his Acceptance / Joining Letter to Science & Engineering Research Board along with the updated details of the bank for transfer of fund through RTGS (in the prescribed format). Based on this letter, SERB will process the file for getting administrative and financial approvals and then a Sanction Order is issued to the Host Institute. The start date, as per joining letter date of the nominee, of the award will be mentioned in the Sanction Order.

scheme_name: Namo Saraswati Vignan Sadhana Yojana
question: What is the "Namo Saraswati Vignan Sadhana Yojana"?
answer: The "Namo Saraswati Vignan Sadhana Yojana" is a financial assistance scheme launched by the Education Department, Government of Gujarat to promote science education among students of Class 11 and 12 by providing monetary support to help them complete their studies.

scheme_name: Namo Saraswati Vignan Sadhana Yojana
question: Who is eligible for the "Namo Saraswati Vignan Sadhana Yojana"?
answer: A student is eligible if they have scored 50% or more in Class 10, enrolled in the science stream in a government, grant-in-aid, or self-financed school recognized by GSHSEB or CBSE, and meet the family income criteria where applicable.

scheme_name: Namo Saraswati Vignan Sadhana Yojana
question: What is the total financial benefit under this scheme?
answer: Under the "Namo Saraswati Vignan Sadhana Yojana", each eligible student receives a total of ₹25,000 over two years of Class 11 and 12 as a monthly stipend and a final installment after passing Class 12.

scheme_name: Namo Saraswati Vignan Sadhana Yojana
question: How is the financial assistance disbursed?
answer: The financial assistance under the "Namo Saraswati Vignan Sadhana Yojana" is disbursed through Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT) into the mother’s bank account or directly into the student’s account if the mother is deceased.

scheme_name: Namo Saraswati Vignan Sadhana Yojana
question: What is the amount given to Class 11 students?
answer: Class 11 students receive ₹10,000 per year, which is paid as ₹1,000 per month for 10 months under the "Namo Saraswati Vignan Sadhana Yojana".

scheme_name: Namo Saraswati Vignan Sadhana Yojana
question: What is the amount given to Class 12 students?
answer: Class 12 students receive ₹15,000 per year, which includes ₹10,000 as monthly stipend and ₹5,000 after passing the Class 12 board exam.

scheme_name: Namo Saraswati Vignan Sadhana Yojana

answer: The "Namo Saraswati Vignan Sadhana Yojana" is implemented by the Education Department of Gujarat.

scheme_name: Namo Saraswati Vignan Sadhana Yojana

scheme_name: Namo Saraswati Vignan Sadhana Yojana

answer: Students must maintain a minimum of 80% attendance every month, which is updated by schools on the Vidya Samiksha Kendra’s online attendance portal to continue receiving assistance.

scheme_name: Namo Saraswati Vignan Sadhana Yojana

scheme_name: Namo Saraswati Vignan Sadhana Yojana

scheme_name: Noni Suraksha Yojana

scheme_name: Noni Suraksha Yojana

scheme_name: Noni Suraksha Yojana

scheme_name: Noni Suraksha Yojana

scheme_name: Noni Suraksha Yojana

answer: The following are the objectives of the scheme: | To build national capacity in frontier areas of Science and Engineering, which are of interest to India by providing research training to PhD students admitted in Indian institutions in overseas universities/institutions of repute. | To provide an opportunity for performing Indian research students to gain exposure and access to top-class research facilities in academia and labs in specific Overseas Universities. | To create opportunities to build long-term R&D linkages and collaborations with accomplished scientists and technologists from around the world. | To tap the expertise gained by these young scientists to strengthen/ initiate national programmes in their domain knowledge.

scheme_name: Overseas Visiting Doctoral Fellowship
question: Which is the implementing agency of this scheme?
answer: Science and Engineering Research Board, Government of India

scheme_name: Overseas Visiting Doctoral Fellowship
question: What are the eligibility criteria for applying/availing the Fellowship?
answer: The scheme is open to Indian nationals only. | The applicant should have registered for full-time Ph.D. Degree in any of the recognized Institutions / Universities in India in Science, Technology, Engineering and Mathematics (including Medicine, Pharma, Agriculture and related S&T areas) disciplines. | Part-time and sponsored students are not considered under the Program. Also students who have submitted their thesis for award of the Degree of Ph.D. are not eligible to apply.

scheme_name: Overseas Visiting Doctoral Fellowship
question: What are the areas covered under this Fellowship?
answer: All areas of Science, Technology, Engineering and Mathematics (including Medicine, Pharma, Agriculture and related S&T areas) disciplines will be covered by this fellowship.

scheme_name: Overseas Visiting Doctoral Fellowship
question: What is the nature of support for the Fellow?
answer: The selected fellows will be paid a monthly fellowship amount equivalent to US $ 2000, one-time Contingency/Preparatory allowances of [?]60,000/- to cover visa fee, airport transfer charges, medical insurance etc. The selected fellows will also be provided shortest route economy class air fare from their place of work in India to the place of the host institute and back. Students should make their own arrangement for accommodation etc.

scheme_name: Overseas Visiting Doctoral Fellowship
question: Will SERB provide any leave, medical, etc. to the Supervisor of the fellowship awardee during his/her visit to the Overseas Host Institute?
answer: For supervisors who are in regular employment, rules governing payment of salary, leave, medical, gratuity, GPF and pension etc. of the organization/ institution/ university to which the fellow belongs would continue to be applicable. No liability on any of these accounts will be borne by SERB.

scheme_name: Overseas Visiting Doctoral Fellowship
question: When can we apply for the OVD Fellowship Programme? Is it open throughout the year?
answer: The application for consideration under the Overseas Visiting Doctoral Fellowship Program (OVDF) can be submitted only when the call for application is made by Purdue University, West Lafayette, USA and University of Alberta, Edmonton, Canada.

scheme_name: Overseas Visiting Doctoral Fellowship
question: Can the Fellowship awardee claim their regular institute fellowship while during OVDF period?
answer: The selected fellows while taking up the SERB overseas fellowship should not draw their regular research fellowship in India.

scheme_name: Overseas Visiting Doctoral Fellowship
question: When should the selected fellows start their OVDF Fellowship?
answer: The candidates selected for the award of the fellowship should commence their research in the overseas institution as per the letter of offer given by Purdue University, West Lafayette, USA and University of Alberta, Edmonton, Canada.

scheme_name: Overseas Visiting Doctoral Fellowship
question: Is there any time limit to the visit of Supervisors to their respective Overseas Institutes?
answer: The exchange visit of the supervisors should be during the tenure of the Ph.D. work of the applicant. Both supervisors should ensure a residency period of at least two weeks and not exceeding 30 days in their respective foreign institutes.

scheme_name: Financial Assistance under Odisha Working Journalist Welfare Scheme
question: What is the ‘Odisha Working Journalist Welfare Scheme’?
answer: The 'Odisha Working Journalist Welfare Scheme' is an initiative launched by the Information & Public Relations Department, Government of Odisha. The scheme aims to provide financial assistance to the legal heir of a working journalist in the event of the journalist's death or permanent incapacitation.

scheme_name: Financial Assistance under Odisha Working Journalist Welfare Scheme
question: Who is eligible to benefit from the scheme?
answer: The scheme is designed to provide financial assistance to the legal heirs of working journalists in Odisha who face financial challenges due to the death or permanent incapacitation of the journalist.

scheme_name: Financial Assistance under Odisha Working Journalist Welfare Scheme
question: What is the ex-gratia amount provided under the scheme in case of a journalist's death?
answer: In the event of a working journalist's death, the scheme provides an ex-gratia amount of [?]4,00,000/- to the legal heir of the deceased journalist.

scheme_name: Financial Assistance under Odisha Working Journalist Welfare Scheme
question: How much ex-gratia is offered under the scheme in case of permanent incapacitation of a journalist?
answer: In case of permanent incapacitation of a working journalist, the Ex-Gratia Scheme provides a financial assistance amounting to [?]2,00,000/- to the legal heir of the deceased journalist.

scheme_name: Financial Assistance under Odisha Working Journalist Welfare Scheme
question: Who can apply for the benefits in case of the journalist's death or permanent incapacitation?
answer: The applicant should be a legal heir of the working journalist to claim benefits under the Scheme. In the event of the journalist's death or permanent incapacitation, the legal heir can apply for financial assistance.

scheme_name: Financial Assistance under Odisha Working Journalist Welfare Scheme
question: How is "Permanent Incapacitation" defined under the scheme?
answer: "Permanent Incapacitation" refers to a condition where the working journalist becomes wholly unfit for the profession due to accident, disease, or any other reason.

scheme_name: Financial Assistance under Odisha Working Journalist Welfare Scheme
question: Where can I get more information about the Odisha Working Journalist Welfare Scheme?
answer: For detailed information, individuals can contact the Information & Public Relations Department of the Government of Odisha.

scheme_name: Financial Assistance under Odisha Working Journalist Welfare Scheme
question: How to apply under the scheme?
answer: The eligible applicants need to visit and apply through the official web portal of the "Odisha Working Journalist Welfare Scheme Application". i.e. https://owjws.odisha.gov.in/

scheme_name: P1, P2, P3, P4, SIV, Guided Flying

scheme_name: Poshan Aahaar- Madhya Pradesh

scheme_name: Poshan Aahaar- Madhya Pradesh

scheme_name: Poshan Aahaar- Madhya Pradesh

scheme_name: Poshan Aahaar- Madhya Pradesh

scheme_name: Poshan Aahaar- Madhya Pradesh

scheme_name: Poshan Aahaar- Madhya Pradesh

answer: Visit the nearest Anganwadi center during working hours with necessary identification and documentation.

scheme_name: Poshan Aahaar- Madhya Pradesh
question: Is there any cost involved for the beneficiaries?
answer: No, the scheme provides free supplementary nutrition to eligible beneficiaries.

scheme_name: Poshan Aahaar- Madhya Pradesh
question: Can beneficiaries outside Madhya Pradesh avail of this scheme?
answer: No, the scheme is only for residents of Madhya Pradesh.

scheme_name: Padma Awards

scheme_name: Padma Awards

scheme_name: Padma Awards

answer: Any individual, irrespective of race, occupation, position, or gender, who has made exceptional contributions in any field can receive the Padma Awards.

scheme_name: Padma Awards
question: Are government employees eligible for Padma Awards?
answer: Serving government employees are generally not eligible, except for doctors and scientists who can be considered.

scheme_name: Padma Awards
question: Can a person nominate themselves for Padma Awards?
answer: Yes, any individual can nominate themselves for the Padma Awards through the prescribed process.

scheme_name: Padma Awards
question: Is there any cash reward in Padma Awards?
answer: No, there is no monetary reward or cash benefit associated with the Padma Awards.

scheme_name: Padma Awards

answer: The Padma Awards are announced every year on 26th January, on the occasion of Republic Day.

scheme_name: Padma Awards

answer: The Padma Awards ceremony is usually held in the months of March or April at Rashtrapati Bhavan.

scheme_name: Padma Awards
question: Can Padma Awards be given posthumously?
answer: Yes, Padma Awards can be conferred posthumously, but only in rare and highly deserving cases.

scheme_name: Padma Awards

answer: A maximum of 120 Padma Awards are given each year, excluding posthumous awards and awards to foreigners.

scheme_name: Padma Awards

answer: The Padma Awards Committee, constituted by the Prime Minister, selects the awardees.

scheme_name: Padma Awards
question: Can a Padma Award be withdrawn after being given?
answer: Yes, the President of India has the authority to cancel or annul a Padma Award if required.

scheme_name: Padma Awards

answer: No, the Padma Award cannot be used as a prefix or suffix to the awardee’s name in any manner.

scheme_name: Padma Awards

answer: The names of Padma Awardees are officially published in the Gazette of India.

scheme_name: Prosthetic Aid and Appliances for Person with Disabilities

scheme_name: Prosthetic Aid and Appliances for Person with Disabilities
question: What benefits does the scheme offer?
answer: The scheme provides relief in disability as well as equipment for self-employment within the limit of [?]20,000.

scheme_name: Prosthetic Aid and Appliances for Person with Disabilities
question: What type of equipment is provided under the scheme?
answer: Equipment such as artificial limbs, crutches, tricycles, folding wheelchairs, hearing aids, musical instruments, Braille kits, and more are provided.

scheme_name: Prosthetic Aid and Appliances for Person with Disabilities
question: Is the scheme funded by the state government?
answer: Yes, the scheme is fully funded by the state government of Gujarat.

scheme_name: Prosthetic Aid and Appliances for Person with Disabilities

answer: Yes, individuals below the age of 16 are not provided with employment-oriented tools under the scheme.

scheme_name: Prosthetic Aid and Appliances for Person with Disabilities
question: How often can an individual avail of equipment under the scheme?
answer: Equipment, both employment-oriented and disability-relieving, are available once in a period of 5 years.

scheme_name: Prosthetic Aid and Appliances for Person with Disabilities
question: How to apply for the scheme?
answer: Eligible applicants can apply through the e-Samaj Kalyan Portal: https://esamajkalyan.gujarat.gov.in/

scheme_name: Personal Accident Assistance Scheme
question: Who is eligible for this scheme?
answer: Residents of Uttarakhand engaged in agricultural work or operating agricultural equipment in Mandi areas are eligible. The minimum age for claiming assistance is 18 years.

scheme_name: Personal Accident Assistance Scheme
question: What types of accidents are covered under the scheme?
answer: Accidents occurring during agricultural work, operation of agricultural machinery, digging or deepening wells and ponds, using tractors for threshing or transporting produce, or while working in the field are covered.

scheme_name: Personal Accident Assistance Scheme
question: How soon must an accident be reported?
answer: The affected farmer/laborer must report the accident to the local market committee or district officer as soon as possible, and within 45 days of the incident.

scheme_name: Personal Accident Assistance Scheme
question: Who conducts the investigation after an accident report is submitted?
answer: An investigation is conducted by the individual submitting the report or a designated market committee employee within 15 days of receiving the report.

scheme_name: Personal Accident Assistance Scheme
question: How should the claim form be filled?
answer: The claim form must be completely filled out, signed by the applicant, and include the left or right thumb impression. If thumbs are missing, other fingerprints as specified may be used.

scheme_name: Personal Accident Assistance Scheme
question: Who approves and sanctions the claim?
answer: After scrutiny by the Secretary, the claim form along with recommendations is sent to the Chairman/Administrator for approval. The claim is also reviewed by Revenue Department officials before approval.

scheme_name: Personal Accident Assistance Scheme
question: How is the payment processed after approval?
answer: Once approved, the claim form is sent to the Managing Director of the Uttarakhand Agricultural Produce Marketing Board. The Mandi Board prepares a draft of the claim amount in the claimant’s name and sends it to the concerned Mandi Secretary for payment.

scheme_name: Production of Audio Albums of songs on Patriotism & National Integration
question: What is the minimum number of songs required in the audio album and what specific themes must they address?
answer: The audio album must contain at least 10 songs specifically focused on Patriotism & National Integration themes. Each song's melody and musical arrangement must be appropriate to the content, ensuring alignment with the patriotic values the program aims to promote.

scheme_name: Production of Audio Albums of songs on Patriotism & National Integration
question: Can I include only solo performances in my audio album or are there specific composition requirements I must follow?
answer: You cannot have an album with solo songs only. At least 50% of your songs must be group songs and children's songs, ensuring variety in vocal arrangements and making the content suitable for educational and community participation.

scheme_name: Production of Audio Albums of songs on Patriotism & National Integration
question: What type of content restrictions apply to the lyrics I compose for the patriotic songs in my album?
answer: You must not include any adverse remarks in written or verbal form against any Governments, Individuals, or Institutions, nor anything against caste, creed, and religion that may hurt anybody's sentiments. All content must promote positive patriotic and national integration values.

scheme_name: Production of Audio Albums of songs on Patriotism & National Integration
question: How many copies of the finished audio album must I provide and what happens to these copies after submission?
answer: You must provide 300 copies of your completed audio albums to Tiatr Academy of Goa. These copies will be distributed to schools and groups participating in various competitions, and may also be offered to other educational institutions and individuals interested in promoting patriotism.

scheme_name: Production of Audio Albums of songs on Patriotism & National Integration
question: Who is eligible to apply for this financial support program for producing patriotic audio albums in Konkani language?
answer: Any tiatr artiste, whether commercial or non-commercial, can apply for this program. You must demonstrate your involvement in the tiatr fraternity and commitment to producing quality Konkani songs focused on patriotic themes.

scheme_name: Production of Audio Albums of songs on Patriotism & National Integration
question: What documents must I submit along with my application form to be considered for this audio album production scheme?
answer: You need to submit a prescribed application form, self-attested copy of Aadhaar Card, self-attested copy of Permanent Account Number Card, and a typed copy of lyrics for all songs you plan to include in your album.

scheme_name: Production of Audio Albums of songs on Patriotism & National Integration
question: Is there a quality control process for the song lyrics I submit, and who evaluates the content before approval?
answer: Yes, your lyrics will be scrutinized by a Recommendation Committee appointed by Tiatr Academy of Goa. The committee has the authority to advise improvements to enhance lyrical quality and the academy reserves the right to disapprove lyrics based on committee recommendations.

scheme_name: Production of Audio Albums of songs on Patriotism & National Integration
question: Can I seek additional financial support through sponsorship while participating in this government-supported audio album production program?
answer: Yes, you are permitted to take sponsorship to meet the cost of album production in addition to the financial support provided by Tiatr Academy of Goa. This flexibility helps ensure you can produce a high-quality album meeting all specified standards.

scheme_name: Production of Audio Albums of songs on Patriotism & National Integration
question: What commercial rights do I retain after providing the required copies to the academy for distribution purposes?
answer: You retain full commercial rights to sell the remaining Compact Discs after providing the mandatory 300 copies to Tiatr Academy of Goa. This allows you to recover additional production costs and potentially earn from your creative work.

scheme_name: Production of Audio Albums of songs on Patriotism & National Integration
question: Must I obtain any official approval before beginning the actual production of my patriotic audio album?
answer: Yes, you must obtain an official letter of acceptance from Tiatr Academy of Goa before commencing production. This letter confirms approval of your lyrics and authorization to proceed with album production according to the specified norms.

scheme_name: Production of Audio Albums of songs on Patriotism & National Integration
question: What specific information must I provide in the application form regarding the composition breakdown of my proposed album?
answer: You must provide details including your name, complete address, contact number, Permanent Account Number, Aadhaar Card number, album title, producer name, and detailed breakdown of Kantaram specifying the number of solos, duets, duos, trios, quartets/quintets, and choral songs.

scheme_name: Production of Audio Albums of songs on Patriotism & National Integration
question: Where can I obtain the application form for this audio album production scheme and is online submission available?
answer: You must visit the office of Tiatr Academy of Goa to collect the prescribed application form. The scheme accepts applications through offline mode only, requiring physical submission of all documents and materials.

scheme_name: Production of Audio Albums of songs on Patriotism & National Integration
question: What happens if the Recommendation Committee suggests changes to my submitted song lyrics during the review process?
answer: You must incorporate any suggestions or improvements recommended by the committee to enhance the quality of your lyrics. The committee provides advisory support to ensure your content meets the required standards for patriotism and national integration themes.

scheme_name: Production of Audio Albums of songs on Patriotism & National Integration
question: Are there any restrictions on the musical arrangement and melody choices I make for the patriotic songs?
answer: The melody and musical arrangement must be appropriate to the content of each song. This ensures that the musical elements complement and enhance the patriotic themes, creating an effective audio experience for listeners in educational settings.

scheme_name: Protection Against Domestic Violence

scheme_name: Protection Against Domestic Violence

scheme_name: Protection Against Domestic Violence

answer: The scheme "Protection Against Domestic Violence" is not limited to married women; it applies to all females in domestic relationships, including daughters, sisters, mothers, and women in live-in relationships who are subjected to violence or abuse.

scheme_name: Protection Against Domestic Violence
question: What kind of benefits can a woman expect to receive through the scheme?

scheme_name: Protection Against Domestic Violence

scheme_name: Protection Against Domestic Violence

scheme_name: Protection Against Domestic Violence

scheme_name: Protection Against Domestic Violence

scheme_name: Pratyaksh Hanstantrit Labh / Direct Benefits Transfer For LPG
question: What Will Have To Be Done By The LPG Consumer Who Had Already Joined The Scheme Earlier?
answer: LPG consumers who had joined the scheme earlier by linking their Aadhaar number in LPG and Bank database do not need to do anything. Such consumers will get the cylinder at Market price w.e.f the date on which the scheme is launched and the cash will be transferred into their bank account. They do not have to do anything further. They can check their CTC (Cash Transfer Compliance) status on www.mylpg.in or check with their LPG distributor.

scheme_name: Pratyaksh Hanstantrit Labh / Direct Benefits Transfer For LPG
question: What Does An LPG Consumer Do To Join PAHAL (DBTL) Scheme?
answer: Option I (Primary): LPG consumers who have an Aadhaar number must provide their Aadhaar number to LPG distributor using Form 2 and to Bank using Form 1. This is the preferred mode of joining the scheme. | Option II (Secondary): If the LPG consumer does not have an Aadhaar number, he/she can do one of the following: | a. Give Bank details to the LPG distributor in Form 4 | OR | b. Give a 17-digit LPG ID to the Bank using Form 3.

scheme_name: Pratyaksh Hanstantrit Labh / Direct Benefits Transfer For LPG
question: When Can An LPG Consumer Visit The Distributorship For Submitting Aadhaar And Bank Details Seeding Forms To Join PAHAL (DBTL) Scheme?
answer: The LPG consumers can visit their LPG distributorship on any weekday during office hours for submitting the forms. For the convenience of LPG consumers, all distributorships will also remain open on their weekly off day for exclusively receiving Aadhaar & Bank detail seeding forms of the PAHAL (DBTL) scheme till the end of the grace period.

scheme_name: Pratyaksh Hanstantrit Labh / Direct Benefits Transfer For LPG
question: How Does An LPG Consumer Check His/Her PAHAL (DBTL) Joining Status?
answer: To check PAHAL (DBTL) joining status, consumers can log on to the transparency portal of their LPG Company (IOC, BPC, HPC) through www.myLPG.in and follow instructions. On each of the OMC's transparency portals, a call out with the name 'Check DBTL (CTC) Status' has been provided. Consumers can click on this and see the status both for ATC as well as BTC methods.

scheme_name: Pratyaksh Hanstantrit Labh / Direct Benefits Transfer For LPG
question: What Happens Where Transactions Sent To The Bank Fail And How Are They Dealt With?
answer: A) In case some transfers cannot be processed by the banks, they are termed as failures, and the failure cases if any along with the amount is received back from the Sponsor Bank by the OMCs. A report on such failure cases has been provided by the OMC on their portal which is accessible to the distributors as well | as Call Centre. | b) Payments returned will be re-processed twice in a span of 15 days each and if it is still not transferred, the amount will be kept for payment as and when the bank-related issues are resolved. | c) If the amount towards the subsequent cylinder delivered is successfully transferred then the pending amount also will be transferred thereafter. | d) The time period up to which such payments will be kept pending will be 3 months or the end of the current financial year whichever is later.

In other words, when the Termination Voucher is made the net amount of the Security Deposit of equipment minus the Permanent Advance amount will be refunded to consumers. | b) If such consumers are transferred to another district where PAHAL (DBTL) has been launched, they will be given an advance once they become a consumer at the new location and are handed over the Subscription Voucher. | c) OMC Software has the provision to capture Security deposits and advance amounts separately and account for them in the ERP accounting system. | d) For CTC consumers located in the same city on transfer without any surrendering of equipment and refund of deposit (TTV/CTA), Permanent Advance amount will not be refunded.

scheme_name: Personality Development and Yogasan Training Camp for Schedule Caste
question: Who is eligible to apply under this scheme?

scheme_name: Personality Development and Yogasan Training Camp for Schedule Caste
question: Is there any educational qualification required to be eligible for this scheme?

scheme_name: Personality Development and Yogasan Training Camp for Schedule Caste

scheme_name: Personality Development and Yogasan Training Camp for Schedule Caste

scheme_name: Personality Development and Yogasan Training Camp for Schedule Caste

scheme_name: Personality Development and Yogasan Training Camp for Schedule Caste
question: What is the duration of the training camp?

scheme_name: Personality Development and Yogasan Training Camp for Schedule Caste

scheme_name: Personality Development and Yogasan Training Camp for Schedule Caste

scheme_name: Personality Development and Yogasana Training Camp (TASP)

scheme_name: Promotion of Energy Audit and Conservation of Energy (PEACE): Awareness Programme

scheme_name: Promotion of Energy Audit and Conservation of Energy (PEACE): Awareness Programme

scheme_name: Promotion of Energy Audit and Conservation of Energy (PEACE): Awareness Programme

scheme_name: Promotion of Energy Audit and Conservation of Energy (PEACE): Awareness Programme
question: What are the key components of the PEACE scheme by the MSME Department, Government of Tamil Nadu?

scheme_name: Promotion of Energy Audit and Conservation of Energy (PEACE): Detailed Energy Audit
question: What is the purpose of the "Promotion of Energy Audit and Conservation of Energy (PEACE)" scheme's overall effort in promoting energy efficiency?
answer: The scheme endeavors to promote energy efficiency in MSMEs by providing financial incentives, expert guidance through audits, and encouraging the adoption of sustainable energy practices.

scheme_name: Promotion of Energy Audit and Conservation of Energy (PEACE): Detailed Energy Audit
question: Are enterprises with subsequent energy audits subject to the same eligibility criteria as those undergoing an energy audit for the first time under the PEACE scheme?

scheme_name: Promotion of Energy Audit and Conservation of Energy (PEACE): Detailed Energy Audit
question: What is the maximum ceiling for the subsidy under the PEACE scheme?
answer: The maximum subsidy is 75% of the audit cost, with a cap of [?]1,00,000 per energy audit.

scheme_name: Promotion of Energy Audit and Conservation of Energy (PEACE): Detailed Energy Audit
question: Can enterprises with multiple units avail the subsidy separately for each unit under the PEACE scheme?
answer: Yes, enterprises with multiple units can avail the subsidy separately for each unit, but the overall ceiling should not be applied for both the original and subsequent energy audits.

scheme_name: Promotion of Energy Audit and Conservation of Energy (PEACE): Detailed Energy Audit
question: Is there a specific time gap requirement between the previous and subsequent energy audits for MSMEs under the PEACE scheme?
answer: Yes, there should be a minimum gap of three years between the completion of the previous energy audit and the subsequent energy audit.

scheme_name: Promotion of Energy Audit and Conservation of Energy (PEACE): Detailed Energy Audit
question: How is the subsidy released if an MSME avails a loan for the energy audit under the PEACE scheme?

scheme_name: Promotion of Energy Audit and Conservation of Energy (PEACE): Detailed Energy Audit

scheme_name: Promotion of Energy Audit and Conservation of Energy (PEACE): Detailed Energy Audit

scheme_name: Promotion of Energy Audit and Conservation of Energy (PEACE): Detailed Energy Audit

scheme_name: Promotion of Energy Audit and Conservation of Energy (PEACE): Detailed Energy Audit

scheme_name: Promotion of Energy Audit and Conservation of Energy (PEACE): Detailed Energy Audit

scheme_name: Promotion of Energy Audit and Conservation of Energy (PEACE): Detailed Energy Audit
question: Are there any restrictions on the eligibility of enterprises for the subsidy under the PEACE scheme?
answer: All existing manufacturing MSMEs in the state are eligible for the subsidy, particularly those undergoing energy audit for the first time or taking up subsequent audits after a gap of three years.

scheme_name: Promotion of Energy Audit and Conservation of Energy (PEACE): Detailed Energy Audit
question: What financial support does the scheme provide for MSMEs undergoing energy audits, and are there any specific conditions?
answer: MSMEs can avail 75% of the audit cost, up to [?]1,00,000, with the subsidy released after completion and certification of the Energy Audit Report.

scheme_name: Promotion of Energy Audit and Conservation of Energy (PEACE): Detailed Energy Audit
question: What information does the Energy Audit Final Report for the PEACE scheme include?
answer: The report includes specific recommendations, quantitative and qualitative details, outlay, projections of energy/cost savings, payback period, executive summary, period of conduct, and conclusions.

scheme_name: Promotion of Energy Audit and Conservation of Energy (PEACE): Detailed Energy Audit
question: Who constitutes the Energy Audit team for the PEACE scheme, and what are the accreditation requirements?
answer: The team consists of Bureau of Energy Efficiency empanelled firms or individuals led by accredited Energy Auditors. Accreditation by the Bureau of Energy Efficiency is mandatory.

scheme_name: Promotion of Energy Audit and Conservation of Energy (PEACE): Detailed Energy Audit
question: What is the methodology involved in the "Detailed Energy Audit" component of the PEACE scheme?
answer: The methodology includes a plant survey, discussions with plant personnel, analysis of past performance data, measurements of electrical parameters, energy performance assessment, and detailed techno-economic analysis.

scheme_name: Promotion of Energy Audit and Conservation of Energy (PEACE): Detailed Energy Audit
question: How does an effective energy management system benefit MSMEs participating in the PEACE scheme?
answer: Implementing an effective energy management system helps MSMEs reduce energy costs, cut negative environmental impact, and identifies opportunities for cost savings through improved services.

scheme_name: Promotion of Energy Audit and Conservation of Energy (PEACE): Incentive for Implementing Energy Audit Recommendations
question: Why is there a requirement for a minimum three-year gap between energy audits?
answer: The gap ensures a meaningful assessment of energy savings and the impact of implemented recommendations.

scheme_name: Promotion of Energy Audit and Conservation of Energy (PEACE): Incentive for Implementing Energy Audit Recommendations
question: What does the application status tracking link entail?

scheme_name: Promotion of Energy Audit and Conservation of Energy (PEACE): Incentive for Implementing Energy Audit Recommendations
question: How is the percentage of savings in specific energy consumption calculated?

scheme_name: Promotion of Energy Audit and Conservation of Energy (PEACE): Incentive for Implementing Energy Audit Recommendations
question: Why is proof of connected load required in the application documents?

scheme_name: Promotion of Energy Audit and Conservation of Energy (PEACE): Incentive for Implementing Energy Audit Recommendations

scheme_name: Promotion of Energy Audit and Conservation of Energy (PEACE): Incentive for Implementing Energy Audit Recommendations

scheme_name: Promotion of Energy Audit and Conservation of Energy (PEACE): Incentive for Implementing Energy Audit Recommendations

scheme_name: Promotion of Energy Audit and Conservation of Energy (PEACE): Incentive for Implementing Energy Audit Recommendations

scheme_name: Promotion of Energy Audit and Conservation of Energy (PEACE): Incentive for Implementing Energy Audit Recommendations

scheme_name: Promotion of Energy Audit and Conservation of Energy (PEACE): Incentive for Implementing Energy Audit Recommendations
question: When should MSMEs file an online application after implementing energy audit recommendations?

scheme_name: Promotion of Energy Audit and Conservation of Energy (PEACE): Incentive for Implementing Energy Audit Recommendations
question: What costs are covered under the eligible components for subsidy?

scheme_name: Promotion of Energy Audit and Conservation of Energy (PEACE): Incentive for Implementing Energy Audit Recommendations

scheme_name: Promotion of Energy Audit and Conservation of Energy (PEACE): Incentive for Implementing Energy Audit Recommendations

scheme_name: Promotion of Energy Audit and Conservation of Energy (PEACE): Incentive for Implementing Energy Audit Recommendations

scheme_name: Promotion of Energy Audit and Conservation of Energy (PEACE): Incentive for Implementing Energy Audit Recommendations

scheme_name: Promotion of Energy Audit and Conservation of Energy (PEACE): Training Programme

scheme_name: Promotion of Energy Audit and Conservation of Energy (PEACE): Training Programme

scheme_name: Promotion of Energy Audit and Conservation of Energy (PEACE): Training Programme

scheme_name: Promotion of Energy Audit and Conservation of Energy (PEACE): Training Programme

scheme_name: Paired Early Career Fellowship in Applied Research

scheme_name: Paired Early Career Fellowship in Applied Research

question: What is the objective of the "Promotion of Intensive Aquaculture through Introduction of Bio-floc Technology" initiative by the government of Odisha?
answer: The objective of the "Promotion of Intensive Aquaculture through Introduction of Bio-floc Technology" initiative by the government of Odisha is to promote and enhance aquaculture practices through the introduction of bio-floc technology. The initiative aims to encourage the adoption of sustainable and intensive aquaculture methods using bio-floc technology, which utilizes microbial communities to maintain water quality and support high-density fish and shrimp farming.

scheme_name: Promotion Of Intensive Aquaculture Through Introduction Of Bio-floc Technology During The Year 2021-22
question: What is bio-floc technology, and how does it benefit aquaculture practices?
answer: Bio-floc technology is a sustainable aquaculture approach that utilizes microbial communities called bio-flocs to improve water quality and enhance productivity in aquaculture systems. In this technique, a carbon source, typically in the form of organic matter or carbohydrate-based feed, is provided to stimulate the growth of beneficial microorganisms. These microorganisms form clusters or aggregates called bio-flocs, which consist of bacteria, protozoa, and other microorganisms.

scheme_name: Promotion Of Intensive Aquaculture Through Introduction Of Bio-floc Technology During The Year 2021-22
question: Who is eligible to participate in the initiative?
answer: Farmers or individuals engaged in aquaculture activities. Fish or shrimp farmers in specific geographical areas or regions within Odisha. Ownership status of the aquaculture farms (individuals, cooperatives, self-help groups, etc.). Farm size or production capacity. Compliance with any specific requirements or regulations related to aquaculture practices.
