scheme_name: Pradhan Mantri Bhartiya Janaushadhi Pariyojana
question: What Is Pradhan Mantri Bhartiya Janaushadhi Pariyojana (PMBJP)?
answer: 'Pradhan Mantri Bhartiya Janaushadhi Pariyojana (PMBJP)' is a campaign launched by the Department of Pharmaceuticals in association with Central Pharma Public Sector Undertakings to provide quality medicines at affordable prices to the masses through dedicated outlets called 'Pradhan Mantri Bhartiya Janaushadhi Kendra'. These provide generic medicines at a much lower price. The potency of these medicines is the same as compared to expensive branded medicines available on the open market.

scheme_name: Pradhan Mantri Bhartiya Janaushadhi Pariyojana
question: What Is A Generic Medicine?
answer: Generic drugs are marketed under a non-proprietary or approved name rather than a proprietary or brand name. Generic drugs are equally effective and inexpensive compared to their branded counterparts.

scheme_name: Pradhan Mantri Bhartiya Janaushadhi Pariyojana
question: What Is PMBI?
answer: PMBI (Pharmaceuticals & Medical Devices Bureau of India) has been established under the Department of Pharmaceuticals, Govt. of India, with the support of all the CPSUs for co-coordinating procurement, supply, and marketing of generic drugs through the Pradhan Mantri Bhartiya Janaushadhi Kendras.

scheme_name: Pradhan Mantri Bhartiya Janaushadhi Pariyojana
question: How The Quality, Safety And Efficacy Of Medicines Are Ensured?
answer: The quality, safety, and efficacy of medicines are ensured by getting each batch of medicines procured from CPSUs as well as private suppliers tested from NABL-approved laboratories and conforming to the required standards before the same are supplied to Super stockists /Pradhan Mantri Bhartiya Janaushadhi Kendras from the warehouse of PMBI.

scheme_name: Pradhan Mantri Bhartiya Janaushadhi Pariyojana
question: Are Generic Drugs As Effective As Branded Ones?
answer: Generic drugs have the same efficacy and therapeutic value as that of branded medicines.

scheme_name: Pradhan Mantri Bhartiya Janaushadhi Pariyojana
question: How Do Generic Medicines Benefit The Patients?
answer: By taking generic medicines, a patient can reduce his/her expenditure on medicines drastically.

scheme_name: Pradhan Mantri Bhartiya Janaushadhi Pariyojana
question: What Are The Medicines Available From Pradhan Mantri Janaushadhi Kendras And What Are Their Prices?
answer: The endeavor of PMBI is to make available all therapeutic medicines at Jan Aushadhi Stores. A list of medicines with their MRP which are presently available is given under the heading "PMBJP Products- Therapeutic groups" on the website of PMBI. More medicines are being added to this list.

scheme_name: Pradhan Mantri Bhartiya Janaushadhi Pariyojana
question: How Many Pradhan Mantri Janaushadhi Kendras Have Been Opened And What Are Their Locations?
answer: More than 8604 are currently functional. A list of State-wise / District-wise PMBJK along with their locations are available under the heading "PMBJP => PMBJP Kendra" on the website of PMBI.

scheme_name: Pradhan Mantri Bhartiya Janaushadhi Pariyojana
question: What Is The Timing (Opening And Closing) Of The Pradhan Mantri Janaushadhi Kendras?
answer: The normal working hours of PMBJK are 8 AM to 8 PM.

scheme_name: Pradhan Mantri Bhartiya Janaushadhi Pariyojana
question: How The Medicines Are Procured And Supplied To Pradhan Mantri Janaushadhi Kendras?
answer: Medicines are procured through an open tender system from private manufacturers as well as CPSUs. Each batch of procured medicines are duly tested from impanelled NABL laboratories and sent to Kendra through distribution network.

scheme_name: Pradhan Mantri Bhartiya Janaushadhi Pariyojana
question: Who Can Open A Pradhan Mantri Janaushadhi Kendras?
answer: Individual entrepreneur / Proprietor | Partnership | Charitable Institute/Hospital | NGO/ Trust/ Society | Government/ Government Nominated Agency | Any Other (Please specify)

scheme_name: Pradhan Mantri Bhartiya Janaushadhi Pariyojana
question: What Are The Requirements For Opening A Pradhan Mantri Janaushadhi Kendra By An Organization / Individual Other Than A Government Nominated?
answer: Own space or hired space duly supported by the proper lease agreement Minimum required space conforming to standards as approved by the PMBI Sale license from competent authority (Retail drug license in the name of the applicant and/or Tin No.) | Proof of securing a pharmacist (name of the pharmacist, Registration with the State Council etc. needs to be furnished) | Financial capacity to run the Store by submitting the document (ITR, Bank Statement, PAN/Aadhar, etc.) | Drug License in name of "Pradhan Mantri Janaushadhi Kendra".

scheme_name: Pradhan Mantri Bhartiya Janaushadhi Pariyojana
question: What is the procedure for opening a Pradhan Mantri Bhartiya Janaushadhi Kendras?
answer: For detailed guidelines and procedures, please click "Apply for Kendra" on our website.

scheme_name: Post Matric College Scholarship (Scheduled Caste)
question: What is the "Post Matric College Scholarship" scheme?
answer: The scheme provides financial assistance to Scheduled Caste students for pursuing higher education.

scheme_name: Post Matric College Scholarship (Scheduled Caste)
question: Who is eligible for this scholarship?
answer: The student must belong to the Scheduled Caste category and come from a family with an income limit of up to [?]6.00 lakh.

scheme_name: Post Matric College Scholarship (Scheduled Caste)
question: What is the income limit for eligibility?
answer: The family's income must be up to [?]6.00 lakh per year.

scheme_name: Post Matric College Scholarship (Scheduled Caste)
question: Can students from non-government institutions apply?
answer: Yes, but students whose parents' income exceeds [?]2.50 lakh are not eligible for subsistence allowance.

scheme_name: Post Matric College Scholarship (Scheduled Caste)
question: What amount is reimbursed under this scheme?

scheme_name: Post Matric College Scholarship (Scheduled Caste)
question: Are government school students eligible for fee reimbursement?

scheme_name: Post Matric College Scholarship (Scheduled Caste)
question: Can students living in departmental hostels apply?

scheme_name: Post Matric College Scholarship (Scheduled Caste)
question: Is there a hostel facility provided under this scheme?
answer: Yes, students residing in departmental hostels may be eligible for one-third of the subsistence allowance.

scheme_name: Post Matric College Scholarship (Scheduled Caste)
question: Are students from Sambal Yojana families eligible for this scheme?

scheme_name: Post Matric College Scholarship (Scheduled Caste)
question: Do students need to submit any documents for this scheme?

scheme_name: Prime Minister Early Career Research Grant
question: What is the age limit for availing PM ECRG?
answer: The upper age limit for PM ECRG is 42 years, with a relaxation of three years for SC/ST/OBC/ Physically challenged and women candidates.

scheme_name: Prime Minister Early Career Research Grant
question: What is the nature of support under PM ECRG scheme?
answer: PM ECRG is a one-time grant and carries a maximum research grant of Rs. 60 Lakhs (excluding overheads) for a period of three years. The research grant covers equipment, research personnel, consumables, travel and contingency apart from overheads.

scheme_name: Prime Minister Early Career Research Grant
question: What is the duration of the PM ECRG project? Can it be extended?
answer: PM ECRG project period is of 3 years. There is no provision for extension of the project duration.

scheme_name: Prime Minister Early Career Research Grant
question: When should I apply for PM ECRG? Can I apply for the projects throughout the year?
answer: The Call for applications will be notified through the website www.anrfonline.in and www.anrf.gov.in . The application form along with a proper research proposal highlighting the research work to be undertaken should be submitted online through the website www.anrfonline.in during the call opening period.

scheme_name: Prime Minister Early Career Research Grant
question: How should I apply for PM ECRG?
answer: All applications should be submitted through the ANRF online portal www.anrfonline.in

scheme_name: Prime Minister Early Career Research Grant
question: Can I have a Co-PI in PM ECRG project? Can I have a Mentor in PM ECRG?
answer: Co-PI or Mentors are not allowed in this scheme. However, foreign nationals are mandated to have an Indian Co-PI.

scheme_name: Prime Minister Early Career Research Grant
question: I am working abroad as post-doc, and I want to return to India. I intend to apply for PM ECRG. But I have not yet finalized my place of work. Am I eligible to apply under the scheme?
answer: No. The applicant must hold a regular academic/research position in a recognized academic institution/ or national laboratories or any other recognized R&D institutions. Only after joining a research or academic institution, one can apply for the grants under this scheme.

scheme_name: Prime Minister Early Career Research Grant
question: I am implementing an PM ECRG project for the last one year. Am I eligible to apply for another project under any other scheme/award or fellowship programs of ANRF?
answer: In general, a PI is allowed to operate only one ANRF project at a time. Exceptions are allowed for some specific calls under certain topics/programs/schemes. In all other cases, PI can submit another proposal under regular schemes of ANRF six months prior to the date of completion of the ongoing PM ECRG project.

scheme_name: Prime Minister Early Career Research Grant
question: What documents should I send for receiving the next instalments of the grant?
answer: The PIs should upload annual Progress Report and financial statements at the end of each financial year. The release of the next instalment of the grant will be considered only after submission of Utilization Certificate (separately for Recurring & Non-recurring) and Statement of Expenditure, financial year wise.

scheme_name: Prime Minister Early Career Research Grant
question: I intend to change my Host Institution? What procedure should I follow?
answer: Change of host institute will be considered only (i) from a private/public/government institution to any other public/government institution or (ii) General administrative transfers in government or public funded institutions. Change of institute will not be considered for any other cases. Change of host institution can be undertaken only after obtaining due approval from ANRF.Transfer of the project along with balance grant and the assets to the new institute is allowed, provided the administrative authority of both institutes agree in writing. NOC from the previous host institute and Endorsement Form from the new host Institute must be sent to ANRF through the online portal.

scheme_name: Prime Minister Early Career Research Grant
question: What is the procedure for surrendering PM ECRG project?
answer: For termination of the project, PI need to inform the ANRF through the host institution immediately. The implementing institute should not incur any expenditure from the date of termination of the project or the date of resignation of PI. The institute must also arrange for the submission of relevant documents.

scheme_name: Prime Minister Early Career Research Grant
question: Can I be away from the implementing Institute when I am implementing the PM ECRG project?
answer: The PIs must seek the consent of ANRF if he/she intends to be away from the implementing institute (except for field work related to the project) continuously for a period of more than eight weeks.

scheme_name: Prime Minister Early Career Research Grant
question: What should be done for the unspent grant under PM ECRG project after the completion of the tenure of the project?
answer: The following documents should be sent to the ANRF after the duration of the project is completed: | - Final Consolidated Statement of Expenditure (in duplicate) , giving expenditure financial year wise (FY) from date of start till date of completion. | - Utilization Certificates (FY wise) for all FYs (in duplicate) matching with Statement of Expenditure figures in that FY. | - Project Completion Report (PCR) with a list of publications, and patents filed/granted. | - DD/ cheque for the unspent grant, drawn in favor of 'Science & Engineering Research Fund'. | - The Principal Investigator is responsible for the timely submission of progress reports, utilization certificates, project closure report (PCR), refund of unspent balance amount etc. at the end or early closure of the project.

scheme_name: Prime Minister Early Career Research Grant
question: I am an INSPIRE Faculty Fellow. Am I eligible to apply for PM ECRG?
answer: Yes. INSPIRE Faculty, Ramanujan and Ramalingaswamy Fellows are eligible to apply under PM ECRG subject to fulfilling all other eligibility criteria.

scheme_name: Prime Minister Early Career Research Grant
question: I was National Post Doctoral Fellow (NPDF). Am I eligible to apply for PM ECRG?
answer: Yes. Applicants who have availed NPDF, SIRE are eligible to apply under PM ECRG subject to fulfilling all other eligibility criteria.

scheme_name: Prime Minister Early Career Research Grant
question: I have an ongoing TARE project. Can I apply for PM ECRG?
answer: Applicants having ongoing TARE project can submit proposal under PM ECRG six months prior to the completion of ongoing project, subject to fulfilling all other eligibility criteria.

scheme_name: Prime Minister Early Career Research Grant
question: What is the budget limit under 'Travel' and 'Contingency' Heads in PM ECRG?
answer: Budget upto Rs.1 lakh per year each under 'Travel' and 'Contingency' heads will be provided. Higher amount under 'Travel' head based on the recommendation of Expert Committee will be provided where the research work involves field work.

scheme_name: Prime Minister Early Career Research Grant
question: Are the funds sanctioned under recurring head flexible?
answer: The funds sanctioned under the Recurring-I head are flexible, meaning the PI can use money allocated for consumables, manpower, travel, contingency, publications, or patent filing. However, there are some conditions to follow (See terms and conditions of the scheme, under travel and contingency).

scheme_name: Prime Minister Early Career Research Grant
question: Are there any upper limit on travel expenditure for the project?
answer: Yes. The expenditure under the travel head is limited to Rs. 3 Lakh for a threeyear project, and proportionately lower for projects of shorter duration, except (where the project entails field work etc.) in cases where a higher amount for travel is explicitly sanctioned in the project. International travel is permitted within this limit.

scheme_name: Prime Minister Early Career Research Grant
question: Are there any limits on contingency expenditure for the project?
answer: Yes, the expenditure under the contingency head is also limited to Rs. 3 Lakh for a three-year project, or proportionately lower for shorter projects.

scheme_name: Prime Minister Early Career Research Grant
question: Can I use the contingency funds for paying registration fees for international conferences?
answer: Yes. Contingency funds can be used for registration charges for international conferences.

scheme_name: Prime Minister Early Career Research Grant
question: Are there specific guidelines for engaging research personnel in the project?
answer: Yes, the PI can engage research personnel as per ANRF norms, as informed through OMs - ANRF/OM/N/01/2024 and SB/S9/Z-06/2019. Additionally, the total funds under the recurring budget should not be exceeded in any case.

scheme_name: Prime Minister Early Career Research Grant
question: One JRF is approved in my project. Can I engage a SRF or an R.A or multiple research personnel in the project?
answer: Yes, the Principal Investigator (PI) has the flexibility to recruit research personnel of any designation, or multiple personnel, as needed during the course of the project. However, the PI / host institution must ensure that (a) guidelines as per ANRF's OMs viz., ANRF/OM/N/01/2024 and SB/S9/Z-06/2019 are followed, (b) total funds sanctioned under the recurring head are not exceeded in any case and (c) Any future revision of emoluments by the ANRF will apply only to the originally approved or sanctioned research personnel for the revised fellowships.

scheme_name: Prime Minister Early Career Research Grant
question: Can I delay the acceptance of the project implementation?
answer: No. The Principal Investigator (PI) must generally complete the documentation process within one month from the date the approval letter is issued. Any delay or lack of correspondence beyond one month from the PI, shall result in the withdrawal of the proposal approval.

scheme_name: Prime Minister Early Career Research Grant
question: Can I reallocate or reappropriate funds between recurring and nonrecurring budgets?
answer: No, interoperability or reappropriation between the non-recurring and recurring budgets is not permitted under any circumstances.

scheme_name: Prime Minister Early Career Research Grant
question: Can the approved equipment list be changed during the project?
answer: The change of approved or sanctioned equipment is generally not permitted and may only be considered on a case-by-case basis. The PI must obtain prior approval from ANRF to change the approved or sanctioned equipment.

scheme_name: Prime Minister Early Career Research Grant
question: How can I seek approval for publication-related expenditures?
answer: The PI must submit a request through the ANRF online portal to obtain prior approval for publication-related expenditure.

scheme_name: Prime Minister's Employment Generation Programme
question: What Is Maximum Project Cost Allowed Under PMEGP?
answer: Rs.25.00 lakhs for the manufacturing unit and Rs.10.00 lakhs for Service Unit

scheme_name: Prime Minister's Employment Generation Programme
question: What Is The Component Of Project Cost?
answer: Capital Expenditure Loan, one cycle of working capital and 10% of project cost as own contribution in case of General category and 5% of project cost in case of weaker section.

scheme_name: Prime Minister's Employment Generation Programme
question: Which Are The Financial Agencies?
answer: 27 Public Sector Banks, Regional Rural Banks(RRB), Co-operative Banks, and Private Scheduled Commercial Banks approved by respective State Task Force Committee.

scheme_name: Prime Minister's Employment Generation Programme
question: How The Capital Expenditure Loan / Cash Credit Limit Be Utilized ?
answer: Working Capital at least once should touch the 100% limit of Cash Credit within three years of the Lock-in period of M.M. and not less than 75% of the utilization of the sanctioned limit on average.

scheme_name: Prime Minister's Employment Generation Programme
question: Where The Beneficiary Has To Submit His/Her Application/ Project?
answer: The beneficiary can submit his/her application/Project online on kvic website www.kvic.org.in / kviconline.gov.in/pmegpeportal. A list of office addresses of KVIC/KVIB/DIC is available at our website.

scheme_name: Prime Minister's Employment Generation Programme
question: What Is Village Industry ?
answer: Any Village Industry (except those mentioned in the negative list) located in the Rural Area which produces any goods or renders any service with or without the use of power and in which the fixed capital investment for head of a full time artisans or worker does not exceed Rs.1.00 lakh in plain area and Rs.1.50 lakhs in hilly areas and for A & N Island and Laxdeep Rs.4.5 Lakhs.

scheme_name: Prime Minister's Employment Generation Programme
question: What Is Rural Area ?
answer: Any area classified as Village as per the revenue record of the State, irrespective of the population. It also includes an area even if classified as town provided its population does not exceed 20000.

scheme_name: Prime Minister's Employment Generation Programme
question: What Is Age Limit ?
answer: Any adult beneficiary above 18 years is eligible for financing under PMEGP.

scheme_name: Prime Minister's Employment Generation Programme
question: What Are The Main Criteria Of Project?
answer: It should fulfill the criteria of rural area (for Rural Area project), per capita investment, own contribution, negative list, and the unit should be a new one

scheme_name: Prime Minister's Employment Generation Programme
question: Whether EDP Training Is Compulsory?
answer: Before MM Claim through the PMEGP portal, EDP training of 10 working days for a Project cost of More than 5.00 lakhs and 6 Working days of training for up to Project Cost of 5.00 lakhs to the beneficiary is compulsory

scheme_name: Prime Minister's Employment Generation Programme
question: Whether Collateral Security Is Mandatory?
answer: As per RBI guidelines, the project costing up to Rs.10.00 lakhs under PMEGP loans are free from collateral security. The CGTSME provided a collateral guarantee for the project beyond Rs.5.00 lakhs and up to Rs.25.00 lakhs under the PMEGP scheme.

scheme_name: Prime Minister's Employment Generation Programme
question: What Is PMEGP Scheme, And What Are Its Objectives?
answer: Answer: PMEGP stands for Prime Minister's Employment Generation Programme, which is a credit-linked subsidy scheme launched by the Ministry of MSME, Government of India, to generate employment opportunities in the country. The main objective of the scheme is to create self-employment opportunities for unemployed youth and women entrepreneurs in rural and urban areas.

scheme_name: Prime Minister's Employment Generation Programme
question: Who Is Eligible To Apply For PMEGP Scheme, And What Is The Age Limit For The Applicants?
answer: Answer: Any individual above 18 years of age can apply for the PMEGP scheme. However, the maximum age limit for applying is 35 years for general category applicants and 40 years for SC/ST/OBC/PH/Women candidates.

scheme_name: Prime Minister's Employment Generation Programme
question: How Can I Apply For The PMEGP Scheme, And What Is The Application Procedure?
answer: Answer: You can apply for the PMEGP scheme through the online portal of KVIC, or offline by submitting the application form to the nearest KVIC office or bank. The application procedure involves filling up the application form, attaching the necessary documents, and submitting it along with the project report.

scheme_name: Prime Minister's Employment Generation Programme
question: What Are The Different Types Of Projects That Can Be Set Up Under The PMEGP Scheme?
answer: Answer: The PMEGP scheme supports various types of projects, including manufacturing, service, and business projects. The projects should be viable and have the potential to generate employment opportunities.

scheme_name: Prime Minister's Employment Generation Programme
question: How Much Financial Assistance Can I Expect To Receive Under The PMEGP Scheme, And What Is The Repayment Period?
answer: Answer: Under the PMEGP scheme, financial assistance is provided in the form of a subsidy, which ranges from 15% to 35% of the project cost, depending on the category of the applicant. The remaining amount can be obtained as a bank loan. The repayment period for the loan is generally 3 to 7 years.

scheme_name: Prime Minister's Employment Generation Programme
question: Can I Apply For Multiple Projects Under The PMEGP Scheme, And What Is The Maximum Limit?
answer: Answer: No, an individual can apply for only one project under the PMEGP scheme. However, a group of individuals can apply for a group project, subject to a maximum of 10 members.

scheme_name: Prime Minister's Employment Generation Programme
question: What Are The Documents Required To Apply For The PMEGP Scheme?
answer: Answer: The documents required for PMEGP scheme application include a project report, proof of identity and address, caste certificate (if applicable), educational qualification certificate, and bank account details.

scheme_name: Prime Minister's Employment Generation Programme
question: How Long Does It Take For The PMEGP Scheme Application To Be Processed?
answer: Answer: The processing time for the PMEGP scheme application varies from state to state and depends on various factors such as the completeness of the application, the availability of funds, and the number of applications received.

scheme_name: Prime Minister's Employment Generation Programme
question: Can I Apply For The PMEGP Scheme For An Existing Business?
answer: Answer: No, the PMEGP scheme is meant for setting up a new business or for expanding an existing business. An existing business is not eligible for financial assistance under the PMEGP scheme.

scheme_name: Prime Minister's Employment Generation Programme
question: What Is The Role Of The Khadi And Village Industries Commission (KVIC) In The PMEGP Scheme?
answer: Answer: KVIC is the nodal agency for implementing the PMEGP scheme. It is responsible for receiving and processing the applications, conducting training programs, and disbursing the subsidy to the beneficiaries through the banks.

scheme_name: Prime Minister's Employment Generation Programme
question: What Is The Project Report, And How Do I Prepare It?
answer: Answer: The project report is a detailed document that provides information about the proposed project, its feasibility, and financial viability. It includes details like project cost, sources of funding, marketing plan, and expected income and expenses. KVIC provides a format for preparing the project report, which can be downloaded from their website.

scheme_name: Prime Minister's Employment Generation Programme
question: Can I Apply For The PMEGP Scheme Offline?
answer: Answer: Yes, you can apply for the PMEGP scheme offline by submitting the application form along with the project report and necessary documents to the nearest KVIC office or bank.

scheme_name: Prime Minister's Employment Generation Programme
question: Can I Apply For The PMEGP Scheme Online?
answer: Answer: Yes, you can apply for the PMEGP scheme online through the KVIC portal. The process involves registering on the portal, filling up the application form, and uploading the necessary documents.

scheme_name: Prime Minister's Employment Generation Programme
question: What Are The Documents Required For The PMEGP Scheme Application?
answer: Answer: The documents required for the PMEGP scheme application include proof of identity and address, educational qualification certificate, caste certificate (if applicable), project report, and bank account details.

scheme_name: Prime Minister's Employment Generation Programme
question: Can I Make Changes To My PMEGP Scheme Application After Submission?
answer: Answer: No, you cannot make changes to your PMEGP scheme application after submission. Therefore, it is important to ensure that all the information provided in the application is accurate and complete before submitting it.

scheme_name: Prime Minister's Employment Generation Programme
question: How Long Does It Take For The PMEGP Scheme Application To Be Processed?
answer: Answer: The processing time for the PMEGP scheme application varies from state to state and depends on various factors such as the completeness of the application, the availability of funds, and the number of applications received.

scheme_name: Prime Minister's Employment Generation Programme
question: How Will I Know If My PMEGP Scheme Application Has Been Approved?
answer: Answer: Once your PMEGP scheme application is approved, you will receive an approval letter from KVIC or the bank, along with the sanction letter stating the amount of subsidy and loan that you are eligible for.

scheme_name: Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojna (PMFBY)
question: I'm a tenant farmer without formal land ownership documents. Can I still apply for crop insurance under PMFBY if I can prove I cultivate the land?
answer: Yes, tenant farmers and sharecroppers can apply with a valid land tenure agreement. You must provide evidence of your cultivation rights through state-recognized documents or agreements.

scheme_name: Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojna (PMFBY)
question: My crops were damaged by unseasonal rains after harvesting while drying in the field. Does PMFBY cover such losses?
answer: Coverage is available for up to 14 days post-harvest for crops kept in "cut & spread" condition in the field, specifically for damage from cyclonic/unseasonal rains. You must report the damage immediately.

scheme_name: Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojna (PMFBY)
question: What is the exact premium rate for Kharif paddy, and how is the government subsidy calculated?
answer: Farmers pay 2% of the sum insured for Kharif food crops. The difference between the actuarial premium rate and farmer's share is jointly subsidized by Central and State governments equally.

scheme_name: Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojna (PMFBY)
question: If a drought prevents me from sowing crops despite preparation, what percentage of compensation can I claim?
answer: You can claim up to 25% of the sum insured under prevented sowing coverage, provided the majority of farmers in your notified area were also prevented from sowing due to adverse conditions.

scheme_name: Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojna (PMFBY)
question: I farm in Himachal Pradesh. Do I need to pay any premium for my apple crop under PMFBY?
answer: No, farmers in Himachal Pradesh, along with other North-Eastern states and Jammu & Kashmir, receive 100% premium subsidy from the government for all notified crops.

scheme_name: Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojna (PMFBY)
question: Can I claim compensation if my entire village faced crop damage from a landslide, but neighboring villages were unaffected?
answer: Yes, PMFBY covers localized calamities like landslides on an individual farm basis, even if the damage is isolated to specific areas within the notified region.

scheme_name: Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojna (PMFBY)
question: How long after reporting crop damage should I expect to receive the claim amount?
answer: PMFBY aims to process and settle claims within two months of harvest, provided all documentation is complete and damage assessment is finalized.

scheme_name: Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojna (PMFBY)
question: If I've taken a bank loan for farming, do I need to separately apply for PMFBY, or is it automatic?
answer: For loanee farmers, coverage is compulsory but not automatic. You must ensure your bank has processed your PMFBY enrollment within the specified timeframe.

scheme_name: Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojna (PMFBY)
question: What happens if I'm unable to pay the premium online due to technical issues on the last date?
answer: You can visit a nearby CSC or bank branch to submit your premium payment. Keep proof of your online payment attempt for any deadline-related disputes.

scheme_name: Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojna (PMFBY)
question: If I've already registered on the PMFBY portal last season, do I need to create a new registration for this season?
answer: No, use your existing registration. However, you must submit a fresh application and premium payment for each season you want coverage.

scheme_name: Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojna (PMFBY)
question: I discovered pest damage in my field but couldn't document it immediately due to hospitalization. Will my claim be rejected?
answer: Report the damage as soon as possible with medical documentation of your hospitalization. Each case is evaluated based on provided evidence and circumstances.

scheme_name: Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojna (PMFBY)
question: How can I ensure my claim isn't rejected due to wrong information if the CSC operator fills my form?
answer: Always verify the entered details before final submission. Request a printed copy of your application form and keep the acknowledgment receipt with the application number.

scheme_name: Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojna (PMFBY)
question: If my crop loss assessment shows 60% damage but I'm not satisfied with the evaluation, what's the grievance process?
answer: File an appeal through the PMFBY portal or submit a written complaint to your district agriculture officer within 7 days of assessment. Include evidence supporting your claim.

scheme_name: Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojna (PMFBY)
question: Does PMFBY cover damage from wild animals or fire caused by neighboring fields?
answer: Natural fire is covered, but damage from wild animals isn't. For fire spreading from neighboring fields, you must provide evidence that it wasn't due to negligence.

scheme_name: Prime Minister’s Fellowship for Doctoral Research
question: What is the “Prime Minister’s Fellowship for Doctoral Research”?
answer: Prime Minister's Fellowship for Doctoral Research scheme is a prestigious initiative of Science and Engineering Research Board, Department of Science & Technology, Government of India towards the advancement of university research engagements in line with industry requirement. The scheme encourages full time PhD scholars to pursue research in "focus areas" identified by industries as well as of national priorities.

scheme_name: Prime Minister’s Fellowship for Doctoral Research
question: What is the aim of this scheme?
answer: The aim of the scheme is to encourage and inspire promising young Indian Ph.D. researchers to pursue industry relevant research in the areas of Science, Technology, Engineering, Agriculture & Medicine, build industry academia partnership for advancing R&D and boost research on industrially relevant subject areas.

scheme_name: Prime Minister’s Fellowship for Doctoral Research
question: What are the Key Features of the Fellowship?
answer: In addition to attractive scholarship, the Prime Minister's Fellowship emphasizes providing a unique and invigorating experience to selected fellows. It ensures the best national and international exposure for them and provides mentoring through industry and academic experts through the mechanism of annual review meetings. In addition, periodic mentorship sessions are also organized with the help of expert external agencies.

scheme_name: Prime Minister’s Fellowship for Doctoral Research
question: Which is the implementing agency of this scheme?
answer: Confederation of Indian Industry (CII) and Federation of Indian Chambers of Commerce & Industry (FICCI) on behalf of SERB implement the scheme.

scheme_name: Prime Minister’s Fellowship for Doctoral Research
question: What are the eligibility criteria for applying/availing the Fellowship?
answer: The applicant should be a full-time PhD scholar in any recognized Indian university/institute/research laboratory. The scholar's PhD registration date should not be more than 14 months from the date of submission of application. | The applicant should have a valid industry partner who should be ready to support the research project financially as well as provide guidance and mentorship. | The mutually agreed topic of research, between the applicant and the supporting company, should be innovative, have practical relevance, and have industrial application. | The selected applicant should be willing to work with/in the supporting company as and when required during the project period. | The applicant should not draw any other fellowship after the selection.

scheme_name: Prime Minister’s Fellowship for Doctoral Research
question: What are the areas covered under this Fellowship?
answer: Science, Technology, Engineering, Agriculture, and Medicine

scheme_name: Prime Minister’s Fellowship for Doctoral Research
question: What is the nature of support for the Fellow?
answer: Under this scheme, fulltime PhD scholars get double the JRF/SRF fellowship amount, as scholarship.

scheme_name: Prime Minister’s Fellowship for Doctoral Research
question: What are the Selection Parameters of the projects under the scheme?
answer: The projects should be innovative and of high scientific merit; with discrete R&D as opposed to exploratory investigation. | The proposed research project should have a high commercialization potential. | The applicant, the academic guide, and the industry mentor should have a strong track record.

scheme_name: Prime Minister’s Fellowship for Doctoral Research
question: How can an applicant apply for this fellowship?
answer: The applicant can apply for this fellowship through the website www.primeministerfellowshipscheme.in.

scheme_name: Prime Minister’s Fellowship for Doctoral Research
question: How does the online application work?
answer: Candidates need to refer to Annexure I in the Call for Proposal document which is available on the home page of the portal www.primeministerfellowshipscheme.in. All the required documents and details needed to be given should be collected before filling the online application.

scheme_name: Prime Minister’s Fellowship for Doctoral Research
question: What is the timeline till which the application can be submitted? Will an additional hard copy, stamped / signed of the application required to be sent to CII?
answer: The scheme is open-ended and the scholars can apply anytime during the year subject to the condition that the doctoral fellow should be admitted to a full-time PhD in the last 14 months from the date of submission of application in any recognized Indian university/institute/research laboratory. In case of a different admission/enrollment and registration date, the first date of admission in full-time PhD will be considered. In case of any dispute regarding the submission date, the decision of the Apex Council will be considered as final. No hard copies of any kind need to be sent to CII; only soft copies are required to be uploaded as indicated in the form.

scheme_name: Prime Minister’s Fellowship for Doctoral Research
question: Can I apply if I do not have an industry partner? Will CII help in finding one?
answer: Applications without industry partners will not be accepted by the online system. Candidates have to find industry partners on their own. CII facilitates match-making between research scholars and industry through the portal www.primeministerfellowshipscheme.in. All those who want to search for industry partners are requested to register themselves on this portal. Registration on this portal, however, will not guarantee that the candidate will find an industry partner. The relevance of their project for industry and the extent to which the candidate is able to convey their capability to the industry will determine whether they will find industry partners or not. The interested companies can evaluate the profile and contact the applicants if they find the proposal relevant.

scheme_name: Prime Minister’s Fellowship for Doctoral Research
question: How can I find relevant industry partners?
answer: Candidates should talk to their research guides at the institute and find out about the relevant companies in that field. They can do their own research in and around them to find out the right companies and approach them. Candidates should also keep themselves abreast with the latest technologies, trends and companies working in their field. They should try to interact with industry people in their field as frequently as possible to trigger idea thrashing about a particular project.

scheme_name: Prime Minister’s Fellowship for Doctoral Research
question: If an applicant submits the form, can it be submitted again?
answer: Candidates can review and re-review their forms any number of times before uploading them finally. Once uploaded, however, the form cannot be submitted again.

scheme_name: Prime Minister’s Fellowship for Doctoral Research
question: If I apply this year and am not able to get the scholarship this time, will I be allowed to apply next year?
answer: Yes, you can apply as a fresh candidate with updated information, provided you satisfy all the eligibility conditions.

scheme_name: Prime Minister’s Fellowship for Doctoral Research
question: Will applicants get automated response to submission? Will somebody call from CII to confirm the receipt of application?
answer: Applicants will get an automatic response at the submission of applications. They will not receive any calls from CII. In case you do not receive a system generated email regarding the submission of their application within 24 hours, the applicant must contact CII at pm.scheme@cii.in

scheme_name: Prime Minister’s Fellowship for Doctoral Research
question: Which are the institutes where PM Fellows are doing their research?
answer: Following are some of the institutes where PM Fellows are pursuing their PhD: Acharya Nagarjuna University, Academy of Scientific & Innovative Research, Alagappa University, Amity University, Anna University, Banaras Hindu University, Bidhan Chandra Krishi Viswavidyalaya, Hemchandracharya North Gujarat University, Institute of Chemical Technology, Indian Institute of Engineering Science and Technology, Indraprastha Institute of Information Technology, Indian Institute of Science, Indian Institutes of Technology, IIT Bombay - Monash University Research Academy, Indian Agricultural Research Institute, Manipal University, National Chemical Laboratory, National Institutes of Technology, PSG College, Punjab Agricultural University, Saurashtra University, Savitribai Phule Pune University, Tamil Nadu Agricultural University, Tata Memorial Hospital, Thiagarajar College of Engineering and Kurukshetra University.

scheme_name: President’s Medal for Distinguished Service
question: Who awards the PSM?
answer: The awards are conferred by the President of India.

scheme_name: President’s Medal for Distinguished Service
question: Who is eligible for these awards?
answer: Personnel from police, CAPFs, fire services, prisons, and civil defence are eligible.

scheme_name: President’s Medal for Distinguished Service
question: What is the minimum service required for PSM?
answer: A minimum of 25 years of service is required.

scheme_name: President’s Medal for Distinguished Service
question: Are ACR/APAR records important for selection?
answer: Yes, performance records are a key evaluation criterion.

scheme_name: President’s Medal for Distinguished Service
question: Can a person with disciplinary action apply?
answer: No, candidates must have a clean service record.

scheme_name: President’s Medal for Distinguished Service
question: Is there any reservation or preference?
answer: Yes, preference is given to SC/ST, women, and minorities.

scheme_name: President’s Medal for Distinguished Service
question: Can the award be withdrawn?
answer: Yes, it can be withdrawn in case of misconduct or criminal activity.

scheme_name: President’s Medal for Distinguished Service
question: Is there a monetary reward under this scheme?
answer: No monetary benefit is specified; recognition is honorary.

scheme_name: President’s Medal for Distinguished Service
question: How often are the awards given?
answer: The awards are given annually.

scheme_name: President’s Medal for Distinguished Service
question: What is the role of vigilance clearance?
answer: It ensures the candidate has no pending disciplinary or criminal cases.

scheme_name: President’s Medal for Distinguished Service
question: Can missing ACRs affect eligibility?
answer: Yes, more than one missing ACR leads to disqualification.

scheme_name: President’s Medal for Distinguished Service
question: Is physical fitness required?
answer: Yes, SHAPE 1 category fitness is generally required.

scheme_name: President’s Medal for Distinguished Service
question: Who recommends candidates for the award?
answer: State Governments and Central organizations recommend candidates.

scheme_name: President’s Medal for Distinguished Service
question: Can the award be given multiple times?
answer: There are restrictions; repeated awards depend on eligibility and criteria.

scheme_name: Pradhan Mantri Formalisation Of Micro Food Processing Enterprises
question: What Is PM FME Scheme?
answer: PM FME stands for "Prime Minister Micro Food Processing Enterprises". PMFME is an all-India Centrally Sponsored Scheme with an outlay of Rs. 10,000 crores for coverage of 2,00,000 enterprises over 5 years from 2020-21 to 2024-25 being implemented by MOFPI.

scheme_name: Pradhan Mantri Formalisation Of Micro Food Processing Enterprises
question: What Are Micro Enterprises?
answer: A Micro Enterprise is an enterprise where the investment in Plant and Machinery or Equipment is not more than Rs. 1 crore and the Annual Turnover is not more than Rs. 5 crore.

scheme_name: Pradhan Mantri Formalisation Of Micro Food Processing Enterprises
question: Is There Any Limit Of Credit Subsidy/Grant?
answer: Yes, it would be 35% of the project cost with a maximum ceiling of Rs 10 lacs for an individual beneficiary. For SHG members involved in food processing, seed capital of Rs 40,000/- per member will be distributed as working capital and for the purchase of small tools.

scheme_name: Pradhan Mantri Formalisation Of Micro Food Processing Enterprises
question: Is There Any Initial Investment Required By The Person For The Scheme?
answer: Yes, the applicant should be willing to contribute 10% of the project cost.

scheme_name: Pradhan Mantri Formalisation Of Micro Food Processing Enterprises
question: What Is The Process Of Crediting Subsidies?
answer: At the national level, a Nodal bank would be appointed for the disbursement of subsidies to the banks and liaison with the banks

scheme_name: Pradhan Mantri Formalisation Of Micro Food Processing Enterprises
question: Is There Any Provision Of Special Benefits For SC/ST Applying In The Scheme?
answer: Yes, the specific allocation has been made for Scheduled Caste/ Scheduled Tribe and the North-Eastern region.

scheme_name: Pradhan Mantri Formalisation Of Micro Food Processing Enterprises
question: When The Subsidy Amount Will Be Credited To My Account?
answer: On sanction of the loan, the Central and State government will transfer the fund to the beneficiary mirror account. The beneficiary needs to pay the EMI on time for the next three years and the unit needs to be operational. Post 3 years, if the loan category is standard, the subsidy amount will be credited to the beneficiary account

scheme_name: Pradhan Mantri Formalisation Of Micro Food Processing Enterprises
question: I Have Applied For The Benefits Of The Scheme. Can My Son/Daughter/Sprouse Also Apply For The Same As They Are Dealing In ODOP Processing?
answer: No, only one person from one family would be eligible for obtaining financial assistance. The "family" for this purpose would include self, spouse and children.

scheme_name: Pradhan Mantri Formalisation Of Micro Food Processing Enterprises
question: Can I Avail Of Other Government Schemes With The PMFME Scheme?
answer: Yes, you can avail of other Government schemes with PMFME Scheme

scheme_name: Pradhan Mantri Formalisation Of Micro Food Processing Enterprises
question: How Branding And Marketing Support Will Be Provided Under This Scheme?
answer: Marketing and branding support would be provided to groups of FPOs/SHGs/Cooperatives under the Scheme following the ODOP approach in the following ways: | Training relating to marketing to be fully funded under the scheme | Developing a common brand and packaging including standardization to participate | in common packaging | Marketing tie up with national and regional retail chains and state level institutions | Quality control to ensure product quality meets required standards

scheme_name: Pradhan Mantri Formalisation Of Micro Food Processing Enterprises
question: Is There Any Provision Of Financial Assistance For The Preparation Of DPR?
answer: Yes, the assistance of Rs 50,000/- per case would be provided to FPOs/SHGs/ Cooperative for preparation of DPR on all successful sanctions of the loan application.

scheme_name: Pradhan Mantri Formalisation Of Micro Food Processing Enterprises
question: What Is The Duration Of The Scheme?
answer: The scheme is for a period of 5 years from 2020-21 to 2024-25.

scheme_name: Pradhan Mantri Formalisation Of Micro Food Processing Enterprises
question: Is Any Processing Fees Or Application Fees Will Be Charged?
answer: No, it's a centrally sponsored scheme, you need not to pay any fees for filling application or any handholding

scheme_name: Pradhan Mantri Formalisation Of Micro Food Processing Enterprises
question: Is There Any Age Limit To Apply?
answer: Yes, the applicant should be above 18 years of age

scheme_name: Pradhan Mantri Formalisation Of Micro Food Processing Enterprises
question: Is There Any Qualification Required To Avail Of The Benefits Of The Scheme?
answer: Yes, the applicant should possess at least VIII standard pass educational qualification.

scheme_name: Pradhan Mantri Formalisation Of Micro Food Processing Enterprises
question: Are There Any Other Eligibility Criteria To Avail Of The Benefits Of The Scheme?
answer: Yes, the applicant should have an ownership right of the enterprise and an enterprise could be a proprietorship or a partnership firm.

scheme_name: Pradhan Mantri Formalisation Of Micro Food Processing Enterprises
question: If My Application Is Rejected, Can I Resubmit The Application?
answer: Yes, if the application is rejected by one bank, you can resubmit the application with another bank.

scheme_name: Pradhan Mantri Formalisation Of Micro Food Processing Enterprises
question: More Than 10 Workers Are Employed In My Enterprise. Can I Apply For This Scheme?
answer: No, according to the eligibility criteria, the enterprise should be unincorporated and should employ less than 10 workers for availing the benefits of the scheme.

scheme_name: Police Medal for Meritorious Service
question: What is the minimum service required?
answer: A minimum of 18 years of service is required.

scheme_name: Police Medal for Meritorious Service
question: Are ACRs mandatory for eligibility?
answer: Yes, ACRs of the last 10 years are essential for evaluation.

scheme_name: Police Medal for Meritorious Service
question: How many Very Good ACRs are required?
answer: At least 8 Very Good or above ACRs are required.

scheme_name: Police Medal for Meritorious Service
question: Is an Outstanding ACR required?
answer: Yes, at least 1 Outstanding ACR is mandatory.

scheme_name: Police Medal for Meritorious Service
question: Can a candidate with an Average ACR apply?
answer: No, candidates with any Average ACR are ineligible.

scheme_name: Police Medal for Meritorious Service
question: Is there a limit on missing ACRs?
answer: Yes, more than 1 missing ACR leads to disqualification.

scheme_name: Police Medal for Meritorious Service
question: Is physical fitness required?
answer: Yes, SHAPE 1 fitness is required, with limited relaxation.

scheme_name: Police Medal for Meritorious Service
question: Can the medal be awarded multiple times?
answer: Yes, but with restrictions such as nomination limits.

scheme_name: Police Medal for Meritorious Service
question: Is there any reservation or preference?
answer: Yes, preference is given to SC/ST, women, and minorities.

scheme_name: Police Medal for Meritorious Service
question: What is the role of vigilance clearance?
answer: It ensures the candidate has no disciplinary or criminal issues.

scheme_name: Police Medal for Meritorious Service
question: Can a duplicate medal be issued?
answer: Yes, only once in exceptional cases with penalty and documentation.

scheme_name: Police Medal for Meritorious Service
question: When are the awards announced?
answer: They are announced annually on national occasions.

scheme_name: Police Medal for Meritorious Service
question: What is the penalty for losing the medal?
answer: A penalty of ₹10,000 must be paid.

scheme_name: Pradhan Mantri Gramin Digital Saksharta Abhiyaan
question: Who Can Be The Training Partners?
answer: The basic requirements to become a training partner under the PMGDISHA scheme are as follows: | A training partner must be an organization registered in India, conducting business in the domain of education/ IT literacy for more than three years and having Permanent Income Tax Account Number (PAN) and audited statements of accounts for at least last three years. | The institution/organization should be registered under any act of law in India, e.g., in the case of a company it must be registered with the Registrar of Companies, in case of Society, it must be registered with the Registrar of Societies and so on and so forth. | The partner must have clearly defined objectives, and well-documented processes and procedures covering the entire range of education/ IT literacy training.

scheme_name: Pradhan Mantri Gramin Digital Saksharta Abhiyaan
question: What Is The Role Of A Training Partner Under The Scheme?
answer: A training partner shall be responsible to own or set up the Training Centres in the identified Districts / Gram Panchayats that would impart digital literacy training to the candidates. | A training partner shall be responsible for ensuring that the training centres adhere to the scheme requirements. | A training partner shall be accountable for monitoring the overall working of the centres under its purview. | A training partner shall be liable for accurate and timely reporting of the aforementioned work ascribed in respect of its Centres. | Detailed Norms for the Training Partners shall be as per Standard Operating Procedure (SOP) published by CSC-SPV.

scheme_name: Pradhan Mantri Gramin Digital Saksharta Abhiyaan
question: What Is The Training Fees Under PMGDISHA ?
answer: A training fee of Rs. 300/- per candidate is payable directly to respective Training Partners/Centres through CSC-SPV on successful certification of candidates trained by them.

scheme_name: Pradhan Mantri Gramin Digital Saksharta Abhiyaan
question: What Is The Payment Process For The Partners ?
answer: The invoice has to be sent printed on the letterhead of the partner and duly stamped. All the necessary details in the invoice should be completed i.e. Invoice number (assigned by the partner), PAN number, service tax number, bank details, etc. Also, an affidavit must also be submitted to the PMU. | The address for correspondence is: | CSC e-Governance Services India Ltd. | 238, Okhla Phase III | Behind Modi Mill | New Delhi -110020

scheme_name: Pradhan Mantri Gramin Digital Saksharta Abhiyaan
question: How Will The Partners Provide Training To The Candidates?
answer: An authorized partner will provide training to the candidates through the training centres. The partner will register the centers on the portal through their login credentials. Upon verification of the training centres by the monitoring organization the login credential are created for the training center. The login credentials will be used to register and train the candidates.

scheme_name: Pradhan Mantri Gramin Digital Saksharta Abhiyaan
question: What Is The Duration Of The Training Program ?
answer: The duration of the training program is for 20 hours which has to be completed in a minimum of 10 days and a maximum of 30 days.

scheme_name: Pradhan Mantri Gramin Digital Saksharta Abhiyaan
question: How Will The Partners Receive My Login Credentials And How Will I Activate My Account ?
answer: The instructions to activate your account will be sent to your E-mail once you have completed the process and submitted all the relevant documents. If you do not receive an E-mail, kindly check that your E-mail service provider's mailing software is not blocking it. Also, the status of the application can be checked on the www.pmgdisha.in

scheme_name: Pradhan Mantri Gramin Digital Saksharta Abhiyaan
question: What Would Be The Tenure Of The Accreditation Of Training Partner ?
answer: The training partner will be accredited for a period of one year under PMGDISHA project and its accreditation will be renewed after accessing the work done during that period.

scheme_name: Pradhan Mantri Gramin Digital Saksharta Abhiyaan
question: Is There A Limit To The Number Of States Wherein An Accredited Training Partner May Work Under PMGDISHA ?
answer: Accredited Training Partners would be assigned with a specified area of operation and target preferably within the same state.

scheme_name: Pradhan Mantri Gramin Digital Saksharta Abhiyaan
question: Who Should A Training Partner/Centre Contact If It Comes Across Any Challenges During The Implementation Of The Project ?
answer: Any Training partner/center can contact PMGDISHA Toll-Free No: 1800 3000 3468, Email Id : helpdesk@disha.mettl.in

scheme_name: Pradhan Mantri Gramin Digital Saksharta Abhiyaan
question: Where Should An Organization Send In The Documents In Order To Become A Training Partner/Training Centre Under PMGDISHA ?
answer: Training Partner/Centre has to send duly filled form (available on our website) and other documents to our Address: | CSC e-Governance Services India Ltd. | 238, Okhla Phase III | Behind Modi Mill | New Delhi -110020

scheme_name: Pradhan Mantri Gramin Digital Saksharta Abhiyaan
question: Where Can I Check The Status Of My Payment ?
answer: The payment status can be checked through VLEs dashboard.

scheme_name: Pradhan Mantri Gramin Digital Saksharta Abhiyaan
question: What Is The Process Of Payment For The CSC Centres ?
answer: Training Centre can raise invoices every month. To generate an invoice click on the tab Invoicing and Payments. Choose the Year/Month/date and click on generate, invoice for that period will be generated. Also, Training Centre can also check the payment history for the past months.

scheme_name: Pradhan Mantri Garib Kalyan Package : Insurance Scheme For Health Workers Fighting COVID-19
question: What does this Scheme cover?
answer: This accident insurance scheme covers; Loss of life due to COVID19, and Accidental death on account of COVID-19 related duty.

scheme_name: Pradhan Mantri Garib Kalyan Package : Insurance Scheme For Health Workers Fighting COVID-19
question: What is the definition of Accident?
answer: An accident is sudden, unforeseen and involuntary event caused by external, visible and violent means.

scheme_name: Pradhan Mantri Garib Kalyan Package : Insurance Scheme For Health Workers Fighting COVID-19
question: Who all are covered under the scheme?
answer: - Public healthcare providers including community health workers, who may have to be in direct contact and care of COVID-19 patients and who may be at risk of being impacted by this. | - Private hospital staff and retired /volunteer /local urban bodies/ contracted /daily wage/ad-hoc/outsourced staff requisitioned by States/ Central hospitals/ autonomous hospitals of Central/ States/UTs, AIIMS and INIs/ hospital of Central Ministries can also be drafted for COVID 19 related responsibilities.

scheme_name: Pradhan Mantri Garib Kalyan Package : Insurance Scheme For Health Workers Fighting COVID-19
question: Who can be a volunteer under this scheme?
answer: Volunteers are those who are drafted by the Government Official authorized by Central/State/ UT Government for care and may have come in direct contact of the COVID-19 patient

scheme_name: Pradhan Mantri Garib Kalyan Package : Insurance Scheme For Health Workers Fighting COVID-19
question: Who are ‘Private persons’ under this scheme?
answer: Private persons are those who are engaged by both public & private health care institutions/organization through an agency and were deployed /drafted for care and may have come in direct contact of the COVID-19 patient (with the proof that the service of the agencies were engaged by the institution/organization).

scheme_name: Pradhan Mantri Garib Kalyan Package : Insurance Scheme For Health Workers Fighting COVID-19
question: When does insurance coverage policy begins and ends?
answer: The duration of the policy is for a period of 90 days, starting from March 30, 2020.

scheme_name: Pradhan Mantri Garib Kalyan Package : Insurance Scheme For Health Workers Fighting COVID-19
question: Is there any age-limit for health workers under this scheme?
answer: There's no age limit for this scheme.

scheme_name: Pradhan Mantri Garib Kalyan Package : Insurance Scheme For Health Workers Fighting COVID-19
question: Is individual enrolment required?
answer: Individual enrolment is not required.

scheme_name: Pradhan Mantri Garib Kalyan Package : Insurance Scheme For Health Workers Fighting COVID-19
question: Whether an individual is required to pay any premium to be eligible under the scheme?
answer: The entire amount of premium for this scheme is being borne by the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare, Government of India.

scheme_name: Pradhan Mantri Garib Kalyan Package : Insurance Scheme For Health Workers Fighting COVID-19
question: What is the benefit available to the insured persons?
answer: INR 50,00,000/- will be paid to the claimant of the insured person

scheme_name: Pradhan Mantri Gram Sadak Yojana
question: Does The Programme Provide Connectivity To Only Revenue Villages? Are Hamlets Eligible To Be Connected?
answer: The spirit and objective of PMGSY-I was to provide good all-weather road connectivity to eligible unconnected habitations. The unit of this programme is a habitation and not a revenue village or a Panchayat. A habitation is a cluster of population, living in an area, the location of which does not change over time. Desam, Dhanis, Tolas, Majras, Hamlets, etc. are commonly used to describe habitations. | The population, as recorded in the Census 2001, shall be the basis for determining the population size of the habitation. The population of all Habitations within a radius of 500 metre (1.5 km of path distance in case of Hills) may be clubbed together to determine the population size. In the blocks bordering international boundary in the hill States (as identified by the Ministry of Home Affairs), however, all habitations within a path distance of 10 km may be treated as a cluster for this purpose. This cluster approach would enable the provision of connectivity to a number of Habitations, particularly in Hill/ mountainous areas. | A special dispensation has been allowed to Arunachal Pradesh under PMGSY by extending the Cluster approach to all International border districts in the State by clubbing population with the path distance of 10 km and treating as a Cluster.

scheme_name: Pradhan Mantri Gram Sadak Yojana
question: How Are Habitations Selected For Coverage? Who Decides Which Habitations Will Be Covered In A Year?
answer: Unconnected habitations are listed as per the priority (generally, habitations with a higher population, as per 2001 Census, would be connected first) and depending upon the funds likely to be made available for the State, the list of road works to be taken up under PMGSY-I will be finalized each year by the District Panchayat through a consultative process involving Panchayati Raj Institutions and elected representatives.

scheme_name: Pradhan Mantri Gram Sadak Yojana
question: Can An Individual Apply For Road Connectivity?
answer: The objective of PMGSY-I was to provide road connectivity to unconnected habitations as mentioned in response to Question 1 above. Any proposal for road connectivity may be perceived as per the programme guidelines.

scheme_name: Pradhan Mantri Gram Sadak Yojana
question: How Is Alignment Selected? Are Local Villagers Associated With This Process?
answer: A simple, non-formal transect walk shall be organised by the Assistant Engineer at the time of preparation of DPRs to finalise the alignment. The Panchayat Pradhan, local patwari, the JE, Local Revenue and Forest officials, Women PRI members and representatives of Women Self Help Groups (SHGs) also participate in the transect walk to determine the most suitable alignment, sort out the issues of land availability and to moderate any adverse social and environmental impact, eliciting necessary community participation in the programme. After transect walk, the minutes should be placed and approved by the Grama Sabha.Local people including those likely to be affected by proposed alignment are also allowed to put forth their view in this process.

scheme_name: Pradhan Mantri Gram Sadak Yojana
question: What Does All-Weather Connectivity Mean? Does It Mean Only Black- Topped Or Cement Concrete Roads?
answer: An all-weather road is one that is negotiable in all seasons of the year. This implies that the road-bed is drained effectively but this does not necessarily imply that it should be paved surface with blacktopping or cement concrete. A gravel road can also be an all-weather road.

scheme_name: Pradhan Mantri Gram Sadak Yojana
question: How Is The Problem Of Drainage Tackled In The Portion Of Roads Passing Through Built-Up Residential Areas?
answer: Road portions passing through built-up residential areas are prone to damages caused by wastewater from households. Programme guidelines provide for the construction of cement concrete pavement or cement/stone block pavements along with covered or uncovered Pucca side drains as per site conditions.

scheme_name: Pradhan Mantri Gram Sadak Yojana
question: Is The Adequate Provision For Culverts Or Cross-Drainage Works Made?
answer: The objective of the PMGSY is to provide an All-weather Road with necessary culverts and other cross drainage structures, which is operable throughout the year to the eligible unconnected habitations as per PMGSY guidelines in the rural areas. Rural roads constructed under PMGSY must have proper embankment and drainage. Adequate number and type of Cross Drainage (CD) works, including causeways, where appropriate, must be provided based on site requirements ascertained through necessary investigation. Minor bridges can be provided wherever necessary. | A necessary advisory has been already issued to the State Governments to include the culverts/CDs bridges along with the road proposals. | The proposal of long-span Bridges should be prepared as a separate DPR. However, such proposals of Bridges should be submitted with road proposals in the same batch.

scheme_name: Pradhan Mantri Gram Sadak Yojana
question: What About Bridges On Rivers/Streams?
answer: Bridges on rivers/streams crossing the alignment of the road are taken up under the program along with the road proposal. The Ministry issued PMGSY-III guidelines increasing the span of Long-Span Bridges (LSBs) for funding under PMGSY as follows: | Up to 200 m in respect of Special Category States and LWE districts identified by the MHA. | Upto 150 m in respect of other States.

scheme_name: Pradhan Mantri Gram Sadak Yojana
question: Whether Compensation For Land Acquisition Is Paid In The Program?
answer: The rural road is a State subject and it is the responsibility of State Government/ District Panchayat to ensure the availability of land for construction of road works under the programme. In view of the common benefit, generally, the land for construction of roads under PMGSY is made available by the villagers/Panchayat free of cost through voluntary donation. However, in rare cases, if the land is acquired for construction of roads under PMGSY, the State Government is required to pay compensation.

scheme_name: Pradhan Mantri Gram Sadak Yojana
question: How Are Executants Selected For The Construction Of Roads?
answer: Executants for construction of roads are selected through open competitive bidding for which well-established procedure for tendering is followed by the State Government. As per provisions, the bidders who have the prescribed qualifications and have the capacity to execute the works are required to take part in the bidding process. To enhance the transparency in tendering and speed up the tendering process, e- procurement of bids has been made mandatory.

scheme_name: Pradhan Mantri Gram Sadak Yojana
question: If Defects Are Noticed After Completion Of The Road, How Are They Rectified?
answer: As per provisions of the contract, the contractor is liable for any defect that may occur until 5 years after completion of the road work. To enforce liability of defects, the security amount is deducted from the bills of the contractors. The contractor has to rectify the defect in the above period and if the rectification has not been carried out, the Project Implementation Unit (PIU) is required to rectify the defect and recover the cost from the security deposit of the contractor.

scheme_name: Pradhan Mantri Gram Sadak Yojana
question: How Is The Quality Of Work Checked And Monitored?
answer: Every contractor is required to establish a field laboratory in every package of road works in which he/she required to test the quality of material and workmanship under the supervision of executing agency. In addition to checking of quality by departmental officers of executing agency, the State Government is required to deploy independent monitors for monitoring of the quality of road works. Independent National Quality Monitors (NQMs) are also deployed by the Central Government for monitoring the quality of works randomly.

scheme_name: Pradhan Mantri Gram Sadak Yojana
question: Is There A Provision For The Display Of Project-Related Information At Project Sites?
answer: Citizen Information Board in the local language containing the following detailed information of work is provided on each work:- | Description of every layer of work. | Description of the quantity of material involved in work. | How the road will be built and description. | General information board containing information about executing agency, contractor, estimated cost of work and time for completion is also provided on every worksite.

scheme_name: Pradhan Mantri Gram Sadak Yojana
question: What Is The Role Of Public Representatives In Checking The Quality Of Implementation Of The Programme?
answer: In the interest of total transparency and to ensure the pro-active role of public representatives, the States have been advised to organize a time-bound inspection of road works with local public representatives in the following manner:- | The Superintending Engineer would request the Hon'ble M.P. and Zila Pramukh once in 6 months duration to select road works in respective areas and joint inspection/visit would be organized. | The Executive Engineer would request the Hon'ble MLA and Chairperson of Intermediate Panchayat once in three months duration to select road works in respective areas and joint inspection/visit would be organized. | The Assistant Engineer would request the Sarpanch once in two months duration to select road works in respective areas and joint inspection/visit would be organized.

scheme_name: Pradhan Mantri Gram Sadak Yojana
question: Whether Information About The Programme Is Available On Any Website?
answer: Yes, information about the programme and details about every work is available on programme website www.omms.nic.in and www.pmgsy.nic.in.The Online Monitoring and Management System (OMMS) is being used for effective management and monitoring under the programme. The required data is entered by the field level staff and the State units under this web-based package.

scheme_name: Pradhan Mantri Gram Sadak Yojana
question: How Are The Roads Maintained?
answer: Along with the tendering for the construction the routine maintenance of road works for five years after completion of work is also included. Programme guidelines envisage a transfer of road works for maintenance to Panchayati Raj Institutions (PRIs) after 5 years upon completion of the road work.

scheme_name: Pradhan Mantri Gram Sadak Yojana
question: What Should Be The Population Of Habitations To Be Covered Under PMGSY-I For Providing Connectivity?
answer: The programme envisages connecting all eligible unconnected habitations by way of an all-weather road as per Core Network with a population of 500 persons (as per 2001 Census) and above in plain areas and 250 persons and above (as per 2001 Census) in the Special Category States (Arunachal Pradesh, Assam, Manipur, Meghalaya, Mizoram, Nagaland, Sikkim, Tripura Himachal Pradesh, Jammu & Kashmir, and Uttarakhand), Tribal (Schedule-V) areas, the Desert Areas (as identified in Desert Development Programme) and in Selected Tribal and Backward Districts (as identified by the Ministry of Home Affairs/Planning Commission). In the critical 267 Left Wing Extremism (LWE) affected blocks (as identified by MHA), additional relaxation has been given to connect habitations with population 100 persons and above (2001 census).

scheme_name: Prime Minister’s Internship Scheme
question: Will I get financial assistance for doing my internship?
answer: After joining the internship, each intern will receive monthly assistance of [?]5,000 for the entire duration of the 12-month internship.

scheme_name: Prime Minister’s Internship Scheme
question: What is the eligibility of interns to receive initial DBT and the monthly internship allowance?
answer: Only those interns who have physically joined the internship, their joining is verified by HR, and they have Aadhaar Seeded Bank Account are eligible to receive the initial DBT and monthly internship allowance. Interns must complete their Aadhaar seeding process in order to receive the payments.

scheme_name: Prime Minister’s Internship Scheme
question: Will I get travel allowances or other support during the duration of the internship?
answer: Partner companies may consider providing additional financial assistance or any other facilities as per their discretion. The internships that you opt for may or may not have any other benefits attached to them. | A one-time grant [?]6,000 will be provided by the Government of India to each intern after joining the internship. This grant is to support you at the beginning of your internship journey. | - Throughout your internship, you will receive monthly assistance of [?]5,000.

scheme_name: Prime Minister’s Internship Scheme
question: Will the insurance cover continue after the internship?
answer: No, upon the completion of your internship the benefits of the insurance will lapse.

scheme_name: Prime Minister’s Internship Scheme
question: Will I receive financial assistance during the sabbatical (break) period?
answer: Financial assistance will not be provided during the sabbatical (break) period.

scheme_name: Prime Minister’s Internship Scheme
question: Will I get any financial assistance to purchase clothes for my internship?
answer: No specific financial assistance shall be provided for the purchase of clothes. However, after you join your internship, a onetime grant of [?]6000 will be transferred to your Aadhaar seeded bank account by the Government of India as financial assistance.

scheme_name: Prime Minister’s Internship Scheme
question: Will I receive the monthly internship allowance if I discontinue the internship midway?
answer: No, if you withdraw/dropout from the internship before completion, you will be ineligible to receive the monthly internship allowance. You will not receive the internship completion certificate if you discontinue the internship midway.

scheme_name: Prime Minister’s Internship Scheme
question: How many internship opportunities can I apply for?
answer: Candidates can apply for up to 3 internship options in one cycle, which can be selected based on their preferred location, sector and field.

scheme_name: Prime Minister’s Internship Scheme
question: Can I change my three internship preferences on the portal?
answer: Yes, you are permitted to change your three preferences on the portal as many times as you want to, before the application deadline. You can choose to withdraw from any application and apply into a different one, before the application deadline closes. Post application deadline closes, you cannot make changes anymore.

scheme_name: Prime Minister’s Internship Scheme
question: What if I am not selected for any of my three preferred opportunities?
answer: Candidates can reapply for the future cycles of PM Internship Scheme if he/she is not selected for any of the three applied opportunities.

scheme_name: Prime Minister’s Internship Scheme
question: What is the maximum number of internships offers I can receive?
answer: A candidate can receive up to two internship offers. Once an offer is received, the candidate may accept/reject the offer within the stipulated time window. Candidates are advised to view the complete details of internship in the provisional offer letter and take the appropriate action (accept or reject the offer).

scheme_name: Prime Minister’s Internship Scheme
question: What If I do not wish to accept the internship(s) I have been shortlisted for?
answer: Candidate can accept or reject their offer of internships. However, in case a candidate rejects an internship, he/she will only be able to reapply in future cycles of the PM Internship Scheme.

scheme_name: Prime Minister’s Internship Scheme
question: If I accept an internship offer, how will I get the final offer letter?
answer: Your final offer letter will be uploaded on the PMIS portal, apart from being sent to your registered email address.

scheme_name: Prime Minister’s Internship Scheme
question: Through the PM Internship Scheme, what kind of internships will I get?
answer: Eligible candidates will get internships in different roles across sectors including IT and Software Development, Banking and Financial Services, Oil, Gas & Energy, Metals & Mining, FMCG (Fast-Moving Consumer Goods), Telecom, Infrastructure & Construction, Retail & Consumer Durables, Cement & Building Materials, Automotive, Pharmaceutical, Aviation & Defence, Manufacturing & Industrial, Chemical, Media, Entertainment & Education, Agriculture and Allied, Consulting Services, Textile Manufacturing, Gems and Jewellery, Travel & Hospitality and Healthcare.

scheme_name: Prime Minister’s Internship Scheme
question: What kind of companies will I get to intern with?
answer: Selected candidates will have the opportunity to intern with the top companies from across India. Interning with these industry-leading companies will allow you to gain valuable experience, acquire new skills, and build important professional networks. The Company can also provide internship in its forward and backward supply chain and in other companies in its Group or otherwise

scheme_name: Prime Minister’s Internship Scheme
question: What is the duration of the internship?
answer: Internships under the PM Internship Scheme will be for a duration of one year (12 months).

scheme_name: Prime Minister’s Internship Scheme
question: Will I be sitting in a classroom during my internship?
answer: At least half of the internship period (6 months) must be spent in the actual working experience/ job environment, and not in the classroom. While a certain part of the internship will include relevant training, a significant duration (at least 6 months) of your internship will focus on real-world experience in professional setups.

scheme_name: Prime Minister’s Internship Scheme
question: Will I get a job after my internship?
answer: The PM Internship Scheme provides a valuable opportunity to learn and enhance your skills by working with top companies in India. While the scheme does not guarantee a job upon completion, the knowledge, practical experience, and professional networks you develop during the internship will significantly enhance your career prospects.

scheme_name: Prime Minister’s Internship Scheme
question: Can international candidates apply for the PM Internship Scheme?
answer: No, international candidates are not eligible to apply for the PM Internship Scheme.

scheme_name: Prime Minister’s Internship Scheme
