question: If I am enrolled in a full-time training program outside of Goa, what percentage of attendance must I maintain to ensure the scholarship funds are not recovered?
answer: You must maintain 75% attendance for either the total duration of the course or for one year of the course, whichever period is shorter.

scheme_name: Scheme To Provide Assistance To Students Seeking Education Outside Goa In Any Field Of Art And Culture
question: Do I have to commit to a specific mode of study, such as only full-time training, in order to qualify and receive benefits under the scheme?
answer: No, the student is permitted to undergo the specialized training on either a full-time basis or a part-time basis, depending on the requirements of the course.

scheme_name: Scheme To Provide Assistance To Students Seeking Education Outside Goa In Any Field Of Art And Culture
question: Are there any special conditions under which more than one student from the same immediate family might be considered for simultaneous assistance?
answer: In rare cases, the committee may consider a second family application if the training is sought in a stream of art different from the first applicant and is based upon their merit or contribution.

scheme_name: Scheme to Provide Financial Assistance to Purchase Solar Power Unit/Kit for Solar Fencing around the Farm
question: What is the objective of this scheme?
answer: The scheme aims to support landholding farmers by subsidizing the cost of solar power units/kits for farm fencing.

scheme_name: Scheme to Provide Financial Assistance to Purchase Solar Power Unit/Kit for Solar Fencing around the Farm
question: Who is eligible to apply for this scheme?
answer: Any landholding farmer in the state is eligible to apply for the scheme.

scheme_name: Scheme to Provide Financial Assistance to Purchase Solar Power Unit/Kit for Solar Fencing around the Farm
question: What is the financial assistance provided under this scheme?
answer: The scheme provides 50% of the actual cost or ₹15,000/-, whichever is lower, for purchasing a solar power unit/kit.

scheme_name: Scheme to Provide Financial Assistance to Purchase Solar Power Unit/Kit for Solar Fencing around the Farm
question: Can a joint landholder apply separately for the scheme?
answer: No, only one joint landholder listed in the 8-A land record can apply, and they must have the consent of all other joint landholders.

scheme_name: Scheme to Provide Financial Assistance to Purchase Solar Power Unit/Kit for Solar Fencing around the Farm
question: How frequently can a farmer apply for this scheme?
answer: A farmer can avail of the benefits only once in 10 years.

scheme_name: Scheme to Provide Financial Assistance to Purchase Solar Power Unit/Kit for Solar Fencing around the Farm
question: Are farmers who have availed benefits under the "Wire Fencing Scheme" eligible for this scheme?
answer: No, farmers who have already received assistance under the Wire Fencing Scheme are not eligible for this scheme.

scheme_name: Scheme to Provide Financial Assistance to Purchase Solar Power Unit/Kit for Solar Fencing around the Farm
question: Can a farmer apply if they own multiple landholdings?
answer: No, a farmer can apply for assistance under this scheme for only one landholding account.

scheme_name: Scheme to Provide Financial Assistance to Purchase Solar Power Unit/Kit for Solar Fencing around the Farm
question: What additional document are required for farmers in forest areas?
answer: Farmers in forest areas must submit a "Van Adhikar Patra or Sanad" to be eligible for the scheme.

scheme_name: Scheme to Provide Financial Assistance to Purchase Solar Power Unit/Kit for Solar Fencing around the Farm
question: Where should a farmer submit the application?
answer: The application must be submitted online through the i-Khedut Portal: https://ikhedut.gujarat.gov.in/.

scheme_name: Scheme to Provide Financial Assistance to Purchase Solar Power Unit/Kit for Solar Fencing around the Farm
question: Who can a farmer contact for further assistance regarding the scheme?
answer: Farmers can reach out to their Gram Sevak, Extension Officer, or District Agriculture Officer for more information.

scheme_name: Sardar Patel Awas Yojana
question: What are the benefits of the Sardar Patel Awas Yojana?
answer: The Sardar Patel Awas Yojana is a housing scheme for people living below the poverty line in rural areas. The benefits of the scheme include providing eligible applicants with a pucca house with basic amenities such as water and electricity connections

scheme_name: Sardar Patel Awas Yojana
question: Can a person avail of the benefits of the Sardar Patel Awas Yojana more than once?
answer: No, a beneficiary can only avail of the benefits of the scheme once.

scheme_name: Sardar Patel Awas Yojana
question: Is there any fee for applying to the Sardar Patel Awas Yojana?
answer: There is no fee for applying to the scheme. However, additional fees may apply for certain services, such as water and electricity connections, and for maintenance of the house after construction.

scheme_name: Sardar Patel Awas Yojana
question: Who is eligible for the Sardar Patel Awas Yojana?
answer: - This scheme of the State Govt. being poor-oriented the persons registered Below the Poverty Line in rural areas may avail the benefit of the scheme. | - A person who has no plot or house may avail the benefit of the scheme. | - The applicant should not have taken benefit of any other housing scheme. | - The applicant who has a maximum of half a hectare of irrigated land or a maximum of one hectare of unrelated land may also avail advantage of the scheme. | - If husband and wife live together and if there is a plot or house in the name of the husband or wife and living in the same village for the last five years, either of them may avail the benefit of the scheme. | - If a beneficiary is a native of the village he should hold a card Below the Poverty Line of that village such person should obtain a certificate from the Sarpanch of his native village that "this beneficiary has not taken advantage of Sardar Patel Awas Yojana in our village. A certificate should be produced that there is no house in his name or in the name of his wife in his native place and they should fall in the definition of B.P.L. | - Benefit under Sardar Patel Awas Yojana is available to the villager living Below Poverty Line only once.

scheme_name: Sardar Patel Awas Yojana
question: What documents are required for applying to the Sardar Patel Awas Yojana?
answer: - Proof of registration as below the poverty line in a rural area. | - Identity proof such as Aadhaar Card, Voter ID, etc. | - Address proof such as ration card, electricity bill, etc. | - Land documents to prove that the applicant does not own a house or plot. | - Certificate from the Sarpanch of the native village stating that the applicant has not previously taken advantage of the Sardar Patel Awas Yojana and meets the B.P.L criteria. | - Income certificates or proof of income such as salary slips, bank statements, etc. | - Any other documents that may be required by the authorities for the application process.

scheme_name: Sardar Patel Awas Yojana
question: List of the required documents
answer: - Download the application from the official website. | - Fill out the application form with the required details. | - Include all the required documents. | - Applicant should apply to Nearest Taluka Vistar Adhikari/Taluka Panchayat/Jila Panchayat with the application form.

scheme_name: Shooting Permission Certificate
question: Who can apply for film shooting permission?
answer: Any film producer or an authorized line producer can apply for film shooting permission.

scheme_name: Shooting Permission Certificate
question: Where can applicants apply for the shooting permission?
answer: Applications must be submitted online through the Single Window System portal: https://investuttarakhand.uk.gov.in/filmshooting/

scheme_name: Shooting Permission Certificate
question: How long does it take to receive the shooting permission?
answer: The permission is issued within 14 days of application submission.

scheme_name: Shooting Permission Certificate
question: How is the permission certificate shared after approval?
answer: Once approved, a copy of the Film Shooting Permission Certificate is automatically emailed to all relevant government departments.

scheme_name: Shooting Permission Certificate
question: How will applicants be informed of their approval?
answer: Applicants receive the approval and certificate directly via email.

scheme_name: "Subsidy to Pollution Control Equipment" under "Motivation of Entrepreneurs to Start Industries and Fiscal Assistance to Capital Intensive Industries"
question: How much employment must be provided to residents of Puducherry for a unit to be eligible for incentives/subsidies/assistance?
answer: At least 60% of employment must be provided to the people of Puducherry out of the total employment strength of the industrial units.

scheme_name: "Subsidy to Pollution Control Equipment" under "Motivation of Entrepreneurs to Start Industries and Fiscal Assistance to Capital Intensive Industries"
question: What is the composition of the State Level Committee responsible for evaluating subsidy applications?
answer: The State Level Committee consists of the Secretary to Government (Industries & Commerce), the Managing Director of PIPDIC, the Deputy Secretary/Under Secretary (Finance), and the Director of Industries and Commerce, all from Puducherry.

scheme_name: "Subsidy to Pollution Control Equipment" under "Motivation of Entrepreneurs to Start Industries and Fiscal Assistance to Capital Intensive Industries"
question: Under what circumstances would the entire amount of subsidies and incentives availed need to be refunded, according to the content?
answer: If the unit undergoes any amendments in new partners or shareholders within five years from the date of availing the subsidy, the entire amount of subsidies and incentives availed must be refunded with a simple interest of 14% per annum.

scheme_name: "Subsidy to Pollution Control Equipment" under "Motivation of Entrepreneurs to Start Industries and Fiscal Assistance to Capital Intensive Industries"
question: Which types of investments are ineligible for investment subsidy according to the provided conditions?
answer: Working capital, commissioning fees, goodwill fees, royalty, preliminary and pre-operative expenses, capitalized interest, transportation and erection charges, goods vehicles, office equipment, furniture, crates, pallets, and consumable stores, etc., are ineligible for investment subsidy.

scheme_name: "Subsidy to Pollution Control Equipment" under "Motivation of Entrepreneurs to Start Industries and Fiscal Assistance to Capital Intensive Industries"
question: Through whom is the subsidy amount disbursed if the unit is financed by financial institutions/banks?
answer: The subsidy amount is disbursed through financial institutions/banks towards the adjustment against the loan availed by the entrepreneurs or for the creation of additional fixed assets or for working capital purposes.

scheme_name: "Subsidy to Pollution Control Equipment" under "Motivation of Entrepreneurs to Start Industries and Fiscal Assistance to Capital Intensive Industries"
question: What happens if an industrial unit has availed investment subsidy from the Central Government/State Government or any other agency?
answer: If an industrial unit has availed investment subsidy from any other agency, it is not eligible to apply for a subsidy for the same investment again under this Scheme.

scheme_name: "Subsidy to Pollution Control Equipment" under "Motivation of Entrepreneurs to Start Industries and Fiscal Assistance to Capital Intensive Industries"
question: What is the condition for industrial units set up by the same person to be eligible for subsidy as separate entities?
answer: Industrial units set up by the same person as proprietor, common partners, or common Board of Directors/shareholders are eligible for subsidy as separate entities provided the location of the units is different and licenses/clearances/registrations are obtained separately for the enterprises.

scheme_name: "Subsidy to Pollution Control Equipment" under "Motivation of Entrepreneurs to Start Industries and Fiscal Assistance to Capital Intensive Industries"
question: How is the commencement date for regular commercial production determined?
answer: The commencement date is verified by Officials of the Industries Department based on the entrepreneur's admission.

scheme_name: "Subsidy to Pollution Control Equipment" under "Motivation of Entrepreneurs to Start Industries and Fiscal Assistance to Capital Intensive Industries"
question: What is the employment requirement for qualifying for incentives/subsidies?
answer: To qualify for incentives/subsidies, the industrial unit must provide at least 60% of employment to residents of Puducherry out of the total employment strength.

scheme_name: "Subsidy to Pollution Control Equipment" under "Motivation of Entrepreneurs to Start Industries and Fiscal Assistance to Capital Intensive Industries"
question: What is the role of the State Level Committee in the subsidy application process?
answer: The State Level Committee scrutinizes applications, determines eligibility, and recommends the quantum of incentive/subsidy admissible to the unit.

scheme_name: "Subsidy to Pollution Control Equipment" under "Motivation of Entrepreneurs to Start Industries and Fiscal Assistance to Capital Intensive Industries"
question: Who sanctions the subsidies based on the Committee's recommendations?
answer: The Director of Industries and Commerce sanctions the subsidies based on the Committee's recommendations.

scheme_name: "Subsidy to Pollution Control Equipment" under "Motivation of Entrepreneurs to Start Industries and Fiscal Assistance to Capital Intensive Industries"
question: When is the entire amount of subsidies and incentives availed required to be refunded?
answer: The amount must be refunded if there are amendments in partners or shareholders within five years of availing the subsidy, with an interest of 14% per annum.

scheme_name: Scheme for Providing Counseling to the Trainees of Government Industrial Training Institutes at Directorate of Skill Development & Entrepreneurship
question: Which specific regional language is considered an essential and required element of knowledge for successful fulfillment of the duties in this role?
answer: The applicant must possess essential knowledge of the Konkani language to fulfill the linguistic requirements necessary for successful engagement with the scheme's beneficiaries.

scheme_name: Scheme for Providing Counseling to the Trainees of Government Industrial Training Institutes at Directorate of Skill Development & Entrepreneurship
question: If I hold a Masters degree in Social Work, what precise specialization must have been pursued to meet the essential educational requirement for the Counselor role?
answer: If possessing a Masters in Social Work (MSW), the applicant must have specialized in both medical and psychiatric fields to meet the required educational criteria for the Counselor profile.

scheme_name: Scheme for Providing Counseling to the Trainees of Government Industrial Training Institutes at Directorate of Skill Development & Entrepreneurship
question: For the Supervisor role overseeing the professional counseling team, what is the minimum length of professional experience that is considered mandatory?
answer: Applicants for the Supervisor role must possess a minimum of 3 years experience specifically in the field of Counselling to qualify for the position.

scheme_name: Scheme for Providing Counseling to the Trainees of Government Industrial Training Institutes at Directorate of Skill Development & Entrepreneurship
question: How long must the computer training course certificate cover to satisfy the technical requirement for the Data Entry Operator role?
answer: The required certificate must confirm that the applicant has completed a computer course for a minimum period of 3 months from a recognized institution.

scheme_name: Scheme for Providing Counseling to the Trainees of Government Industrial Training Institutes at Directorate of Skill Development & Entrepreneurship
question: What is the maximum age limit prescribed by the official guidelines for individuals seeking to apply for any of the contract positions under this initiative?
answer: Applicants seeking employment for any of the contract positions, including Counselor, Supervisor, or Data Entry Operator, must not exceed the age limit of 45 years.

scheme_name: Scheme for Providing Counseling to the Trainees of Government Industrial Training Institutes at Directorate of Skill Development & Entrepreneurship
question: What advanced academic degree specializing in psychological study is required as an essential qualification for the specific Counselor position?
answer: Applicants for the Counselor position must possess a Regular Masters degree in Clinical Psychology or Counseling Psychology from a recognized university or institution.

scheme_name: Scheme for Providing Counseling to the Trainees of Government Industrial Training Institutes at Directorate of Skill Development & Entrepreneurship
question: Regarding my prior work history, must I show specific experience in organizing and executing professional skill development sessions?
answer: Yes, it is mandatory for the applicant to possess verifiable experience of conducting training and workshops relevant to the scope of work described under the scheme.

scheme_name: Scheme for Providing Counseling to the Trainees of Government Industrial Training Institutes at Directorate of Skill Development & Entrepreneurship
question: Is it absolutely mandatory for all candidates, regardless of their position, to provide official proof of extended residency in the State?
answer: Yes, every applicant must mandatorily possess and submit a 15 years residence certificate of the State of Goa to satisfy the essential residency requirement.

scheme_name: Scheme for Providing Counseling to the Trainees of Government Industrial Training Institutes at Directorate of Skill Development & Entrepreneurship
question: Which specific certification or diploma related to guidance services is required as a mandatory supplement to the Masters degree for the Supervisor role?
answer: The applicant must possess a Diploma in Guidance and Counseling issued by an officially recognized institution as an essential criterion for the Supervisor role.

scheme_name: Scheme for Providing Counseling to the Trainees of Government Industrial Training Institutes at Directorate of Skill Development & Entrepreneurship
question: What is the basic mandatory educational certificate required for an applicant applying for the supportive Data Entry Operator position?
answer: The applicant must have successfully passed the Higher Secondary School Certificate Examination (HSSCE) from an officially recognized educational institution.

scheme_name: Scheme for Providing Counseling to the Trainees of Government Industrial Training Institutes at Directorate of Skill Development & Entrepreneurship
question: Will my application receive favorable consideration if I have pursued doctoral or higher-level research degrees in the field of psychological studies?
answer: Yes, possessing a Master of Philosophy (M. Phil) or a Doctor of Philosophy (Ph. D.) degree in Psychology is listed as a desirable qualification for the Supervisor position.

scheme_name: Scheme for Providing Counseling to the Trainees of Government Industrial Training Institutes at Directorate of Skill Development & Entrepreneurship
question: Is having competency or prior knowledge of the Marathi language considered a mandatory prerequisite for securing an employment contract?
answer: No, while knowledge of the Marathi language is considered a desirable qualification, it is not listed as an essential or mandatory prerequisite criterion for application.

scheme_name: Scheme for Providing Counseling to the Trainees of Government Industrial Training Institutes at Directorate of Skill Development & Entrepreneurship
question: How much professional experience is required in the field of guidance or psychological services for me to be deemed eligible for the Counselor role?
answer: The applicant must have a minimum of 1 year experience specifically in the field of Counseling to meet the mandatory professional qualification criteria.

scheme_name: Scheme for Providing Counseling to the Trainees of Government Industrial Training Institutes at Directorate of Skill Development & Entrepreneurship
question: Are there alternative academic pathways that can be considered sufficient for meeting the educational requirements if I do not hold a Masters degree in Psychology?
answer: Yes, a Regular Graduation degree in Psychology (6 units), Social Work, or Home Science (Human Resources) combined with a Diploma in Guidance and Counseling is also acceptable.

scheme_name: Scheme of Production of Domestic Indigenous Certified Seed of Cotton Varieties
question: What is the objective of the "Scheme of Production of Domestic Indigenous Certified Seed of Cotton Varieties" scheme?
answer: The objective of the "Scheme of Production of Domestic Indigenous Certified Seed of Cotton Varieties" scheme is to promote the cultivation and production of local cotton seed varieties across Gujarat. It supports farmers in producing foundation and certified cotton seeds, enhancing seed self-reliance and promoting the use of indigenous cotton strains.

scheme_name: Scheme of Production of Domestic Indigenous Certified Seed of Cotton Varieties
question: What kind of financial assistance is provided to the farmers through this scheme?
answer: Under this scheme, the Government of Gujarat provides financial assistance at the rate of ₹750 per quintal for the production of foundation and certified seeds, provided that the seeds are certified by the Gujarat State Seed Certification Agency.

scheme_name: Scheme of Production of Domestic Indigenous Certified Seed of Cotton Varieties
question: Is the scheme open to all farmers regardless of their income level or social category?
answer: Yes, the scheme is designed to be inclusive and is open to all farmers in the state of Gujarat, without any restrictions based on income level, educational background, caste, religion, or gender.

scheme_name: Scheme of Production of Domestic Indigenous Certified Seed of Cotton Varieties
question: Is seed certification mandatory to receive financial assistance under this scheme?
answer: Yes, in order to avail the financial benefits under this scheme, it is mandatory that the seeds produced by the farmer are certified by the Gujarat State Seed Certification Agency.

scheme_name: Scheme of Production of Domestic Indigenous Certified Seed of Cotton Varieties
question: What types of seeds are eligible for financial support under this scheme?
answer: Only indigenous varieties of cotton seeds that fall under the categories of foundation seeds and certified seeds and are approved by the Gujarat State Seed Certification Agency are eligible for financial support.

scheme_name: Scheme of Production of Domestic Indigenous Certified Seed of Cotton Varieties
question: What is the purpose of requiring a 7/12 certificate while applying for this scheme?
answer: The 7/12 certificate serves as proof of land ownership or lawful cultivation rights, and it is required to verify that the applicant is indeed a practicing farmer engaged in agriculture within Gujarat.

scheme_name: Scheme of Production of Domestic Indigenous Certified Seed of Cotton Varieties
question: How is the subsidy amount disbursed to the selected beneficiaries under the scheme?
answer: The subsidy amount of ₹750/- per quintal is transferred directly to the bank account of the beneficiary farmer after successful verification and approval of the application and seed certification.

scheme_name: Scheme of Production of Domestic Indigenous Certified Seed of Cotton Varieties
question: What role does the Gujarat State Seed Certification Agency play in the implementation of this scheme?
answer: The Gujarat State Seed Certification Agency is responsible for evaluating and certifying the quality of foundation and certified seeds produced by the farmers, which is a prerequisite for receiving financial assistance.

scheme_name: Scheme of Production of Domestic Indigenous Certified Seed of Cotton Varieties
question: Is there any application fee or processing charge for applying to this scheme?
answer: No, the Government of Gujarat does not charge any fee for applying to this scheme, and the entire application process is provided free of cost through the official iKhedut portal.

scheme_name: Scheme of Production of Domestic Indigenous Certified Seed of Cotton Varieties
question: Through which platform can eligible farmers submit their applications for this scheme?
answer: Eligible farmers can submit their applications only through the official online platform of the Government of Gujarat, which is the iKhedut portal.

scheme_name: Scheme for Plantation Development (New planting & Replanting) under Medium Term Framework Plan (MTFP) in Traditional Areas (Kerala and Tamil Nadu), Non-Traditional and North Eastern Region
question: Is it mandatory to provide the bill of planting material for certain years?
answer: For plantations in 2018, 2019, 2020, and 2021, the bill of planting material is not mandatory. Instead, a self-declaration containing purchase details is to be uploaded.

scheme_name: Scheme for Plantation Development (New planting & Replanting) under Medium Term Framework Plan (MTFP) in Traditional Areas (Kerala and Tamil Nadu), Non-Traditional and North Eastern Region
question: When is a nomination required in the application?
answer: A nomination is required in case of joint ownership or minor ownership. It is included in Annexure-1 of the application.

scheme_name: Scheme for Plantation Development (New planting & Replanting) under Medium Term Framework Plan (MTFP) in Traditional Areas (Kerala and Tamil Nadu), Non-Traditional and North Eastern Region
question: Re there any specific requirements for SC applicants in terms of documents?
answer: SC applicants are required to provide a caste certificate as part of the application.

scheme_name: Scheme for Plantation Development (New planting & Replanting) under Medium Term Framework Plan (MTFP) in Traditional Areas (Kerala and Tamil Nadu), Non-Traditional and North Eastern Region
question: Is there a requirement to provide a sketch of the applied area?
answer: Yes, a sketch of the applied area is required, showing descriptions of boundaries on all sides with the names of the owners.

scheme_name: Scheme for Plantation Development (New planting & Replanting) under Medium Term Framework Plan (MTFP) in Traditional Areas (Kerala and Tamil Nadu), Non-Traditional and North Eastern Region
question: How is ownership of the rubber area proven in the application?
answer: Ownership is established by providing a valid certificate from the Village Officer.

scheme_name: Scheme for Plantation Development (New planting & Replanting) under Medium Term Framework Plan (MTFP) in Traditional Areas (Kerala and Tamil Nadu), Non-Traditional and North Eastern Region
question: What information should be present in the bank passbook copy?
answer: The bank passbook copy should show the name of the account holder, the account number, and the IFS Code of the bank.

scheme_name: Scheme for Plantation Development (New planting & Replanting) under Medium Term Framework Plan (MTFP) in Traditional Areas (Kerala and Tamil Nadu), Non-Traditional and North Eastern Region
question: What kind of identity proof is preferred for the application?
answer: Preferred identity proof documents include Voter ID, PAN card, Driving Licence, or Passport.

scheme_name: Scheme for Plantation Development (New planting & Replanting) under Medium Term Framework Plan (MTFP) in Traditional Areas (Kerala and Tamil Nadu), Non-Traditional and North Eastern Region
question: How are sloppy lands protected from soil erosion in the plantation?
answer: Sloppy lands are protected from soil erosion through measures such as contour terracing, construction of contour bunds, digging silt trenches or pits, and planting of cover crops.

scheme_name: Scheme for Plantation Development (New planting & Replanting) under Medium Term Framework Plan (MTFP) in Traditional Areas (Kerala and Tamil Nadu), Non-Traditional and North Eastern Region
question: Can non-rubber trees be retained in the plantation, and if so, what is the limit?
answer: Yes, non-rubber trees can be retained, with a maximum of 20 trees, 40 coconut palms, or 80 areca nut palms per hectare, distributed evenly.

scheme_name: Scheme for Plantation Development (New planting & Replanting) under Medium Term Framework Plan (MTFP) in Traditional Areas (Kerala and Tamil Nadu), Non-Traditional and North Eastern Region
question: What conditions are set for maintaining rubber plantations in terms of plant density?
answer: Rubber plantations should maintain a minimum stand of 450 plants per hectare. The growth must also be satisfactory, as assessed by the inspecting officer.

scheme_name: Scheme for Plantation Development (New planting & Replanting) under Medium Term Framework Plan (MTFP) in Traditional Areas (Kerala and Tamil Nadu), Non-Traditional and North Eastern Region
question: How is the planting subsidy disbursed in Non-Traditional and North Eastern Regions?
answer: In these regions, the planting subsidy is also paid in a single installment upon satisfactory completion of stipulated work items. The payment method is exclusively through bank e-transfer, with the requirement of Aadhar-linked bank account details in the application.

scheme_name: Scheme for Plantation Development (New planting & Replanting) under Medium Term Framework Plan (MTFP) in Traditional Areas (Kerala and Tamil Nadu), Non-Traditional and North Eastern Region
question: What is the subsidy structure for Non-Traditional and North Eastern Regions?
answer: In these regions, the subsidy is [?]35,000 per hectare with an additional [?]5,000 per hectare for planting material. Similar to the Traditional Region, the planting material subsidy is [?]10 per plant, limited to 500 plants per hectare.

scheme_name: Scheme for Plantation Development (New planting & Replanting) under Medium Term Framework Plan (MTFP) in Traditional Areas (Kerala and Tamil Nadu), Non-Traditional and North Eastern Region
question: How is the planting subsidy disbursed in the Traditional Region?
answer: The planting subsidy is paid in a single installment, provided that the stipulated work items are satisfactorily completed. The payment is exclusively through bank e-transfer, requiring Aadhar-linked bank account details in the application.

scheme_name: Scheme for Plantation Development (New planting & Replanting) under Medium Term Framework Plan (MTFP) in Traditional Areas (Kerala and Tamil Nadu), Non-Traditional and North Eastern Region
question: What are the key benefits provided under the Scheme for Plantation Development in Kerala and Tamil Nadu?
answer: In the Traditional Region, general category growers receive [?]20,000 per hectare along with [?]5,000 per hectare for planting material. For SC category growers, the subsidy is [?]35,000 per hectare, also with [?]5,000 per hectare for planting material. The subsidy for planting material is capped at [?]10 per plant for up to 500 plants per hectare.

scheme_name: Subsidy to Purchase E-Bike for Journalists
question: Is there an age limit for journalists to qualify for the subsidy?
answer: Yes, the beneficiary must not be more than 58 years old at the time of application.

scheme_name: Subsidy to Purchase E-Bike for Journalists
question: Can journalists who have availed similar benefits under other government schemes apply?
answer: No, applicants who have already benefited from any other government scheme for e-bikes are not eligible.

scheme_name: Subsidy to Purchase E-Bike for Journalists
question: What proof of employment is required for the subsidy application?
answer: A letter from the Editor or Head of the Organization confirming the applicant’s employment as a journalist for at least 8 years is mandatory.

scheme_name: Subsidy to Purchase E-Bike for Journalists
question: How much subsidy will be provided for the purchase of an e-bike?
answer: The subsidy covers 50% of the e-bike’s price or a maximum of ₹50,000, whichever is lower.

scheme_name: Subsidy to Purchase E-Bike for Journalists
question: Are part-time journalists eligible to apply for the subsidy?
answer: No, only full-time journalists whose sole livelihood depends on journalistic activities qualify for the subsidy.

scheme_name: Subsidy to Purchase E-Bike for Journalists
question: How many e-bikes will be subsidized under this scheme annually?
answer: The government will grant subsidies for 65 e-bikes each year, allocated on a first-come, first-served basis.

scheme_name: Subsidy to Purchase E-Bike for Journalists
question: Can journalists working for electronic media organizations apply for the subsidy?
answer: Yes, journalists working for both print and electronic media organizations are eligible if they meet the other criteria.

scheme_name: Subsidy to Purchase E-Bike for Journalists
question: Is there a limit on the number of beneficiaries per media organization?
answer: Yes, a maximum of two beneficiaries per media organization will be considered per meeting.

scheme_name: Subsidy to Purchase E-Bike for Journalists
question: Who constitutes the committee responsible for scrutinizing and approving applications?
answer: The committee includes the Director of Information and Publicity, Presidents of journalist associations, and a representative from the Finance Department.

scheme_name: Subsidy to Purchase E-Bike for Journalists
question: Can the subsidy be used to purchase any type of e-bike?
answer: The type and cost of the e-bike will be decided by the government, and applicants must submit a quotation from a reputed dealer.

scheme_name: Subsidy to Purchase E-Bike for Journalists
question: What is the validity period of the scheme before it is reviewed?
answer: The scheme will be reviewed after 3 years from its commencement date.

scheme_name: Subsidy to Purchase E-Bike for Journalists
question: Are retired journalists eligible to apply for the subsidy?
answer: No, only working journalists who meet the age and employment criteria are eligible.

scheme_name: Subsidy to Purchase E-Bike for Journalists
question: What is the role of the Mamlatdar in the application process?
answer: The Mamlatdar issues the 15-year residence certificate, which is a mandatory document for proving domicile in Goa.

scheme_name: Subsidy to Purchase E-Bike for Journalists
question: Can journalists who engage in other professions alongside journalism apply?
answer: No, applicants must not engage in any other activity and must rely solely on journalism for their livelihood.

scheme_name: Subsidy to Purchase E-Bike for Journalists
question: Is there a relaxation clause for any of the eligibility conditions?
answer: The government may relax certain conditions on a case-by-case basis, except those related to financial benefits.

scheme_name: Subsidy to Purchase E-Bike for Journalists
question: How is the subsidy amount calculated if the e-bike’s price exceeds ₹1,00,000?
answer: The subsidy will be 50% of the price or ₹50,000, whichever is lower, regardless of the e-bike’s total cost.

scheme_name: Ashirbad: Scheme for Specially Cared Children
question: Who is considered a specially cared child under this scheme?
answer: A specially cared child is one who lost both parents, a single parent, or a primary bread earner on or after 1 April 2020.

scheme_name: Ashirbad: Scheme for Specially Cared Children
question: What support does the scheme provide if both my parents have passed away?
answer: If both parents have died, you may receive monthly financial assistance along with health, education, and food security benefits.

scheme_name: Ashirbad: Scheme for Specially Cared Children
question: What help can I receive if only one of my parents has passed away?
answer: If a single parent has died, the same benefits apply as long as the death occurred on or after 1 April 2020.

scheme_name: Ashirbad: Scheme for Specially Cared Children
question: What does the scheme offer if my primary bread earner has died but I live with the remaining parent?

scheme_name: Scheme for Promotion of Manufacturing of Electronic Components and Semiconductors (SPECS)"
question: What is the SPECS scheme?
answer: To help offset disabilities w.r.t to domestic manufacturing of electronic components & semiconductors, and in order to strengthen the electronics manufacturing ecosystem in the country, the Scheme for Promotion of Manufacturing of Electronic Components and Semiconductors (SPECS) | was notified vide Gazette Notification CG-DL-E-01042020-218992 dated 01.04.2020 in Part-I, Section 1 of the Gazette of India (Extraordinary). The Scheme offers a financial incentive of 25% on capital expenditure for the manufacturing of goods as per list annexed in the scheme.

scheme_name: Scheme for Promotion of Manufacturing of Electronic Components and Semiconductors (SPECS)"
question: Who is an Applicant under the Scheme?
answer: An Applicant for the purpose of the Scheme is a legal entity i.e., Private Limited Company, Public Limited Company, Sole Proprietorship, Partnership, or Limited Liability Partnership registered in India.

scheme_name: Scheme for Promotion of Manufacturing of Electronic Components and Semiconductors (SPECS)"
question: Can an applicant make more than one application under the scheme?
answer: There is no restriction on any applicant from making multiple applications under the Scheme. A Project / Unit proposed under the Scheme may include manufacturing facilities at one or more proposed locations.

scheme_name: Scheme for Promotion of Manufacturing of Electronic Components and Semiconductors (SPECS)"
question: Is an acknowledgement issued to applicants under the scheme?
answer: Based on initial scrutiny, the Project Management Agency (PMA) shall issue an acknowledgement within 15 working days of receipt of an application if the application prima facie meets the criteria defined in Annexure 3 of the Scheme Guidelines. However, this acknowledgement shall not be construed as approval under the Scheme.

scheme_name: Scheme for Promotion of Manufacturing of Electronic Components and Semiconductors (SPECS)"
question: How is commercial production defined? Is trial production also covered under the definition of ‘Commercial Production’?
answer: Commercial production is production that is undertaken for the sale of manufactured goods by the approved Project / Unit. Trial production is not covered under the definition of ‘Commercial Production’.

scheme_name: Scheme for Promotion of Manufacturing of Electronic Components and Semiconductors (SPECS)"
question: Does the expenditure incurred on associated utilities include utilities such as electric works, firefighting and sanitary works? Is there a cap on capital expenditure incurred on associated utilities for determining eligible capital expenditure under the Scheme?
answer: Associated utilities don’t include civil works related to firefighting arrangements and sanitary works. Associated utilities shall inter-alia include captive powerplants, effluent treatment plants, essential equipment required in operations areas such as clean rooms, air curtains, temperature and air quality control systems, compressed air, water, power supply and control systems, etc. capped at rates specified in the CPWD plinth area rates. Associated utilities shall also include IT and ITES infrastructure related to manufacturing including servers, software and ERP solutions. | The total expenditure incurred on associated utilities not exceeding 20% of the total eligible capital expenditure on plant, machinery and equipment shall be considered for determining eligible capital expenditure under the Scheme.

scheme_name: Scheme for Promotion of Manufacturing of Electronic Components and Semiconductors (SPECS)"
question: Does the expenditure incurred on Research and Development (R&D) include outsourced R&D work? Is there a cap on capital expenditure incurred on R&D for determining eligible capital expenditure under the Scheme?
answer: Expenditure incurred on Research and Development (R&D) includes expenditure on in-house and captive R&D, directly attributable to goods for which the application is made, including all stages in the entire value chain of the goods proposed to be manufactured, including software integral to the functioning of the same. Capital expenditure on R&D not exceeding 20% of the total eligible capital expenditure for plant, machinery, equipment and associated utilities shall be considered for determining eligible capital expenditure under the Scheme.

scheme_name: Scheme for Promotion of Manufacturing of Electronic Components and Semiconductors (SPECS)"
question: Is manpower cost for R&D included in the capital expenditure incurred on R&D?
answer: No

scheme_name: Scheme for Promotion of Manufacturing of Electronic Components and Semiconductors (SPECS)"
question: Does the expenditure incurred on Transfer of Technology (ToT), include cost amortised over a period of time or royalty paid over a period of time? Is there a cap on capital expenditure incurred on ToT for determining eligible capital expenditure under the Scheme?
answer: The expenditure incurred on Transfer of Technology (ToT) includes onetime cost of technology and initial technology purchase related to goods for which the application is made. Thus, cost amortised over a period of time or royalty paid over a period of time is not included under the Scheme. The total expenditure incurred on Transfer of Technology Agreements not exceeding 10% of the total eligible capital expenditure for plant, machinery and equipment and associated utilities shall be considered for determining eligible capital expenditure under the Scheme.

scheme_name: Scheme for Promotion of Manufacturing of Electronic Components and Semiconductors (SPECS)"
question: Will the expenditure incurred on Land and Building be considered towards determining eligible capital expenditure under the Scheme?
answer: No, the expenditure incurred on land and building (including factory building / construction) required for the project / unit is not covered and, therefore, will not be considered towards determining eligible capital expenditure under the Scheme.

scheme_name: Scheme for Promotion of Manufacturing of Electronic Components and Semiconductors (SPECS)"
question: Will the expenditure incurred on consumables and raw material used for manufacturing be considered towards determining eligible capital expenditure under the Scheme?
answer: No, the expenditure on consumables and raw materials used for manufacturing shall not be considered as eligible capital expenditure under the Scheme.

scheme_name: Scheme for Promotion of Manufacturing of Electronic Components and Semiconductors (SPECS)"
question: How will the PMA verify capital expenditure?
answer: The PMA shall have a right to verify (through relevant documents and/or site visits) the expenditure incurred on plant, machinery and equipment (including for associated utilities, R&D and ToT) approved under the Scheme, as deemed necessary, which forms the basis of the disbursement claim. A Chartered Engineer / Registered Valuer shall validate the reasonableness of the cost of plant, machinery and equipment (including for associated utilities, R&D and ToT) for which an incentive is being claimed and provide a Certificate to that effect.

scheme_name: Scheme for Promotion of Manufacturing of Electronic Components and Semiconductors (SPECS)"
question: What if land has not been purchased or taken on rent / lease at the time of application?
answer: In case land has not been purchased or taken on rent / lease at the time of application, the applicant shall provide a definite location / plot details and a suitable document which confirms availability of the land at the time of application. However, the applicant shall provide the final registered document such as sale deed and / or registered rent / lease agreement on the land before the submission of Appraisal report by the PMA for consideration of the Executive Committee (EC).

scheme_name: Scheme for Promotion of Manufacturing of Electronic Components and Semiconductors (SPECS)"
question: What if the land has been taken on rent / leased for a period of less than 10 years by the Applicant?
answer: The application shall contain the requisite land documents such as registered sale deed and / or registered rent / lease agreement on the land for a period of not less than 10 years from the date of application in usual circumstances. In case of the land having been taken on rent / lease for a period less than 10 years, such application shall be processed if there is a renewal clause for extension of such rent / lease agreement in the registered document. If a renewal clause is not present in the registered rent / lease agreement, the same may be referred by the PMA to the Governing Council for taking an appropriate decision on whether to allow such an application with an exemption provision.

scheme_name: Scheme for Promotion of Manufacturing of Electronic Components and Semiconductors (SPECS)"
question: What information will an Approval Letter carry? Will an Approval Letter guarantee disbursement under the Scheme?
answer: After receiving recommendations of the EC in the form of approved minutes of the meeting of the EC, the PMA shall issue a letter to the applicant within 5 (five) working days, communicating approval under the Scheme, with a copy to MeitY. The approval letter shall clearly state the following: | - Name of Applicant | - Project / Unit Location (s) | - Date of Acknowledgement | - Eligible Product Category | - Minimum Threshold of Capital Expenditure | - Eligible Capital Expenditure and Proposed Capacities | - Total Eligible Incentive | - Last Date for making Capital Expenditure | The aforesaid approval letter shall not be construed as a guarantee for the disbursement of the incentive, as the same shall be dependent upon verification of eligibility after submission of the disbursal claim and other criteria defined in these Guidelines.

scheme_name: Scheme for Promotion of Manufacturing of Electronic Components and Semiconductors (SPECS)"
question: Will investments made by subsidiaries or affiliate companies of the applicant company be considered for the purpose of determining the eligible capital expenditure under the Scheme?
answer: Investments made by entities other than the applicant company shall not be considered for the purpose of determining eligible capital expenditure under the Scheme.

scheme_name: Scheme for Promotion of Manufacturing of Electronic Components and Semiconductors (SPECS)"
question: Is there any provision for claiming capital expenditure incurred on accrual basis?
answer: All capital expenditure relating to the project/unit that has been incurred and paid for directly by the applicant or on behalf of the applicant is to be claimed only after actual payment has been made (on a cash basis) and not on an accrual basis.

scheme_name: Scheme for Promotion of Manufacturing of Electronic Components and Semiconductors (SPECS)"
question: What if an Approved Project / Unit stops commercial production after a few years? Is there any penalty for the same?
answer: The Scheme proposes that the units receiving incentive under SPECS shall have to remain in commercial production for a period of at least 3 (three) years from the date of commencement of commercial production or 1 (one) year from the date of receipt of last incentive, whichever is later. However, in the event of default or closure of an applicant unit that has availed incentive under the Scheme before the period, the applicant unit shall be required to refund the incentive disbursed, failing which, recovery shall be done from the liquidated assets of such unit as per established procedures.

scheme_name: Scheme for Promotion of Manufacturing of Electronic Components and Semiconductors (SPECS)"
question: What is meant by electronic applications w.r.t. goods eligible for incentive under SPECS?
answer: Goods eligible for incentive under SPECS should have an electronic application and not an electrical, mechanical, or general-purpose function. | The components eligible under SPECS should be mounted on a PCBA with other active and passive components. The said components should be integrated with / mounted on a PCBA to perform their functions and should not be used independently on a standalone basis without a PCBA

scheme_name: Scheme for Promotion of Manufacturing of Electronic Components and Semiconductors (SPECS)"
question: Do plastic parts include moulded parts and do metal parts include sheet metal parts manufactured through stamping process?
answer: Yes, plastics include moulded parts and metal parts include sheet metal parts manufactured through stamping process. The mechanics (plastic and metal parts) manufactured should be for electronic applications only.

scheme_name: Scheme for Promotion of Manufacturing of Electronic Components and Semiconductors (SPECS)"
question: What are Assembly, Testing, Marking and Packaging (ATMP) units?
answer: Semiconductor manufacturing involves pre-fabrication, fabrication (fab) and post-fabrication processes. ATMP is the post-fabrication/ after -fabrication stage, which come into play at the end stage of the Semiconductor manufacturing process, where the wafer goes for (a)Assembly solutions, which involve processing of bare Semiconductor die (stages include Dicing, Die-bonding, Wire-bonding, Molding, Plating & Packaging) into finished ICs (b) Testing in order to ensure the IC meets performance specifications, which includes a wide range of Final, Systemlevel, Wafer or Strip Testing along with the complete end-of-line services. “Marking” is part & parcel of the Assembly process. The process is also called Outsourced Semiconductor Assembly and Test (OSAT) where in 3rd Party IC (Integrated Circuits) Assembly & Test services is provided.

scheme_name: Scheme for Promotion of Manufacturing of Electronic Components and Semiconductors (SPECS)"
question: Is LED Lighting (Lamps, Luminaries, etc) eligible under SPECS?
answer: LED lights (Lamps, Luminaries, etc) are not eligible under the SPECS, being finished products. However, the LED chips manufactured as SMT components under the category A1 (SMT components including LED Chips) or populated as COB or COG under the category A2 (Chip Modules for Smart Cards, RFID Antenna & Labels, CoB/ System in Package) is eligible under SPECS. The minimum investment threshold required for the goods covered under category A1 and A2 is INR 5 crore.

answer: The primary objective of the Scheme to Provide Electric Scooter to Disabled Person is to enhance the mobility, independence, and quality of life of orthopedic disabled individuals in Gujarat by offering financial assistance for the purchase of an electric scooter through a state-approved process.

scheme_name: Scheme to Provide Electric Scooter to Disabled Person
question: How much financial assistance is provided under this scheme?
answer: Under this scheme, the Government of Gujarat provides financial assistance of up to ₹25,000 or 50 percent of the basic cost of the electric scooter and the disability modification kit, whichever is lower, directly into the beneficiary’s bank account.

scheme_name: Scheme to Provide Electric Scooter to Disabled Person
question: Who can apply for benefits under this scheme?
answer: Any orthopedic disabled person who is a resident of Gujarat, aged between 18 and 50 years, having a certified disability of 40% or more, and listed in the BPL category with a 0 to 20 score, is eligible to apply under this scheme, subject to the prescribed conditions.

scheme_name: Scheme to Provide Electric Scooter to Disabled Person
question: Are both men and women eligible for this scheme?
answer: Yes, both male and female applicants with orthopedic disabilities meeting all eligibility conditions are considered eligible for assistance under this scheme, without any gender-based exclusion.

scheme_name: Scheme to Provide Electric Scooter to Disabled Person
question: Is the scheme limited to individuals with specific types of disabilities?
answer: Yes, the scheme is exclusively applicable to individuals with orthopedic disabilities and does not cover those with other forms of disabilities.

scheme_name: Scheme to Provide Electric Scooter to Disabled Person
question: What kind of priority is given to applicants during selection?
answer: Priority in the selection process is given to applicants whose names appear in the SECC-2011 (Socio-Economic Caste Census-2011) list, especially those falling under the BPL category with a score ranging from 0 to 20.

scheme_name: Scheme to Provide Electric Scooter to Disabled Person
question: How does one obtain the application form for this scheme?
answer: The application form for this scheme is made available free of cost and may be obtained from the office of the District Social Security Officer and submitted when the government issues a public advertisement inviting applications.

scheme_name: Scheme to Provide Electric Scooter to Disabled Person
question: How are beneficiaries selected after submitting their application?
answer: After the verification of applications by the District Social Security Officer, beneficiaries are selected through a computerized draw to ensure transparency and fairness in the distribution process.

scheme_name: Scheme to Provide Electric Scooter to Disabled Person
question: From where the beneficiaries are required to purchase the electric scooter?
answer: Beneficiaries are required to purchase the electric scooter only from an agency designated by JEDA (Gujarat Energy Development Agency), at a price determined and approved at the state level.

scheme_name: Scheme to Provide Electric Scooter to Disabled Person
question: How is the assistance amount disbursed to the selected beneficiary?
answer: Once the beneficiary is selected and the purchase conditions are fulfilled, the assistance amount is deposited directly into the beneficiary’s registered bank account by the Director’s Office through the designated dealer.

scheme_name: Scheme to Provide Electric Scooter to Disabled Person
question: Can an individual apply again if the previously provided scooter gets damaged?
answer: If an individual has previously received a scooter under this scheme and the scooter has been damaged, the applicant can reapply after a minimum period of five years, provided they continue to meet the eligibility conditions.

answer: The purpose of the "Shaktidoot Scheme" is to support talented sportspersons in Gujarat by providing them with resources and financial assistance to excel at national and international levels.

scheme_name: Shaktidoot Scheme
question: Who is eligible to apply for the "Shaktidoot Scheme"?
answer: Applicants must be residents of Gujarat, meet the specified age and achievement criteria, and participate in recognized sports events to be eligible for the scheme.

scheme_name: Shaktidoot Scheme
question: What age group does the scheme cover?
answer: The scheme generally covers athletes up to 20 years of age, but age relaxation may be granted for exceptional cases based on merit.

scheme_name: Shaktidoot Scheme
question: Which sports are recognized under this scheme?
answer: The scheme recognizes games approved by the School Games Federation of India, Commonwealth Games, Asian Games, the Afro-Asian Games, and the Olympics.

scheme_name: Shaktidoot Scheme
question: What kind of financial assistance is provided?
answer: Financial assistance up to [?]25,00,000/- per year, depending on the athlete's achievements and level of competition.

scheme_name: Shaktidoot Scheme
question: Are state-level achievements considered for selection?
answer: Yes, athletes below the age of 12 who win state-level competitions are eligible for selection under the scheme.

scheme_name: Shaktidoot Scheme
question: Is participation in international competitions supported?
answer: Yes, the scheme provides financial support for travel, training, and other expenses related to international competitions.

scheme_name: Shaktidoot Scheme
question: How are applicants selected for the scheme?
answer: A committee evaluates the applications based on the applicant's achievements, potential, and adherence to eligibility criteria.

scheme_name: Shaktidoot Scheme
question: What is the duration of benefits under the scheme?
answer: The initial duration is two years, which can be extended for up to seven years based on the athlete's performance and progress.

scheme_name: Shaktidoot Scheme
question: Are athletes provided with insurance coverage?
answer: Yes, each athlete is provided with [?]5,00,000/- mediclaim insurance and [?]5 lakh accidental death insurance under the scheme.

scheme_name: Shaktidoot Scheme
question: Can athletes purchase their own equipment under the scheme?
answer: Yes, athletes can purchase their required equipment with prior approval, and expenses are reimbursed upon submission of valid bills.

scheme_name: Shaktidoot Scheme
question: What happens if an athlete does not show progress?
answer: Athletes who fail to demonstrate satisfactory progress during annual evaluations may be disqualified from the scheme.

scheme_name: Shaktidoot Scheme
question: Are workshops included in the scheme benefits?
answer: Yes, psychological workshops are organized to enhance the mental strength and focus of athletes.

scheme_name: Shaktidoot Scheme
question: How can applicants stay updated about the scheme?
answer: Applicants can stay updated by regularly checking public tenders in newspapers and the official notifications from the Sports Authority of Gujarat.

scheme_name: Stipend Scheme for Grandchildren of Freedom Fighters
question: Where can I apply for the stipend scheme?
answer: Applications should be submitted to the principal of the government or government-aided college/university where the student is enrolled.

scheme_name: Stipend Scheme for Grandchildren of Freedom Fighters
question: Who is eligible for the stipend scheme?
answer: Only third-generation descendants (grandchildren) of freedom fighters who are Haryana residents and enrolled in non-professional courses in government or government-aided colleges/universities are eligible.

scheme_name: Stipend Scheme for Grandchildren of Freedom Fighters
question: What financial assistance does this scheme provide?
answer: Eligible students receive [?]1,000 per month as a stipend for 12 months and [?]2,000 annually for books.

scheme_name: Stipend Scheme for Grandchildren of Freedom Fighters
question: What documents are required for application?
answer: Applicants must provide proof of relationship to a freedom fighter, Haryana domicile certificate, matriculation certificate, previous examination marksheet, good conduct certificate, and bank account details.

scheme_name: Stipend Scheme for Grandchildren of Freedom Fighters
question: When are the stipend payments made?
answer: Payments are made in September (for July & August), November (for September & October), January (for November & December), and March (for January to June).

scheme_name: Stipend Scheme for Grandchildren of Freedom Fighters
question: What if I drop out and later rejoin?
answer: If a student re-joins classes and attends at least 50% of classes within three months, both the previous and current quarter's stipend installments will be released.

scheme_name: Stipend Scheme for Grandchildren of Freedom Fighters

scheme_name: Stipend Scheme for Grandchildren of Freedom Fighters

answer: Students should contact their college principal or the Directorate of Higher Education for stipend status updates.

scheme_name: Stipend Scheme for Grandchildren of Freedom Fighters
question: Can I apply if my grandparent was a freedom fighter from another state?
answer: No, only the grandchildren of Haryana-based freedom fighters are eligible.

scheme_name: Stipend Scheme for Grandchildren of Freedom Fighters
question: What if my stipend is delayed?
answer: Students should report any delays to their college principal or the Directorate of Higher Education for resolution.

scheme_name: Stipend Scheme for Grandchildren of Freedom Fighters
question: Can students in private universities apply?
answer: No, only students in government and government-aided colleges/universities are eligible.

scheme_name: Stipend Scheme for Grandchildren of Freedom Fighters
question: Can I apply for this stipend in addition to other scholarships?
answer: The scheme does not mention restrictions regarding other scholarships. Students should verify with their institution.

scheme_name: Prani Sampad Samruddhi Yojana: Small Scale Goat / Sheep Farming (10+1 Capacity)
question: What is the objective of the scheme?
answer: The scheme intends to provide livelihood support to the interested small, marginal farmers and landless labourers and to improve the livelihoods of the weaker sections, especially belonging to the Scheduled Caste and Scheduled Tribe categories.

scheme_name: Prani Sampad Samruddhi Yojana: Small Scale Goat / Sheep Farming (10+1 Capacity)
question: Who are eligible to apply under this scheme?
answer: Interested small and marginal farmers and landless labourers are eligible to apply. The scheme covers beneficiaries belonging to the Scheduled Caste, Scheduled Tribe, Women, Transgender, differently-abled, and General (Male) categories, with specific subsidy provisions applicable to each category.

scheme_name: Prani Sampad Samruddhi Yojana: Small Scale Goat / Sheep Farming (10+1 Capacity)
question: What is the subsidy pattern under the scheme?
answer: Back-end subsidy will be provided through the Direct Benefit Transfer mode in two phases, as 60% of the unit cost to Scheduled Caste, Scheduled Tribe, Women, Transgender, and differently-abled categories, and 50% of the unit cost only for General (Male) categories. The first phase (40%) is released after completion of the shed, and the second phase (60%) after stocking of animals.

scheme_name: Prani Sampad Samruddhi Yojana: Small Scale Goat / Sheep Farming (10+1 Capacity)
question: What is the unit cost of a Goat / Sheep unit (10+1)?
answer: The unit cost of one Goat / Sheep unit (10+1) is ₹1,02,000/-, which includes the construction of a shed of 180 sq ft costing ₹36,000/-, the cost of animals ₹56,000/-, the insurance premium ₹8,000/-, and other miscellaneous expenses ₹2,000/-.

scheme_name: Prani Sampad Samruddhi Yojana: Small Scale Goat / Sheep Farming (10+1 Capacity)
question: How is the subsidy released to the beneficiary?
answer: The subsidy amount shall be released to the Aadhar-linked bank account of the beneficiary through the Direct Benefit Transfer mode in two installments after due asset verification by the Block Level Inspection Team. The Chief District Veterinary Officer may directly pay the amount towards the insurance premium to the Insurance Company as per guidelines.

scheme_name: Prani Sampad Samruddhi Yojana: Small Scale Goat / Sheep Farming (10+1 Capacity)
question: Is construction of a new shed mandatory?
answer: The beneficiary is required to construct a Goat Shed as per the specified floor space at Annexure-V. However, 60% of the subsidy may be released if the farmer inducted the animals first, even without the construction of a new shed, and the remaining 40% subsidy shall be released on completion of the shed. In case of non-construction of the shed, no subsidy shall be released on the shed component cost of ₹36,000/-, and it shall be deducted from the total subsidy.

scheme_name: Prani Sampad Samruddhi Yojana: Small Scale Goat / Sheep Farming (10+1 Capacity)
question: What is the application process for the scheme?
answer: The willing applicant shall apply in the “Go-Sugam Portal”. The Programme Assistant may facilitate uploading of the application and documents. After submission, the proposed site is verified by the Block Level Inspection Team with geo-tagged photographs, and on recommendation, the application is forwarded to the Chief District Veterinary Officer for approval by the District Level Committee, after which a Go-ahead letter is issued.

scheme_name: Prani Sampad Samruddhi Yojana: Small Scale Goat / Sheep Farming (10+1 Capacity)
question: Can a beneficiary who has already availed subsidy under similar schemes apply again?
answer: Those beneficiaries who have availed subsidies in similar types of schemes of the Government of India or the State Government or through Women Self Help Groups previously shall not be included under this scheme again.

scheme_name: Prani Sampad Samruddhi Yojana: Small Scale Goat / Sheep Farming (10+1 Capacity)
question: What is the income potential from the Goat / Sheep unit?
answer: As per the cash flow analysis provided in the guidelines, one beneficiary can earn up to ₹6,500/- per month by establishing a (10+1) Goat / Sheep unit and running it for 5 years, subject to the technical assumptions mentioned in the scheme.

scheme_name: Stipends to Students of Socially and Educationally Backward Classes for Technical and Vocational Courses after SSC

scheme_name: Stipends to Students of Socially and Educationally Backward Classes for Technical and Vocational Courses after SSC

scheme_name: Stipends to Students of Socially and Educationally Backward Classes for Technical and Vocational Courses after SSC

scheme_name: Stipends to Students of Socially and Educationally Backward Classes for Technical and Vocational Courses after SSC

scheme_name: Swatantrata Sainik Samman Pension Scheme

scheme_name: Swatantrata Sainik Samman Pension Scheme

scheme_name: Swatantrata Sainik Samman Pension Scheme

scheme_name: Swatantrata Sainik Samman Pension Scheme

answer: Applicants can request a free copy of the prescribed application form from either the State Government/UT concerned or the Freedom Fighters' Division, Ministry of Home Affairs, New Delhi.

scheme_name: Swatantrata Sainik Samman Pension Scheme
question: Are the movements for the merger of Princely States within the Indian Union after 15th August 1947 included in the National Freedom Movement?

scheme_name: Swatantrata Sainik Samman Pension Scheme
question: What movements/mutinies are considered as part of the National Freedom Struggle for pension eligibility?
answer: Movements/mutinies directed against the British, French (in the case of Pondicherry), and Portuguese (in the case of Goa) with the goal of India's freedom are considered part of the National Freedom Struggle.

scheme_name: Swatantrata Sainik Samman Pension Scheme
question: What is the definition of a martyr under this scheme?
answer: A martyr is someone who died or was killed in action, detention, or received capital punishment while participating in a National Movement for the emancipation of India.

scheme_name: Swatantrata Sainik Samman Pension Scheme
question: Hat are the conditions for a person who was interned in their home or externed from their district to be eligible for a pension?

scheme_name: Swatantrata Sainik Samman Pension Scheme
question: What are the criteria for a person who remained underground to be eligible for a pension?
answer: A person who remained underground for more than six months should have been a proclaimed offender, one with an arrest/head award, or one for whom a detention order was issued but not served.

scheme_name: Swatantrata Sainik Samman Pension Scheme
question: Who qualifies as eligible dependents under the scheme if the freedom fighter is not alive?
answer: Eligible dependents include mother, father, widower/widow if not remarried, and unmarried daughters. The sequence of eligibility is determined as widow/widower, unmarried daughters, mother, and father.

scheme_name: Swatantrata Sainik Samman Pension Scheme
question: How are broken periods of imprisonment accounted for in determining the qualifying period for pension eligibility?
answer: Broken periods of imprisonment are totaled up to compute the qualifying period.

scheme_name: Swatantrata Sainik Samman Pension Scheme
question: How is the period of undertrial counted in calculating the qualifying period for pension eligibility?
answer: In the case of a trial ending in conviction, the undertrial period is counted towards the actual imprisonment suffered.

scheme_name: Swatantrata Sainik Samman Pension Scheme
question: What is the significance of the period of normal remission in imprisonment calculations?
answer: Up to one month of normal remission is treated as part of actual imprisonment.

scheme_name: Swatantrata Sainik Samman Pension Scheme
question: How is "imprisonment" defined under the scheme?
answer: Detention under the orders of the competent authority is considered as imprisonment.

answer: The "Scheme to Provide Financial Assistance for the Production and Publication of Excellent Original Children's Literature" aims to promote the creation and dissemination of high-quality, original, and culturally valuable children's literature in Gujarati by providing financial support to eligible authors for publishing their manuscripts.

scheme_name: Scheme to Provide Financial Assistance for the Production and Publication of Excellent Original Children's Literature
question: Who is eligible to apply under this scheme?

scheme_name: Scheme to Provide Financial Assistance for the Production and Publication of Excellent Original Children's Literature
question: What type of literary works are supported under this scheme?

scheme_name: Scheme to Provide Financial Assistance for the Production and Publication of Excellent Original Children's Literature
question: Can previously published works be considered under this scheme?
answer: No, the scheme strictly supports only those manuscripts that are original and unpublished at the time of application; previously published or printed works are not eligible for financial assistance.

scheme_name: Scheme to Provide Financial Assistance for the Production and Publication of Excellent Original Children's Literature
question: What is the amount of financial assistance provided under the scheme?
answer: Authors may receive ₹5,000 for books up to 64 pages and ₹10,000 for books exceeding 64 pages, subject to the cost ceiling fixed for different book sizes and formats as specified by the Gujarat Sahitya Academy.

scheme_name: Scheme to Provide Financial Assistance for the Production and Publication of Excellent Original Children's Literature
question: Is there a maximum number of grants an author can receive from the Academy?
answer: Yes, authors who have already received financial assistance five times under any of the Sahitya Academy’s publishing-related schemes are not eligible to apply under this scheme again.

scheme_name: Scheme to Provide Financial Assistance for the Production and Publication of Excellent Original Children's Literature
question: How many applications can an author submit in a financial year?
answer: An author can submit only one application under this scheme during a financial year, and multiple submissions for different manuscripts in the same year will not be entertained.

scheme_name: Scheme to Provide Financial Assistance for the Production and Publication of Excellent Original Children's Literature
question: What are the formatting requirements for manuscript submission?
answer: The manuscript must be typed in Gujarati, properly bound, clearly paginated, and submitted in two hard copies along with the completed application form, author details, and declaration documents.

scheme_name: Scheme to Provide Financial Assistance for the Production and Publication of Excellent Original Children's Literature
question: Can the author change the manuscript title or content after submission?
answer: No, the author cannot change the title, content, or format of the manuscript after submission unless written permission is obtained from the Gujarat Sahitya Academy; any unauthorized changes may lead to cancellation of the application.

scheme_name: Scheme to Provide Financial Assistance for the Production and Publication of Excellent Original Children's Literature
question: How is the final selection of manuscripts carried out?
answer: The manuscript is reviewed by expert literary evaluators appointed by the Gujarat Sahitya Academy, and only those manuscripts that meet high literary standards and are suitable for children's reading are approved for assistance, with the Academy's decision being final.

scheme_name: Su-Swastha Yojana
question: What is the amount I am covered for? Can I increase this amount?

scheme_name: Su-Swastha Yojana

scheme_name: Su-Swastha Yojana

scheme_name: Su-Swastha Yojana

scheme_name: Su-Swastha Yojana

Dependents of the eligible employees- a maximum of 5 eligible dependents can be added for each employee

scheme_name: Su-Swastha Yojana

scheme_name: Su-Swastha Yojana

scheme_name: Su-Swastha Yojana

scheme_name: Su-Swastha Yojana
question: What is the amount of contribution for availing the scheme?

scheme_name: Su-Swastha Yojana
question: My spouse is also a government employee. Will both of us be entitled to enrol as a primary insured?
answer: When both spouses are government regular employees they can choose to enrol separately as primary member of Su-Swastha Yojna OR as dependent on the other spouse. However, an employee cannot be enrolled as a primary and dependent at the same time.

scheme_name: Su-Swastha Yojana

scheme_name: SUBHADRA

scheme_name: Goa State Logistics and Warehousing Incentives Scheme: Subsidy towards Upgradation in Transportation through Tracking Devices
question: What mandatory financial documentation or tax requirements must the entity possess and maintain compliance with to be considered an eligible applicant for these incentives?
answer: All entities applying must possess a Permanent Account Number (PAN) and must ensure they regularly file the Income Tax Returns using the name of the legal entity that is applying for the benefits.

scheme_name: Goa State Logistics and Warehousing Incentives Scheme: Subsidy towards Upgradation in Transportation through Tracking Devices
question: After submitting a complete application for any financial incentive under the umbrella scheme, what is the maximum time period generally required for the application to be fully processed and the benefit funds to be disbursed?
answer: The entire processing of the application and the disbursement of the incentive amount will be completed within a maximum period of 90 days, calculated from the date the application was formally received by the Directorate of Industries, Trade and Commerce.

scheme_name: Goa State Logistics and Warehousing Incentives Scheme: Subsidy towards Upgradation in Transportation through Tracking Devices
question: Is there a mandatory requirement regarding the percentage of local employment that my entity must maintain on its official payrolls to qualify for support under this incentives scheme?
answer: Yes, the entity must ensure the provision of a minimum of 40% local employment. This condition considers employees who are continuously employed and maintained on the unit’s payroll during the claim year.

scheme_name: Goa State Logistics and Warehousing Incentives Scheme: Subsidy towards Upgradation in Transportation through Tracking Devices
question: If I have received financial assistance or similar benefits for the same purpose from any program managed by the Central or State Government previously, will I still be considered eligible?
answer: No, this scheme is not applicable to any entity that has already claimed a similar benefit or incentive for the same purpose under any other existing scheme or program managed by either the State Government or the Central Government.

scheme_name: Goa State Logistics and Warehousing Incentives Scheme: Subsidy towards Upgradation in Transportation through Tracking Devices
question: What potential legal repercussions or mandatory refund requirements exist if it is later discovered that an entity obtained financial incentives through the submission of false or incorrect information?
answer: If incentives were obtained through misrepresentation of facts or in case of misuse, the financial incentive shall be revoked, and the entity undertakes to refund 10 times the concessions claimed.

scheme_name: Goa State Logistics and Warehousing Incentives Scheme: Subsidy towards Upgradation in Transportation through Tracking Devices
question: What additional steps must I take if my entity is owned by a woman entrepreneur or an entrepreneur belonging to the Schedule Caste or Schedule Tribe communities to ensure appropriate consideration?
answer: Entities owned by Women Entrepreneurs or those belonging to Schedule Caste/Schedule Tribe communities must explicitly declare their category when submitting the application for incentives on the Goa Online Portal and provide all necessary required documentation.

scheme_name: Goa State Logistics and Warehousing Incentives Scheme: Subsidy towards Upgradation in Transportation through Tracking Devices
question: Since governmental funds are finite, how are applications reviewed and prioritized when multiple entities apply for incentives simultaneously within a given fiscal year?
answer: The benefits under this scheme are subject to the availability of sufficient funds during a particular fiscal year and are generally processed based on the principle of first come first serve.

scheme_name: Goa State Logistics and Warehousing Incentives Scheme: Subsidy towards Upgradation in Transportation through Tracking Devices
question: Is there a mandatory prerequisite for both new and existing units detailing the minimum required period of continuous commercial operations immediately following the announcement of the Policy?
answer: Yes, all eligible entities must have been in continuous operations for a minimum period of six months subsequent to the official date of notification of the Logistics and Warehousing Policy 2023.

scheme_name: Goa State Logistics and Warehousing Incentives Scheme: Subsidy towards Upgradation in Transportation through Tracking Devices
question: How is the final value of the sanctioned financial benefit determined, specifically based on the entity’s ability to meet the prescribed targets for Goan employment on its payrolls?
answer: If Goan employment is 60% or above, the entity receives 100% of the calculated benefit, but if it is more than 40% yet less than 60%, the entity receives 80% of the calculated benefit, otherwise the entity is ineligible.

scheme_name: Goa State Logistics and Warehousing Incentives Scheme: Subsidy towards Upgradation in Transportation through Tracking Devices
question: Which specific government department or administrative body has been officially assigned the crucial responsibility of monitoring and successfully implementing the provisions of this incentives scheme?
