scheme_name: Goa State Logistics and Warehousing Incentives Scheme: Subsidy towards Upgradation in Transportation through Tracking Devices
question: Since the scheme is organized into various specific components, do the general clauses outlined in the main document still apply uniformly to every single target scheme introduced within this framework?

scheme_name: Goa State Logistics and Warehousing Incentives Scheme: Subsidy towards Upgradation in Transportation through Tracking Devices
question: What is the validity period of this incentives policy, and how long can entities expect the umbrella scheme to remain active and available for application submissions?

scheme_name: Goa State Logistics and Warehousing Incentives Scheme: Subsidy towards Upgradation in Transportation through Tracking Devices
question: Should my business unit possess investment or employment figures below certain established thresholds to be eligible to apply for financial assistance under this incentives scheme?

scheme_name: Goa State Logistics and Warehousing Incentives Scheme: Subsidy towards Upgradation in Transportation through Tracking Devices
question: Once an entity has successfully received financial incentives, what obligations are placed upon it regarding external inspections or the disclosure of official records by government officials?
answer: The entity must grant free access to any official authorized by the Directorate of Industries, Trade and Commerce for conducting inspection/supervision of the unit or the registers, or for holding discussions with the employed employees for ensuring the proper utilization of the granted financial incentives.

scheme_name: Skill Development Training - 15 Days Residential Skill Up-gradation Training Programme

scheme_name: Skill Development Training - 15 Days Residential Skill Up-gradation Training Programme

answer: The Telangana Building & Other Construction Workers Welfare Board bears the entire cost of the training.

scheme_name: Stand-Up India

scheme_name: Surakshit Matritva Aashwasan Yojana

scheme_name: Surakshit Matritva Aashwasan Yojana
question: What Is Infant Mortality Rate?

scheme_name: Surakshit Matritva Aashwasan Yojana

answer: Maternal mortality refers to deaths due to complications from pregnancy or childbirth. The maternal mortality ratio (MMR) is defined as the number of maternal deaths during a given time period per 100,000 live births during the same time period.

scheme_name: Skill Upgradation Program Karnataka

scheme_name: Skill Upgradation Program Karnataka

scheme_name: Skill Upgradation Program Karnataka

scheme_name: Skill Upgradation Program Karnataka

scheme_name: Scheme for Financial Assistance to select States/UTs for Skill Development in Electronics System Design and Manufacturing (ESDM) sector

scheme_name: Scheme for Financial Assistance to select States/UTs for Skill Development in Electronics System Design and Manufacturing (ESDM) sector

scheme_name: Scheme for Financial Assistance to select States/UTs for Skill Development in Electronics System Design and Manufacturing (ESDM) sector

scheme_name: Scheme for Financial Assistance to select States/UTs for Skill Development in Electronics System Design and Manufacturing (ESDM) sector

scheme_name: Scheme for Financial Assistance to select States/UTs for Skill Development in Electronics System Design and Manufacturing (ESDM) sector

scheme_name: Scheme for Financial Assistance to select States/UTs for Skill Development in Electronics System Design and Manufacturing (ESDM) sector

scheme_name: Scheme for Financial Assistance to select States/UTs for Skill Development in Electronics System Design and Manufacturing (ESDM) sector

scheme_name: Scheme for Financial Assistance to select States/UTs for Skill Development in Electronics System Design and Manufacturing (ESDM) sector

scheme_name: Scheme for Upliftment of Utsavi Rangabhumi of Goa

scheme_name: Scheme for Upliftment of Utsavi Rangabhumi of Goa

scheme_name: Scheme for Upliftment of Utsavi Rangabhumi of Goa

scheme_name: Scheme for Upliftment of Utsavi Rangabhumi of Goa

scheme_name: Scheme for Upliftment of Utsavi Rangabhumi of Goa

scheme_name: Scheme for Upliftment of Utsavi Rangabhumi of Goa

scheme_name: Scheme for Upliftment of Utsavi Rangabhumi of Goa

scheme_name: Scheme for Upliftment of Utsavi Rangabhumi of Goa

scheme_name: Saksham Yuva Scheme
question: What are the criterion to allocate honorary assignment to the approved applicant under the scheme?
answer: Honorary assignments will be offered seniority-wise and the seniority of the applicants shall be determined as per the following criteria:- | i)	Firstly, the applicant with higher age, as per the list, shall be higher in seniority; | ii)	In case the age is same, then the applicant who has obtained the 10+2/graduate/post-graduate degree earlier, shall be senior (for this the year of successful completion of 10+2/graduate/post-graduate studies shall be considered); | iii)	In the rare case where the age and year of 10+2/Graduate/PG certificate/degree is identical, then the applicant obtaining higher percentage of marks in 10+2/Graduation/Post-Graduation examination shall be senior. In case any applicant acquires more than one Post-Graduation degree, the one with the highest percentage of marks shall be considered. | iv)	The seniority list of a particular district shall be generated on the last working day of the month for the purpose of assigning the honorarium assignment in the succeeding month. | v)	All those applicants who have not been assigned any honorarium assignment in a particular month have to be taken in the seniority list for the assignment of honorary assignment in the succeeding month. | vi)	Notwithstanding above provisions from (i) to (v), the applicant who got seniority in the previous month to get the honorary work will retain his same seniority for the coming months too for all purposes except in those cases where a requisitioning department requests for a specific educational qualification. In addition, priority will be given to all those Saksham Yuva who have attended Skill Training Programme. Overall preference will be given in seniority for deployment to those applicants enrolled under Saksham Yuva Scheme who are eligible under the Mukhyamantri Antyodaya Parivar Utthan Yojana (MMAPUY).

scheme_name: Saksham Yuva Scheme
question: How long honorary assignment will be given to the eligible applicant?
answer: When the SAKSHAM YUVA is deployed by any indenting departments/PSUs/ Universities/Boards, the honorarium shall be paid for a maximum period of 03 years (36 months) or 35 years of age, whichever is earlier. Period of 3 years (36 months) shall start from date of allotment of honorarium assignment and age of 35 years shall be the exact date of completion of 35 years.

scheme_name: Saksham Yuva Scheme
question: Is there any penalty for not reporting on honorary assignment?
answer: If 10+2/graduate/post-graduate qualified Saksham Yuva who fails to attend to/report to any honorary assignment he/she is nominated for within 3 days then:- | a)	In the first instance, if he/she fails to report within 7 days, then the unemployment allowance shall be discontinued and his/her name shall be kept in abeyance/debar from the list of beneficiaries for one month; | b)	In the second instance, if he/she fails to report within 7 days, then the unemployment allowance shall be discontinued and his/her name shall be kept in abeyance/debar from the list of beneficiaries for one year; | c)	In the third instance, if he/she fails to report within 7 days, then he/she will be rejected permanently from the scheme.

scheme_name: Saksham Yuva Scheme
question: What is the remedy if an applicant filled a wrong entry under the application on the portal?
answer: If the applicant has filled/upload any wrong information then his/her application is rejected by the concerned District Employment Exchange then an applicant can make online appeal to concerned ADC/DC of their District within stipulated time period i.e. 30 days to ADC.

scheme_name: Saksham Yuva Scheme
question: How many times an Applicant can apply in the Scheme?
answer: An applicant can apply in the Scheme only once. However, concerned ADC/DC can provide second chance only after finding that his/her rejection from the scheme is on wrong grounds and need reapply.

scheme_name: Saksham Yuva Scheme
question: What is Grievances Redressal Mechanism?
answer: First Appellate Authority: The concerned ADC of the District shall be First Appellate Authority. Where the eligible applicant is aggrieved by any order of the Controlling Officer, he/she may, within 30 days of the date of communication of such order, make an onlineapplicationto the First Appellate Authority for revision against the said order. Taking cognizance of order, the First Appellate Authority may confirm, alter or rescind the decision of the Controlling Officer. | Second Appellate Authority: The Deputy Commissioner of the concerned district shall be second and final appellate authority. Provided that the Second Appellate Authority may entertain the application after the expiry of the said period of fifteen days, if he is satisfied that the eligible applicant was prevented by sufficient cause from filing the application in time.

scheme_name: Saksham Yuva Scheme
question: Is there any time limit to file appeal to ADC/DC in case of application is disapproved by concerned officer?
answer: In case the concerned officer disapproves the application then the Applicant has to file online appeal to concerned ADC/DC of their District within stipulated time periodi.e. 30 days to ADC and 15 days to DCafterthe date of rejection of application. The First/Second Appellate Authority may confirm, alter or rescind the decision of the Controlling Officer.

scheme_name: Saksham Yuva Scheme
question: Is the performance of saksham yuva assessed on assigned honorary work?
answer: Yes, the Performance of Saksham Yuva assigned Honorary Work in various Government Department/Boards/Corporations etc. is assessed on following criteria: | i) Timeline Rating. | ii) Attendance and punctuality. | iii) Quality of work and productivity. | iv) Job Knowledge and attitude towards assigned honorary work. | v) Team Work & Behaviour.

scheme_name: Saksham Yuva Scheme
question: Is the performance of saksham yuva assessed on assigned honorary work?
answer: If the overall performance of Saksham Yuva is assessed as average or poor, then the honorarium shall be deducted as per the following: | Average Performance: 25% deduction | Poor Performance:	100% deduction and rejection from the scheme | Further, in case the overall performance of Saksham Yuva is assessed as average or poor thrice during the deployment period of 36 months, he/she will not be entitled for further deployment on honorary assignment in any indenting department and he/she will avail only UEA as per provision of the scheme.

scheme_name: Saksham Yuva Scheme
question: How to mark attendance on Portal for Honorary work?
answer: An applicant may change district preferencefor doing honorary work twice a year by making an online request in the first fortnight of March & September on saksham portal i.e. https://hreyahs.gov.in.

scheme_name: Saksham Yuva Scheme
question: Is there any certificate required to certify family income?
answer: No, now family income of Applicant is verified online from Parivar Pehchan Patra (PPP ID) Database.

scheme_name: Saksham Yuva Scheme
question: Can applicants with correspondence degrees apply?
answer: Yes, those who have obtained their degrees through correspondence courses and are already benefiting from the scheme will continue to be eligible.

scheme_name: Saksham Yuva Scheme
question: Is the scheme available for students currently enrolled in full-time courses?
answer: No, regular students under full-time courses are not eligible for the scheme.

scheme_name: Saksham Yuva Scheme
question: Are applicants who have passed 10+2 through National Open School eligible?
answer: No, applicants who have passed 10+2 through correspondence or National Open School are not eligible.

scheme_name: Saksham Yuva Scheme
question: Can applicants dismissed from government service apply?
answer: No, applicants who have been dismissed from government service are not eligible for the scheme.

scheme_name: Saksham Yuva Scheme
question: Are self-employed individuals eligible for the scheme?
answer: No, applicants must not be engaged in any kind of employment, including self-employment.

scheme_name: Saksham Yuva Scheme
question: How can eligible applicants apply for the scheme?
answer: Applicants can apply online through the Saksham Yuva portal (https://hreyahs.gov.in) or the Antyodaya-SARAL Portal (https://saralharyana.gov.in).

scheme_name: Skilled Youth Startup Scheme
question: Who can apply for the Skilled Youth Startup Scheme (SYSS)?
answer: Applicants must be residents of Sikkim possessing a Certificate of Identification (COI), Sikkim Subject Certificate, or Residential Certificate (for urban areas).

scheme_name: Skilled Youth Startup Scheme
question: What is the age limit to apply under SYSS?
answer: The applicant must be between 18 and 45 years of age at the time of submitting the application.

scheme_name: Skilled Youth Startup Scheme
question: Is there any minimum educational qualification required?
answer: Yes, the applicant must have passed at least Class V from a recognized school. For technical or service-based projects, a relevant technical certificate is required.

scheme_name: Skilled Youth Startup Scheme
question: Can more than one member from the same family apply?
answer: No, only one member per family is eligible to avail benefits under the scheme.

scheme_name: Skilled Youth Startup Scheme
question: Is there an income limit to be eligible for the scheme?
answer: Yes, the applicant's family income must not exceed ₹8 lakhs per annum.

scheme_name: Skilled Youth Startup Scheme
question: Are government employees' children eligible?
answer: Only children of Group ‘C’ and Group ‘D’ government employees are eligible to apply under this scheme.

scheme_name: Skilled Youth Startup Scheme
question: Can an applicant who has availed subsidy under PMEGP or CMSS apply?
answer: No, applicants who have previously availed subsidy under PMEGP or CMSS are not eligible for this scheme.

scheme_name: Skilled Youth Startup Scheme
question: What financial contribution is expected from the applicant?
answer: Applicants must contribute 5% to 15% of the project cost, depending on the norms of the financing bank.

scheme_name: Skilled Youth Startup Scheme
question: Is trade license necessary at the time of application?
answer: Yes, the applicant must have a valid trade license or permit for the proposed project at the time of bank loan sanction.

scheme_name: Skilled Youth Startup Scheme
question: Is there any special provision for Persons with Disabilities (PwD)?
answer: Yes, PwD applicants are given priority and are eligible for a 50% loan subsidy under the scheme.

scheme_name: West Bengal Handloom and Khadi Weavers Financial Benefit Scheme 2024: Supply of Yarn to Societies etc. at Subsidized Rate

scheme_name: West Bengal Handloom and Khadi Weavers Financial Benefit Scheme 2024: Supply of Yarn to Societies etc. at Subsidized Rate

scheme_name: West Bengal Handloom and Khadi Weavers Financial Benefit Scheme 2024: Supply of Yarn to Societies etc. at Subsidized Rate

scheme_name: West Bengal Handloom and Khadi Weavers Financial Benefit Scheme 2024: Supply of Yarn to Societies etc. at Subsidized Rate

scheme_name: West Bengal Handloom and Khadi Weavers Financial Benefit Scheme 2024: Supply of Yarn to Societies etc. at Subsidized Rate
question: Is an eligible PWC/ Khadi Society that has already received an incentive or subsidy under a different scheme before the introduction of this new scheme still eligible to receive benefits under the new scheme?
answer: Yes, an eligible PWC/Khadi Society etc. which has availed of incentive/subsidy under any other scheme prior to the introduction of this scheme shall be eligible to get the benefits under this scheme.

scheme_name: West Bengal Handloom and Khadi Weavers Financial Benefit Scheme 2024: Supply of Yarn to Societies etc. at Subsidized Rate
question: What is the definition of “Societies”?
answer: "Societies" means and includes PWCS, Handloom Clusters, JLG groups, Handloom Groups.

scheme_name: West Bengal Handloom and Khadi Weavers Financial Benefit Scheme 2024: Supply of Yarn to Societies etc. at Subsidized Rate

scheme_name: West Bengal Handloom and Khadi Weavers Financial Benefit Scheme 2024: Supply of Yarn to Societies etc. at Subsidized Rate

scheme_name: West Bengal Handloom and Khadi Weavers Financial Benefit Scheme 2024: Supply of Yarn to Societies etc. at Subsidized Rate

scheme_name: West Bengal Handloom and Khadi Weavers Financial Benefit Scheme 2024: Supply of Yarn to Societies etc. at Subsidized Rate

scheme_name: West Bengal Handloom and Khadi Weavers Financial Benefit Scheme 2024: Supply of Yarn to Societies etc. at Subsidized Rate
question: How can the benefits be availed?
answer: An eligible PWCs/ Khadi society/ Individual Weaver will apply either in online or in offline mode in the prescribed format (as would be notified by this department) before the Director, Textiles.

scheme_name: West Bengal Handloom and Khadi Weavers Financial Benefit Scheme 2024: Supply of Yarn to Societies etc. at Subsidized Rate
question: What is the frequency of the assistance?
answer: The assistance will be provided one time to the beneficiaries.

scheme_name: Tholkappiar Award
question: Who is eligible to apply for the Tolkappyar Prize?
answer: Applicants must be born in Puducherry, have resided in Puducherry for five years, or have continuous residence within the jurisdiction before the application date.

scheme_name: Tholkappiar Award
question: Can an author apply for the Tolkappyar Prize more than once?
answer: No, an awardee under this scheme is ineligible to apply for the subsequent four years.

scheme_name: Tholkappiar Award
question: Are there any restrictions on the types of texts that can be submitted for the competition?
answer: Yes, texts must not be an abridgement, adaptation, translation, or paraphrase of another text. Categories such as novels, short stories, poetry, drama, travelogue, and collection of essays are not eligible.

scheme_name: Tholkappiar Award
question: What is the minimum page requirement for research books applying for the Tolkappyar Prize?
answer: Research books must not be less than 150 pages.

scheme_name: Tholkappiar Award
question: When should the first edition of the text have been printed and published?
answer: The first edition must have been printed and published by December 31 of the year preceding the award year.

scheme_name: Tholkappiar Award
question: What must be included with each publication submission?
answer: A separate application form and five copies of the text must be included with each submission.

scheme_name: Tholkappiar Award
question: Will the submitted texts be returned to the applicants?
answer: No, the texts received for the competition cannot be returned for any reason.

scheme_name: Tholkappiar Award
question: What is the award for winning the Tolkappyar Prize?
answer: The author will receive [?]10,000 and a certificate.

scheme_name: Tholkappiar Award
question: Who selects the prize-winning books?
answer: A panel of experts nominated by the Government will scrutinize and select the prize-winning books.

scheme_name: Tholkappiar Award
question: Is there an age limit for applicants?
answer: No, there is no age limit for applicants.

scheme_name: Tholkappiar Award
question: Can more than one award be given in a given year?
answer: Yes, the Government has the power to provide more than one award if deemed necessary.

scheme_name: Tholkappiar Award
question: What happens if there are issues in the implementation of the scheme?
answer: The Government's decision regarding any issues in the implementation of the scheme is final and cannot be contested in court.

scheme_name: Tholkappiar Award
question: Can the rules of the Tolkappyar Prize be amended?
answer: Yes, the Government has full power to change, delete, or amend the rules relating to the award as necessary.

scheme_name: Technology Acquisition Assistance
question: Who can apply under this scheme?
answer: Micro or Small Enterprise in Rajasthan with a valid Udyam Registration Certificate.

scheme_name: Technology Acquisition Assistance
question: What type of technology/software is eligible?
answer: Technology/software directly related to production or manufacturing processes that lead to performance improvement.

scheme_name: Technology Acquisition Assistance
question: Is performance improvement mandatory?
answer: Yes. Improvement in production rate, cycle time, rejection rate, or waste generation must be demonstrated and certified.

scheme_name: Technology Acquisition Assistance
question: Can I apply before acquiring the technology?
answer: No. Application is submitted after acquisition and deployment of the technology/software.

scheme_name: Technology Acquisition Assistance
question: How many machines/software can I claim assistance for?
answer: Only one machine/software of a similar nature is allowed for assistance.

scheme_name: Technology Acquisition Assistance
question: What’s the maximum financial assistance?
answer: Up to ₹5,00,000, subject to 50% of the technology/software acquisition cost.

scheme_name: Technology Acquisition Assistance
question: Who certifies the performance improvement?
answer: A Chartered Engineer, using data from 3 months before and after deployment.

scheme_name: Technology Acquisition Assistance
question: Who approves the application?
answer: The District Level Task Force Committee (DLTFC) is the approving authority.

scheme_name: Technology Acquisition Assistance
question: Where do I submit my application?
answer: Submit to the General Manager, DICC of your district with all required documents.

scheme_name: Technology Acquisition Assistance
question: How is the assistance disbursed?
answer: After approval, the amount is directly transferred to the enterprise’s registered bank account.

scheme_name: Training Assistance for Competitive Examinations
question: Which competitive exams are covered under this scheme?
answer: This scheme covers competitive exams conducted by UPSC, GPSC (Class-1, Class-2, and Class-3), Bank recruitment exams, the UPSC Subordinate Services Selection Board, and other similar government recruitment examinations.

scheme_name: Training Assistance for Competitive Examinations
question: What is the required eligibility criteria?
answer: To be eligible for this scheme, the applicant must have passed the 12th standard with a minimum of 60% marks.

scheme_name: Training Assistance for Competitive Examinations
question: What is the maximum annual family income allowed to apply for this scheme?
answer: The annual family income of the applicant should not exceed [?]4,50,000/- in order to be eligible for this scheme.

scheme_name: Training Assistance for Competitive Examinations
question: How much financial assistance is provided for competitive exam training?
answer: Under this scheme, eligible students will receive financial assistance of [?]20,000.

scheme_name: Training Assistance for Competitive Examinations
question: What is the minimum age requirement for an institution to be eligible under this scheme?
answer: The institution where the student is receiving training must be at least 3 years old to qualify under this scheme.

scheme_name: Training Assistance for Competitive Examinations
question: Is it mandatory for the coaching class to be registered to be eligible for the scheme?
answer: Yes, it is mandatory for the coaching class to be registered. It should have a valid Registration Number, GST Number, or CIN Number.

scheme_name: Training Assistance for Competitive Examinations
question: If a student resides in one district but is studying in another district, will they still be eligible for financial assistance under this scheme?
answer: Yes, if a student resides in one district but is pursuing coaching in another district, they are still eligible to receive financial assistance under this scheme.

scheme_name: Training Assistance for Competitive Examinations
question: If a student selects a coaching class of their own preference, will they still be eligible for the financial assistance?
answer: Yes, a student can choose a coaching class of their preference, provided it is a recognized institution, and they will still be eligible for the financial assistance.

scheme_name: Training Assistance for Competitive Examinations
question: Who is authorized to issue the income certificate for this scheme?
answer: The income certificate required for this scheme can be issued by the Taluka Development Officer (T.D.O), Mamlatdar, or Chief Officer.

scheme_name: Training Assistance for Competitive Examinations
question: Who is authorized to issue the non-reserved category certificate?
answer: The non-reserved category certificate can be obtained from the Taluka Development Officer (T.D.O), Mamlatdar, District Social Welfare Officer (Non-Reserved Category), or the Deputy Director (Non-Reserved Category).

scheme_name: Training Assistance for Competitive Examinations
question: What steps should be followed after submitting the online application for this scheme?
answer: After submitting the online application, the applicant must take a printout of the application form, sign it, and submit it along with all uploaded and self-attested documents (such as certificates and mark sheets). These documents must be sent to the Deputy Director (Non-Reserved Category) or the District Social Welfare Officer of the district where the applicant is studying. The documents can be submitted in person, through courier, or via post.

scheme_name: Training Assistance for Competitive Examinations
question: What happens if the hard copy of the application is not submitted after completing the online application process?
answer: If the applicant does not submit the hard copy of the application along with the required documents, their application will not be considered valid and will not be processed further.

scheme_name: Teachers Associateship for Research Excellence
question: I am having a DST funded Project as a Co-PI, can I apply for TARE scheme?
answer: Researchers being part of another project as Co-PIs, can apply.

scheme_name: Teachers Associateship for Research Excellence
question: In case of selection, is it mandatory to divide the funding and share 50% each to host and parent institutions? Can it be given to only host institution?
answer: Yes. A research fellowship of [?]60,000/- per year (in addition to the researcher's own salary) will be provided subject to completion of a minimum 90 days of research work per year in the host institution. Research grant of [?]5 lakhs per annum (50% each to host and parent institution) and overheads will be provided.

scheme_name: Teachers Associateship for Research Excellence
question: What kind of management responsibilities does the parent institution get?
answer: Parent institute must undertake all project implementation related work including purchase, preparation of UC/ES, relieving PI for research work in the host institute, etc. as of any other funded projects.

scheme_name: Teachers Associateship for Research Excellence
question: Clarification on the term "Research work", whether it refers to fresh research work only or ongoing research work without any external grant or fund?
answer: Fresh and ongoing research work not supported by any externally funded individual centric projects.

scheme_name: Teachers Associateship for Research Excellence
question: Can I choose Panjab University as Host institution for TARE because Panjab University is not a central university nor state university?
answer: Only central institutes / national research labs and Central Universities are eligible as host institute.

scheme_name: Teachers Associateship for Research Excellence
question: I want to understand the meaning of clause "The applicant(s) must hold a regular academic / research position in State Universities/ Colleges and private Academic Institution"?
answer: The term "Regular" in the context of SERB refers to the applicants who are appointed against the sanctioned post or in a tenure post but are likely to be renewed after the end of the tenure. | [Note: Research Associates, Ad-hoc faculties, Guest Faculty, Visiting Scientist, consultant, Project Fellows and Faculty members whose contract is renewed every year are not eligible] (In cases where it is not covered in any of the above, SERB has the right to determine the eligibility)

scheme_name: Teachers Associateship for Research Excellence
question: Working day: 90 days attendance should include host institute working days attendance only or 90 days working in host institute during institutes working days, summer vacation, winter vacation, public holidays, Saturdays and Sundays?
answer: 90 days working in host institute includes, working days, summer vacation, winter vacation, public holidays, Saturdays and Sundays, provided host institute allows to work and issue attendance certificate by the end of the year.

scheme_name: Teachers Associateship for Research Excellence
question: Is there any limit on how old institute is affiliated for Eg.10 year, 20 year or so?
answer: Age of the institute will not be considered, as long as it is affiliated by UGC / AICTE / MCI or other competent organizations of Government of India / State Governments.

scheme_name: Teachers Associateship for Research Excellence
question: What is the maximum distance between parent and host institute?
answer: Distance is not fixed, you need to justify the reasons for selection of institute whatso ever the distance, which will be evaluated by the committee. PI are advised to find the expertise/mentor nearer to their parent institute. Preference may be given to the candidates proposing host institute nearer to parent institute.

scheme_name: Teachers Associateship for Research Excellence
question: How many candidates can a mentor can guide?
answer: A mentor can forward any number of applications, but only one candidate will be allowed to work with a mentor depending up on the merit of the proposal.

scheme_name: Teachers Associateship for Research Excellence
question: How many applications can an institute forward?
answer: There are no fixed numbers.

scheme_name: Teachers Associateship for Research Excellence
question: Is the mentor and applicant subject areas should match exactly?
answer: The basic concept of this project itself is to execute the project in collaborative mode where the expertise of the mentor should be useful in executing the project work of the applicant. Accordingly, the expertise of mentor and applicant should fulfil the requirements of the proposed project work.

scheme_name: Teachers Associateship for Research Excellence
question: Can I get age relaxation, over and above the relaxation given in the program for filing the application?
answer: The upper age limit for the award is 45 years at the time of the submission of application. Age relaxation of 5 (five) years will be given to candidates belonging to SC/ST/OBC/Physically Challenged & Women candidates.

scheme_name: Teachers Associateship for Research Excellence
question: Is 90 days attendance compulsory requirement to get the fellowship money sanctioned? Can project be granted without the fellowship component?
answer: The basic concept of this project itself is to execute the project in collaborative mode where the applicant should work with the mentor and get trained at higher level. For which the minimum attendance period of 90 days is mandatory and hence the proposals without fellowship component will not be considered.

scheme_name: Teachers Associateship for Research Excellence
question: If the applicant goes to the host institution less than 90 days/year and does not get the scholarship money of ₹60,000/year whether he/she will be eligible to get the project money?
answer: It is mandatory to full fill the minimum 90 days research work per year in the host institution.

scheme_name: Teachers Associateship for Research Excellence
question: I have completed my M.Tech. and continuing my Ph.D. Can I apply for TARE project?
answer: No as per revised eligibility guidelines, only candidates holding Ph.D. degree in Science / Engineering or MS / MD in Medicine are eligible to apply.

scheme_name: Teachers Associateship for Research Excellence
question: Can my Ph.D. supervisor be a mentor for TARE project?
answer: No, however candidates are allowed to work with a different mentor from the same institute where a Ph.D. degree was awarded.

scheme_name: Teachers Associateship for Research Excellence
question: Is only researcher having ongoing project with DST / SERB not eligible for apply or any ongoing projects?
answer: Researchers having any funded projects are not eligible to apply.

scheme_name: Teachers Associateship for Research Excellence
question: Can I apply from any other Central institutes other than mentioned in the TARE scheme? Eg.Centre for Materials for Electronics Technology (C-MET), Ministry of Electronics & Information Technology?
answer: You can apply for any Central institutions having relevant R&D infrastructure.

scheme_name: Teachers Associateship for Research Excellence
question: Whether applications from the regions where very limited Central institutes are available will be given with privilege or not?
answer: Selection for TARE scheme will be purely competitive mode based on the scientific merit of the proposal.

scheme_name: Teachers Associateship for Research Excellence
question: Any clauses that bound for publication of research work findings in conferences / journals?
answer: No, but PI are expected to bring out joint publications with the mentor from the results emanated out of this project and is mandatory to acknowledge SERB funding for the research work.

scheme_name: Teachers Associateship for Research Excellence
question: Can I use the money to hire a project fellow? Can the fellow be paid 50/50 by both institutions?
answer: No, the TARE awardee is expected to do research on his / her own.

scheme_name: Teachers Associateship for Research Excellence
question: If I succeed in getting the TARE grant, can I apply for, say, an extramural grant later?
answer: Applicant should not hold any ongoing research projects or any fellowship at the time of submission of application. You are not eligible to avail of any other project from DST/SERB until you complete the TARE project.

scheme_name: Tablet Assistance to Scheduled Caste Students of 12th Standard
question: Who administers the scheme?
answer: The scheme is administered by the Director, Scheduled Caste Welfare, Government of Gujarat.

scheme_name: Tablet Assistance to Scheduled Caste Students of 12th Standard
question: What are the benefits offered under the scheme?
answer: Students in the 12th standard belonging to the Scheduled Caste category will receive a tablet by paying a token fee of [?]1,000/-.

scheme_name: Tablet Assistance to Scheduled Caste Students of 12th Standard
question: What are the eligibility criteria for students to avail of the tablet assistance?
answer: The student must belong to the Scheduled Caste of Gujarat and be studying in the 12th standard.

scheme_name: Tablet Assistance to Scheduled Caste Students of 12th Standard
question: Is there any income limit for eligibility?
answer: No, there is no income limit specified for eligibility under this scheme.

scheme_name: Tablet Assistance to Scheduled Caste Students of 12th Standard
question: How can eligible students apply for the scheme?
answer: Eligible students can apply for the scheme through the Digital Gujarat Portal: https://www.digitalgujarat.gov.in/.

scheme_name: Tablet Assistance to Scheduled Caste Students of 12th Standard
question: Can students from other states apply for this scheme?

scheme_name: Tool Assistance Scheme for Pottery Artisans

scheme_name: Tirth Barat Yojana

They must also be physically and mentally capable of traveling and not suffer from infectious diseases.

scheme_name: Tirth Barat Yojana

answer: Beneficiaries can visit one or more of the designated pilgrimage sites outside the state once in their lifetime.

scheme_name: Tirth Barat Yojana

answer: No, only one assistant is allowed per elderly pilgrim or group.

answer: Beneficiaries can avail of the pilgrimage assistance only once in their lifetime.

scheme_name: Tiatr Competition

scheme_name: Trekking in Coastal Area for Scheduled Caste

question: What is the age limit specified under the “Trekking in Coastal Area for Scheduled Caste” scheme?

scheme_name: Trekking in Coastal Area for Scheduled Caste
question: Is there any income-based eligibility condition for availing the benefits of the scheme?

scheme_name: Trekking in Coastal Area for Scheduled Caste

scheme_name: Trekking in Coastal Area for Scheduled Caste

scheme_name: Trekking in Coastal Area for Scheduled Caste

scheme_name: Trekking in Coastal Area for Scheduled Caste

scheme_name: Trekking in Coastal Area for Scheduled Caste

scheme_name: Tribals Development Plan: Motor Driving Training [Light & Heavy Vehicles]
question: How many total beneficiaries are specifically aimed to be provided with assistance for Heavy Motor Vehicle driver instruction within a single complete financial reporting period?
answer: It is targeted that 200 persons will receive assistance specifically for Heavy Motor Vehicle training in one financial year.

scheme_name: Tribals Development Plan: Motor Driving Training [Light & Heavy Vehicles]
question: What is the overarching goal that this specific training component is intended to achieve regarding the economic condition of the recipient community?
answer: The primary objective is the economic upliftment of the tribes by creating opportunities in the transport sector, recognizing the State of Goa's bright future in that field.

scheme_name: Tribals Development Plan: Motor Driving Training [Light & Heavy Vehicles]
question: To apply for this support, is it mandatory that I belong to one of the Tribal families officially residing and domiciled within the State of Goa?
answer: Yes, the assistance is targeted exclusively toward all Tribal families who are bona fide residents of the State of Goa.

scheme_name: Tribals Development Plan: Motor Driving Training [Light & Heavy Vehicles]
question: Can I receive financial assistance to cover the expenses for obtaining a license for both smaller, lighter personal vehicles as well as larger, heavy transport vehicles?
answer: Yes, the training assistance is specifically provided for driving instruction programs covering both Light Motor Vehicles (LMV) and Heavy Motor Vehicles (HMV).

scheme_name: Tribals Development Plan: Motor Driving Training [Light & Heavy Vehicles]
question: What is the total estimated count of individuals who are intended to receive assistance for all types of motor driving training courses combined during a financial year?
answer: A total of 400 persons are targeted to receive this training assistance, which includes 200 persons for Light Motor Vehicles and 200 for Heavy Motor Vehicles.

scheme_name: Tribals Development Plan: Motor Driving Training [Light & Heavy Vehicles]
question: How much of the total expense required to complete the necessary motor driving instruction program is financially covered or compensated by the Government?
answer: The Government provides the cost of the entire training program, ensuring 100% financial coverage for the required instruction.

scheme_name: Tribals Development Plan: Motor Driving Training [Light & Heavy Vehicles]
question: Could you please specify which Government directorate or agency is primarily responsible for the introduction, execution, and management of this specific development plan?
answer: This development plan, which includes the driving training, is managed and implemented by the Directorate of Social Welfare, under the Government of Goa.

scheme_name: Tribals Development Plan: Motor Driving Training [Light & Heavy Vehicles]
question: What is the exact monetary amount proposed by the Government as the financial outlay per individual recipient for covering the cost of Light Motor Vehicle training?
answer: The proposed financial outlay for assistance covering the training cost for a Light Motor Vehicle is ₹3,000/- per beneficiary.

scheme_name: Tribals Development Plan: Purchase of Tourist Taxi
question: What kind of assistance is available for a tribal family that wants to start a livelihood in the transport or tourism sector?
answer: Eligible Scheduled Tribe families can receive a subsidy to purchase a tourist taxi for self-employment in the transport and tourism sector.

scheme_name: Tribals Development Plan: Purchase of Tourist Taxi
question: If my family is registered as Below Poverty Line (BPL), what financial help can we receive under this component?
answer: BPL families receive a total subsidy of ₹25,000/-. ₹10,000/- from the District Rural Development Agency (DRDA) under the Swarnajayanti Gram Swarozgar Yojana and ₹15,000/- from the Directorate of Social Welfare.

scheme_name: Tribals Development Plan: Purchase of Tourist Taxi
question: If my family is not part of the BPL list but our income is below ₹1,20,000/- per year, can we still apply?
answer: Yes, families not included in the BPL list but with annual income below ₹1,20,000/- are eligible for a subsidy of ₹15,000/- from the Directorate of Social Welfare.

scheme_name: Tribals Development Plan: Purchase of Tourist Taxi
question: How many tribal families are expected to benefit from this tourist taxi subsidy each year?
answer: Every financial year, approximately 50 tribal households are targeted for assistance under this component.

scheme_name: Tribals Development Plan: Purchase of Tourist Taxi
question: Is the subsidy provided more than once if we plan to buy a second vehicle later?
answer: No, the subsidy is a one-time financial assistance that can be availed only once per eligible household.

scheme_name: Tribals Development Plan: Purchase of Tourist Taxi
question: What is the main purpose of introducing this subsidy for tourist taxi purchase?
answer: The objective is to promote economic self-reliance and provide sustainable employment opportunities to Scheduled Tribe families through tourism-linked transport activities.

scheme_name: Tribals Development Plan: Purchase of Tourist Taxi
question: Are there any specific tribal communities eligible for this subsidy in Goa?
answer: Yes, only applicants belonging to the Gawda, Velip, or Kunbi communities, which are recognised as Scheduled Tribes in Goa, are eligible.

scheme_name: Tribals Development Plan: Purchase of Tourist Taxi
question: What should be the applicant’s income to qualify for this assistance?
answer: The total annual family income of the applicant must be below ₹1,20,000/-.

scheme_name: Tribals Development Plan: Purchase of Tourist Taxi
question: Is it necessary to have a driving licence before applying for the tourist taxi subsidy?
answer: Yes, the applicant must possess or apply for a valid Light Motor Vehicle (LMV) driving licence before receiving the subsidy.

scheme_name: Tribals Development Plan: Purchase of Tourist Taxi
question: Where should an applicant submit the form for this benefit?
answer: The completed application form must be submitted at the office of the Block Development Officer (BDO) or the District Welfare Office under the Directorate of Social Welfare.

scheme_name: Tribals Development Plan: Purchase of Tourist Taxi
question: Can the purchased taxi be used for private or personal purposes?
answer: No, the tourist taxi purchased through this subsidy must be used exclusively for self-employment and livelihood purposes in the tourism or transport sector.

scheme_name: Tribals Development Plan: Purchase of Tourist Taxi
question: What happens if the taxi is sold or transferred soon after receiving the subsidy?
answer: If the vehicle is misused, transferred, or not used for livelihood purposes, the subsidy may be withdrawn or recalled by the Department.

scheme_name: Tribals Development Plan: Purchase of Tourist Taxi
question: How will the subsidy amount be received by the beneficiary?
answer: The Directorate of Social Welfare releases the sanctioned subsidy amount directly into the beneficiary’s registered bank account after verification.

scheme_name: Tribals Development Plan: Purchase of Tourist Taxi
question: What are the key documents needed while applying for this assistance?
answer: Applicants need to submit caste, income, and residence certificates, proof of BPL status (if applicable), a copy of the driving licence, and an identity proof such as Aadhaar Card.

scheme_name: Tribals Development Plan: Subsidy for Purchase of Motorcycle
question: Many tribal families in Goa depend on daily transport services for their livelihood. What type of assistance does the Government provide to them?
answer: Eligible Scheduled Tribe households can receive a one-time financial subsidy for purchasing a motorcycle, enabling them to use it for self-employment and income generation.

scheme_name: Tribals Development Plan: Subsidy for Purchase of Motorcycle
question: If a family’s annual income is below ₹1,20,000/- but not listed as Below Poverty Line, can they still receive assistance?
answer: Yes. Non-BPL tribal families with an annual income below ₹1,20,000/- are entitled to a ₹15,000/- subsidy from the Directorate of Social Welfare.

scheme_name: Tribals Development Plan: Subsidy for Purchase of Motorcycle
question: How much total subsidy can a Below Poverty Line (BPL) tribal household receive for purchasing a motorcycle?
answer: BPL tribal households can receive a total subsidy of ₹25,000/-, comprising ₹10,000/- from the District Rural Development Agency (DRDA) under the Swarnajayanti Gram Swarozgar Yojana and ₹15,000/- from the Directorate of Social Welfare.

scheme_name: Tribals Development Plan: Subsidy for Purchase of Motorcycle
question: Does this assistance cover the entire cost of the motorcycle or only a part of it?
answer: The scheme provides partial financial support in the form of a subsidy; the remaining amount must be borne by the beneficiary.

scheme_name: Tribals Development Plan: Subsidy for Purchase of Motorcycle
question: Can members of the same family apply separately to receive multiple subsidies for motorcycles?
answer: No. Only one member per eligible tribal household can avail of this assistance.

scheme_name: Tribals Development Plan: Subsidy for Purchase of Motorcycle
question: What is the purpose of providing a motorcycle subsidy under this scheme?
answer: The subsidy aims to help tribal beneficiaries start transport-based self-employment activities such as pilot or courier services, thereby promoting economic independence.

scheme_name: Tribals Development Plan: Subsidy for Purchase of Motorcycle
question: Which Government office should an applicant approach to apply for this benefit?
answer: Applicants must approach either the Directorate of Social Welfare, Government of Goa, or their respective District Rural Development Agency (DRDA) office to obtain and submit the prescribed form.

scheme_name: Tribals Development Plan: Subsidy for Purchase of Motorcycle
question: Are there any specific tribal communities that are eligible to apply?
answer: Yes. Only members belonging to the Gawda, Velip, or Kunbi tribal communities are eligible to apply.

scheme_name: Tribals Development Plan: Subsidy for Purchase of Motorcycle
question: Is there a particular mode of payment through which the subsidy is released to beneficiaries?
answer: The approved subsidy amount is released directly to the beneficiary’s bank account by the Directorate of Social Welfare.

scheme_name: Tribals Development Plan: Subsidy for Purchase of Motorcycle
question: What supporting documents should be enclosed while applying for this assistance?
answer: Applicants must attach their Caste Certificate, Income Certificate, Residence Proof, BPL Card (if applicable), and identity proof along with the application form.

scheme_name: Tribals Development Plan: Subsidy for Purchase of Motorcycle
question: What happens if a beneficiary uses the motorcycle for purposes other than self-employment?
answer: If the vehicle is misused or not employed for livelihood activities, the Government may recall or withdraw the benefit.

scheme_name: Tribals Development Plan: Subsidy for Purchase of Motorcycle
question: How many applicants are targeted for assistance under this motorcycle subsidy each year?
answer: The scheme targets approximately 200 tribal beneficiaries annually for financial assistance.

scheme_name: Tribals Development Plan: Subsidy for Purchase of Motorcycle
question: What is the procedure after submitting the application form at the district office?
answer: The concerned office verifies the applicant’s eligibility, income, and caste details; thereafter, shortlisted beneficiaries are approved for subsidy disbursement.

scheme_name: Tribals Development Plan: Subsidy for Purchase of Motorcycle
question: Is the subsidy provided more than once if the beneficiary wishes to buy another motorcycle later?
answer: No. The assistance is strictly a one-time benefit provided only once to each eligible household.

scheme_name: Tribals Development Plan: Tea/Coffee And Coconut Parlor
question: Must an applicant belong to a specific recognized social group within the State of Goa to be considered eligible for this financial assistance project?
answer: Yes, the applicant must be a member of a Tribal family belonging specifically to the Gawdas, Velips, or Kunbis tribal groups, as notified by the Government of India.

scheme_name: Tribals Development Plan: Tea/Coffee And Coconut Parlor
question: What is the consequence if the beneficiary fails to deposit the required installments on time for three sequential months during the repayment period?
answer: If the beneficiary fails to deposit the amount or installments in time for three consecutive months, their right to ownership will be suspended until the entire amount is paid.

scheme_name: Tribals Development Plan: Tea/Coffee And Coconut Parlor
question: Does the applicant need to be residing in a particular state or region to be considered for participation in this economic upliftment plan?
answer: The applicant must be a member of a Tribal family staying in the State of Goa.

scheme_name: Tribals Development Plan: Tea/Coffee And Coconut Parlor
question: What is the expected or estimated cost range associated with starting one of these modernized Tea/Coffee and Coconut Parlor projects?
answer: The estimated cost required for establishing this project is between ₹25,000/- and ₹30,000/-.

scheme_name: Tribals Development Plan: Tea/Coffee And Coconut Parlor
question: How many total payments or monthly intervals are allowed for the beneficiary to complete the required financial deposit toward the project cost?
answer: The required 50% deposit amount toward the total project cost must be paid by the beneficiary in 36 installments.

scheme_name: Tribals Development Plan: Tea/Coffee And Coconut Parlor
question: If a beneficiary diligently fulfills all the mandatory obligations regarding the timely deposition of the required amount, what incentive do they receive?
answer: The beneficiary who successfully deposits the aforesaid 50% amount will be rewarded with the entire amount deposited by them.

scheme_name: Tribals Development Plan: Tea/Coffee And Coconut Parlor
question: Under what specific condition will the amount that has already been repaid by the beneficiary towards the project cost be permanently taken by the Government?
answer: If the beneficiary fails to repay the total outstanding amount for a period of six months, the deposited amount will be forfeited in favor of the Government.

scheme_name: Tribals Development Plan: Tea/Coffee And Coconut Parlor
question: Is there a mandatory financial requirement regarding the annual income ceiling for a family to apply for the benefits provided under this self-employment initiative?
answer: Yes, the applicant must belong to a family whose income is less than ₹1,20,000/- per annum.

scheme_name: Tribals Development Plan: Tea/Coffee And Coconut Parlor
question: If an application is successfully approved, will the financial support provided cover the entire amount needed to establish the proposed new parlor business?
answer: Yes, the financial support provides the entire project financing under the scheme to assist the beneficiary in establishing the parlor.

scheme_name: Tribals Development Plan: Tea/Coffee And Coconut Parlor
question: If a beneficiary manages to make timely payments but accumulates too many missed payments over time, how many total defaults lead to suspension?
answer: If the beneficiary defaults for more than 3 times on making the timely deposit of the required amount, their right to ownership will be suspended.

scheme_name: Tribals Development Plan: Tea/Coffee And Coconut Parlor
question: To maintain the viability and sustainability of the project, what specific portion of the total project cost is the successful applicant required to deposit?
answer: The beneficiary is required to deposit 50% of the total project cost to the Department.

scheme_name: Tribals Development Plan: Tea/Coffee And Coconut Parlor
question: Besides the maximum annual income limit, are there any other required conditions related to the family's financial standing that must be satisfied during the application process?
answer: The applicant must belong to a family that is either enrolled in the Below Poverty Line list or whose annual income is less than ₹1,20,000/-.

scheme_name: Tribals Development Plan: Tea/Coffee And Coconut Parlor
question: If the beneficiary's right to ownership is temporarily suspended due to missed payments, what action is necessary to restore full ownership rights?
answer: The suspension of ownership rights, resulting from failing to deposit amounts in time, will remain in effect until the entire outstanding amount is paid by the beneficiary.

scheme_name: Tea Development Programme in the Hilly Districts of Uttarakhand - Uttarakhand Tea Development Board
question: Who is eligible to apply under this programme?
answer: Applicants must be permanent residents of Uttarakhand and should possess their own measured land suitable for tea cultivation.

scheme_name: Tea Development Programme in the Hilly Districts of Uttarakhand - Uttarakhand Tea Development Board
question: What land conditions are required for tea plantation?
answer: Within a radius of 20 km of the identified area, at least 60 hectares of land should be available for tea plantation, with adequate water supply for establishing nurseries at the initial stage.

scheme_name: Tea Development Programme in the Hilly Districts of Uttarakhand - Uttarakhand Tea Development Board
question: How can a farmer apply for the tea plantation programme?
answer: The cultivator can apply to the Director, Uttarakhand Tea Development Board, Almora, providing details about the availability and measurement of their land.

scheme_name: Tea Development Programme in the Hilly Districts of Uttarakhand - Uttarakhand Tea Development Board
question: What are the benefits of tea cultivation in Uttarakhand’s hilly terrain?
answer: Tea plants thrive in the region’s climate, need minimal irrigation, resist damage by wild animals, and help prevent soil erosion and landslides.

scheme_name: Tea Development Programme in the Hilly Districts of Uttarakhand - Uttarakhand Tea Development Board
question: What is the process followed after the application submission?
answer: After receiving the application, the Board conducts a soil test of the applicant’s land. If suitable, a work plan is prepared and sent to the district administration or government for approval.

scheme_name: Tea Development Programme in the Hilly Districts of Uttarakhand - Uttarakhand Tea Development Board
question: Who approves the tea plantation projects?
answer: The prepared work plans are reviewed and approved by the district administration/government before the plantation work begins.

scheme_name: Tea Development Programme in the Hilly Districts of Uttarakhand - Uttarakhand Tea Development Board
question: Can barren land be used for tea cultivation?
answer: Yes. Apart from agricultural land, barren and unused lands can also be utilized for tea plantation under the programme.

scheme_name: Tea Development Programme in the Hilly Districts of Uttarakhand - Uttarakhand Tea Development Board
question: How much area has been developed under tea cultivation so far?
answer: The Board has developed tea gardens on 1,370 hectares of land leased from 4,011 farmers across 30 development blocks in 9 districts.

scheme_name: Tea Development and Promotion Scheme (TDPS): Plantation Development for Small Tea Growers (PDSTG): Mechanization for Individual Small Growers
question: Is there any limitation on the number of applications a single applicant can submit for each scheme component?
answer: Yes, the scheme specifies that only one application under each component will be considered. However, applicants may apply for more than one activity in a single application, depending on their eligibility.

scheme_name: Tea Development and Promotion Scheme (TDPS): Plantation Development for Small Tea Growers (PDSTG): Mechanization for Individual Small Growers
question: Are there any specific fees associated with the application process, and are there exemptions for certain categories of applicants?
answer: Yes, an application fee of Rs. 100/- (plus GST) is applicable for all applicants, except for those in the SC, ST, female, and differently-abled categories. These exempted stakeholders do not need to pay the application fee.

scheme_name: Tea Development and Promotion Scheme (TDPS): Plantation Development for Small Tea Growers (PDSTG): Mechanization for Individual Small Growers
question: What are the two application modes available for this scheme, and under what circumstances is physical submission of applications accepted?
answer: The two application modes are offline and online. Initially, the scheme allows for physical submission of applications at field offices (ZO/ROs/SROs/HQ) if the online platform is not yet ready for use. The Competent Authority may accept physical submissions until the online platform becomes operational.

scheme_name: Tea Development and Promotion Scheme (TDPS): Plantation Development for Small Tea Growers (PDSTG): Mechanization for Individual Small Growers
question: Could you explain the mode of payment for the scheme's subsidies? What electronic payment methods are employed?
answer: All subsidy payments under the scheme are made through electronic modes, which include RTGS (Real-Time Gross Settlement), NEFT (National Electronic Funds Transfer), and PFMS (Public Financial Management System).

scheme_name: Tea Development and Promotion Scheme (TDPS): Plantation Development for Small Tea Growers (PDSTG): Mechanization for Individual Small Growers
question: What are the specific exclusions mentioned in the scheme, particularly regarding the ownership of tea gardens?
answer: Exclusions are in place to prevent misuse. In the event of a change in ownership of a tea garden before the completion of the subsidy disbursement, the previous owner will cease to receive any further subsidy payments after the transfer or sale is completed.

scheme_name: Tea Development and Promotion Scheme (TDPS): Plantation Development for Small Tea Growers (PDSTG): Mechanization for Individual Small Growers
question: How does the scheme define the eligibility criteria for applicants, particularly small tea growers, including members of self-help groups and Farmers' Producer Organizations?
answer: Eligible applicants include small tea growers who are members of self-help groups or Farmers' Producer Organizations, provided they have Tea Board registration or an identity smart card issued by the Tea Board. The identity card serves as a unique identification number for eligibility verification.

scheme_name: Tea Development and Promotion Scheme (TDPS): Plantation Development for Small Tea Growers (PDSTG): Mechanization for Individual Small Growers
question: What are the ceiling limits and eligibility criteria for small tea growers to obtain equipment like the Pruning Machine and Mechanical Harvester under the PDSTG component?
answer: Small tea growers are eligible for equipment under the PDSTG component. The ceiling limit for a Pruning Machine is [?]30,000, and one machine is allowed for each or up to 5.00 hectares of tea area. For the Mechanical Harvester, the ceiling limit is [?]25,000 for a Single Man Harvester and [?]40,000 for a Double Man Harvester. Eligibility for the Mechanical Harvester is for each or up to 10.00 hectares of tea area.

scheme_name: Tea Development and Promotion Scheme (TDPS): Plantation Development for Small Tea Growers (PDSTG): Mechanization for Individual Small Growers
question: Could you elaborate on the specific components of the TDPS and how they contribute to the Indian tea industry's growth and sustainability?
answer: He TDPS comprises seven major components, each serving distinct purposes within the Indian tea industry. These components are designed to protect, grow, and sustain the industry. One such component is "Plantation Development for Small Tea Growers (PDSTG)," which aims to boost the production and quality of tea and help small growers move up the value chain. Sustainability is addressed through the promotion of organic and climate-resilient tea. Another component focuses on the mechanization for individual small growers.

scheme_name: Tea Development and Promotion Scheme (TDPS): Plantation Development for Small Tea Growers (PDSTG): Mechanization for Individual Small Growers
question: Could you explain what "Self-declaration under PPC compliance" entails and why it's a part of the required documents?
answer: Self-declaration under PPC compliance refers to an assurance by the applicant that they are compliant with all relevant laws and regulations, particularly those related to the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act. It serves as a declaration of adherence to food safety standards in tea production.

scheme_name: Tea Development and Promotion Scheme (TDPS): Plantation Development for Small Tea Growers (PDSTG): Mechanization for Individual Small Growers
question: Are there any specific requirements for the survey map of the tea area, particularly in terms of who can certify it and how it should be prepared?
answer: The scheme requires a survey map of the tea area, preferably A-4 size, to be drawn by a government-approved surveyor or the Land Revenue department. The map should be duly certified and signed by both the issuing authority and the applicant, where applicable. This ensures the accuracy and authenticity of the map.

scheme_name: Tea Development and Promotion Scheme (TDPS): Plantation Development for Small Tea Growers (PDSTG): Mechanization for Individual Small Growers
question: How does the scheme define the concept of "organic tea cultivation" in the context of the PDSTG component, and what practices are encouraged?
answer: Organic tea cultivation refers to the cultivation of tea without the use of synthetic chemicals or pesticides. The PDSTG component encourages practices such as using organic fertilizers, practicing integrated pest management, and promoting sustainability in tea cultivation to ensure the tea is free from harmful chemicals.

scheme_name: Tea Development and Promotion Scheme (TDPS): Plantation Development for Small Tea Growers (PDSTG): Mechanization for Individual Small Growers
question: Could you explain the significance of mechanization for individual small tea growers within the PDSTG component? How does it benefit these growers?
answer: Mechanization is a critical aspect of the PDSTG component. It provides small tea growers with equipment like pruning machines, mechanical harvesters, power sprayers, brush cutters, and plucking shears. These tools significantly improve efficiency, reduce labor costs, and enhance tea quality, making the entire tea cultivation process more sustainable and profitable.

scheme_name: Tea Development and Promotion Scheme (TDPS): Plantation Development for Small Tea Growers (PDSTG): Mechanization for Individual Small Growers
question: Can you provide insights into the objectives of the "Plantation Development for Small Tea Growers (PDSTG)" component and how it contributes to the growth of small tea growers?
answer: The PDSTG component aims to enhance the production, productivity, and quality of tea among small tea growers. It promotes their overall development, encourages organic tea cultivation and climate-resilient tea, and assists in setting up their own processing units. This empowers small growers and helps them move up the value chain.

scheme_name: Tea Development Scheme

answer: - To carry out experimental plantation of tea for the possibility of finding ways to grow tea economically and in a commercial scale as well. | - Raising seedlings in the experimental station for distribution to farmers. | - Encouraging Organic Certification on a cluster-based approach. | - Training and capacity building to Tea growers.

scheme_name: Tea Development Scheme

scheme_name: Tea Development Scheme

scheme_name: Tea Development Scheme

answer: - District Horticulture Officer | - Horticulture Development Officer

scheme_name: Technology Development And Utilization Programme For Women
question: What Is The Full Name Of The TDUPW Scheme?
answer: The full name of the TDUPW Scheme is "Technology Development & Utilization Programme for Women".

scheme_name: Technology Development And Utilization Programme For Women
question: For What Kinds Of Projects Is The Assistance Provided?
answer: In this scheme, DSIR provides assistance for those projects which are relevant to technology development and utilization by women.

scheme_name: Technology Development And Utilization Programme For Women
question: What Objectives Does This Scheme Have?
answer: This scheme has the following objectives - | - Promoting the adoption of new technologies by women. | - Awareness creation and training of women on technology-related issues with regard to women. | - Promoting Technological upgradation of tiny, small and medium enterprises run by women entrepreneurs. | - Showcasing appropriate technologies and organizing demonstration programmes for the benefit of women. | - Design and development of products, and processes beneficial to women.

scheme_name: Technology Development And Utilization Programme For Women
question: What Shall Be The Duration Of The Project? Is The Duration Fixed?
answer: The project should be time-bound, depending upon the nature of the project. Normally a duration of less than 2 years is preferred.

scheme_name: Technology Development And Utilization Programme For Women
question: Will The Financial Assistance Be Provided As A Lump Sum Or In Installments?
answer: The assistance can be by way of financial support (partial or full) and technical guidance.

scheme_name: Technology Development And Utilization Programme For Women
question: Will The Assistance Also Be Provided For Travel Outside The Country?
answer: No, the financial assistance will be provided only for meeting expenditures on Manpower, Consumables, travel within the country and other miscellaneous expenditures.

scheme_name: Technology Development And Utilization Programme For Women
question: Will The Assistance Also Be Provided For Basic Infrastructure?
answer: No support will be provided for basic infrastructure and buildings.

scheme_name: Technology Development And Utilization Programme For Women
question: On What Factors Will The Time And Amount Of Assistance Depend?
answer: The assistance will be released in instalments and will be linked to specific milestones achieved as per the time schedule indicated in the proposal. The release would also be dependent on the completion of formalities like submission of progress reports and Utilization Certificates.

scheme_name: Technology Development And Utilization Programme For Women
question: Where Can I Find The URL Of The User Manual Of The Application Process?

question: Are The Case Studies On Successful R&D, Technology Development And Businesswomen Eligible For Assistance In This Scheme?

scheme_name: TEC Internship Scheme
question: Can I Apply For The Internship If I Have Completed A Master's Degree?
answer: Yes, candidates who have completed a Post Graduate/Master Degree course in relevant disciplines within the last one year with a minimum of 60% marks are eligible to apply.

scheme_name: TEC Internship Scheme
question: Is There Any Chance Of Getting Hired After The Internship
answer: The internship is not a job guarantee, but exceptional interns may be considered for future opportunities based on their performance and TEC's requirements.

scheme_name: TEC Internship Scheme
question: Can Interns Present Their Work At Academic Events
answer: Yes, with prior permission from TEC, interns can present their work at academic bodies, seminars, and conferences.

scheme_name: TEC Internship Scheme
question: What Is The Selection Process For The Internship?
answer: After eligibility screening, shortlisted candidates will go through a selection committee process, which may include a personal or telephonic interview.

scheme_name: TEC Internship Scheme
question: How Will The Interns Be Supervised?
answer: Interns will be attached to officers in various TEC divisions, and their work will be monitored through periodic interactions.

scheme_name: TEC Internship Scheme
question: What Should Interns Do At The End Of The Internship?
answer: Interns must submit a report on their work to the respective division, signed by the concerned officer, to receive a completion certificate.

scheme_name: TEC Internship Scheme
question: Is Owning A Laptop Necessary For The Internship?
answer: Yes, interns are required to have their own laptops. However, TEC will provide necessary workspace and internet facilities.

scheme_name: TEC Internship Scheme
question: Can Interns Interact With The Media During The Internship?

scheme_name: Travel Grant Scheme For College Teachers / College Librarians / Vice Chancellors / Commission Members And UGC Officers

scheme_name: The Goa State Incentives to Encourage Investments Scheme

scheme_name: The Goa State Incentives to Encourage Investments Scheme

scheme_name: The Goa State Incentives to Encourage Investments Scheme

scheme_name: The Goa State Incentives to Encourage Investments Scheme

scheme_name: The Goa State Incentives to Encourage Investments Scheme

answer: The objective of the "Tution Sahay Yojana (Unreserved Category)" launched by the Government of Gujarat is to provide annual financial support to meritorious students belonging to the unreserved category who are studying in Class 11 and 12 in the science stream, so that they can continue their education without facing financial hardship in paying private tuition fees.

scheme_name: Tuition Sahay Yojana (Unreserved Category)

scheme_name: Tuition Sahay Yojana (Unreserved Category)

scheme_name: Tuition Sahay Yojana (Unreserved Category)

scheme_name: Union Home Minister’s Medal for Excellence in Police Training

scheme_name: Union Home Minister’s Medal for Excellence in Police Training

scheme_name: Union Home Minister’s Medal for Excellence in Police Training

scheme_name: Union Home Minister’s Medal for Excellence in Police Training

scheme_name: Union Home Minister’s Medal for Excellence in Police Training

scheme_name: Union Home Minister’s Medal for Excellence in Police Training

scheme_name: Union Home Minister’s Medal for Excellence in Police Training
question: If I have previously received a punishment, will my application be considered if the prescribed period of that punishment is still running?

scheme_name: Union Home Minister’s Medal for Excellence in Police Training

scheme_name: Union Home Minister’s Medal for Excellence in Police Training

scheme_name: Union Home Minister’s Medal for Excellence in Police Training

scheme_name: Union Home Minister’s Medal for Excellence in Police Training

scheme_name: Vasantrao Naik Merit Awards To The Vjnt Students Who Came First In State Or First In Board Of 10th And 12th Standard Examination
question: Can a student receive the Vasantrao Naik Merit Award more than once?

scheme_name: Vasantrao Naik Tanda / Basti Development Scheme
question: What is the purpose of the Vasantrao Naik Tanda/Basti Development Scheme?
answer: To provide basic infrastructure like drinking water, electrification, and sanitation to VJNT Tandas and Bastis.

scheme_name: Vasantrao Naik Tanda / Basti Development Scheme
question: Who is eligible to apply for this scheme?
answer: Tandas and Bastis of Vimukta Jatis and Nomadic Tribes with a minimum population of 50.

scheme_name: Vasantrao Naik Tanda / Basti Development Scheme
question: How is the scheme funded?
answer: The scheme is funded by the Government of Maharashtra.

scheme_name: Vasantrao Naik Tanda / Basti Development Scheme
question: What amenities are covered under this scheme?
answer: The scheme covers basic amenities such as drinking water, latrines, electrification, drainage, and approach roads.

scheme_name: Vasantrao Naik Tanda / Basti Development Scheme

scheme_name: Vasantrao Naik Tanda / Basti Development Scheme
question: Does the Gram Panchayat need to support the proposal?

scheme_name: Vasantrao Naik Tanda / Basti Development Scheme
question: What is the role of the Block Development Officer (B.D.O.)?

scheme_name: Vasantrao Naik Tanda / Basti Development Scheme

scheme_name: Vasantrao Naik Tanda / Basti Development Scheme

scheme_name: Vasantrao Naik Tanda / Basti Development Scheme
question: Is there any contribution required from the beneficiaries?

scheme_name: Visit to Old/Sick Artistes

answer: Yes, contributions made in both commercial and non-commercial tiatr, khell tiatr, or khell performances are considered valid.

scheme_name: Visit to Old/Sick Artistes
question: How many years of active contribution in tiatr performances are required for me to qualify under this scheme?
answer: You must have contributed at least 10 years in tiatr, khell tiatr, or khell to qualify.

scheme_name: Visit to Old/Sick Artistes
question: If I am primarily a writer or director rather than a stage performer, can I apply for support under this scheme?
answer: Yes, writers or directors who have staged at least 10 tiatr, khell tiatr, or khell productions are eligible.

scheme_name: Visit to Old/Sick Artistes
question: Does the minimum requirement of 10 years of contribution apply equally to both commercial and non-commercial productions?
answer: Yes, the requirement of 10 years applies to both commercial and non-commercial contributions.

scheme_name: Visit to Old/Sick Artistes
question: Am I required to be currently active in tiatr performances to receive this support, or is past contribution sufficient?
answer: Past contribution is sufficient; the eligibility is based on years of contribution, not current activity.

scheme_name: Visit to Old/Sick Artistes
question: Can I still qualify if I contributed significantly but for less than 10 years in the tiatr field?
answer: No, the scheme requires a minimum of 10 years of contribution to be eligible.

scheme_name: Visit to Old/Sick Artistes
question: If I am already admitted in a hospital due to illness, will visits still be arranged for me?
answer: Yes, members of the tiatr fraternity may visit you at the hospital to inquire about your health.

scheme_name: Visit to Old/Sick Artistes
question: Who will decide whether I am identified as an old or sick artiste for the purpose of this scheme?
answer: The Tiatr Academy of Goa will identify eligible artistes based on reports from the tiatr fraternity.

scheme_name: Visit to Old/Sick Artistes
question: If my main involvement has been in writing scripts without staging 10 full tiatr productions, do I still qualify?
answer: No, writers must have staged at least 10 tiatr, khell tiatr, or khell productions to be eligible.

scheme_name: Visit to Old/Sick Artistes
question: If I meet the eligibility criteria, will I automatically receive financial assistance, or is it linked to the first visit?
answer: The one-time financial assistance of ₹10,000 is provided during the first visit of this nature.

scheme_name: Visit to Old/Sick Artistes
question: Is the financial assistance under this scheme restricted for use only towards medical treatment?
answer: Yes, the assistance is intended to be used for meeting medical expenses of the artiste.

scheme_name: Visit to Old/Sick Artistes
question: Will the support under this scheme be given more than once if I remain unwell over a long period?
answer: No, the financial assistance is a one-time support provided during the first visit only.

scheme_name: Visit to Old/Sick Artistes
question: Do I need to arrange my own travel if I wish to meet fellow artistes as part of this scheme?
answer: No, the Tiatr Academy of Goa provides either a vehicle or travel allowance for volunteers making the visits.

scheme_name: Visit to Old/Sick Artistes
question: Will the Academy provide any refreshments or meals for volunteers who visit old or sick artistes?
answer: Yes, refreshments or a working meal are provided to the volunteers during their visits.

scheme_name: Veerjyoti Puraskars
question: Can a woman or girl apply for this recognition if she displayed courage while defending a third party, such as another victim?
answer: Yes, eligibility extends to acts of bravery displayed against atrocities, violence, or harassment directed against the applicant or against any other woman or girl.

scheme_name: Veerjyoti Puraskars

scheme_name: Veerjyoti Puraskars

scheme_name: Veerjyoti Puraskars
question: Which high-ranking official within the Directorate of Women and Child Development holds the position of Chairperson of the Selection Committee?

scheme_name: Veerjyoti Puraskars

scheme_name: Veerjyoti Puraskars
question: What is the purpose of the recognition provided by this scheme for women and girls in the State of Goa?
