scheme_name: Veerjyoti Puraskars
question: Besides the monetary compensation, what form of official documentation or non-cash benefit is conferred upon the recipient?
answer: Along with the cash prize, the recipient also receives a scroll or a citation as a formal recognition of their exemplary courage and deeds.

scheme_name: Veerjyoti Puraskars
question: Which specific department or officer within the government is officially responsible for the implementation and execution of this scheme?
answer: The scheme is implemented by the Social Welfare Officer in the Directorate of Women and Child Development.

scheme_name: Veerjyoti Puraskars
question: Is there a limit on the total number of persons who can be recognized and granted this prestigious award during any given year?
answer: The recognition is strictly limited to only two persons in the State of Goa who are selected to receive the award annually.

scheme_name: Veerjyoti Puraskars
question: Who is the designated official serving as the Member-Secretary on the State Level Selection Committee for the award selection process?
answer: The Director (Women and Child Development) is designated to serve as the Member-Secretary for the State Level Selection Committee.

scheme_name: Veerjyoti Puraskars
question: If I wish to apply, where can I obtain the prescribed format necessary for successfully submitting a complete and formal application?
answer: The required application format is available on the official website of the Directorate of Women and Child Development.

scheme_name: Veerjyoti Puraskars
question: What are the general demographic requirements concerning gender that must be met by the individual applying for this specific scheme?
answer: The applicant for this award must be either a woman or a girl who has demonstrated exceptional courage and fought for dignity.

scheme_name: Veerjyoti Puraskars
question: On what specific public holiday or ceremonial day is the recognition typically conferred upon the chosen recipients each year?
answer: The awards are officially conferred annually on Republic Day, which falls on the 26th of January, starting from the year 2016.

scheme_name: Veerjyoti Puraskars
question: Can you confirm the official designation of one of the external committee members, specifically those who are not ex-officio position holders?
answer: The committee includes two named members who are Shri. Elvis Coutinho and Shri. Sharmad Raiturkar.

scheme_name: Visvesvaraya PhD Scheme for Electronics and IT: Full Time PhD Candidates
question: What was the rationale behind initiation of the scheme?
answer: In addition to enhancement of the number of PhDs in Electronics System Design & Manufacturing (ESDM) and IT/IT Enabled Services (IT/ITES) sectors in the country the scheme aims to: | - Give thrust to R&D, create an innovative ecosystem and enhance India’s competitiveness in these knowledge intensive sectors. | - Thrust on significantly increasing the number of PhDs in the country to enable India to compete globally in the coming decades, to develop an ecosystem of research, development and IP creation in these knowledge intensive sectors.

scheme_name: Visvesvaraya PhD Scheme for Electronics and IT: Full Time PhD Candidates
question: How many PhD candidates will the scheme support?
answer: The scheme aims to support 1000 full-time PhD candidates.

scheme_name: Visvesvaraya PhD Scheme for Electronics and IT: Full Time PhD Candidates
question: Which institutions are eligible to participate in the scheme?
answer: Please refer to https://phd.dic.gov.in/eligibility for eligibility.

scheme_name: Visvesvaraya PhD Scheme for Electronics and IT: Full Time PhD Candidates
question: What are the eligibility criteria for PhD candidates?
answer: Visvesvaraya PhD Scheme is an institutional scheme wherein eligible institutions submit proposals requesting Full-time PhD seats against an active call for proposal by Visvesvaraya PhD Scheme, DIC, MeitY. | - The call for proposal for Full-time PhD seats is notified by PhD Cell, DIC; MeitY through the web portal https://phd.dic.gov.in/ | - Proposals for allotment of Full-time PhD seats are to be submitted by eligible institutions only. Suitable number of seats would be allotted to institutions for further enrollment of PDF fellows on these seats following the scheme guidelines. | - The institutions with PhD seats, allotted under the scheme, would conduct their admission process for enrolment of candidates on those seats. | - The support will be for additional PhD candidates taken up by an institution. No support would be provided for current levels of enrolment in the PhD programme at the institutions. Transfer from other scholarship schemes would not be permitted. | - Candidates already availing financial support from other government schemes are not eligible.

scheme_name: Visvesvaraya PhD Scheme for Electronics and IT: Full Time PhD Candidates
question: Can a candidate apply for this scheme if they have already started their PhD?
answer: No, the scheme applies only to new PhD scholars enrolled after the PhD seats are allocated to the eligible institutions.

scheme_name: Visvesvaraya PhD Scheme for Electronics and IT: Full Time PhD Candidates
question: How are institutions allotted seats?
answer: Visvesvaraya PhD Scheme is an institutional scheme wherein eligible institutions submit proposals requesting Full-time PhD seats against an active call for proposal by Visvesvaraya PhD Scheme, DIC, MeitY. | - The call for proposal for Full-time PhD seats is notified by PhD Cell, DIC; MeitY through the web portal https://phd.dic.gov.in/ | - Proposals for allotment of Full-time PhD seats are to be submitted by eligible institutions only. Suitable number of seats would be allotted to institutions for further enrollment of PDF fellows on these seats following the scheme guidelines and evaluation of the submitted proposals.

scheme_name: Visvesvaraya PhD Scheme for Electronics and IT: Full Time PhD Candidates
question: What is the procedure for joining the PhD Scheme?
answer: Visvesvaraya PhD Scheme is an institutional scheme where seats are allocated to eligible institutions for enrolment during particular academic year. The candidates, interested to join the scheme, need to contact respective institutions for admission formalities.

scheme_name: Visvesvaraya PhD Scheme for Electronics and IT: Full Time PhD Candidates
question: What financial support is available for full-time PhD candidates?
answer: - Fellowship | - ₹38,750/- per month (1st & 2nd year) | - ₹43,750/- per month (3rd, 4th & 5th year) | - Reimbursement of Rent (RoR) | - Institutional Overheads of ₹25,000 per year per Full-time PhD candidate. | - Research contingency grant of ₹1,20,000 per year per Full-time PhD candidate. | - Support up to ₹1.5 lakh for attending International Conferences. | - One-time support of ₹10.5 lakh for 250 selected PhD candidates for a 6-month visit to labs abroad.

scheme_name: Visvesvaraya PhD Scheme for Electronics and IT: Full Time PhD Candidates
question: How will the funds be disbursed?
answer: - Fellowships and RoR will be transferred directly to candidates' bank accounts | - Institutional Overheads and Research Contingency Grants will be sent to the respective institutions.

scheme_name: Visvesvaraya PhD Scheme for Electronics and IT: Full Time PhD Candidates
question: What is meant by Reimbursement of Rent (RoR)?
answer: This component is linked with the fellowship of PhD Candidate. The rate of RoR is 24%, 16% & 8% (of fellowship) for X, Y & Z class cities/towns respectively. The classification of the cities is as per the notification issued by the Ministry of Finance for HRA. | RoR the support is applicable to only those PhD candidates who are not availing hostel facility by the institution.

scheme_name: Visvesvaraya PhD Scheme for Electronics and IT: Full Time PhD Candidates
question: What happens if a candidate drops out from the scheme?
answer: The institution has to immediately inform the PhD Cell, DIC and obtain an acknowledgement from PhD Cell. If not reported on time, the institution will be responsible for recovering any excess funds paid to the candidate.

scheme_name: Visvesvaraya PhD Scheme for Electronics and IT: Full Time PhD Candidates
question: Can an institution transfer its PhD seats to another year if not filled?
answer: No, unfilled seats will be reallocated to the general pool and assigned to other institutions.

scheme_name: Visvesvaraya PhD Scheme for Electronics and IT: Full Time PhD Candidates
question: Can the fellowship be extended beyond five years?
answer: No, the maximum duration of support is five years or until PhD completion, whichever is earlier.

scheme_name: Visvesvaraya PhD Scheme for Electronics and IT: Full Time PhD Candidates
question: Is there any funding for laboratory equipment under the research contingency grant?
answer: Yes, institutions can apply for funding for research equipment under Research Contingency Grant, but civil construction/expansion costs are not covered.

scheme_name: Visvesvaraya PhD Scheme for Electronics and IT: Full Time PhD Candidates
question: What is included under support for International Conference?
answer: This covers the travel and other expenses of a PhD candidate for attending an International conference, where the research paper has been accepted for oral (not poster) presentation. There is a list of renowned International Conferences related to the areas of ESDM and IT/ITES where the candidate can visit (https://phd.dic.gov.in/about/ListOfInternationalConferences.pdf)

scheme_name: Visvesvaraya PhD Scheme for Electronics and IT: Post-Doctoral Fellowships (PDF)
question: Who can submit proposals for allotment of PDF seats?
answer: Only eligible institutions can submit proposals for allotment of PDF seats. Individual applicants cannot directly apply to PhD Cell, DIC, MeitY.

scheme_name: Visvesvaraya PhD Scheme for Electronics and IT: Post-Doctoral Fellowships (PDF)
question: What is the educational qualification required?
answer: The applicant must have obtained a PhD degree from a recognized University with first class (in terms of grades) in all preceding levels and a good academic record.

scheme_name: Visvesvaraya PhD Scheme for Electronics and IT: Post-Doctoral Fellowships (PDF)
question: Is there a time limit after PhD completion to apply?
answer: The PhD must have been completed within the last 5 years as of the last date of application submission to the institution.

scheme_name: Visvesvaraya PhD Scheme for Electronics and IT: Post-Doctoral Fellowships (PDF)
question: What is the maximum age limit for applicants?
answer: The upper age limit is 40 years on the date of application submission to the institution.

scheme_name: Visvesvaraya PhD Scheme for Electronics and IT: Post-Doctoral Fellowships (PDF)
question: Can the fellowship be availed in the same institution where the applicant earned their PhD?
answer: No. Applicants should not have completed their PhD from the same institution where the fellowship is to be undertaken.

scheme_name: Visvesvaraya PhD Scheme for Electronics and IT: Post-Doctoral Fellowships (PDF)
question: Will preference be given to any specific applicants?
answer: Yes. Preference will be given to applicants with active industry linkages and research proposals targeting industry-specific problems.

scheme_name: Visvesvaraya PhD Scheme for Electronics and IT: Post-Doctoral Fellowships (PDF)
question: Where can the fellowship be undertaken?
answer: The fellowship can be undertaken only in India at recognized and eligible academic or R&D institutions.

scheme_name: Visvesvaraya PhD Scheme for Electronics and IT: Post-Doctoral Fellowships (PDF)
question: What is the duration of the fellowship?
answer: It is awarded for one year initially, with the possibility of extension based on performance review.

scheme_name: Visvesvaraya PhD Scheme for Electronics and IT: Post-Doctoral Fellowships (PDF)
question: Can fellows hold another fellowship simultaneously?
answer: No. The PDF is a full-time assignment and fellows cannot receive any other fellowship from Government or Non-Government sources during its tenure.

scheme_name: Visvesvaraya PhD Scheme for Electronics and IT: Post-Doctoral Fellowships (PDF)
question: Can the fellowship be transferred to another institution?
answer: No. The fellowship is non-transferable and must be carried out at the same institution where the seat is allocated.

scheme_name: Visvesvaraya PhD Scheme for Electronics and IT: Post-Doctoral Fellowships (PDF)
question: How is Post-doctoral Fellowship (PDF) awarded?
answer: Proposals for allotment of PDF seats are to be submitted by eligible institutions only. Suitable no. of seats would be allotted to institutions for further enrollment of PDF fellows on these seats following the scheme guidelines.

scheme_name: Visvesvaraya PhD Scheme for Electronics and IT: Part Time PhD Candidates
question: What is the main objective of the scheme?
answer: The objective is to increase the number of PhDs in ESDM and IT/ITES, encourage R&D, strengthen the innovation ecosystem, and enhance India’s global competitiveness in these sectors.

scheme_name: Visvesvaraya PhD Scheme for Electronics and IT: Part Time PhD Candidates
question: How many Part-Time PhD candidates will be supported under the scheme?

scheme_name: Visvesvaraya PhD Scheme for Electronics and IT: Part Time PhD Candidates

scheme_name: Visvesvaraya PhD Scheme for Electronics and IT: Part Time PhD Candidates
question: Are candidates already availing other government fellowships eligible?

scheme_name: Visvesvaraya PhD Scheme for Electronics and IT: Part Time PhD Candidates
question: How are Part-Time PhD seats allocated to institutions?
answer: - The call for proposal for Part-time PhD seats is notified by PhD Cell, DIC; MeitY through the web portal https://phd.dic.gov.in/ | - Proposals for allotment of Part-time PhD seats are to be submitted by eligible institutions only. scheme_name: Visvesvaraya PhD Scheme for Electronics and IT: Part Time PhD Candidates
question: Which institutions are eligible to participate in the scheme?
answer: Please refer to https://phd.dic.gov.in/eligibility for eligibility of institutions.

scheme_name: Visvesvaraya PhD Scheme for Electronics and IT: Part Time PhD Candidates
question: What financial support do Part-Time PhD candidates receive?
answer: They receive a one-time incentive of ₹3,00,000 upon successful completion of their PhD degree and submission of completion documents to PhD Cell, DIC.

scheme_name: Visvesvaraya PhD Scheme for Electronics and IT: Part Time PhD Candidates
question: Is the incentive given during the course of study?
answer: No, the incentive is disbursed only after successful completion of the PhD.

scheme_name: Visvesvaraya PhD Scheme for Electronics and IT: Part Time PhD Candidates
question: Who disburses the incentive amount?
answer: The PhD Cell at Digital India Corporation (DIC), MeitY, disburses the incentive.

scheme_name: Visvesvaraya PhD Scheme for Electronics and IT: Part Time PhD Candidates
question: On what grounds can support be terminated?
answer: Support can be terminated due to lack of progress, violation/non-compliance of scheme guidelines, or any other reason deemed appropriate by the PhD Cell, DIC.

scheme_name: Shri Varun Panwar Memorial Award for B.Sc. Agriculture (2nd Year, 3rd Year, and 4th Year) Students

scheme_name: Sishu Saathi
question: What is the "Sishu Saathi" Scheme?
answer: The "Sishu Saathi" Scheme is a health initiative launched by the Government of West Bengal to provide free cardiac surgeries and treatment to children aged 0 to 18 years, irrespective of their financial background.

answer: The main objective of the scheme is to offer free treatment to children with cardiac and congenital conditions, ensuring that no child is denied surgery due to financial constraints.

question: Who is eligible for the "Sishu Saathi" Scheme?
answer: All children between 0 to 18 years of age, living in rural or urban areas of West Bengal, are eligible for the scheme regardless of their family income.

scheme_name: Sishu Saathi
question: Which medical conditions are covered under the Scheme?
answer: The scheme primarily covers paediatric cardiac conditions and is being expanded to include surgeries for congenital cataract, cleft lips, and cleft palates.

scheme_name: Sishu Saathi
question: How can a child be identified for treatment under the scheme?

scheme_name: Sishu Saathi
question: Does the scheme cover the cost of surgery and post-operative care?
answer: Yes, the West Bengal Government bears all expenses related to the surgery, hospital stay, and post-operative care.

scheme_name: Sishu Saathi
question: What steps has the government taken to identify children in need of treatment?
answer: The government conducts regular health screenings in schools to identify children with cardiac or congenital issues and refers them for further treatment.

scheme_name: Sishu Saathi

answer: Parents or guardians can contact government hospitals or partner private hospitals for free surgery under the scheme.
